  `is_already_ptr` forwarded). **Root: a layering violation, not a missing arm** — `lower_call_arg` rebuilt "is this a place?" from the
  TYPE `lower_expr` happened to return (devbook/24 litmus). **Fix: one shared `try_resolve_place` producer with an ENFORCED
  postcondition** (the returned Place is an lvalue of the value, never of a pointer to it), called by both `&`-formation faces,
  ownership-gated at the call-arg face, ordered AFTER the G2 root-materialize and BEFORE `lower_expr`. **Also fixed:** an attributable
  LEAK (`f(&(*box).field)` on a resource field materialized a whole-struct clone nobody dropped — unbounded in a loop), and the
  devbook/24 **rule-3 violation underneath the bug** (the 6× Ptr-wrap predicate → `field_read_yields_ptr` + a one-home lint).
  **Guard (Core #6):** a 3-limb lint whose third limb is load-bearing — short-circuiting the producer leaves arm-sets equal and the
  `emit_borrow_mut` count at 28, so limbs 1+2 both report green; demonstrated RED by executor and reviewer independently.
  Gates: **C 1846/0 · LLVM 1846/0** · lib 1129 · lints 75 · security 126 · ggdef all targets · spec_conformance 3/3 lanes ·
  `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` ok (809s, serial). Merge `2ae21079`.
  ⚠ **FIVE output-review rounds; FOUR found defects the fix itself introduced or did not reach** — a `Ref[T]` pointer-field SIGSEGV, a
  `TupleFieldAccess` swallowed `Error` (callee handed a `Result*` where an `int` was expected, then writing through it), the object-arm
  domain (`(*b).f`, `guard.f`), and `&guard.field` losing the write. **Root of three of them: an INVERTED comment** asserting a `None`
  return was "the conservative answer" that "costs a lost optimisation, never a lost propagation" — while the call site did
  `unwrap_or(false)` → `!false` → **SKIP**. The author reasoned from it every time. The predicate is now **fail-safe by construction**
  (`None => false`), so the invariant is enforced by a `match` rather than asserted in prose. **LESSONS (→ devbook/29-30):**
  (a) *the fold is the dominant defect source* — 15 brief-review passes, 19 blocking, and **six blockers were introduced BY A FOLD**;
  twice the author's anchor-verification command differed from the command written into the brief (`grep -n` vs `grep -nF --`).
  (b) *nine enumerations presented as closed were selections.*
  (c) **THE TWO-MASK INCIDENT** — three parties measured three different answers to one behavioural question and **all three were reading
  their own program correctly**: two independent masks (closure-var annotation `auto` vs `Callable[…]`, and payload `Error` vs `Ok`),
  either alone hiding the defect, exactly one of four cells exposing it. **When two agents disagree on a behavioural claim, the default
  hypothesis is that they are running different programs — arbitrate by diffing the PROGRAMS, not the conclusions.**
  (d) *no lint could ever demand the last two cells* — the arm-set extractor's domain is syntactic, the producer's is partly type-driven
  (Guard auto-deref), so the durable mitigation is the axis-complete write-through fixture, not a guard.
  **Filed, not fixed** (each with a committed `known_gaps` repro): the self-host lane mirror (no `CallArg.ownership` in the SH AST → must
  key on `borrow_flags`, plus forced bootstrap re-convergence) · Family-2's cross-resolver `&t.0.fd` · the indirect-call auto-propagate

Fix computes `is_throws_main = func.name=="main" AND enum_kind==EK_RESULT` in `emit_function_body` (both conjuncts load-bearing — `enum_kind==EK_RESULT` alone fires for EVERY `T throws E` fn and would corrupt them), threads it into `emit_term`, and unwraps a Result-SHAPED return (Ok→0, Error→Error_0) with an INNER value-shape guard so the bare `int32 0` success tail falls through (the self-host, unlike Rust, does NOT wrap the success tail in Ok(unit), so an unconditional unwrap would break the success path). Core #2-clean: `enum_kind` for TYPE meaning, `func.name=="main"` only for entry-point identity (Rust-canonical, `c_lir/mod.rs:3328`). Success path exit 0 `42\nsuccess` byte-identical; a throwing variant (`rethrow 7`) exits 7 on both. **(R42-D `83187328`) `format()` free-fn identity-passthrough intercept (+1):** `string_format` CC-FAILed — the self-host had no `format()` free-fn intercept, so it emitted a raw `format(int)` (undefined → typed int), and `.to_upper()` on the int receiver mis-dispatched to the char method `gorget_uint8_to_upper` → `Str = int`. Fix adds a `format` intercept (identity pass-through of the arg, which EFString/EStringLiteral already lower to a typed drop-clean GorgetString), gated on the arg being a string-literal node (mirroring Rust `calls.rs:807` which intercepts only a StringLiteral arg — a non-literal falls through). - [2026-06-26] **🐛 LLVM BACKEND ABI — `bool` args to C-runtime functions now carry `zeroext` (fixes CI `leak_string_heavy`).** `leak_string_heavy` was failing on the LLVM backend only: it printed `p1..p5 = 0` (no leak) yet `leaked=true`, i.e. `not all_zero` returned `true` when `all_zero` was `true`. Root cause was NOT a leak — it was a miscompiled `not`/comparison. Gorget `bool` lowers to LLVM `i1`, but the C runtime's `gorget_bool_to_str(_Bool)` / `gorget_string_push_bool(_Bool)` / `gorget_string_push_line_bool(_Bool)` were declared `(…, i1)` with **no `zeroext`**. Per the x86-64 psABI a `_Bool` arg must be zero-extended; an `i1` produced by `icmp`/`xor` lives in a register with undefined high bits, so the separately-`cc`-compiled C runtime read garbage. The IR was correct (`%v19 = xor i1 %v4, 1`) — the defect was purely the ABI attribute, which is why it was latent and only surfaced after ~40 commits of unrelated codegen churn shifted register allocation (a literal `0` operand const-folds the comparison and hides it; the trigger needs a *runtime* comparison result). Fix (`src/backend/llvm/mod.rs`): added `llvm_c_param_type` (returns `i1 zeroext` for `Bool`, else `llvm_arg_type`); annotated the three manual runtime declares + routed the user-FFI `extern`-block param path through it so the class can't recur (declare-only suffices — llc applies the declaration's param attribute to direct call sites; verified by hand-patching the `.ll` and relinking). Process: no Rust toolchain on the box → installed rustup, rebuilt from current HEAD (the prebuilt `gg` was 10 days/61-src-files stale and passed), reproduced on LLVM, bisected to a 6-line repro, root-caused via the emitted `.ll`, proved the fix end-to-end (llc + relink) before touching Rust. Added regression fixture `bool_not_runtime_cmp_abi` (runtime cmp → `not` → bool_to_str + `String.push(bool)`; both backends byte-identical). Full LLVM sweep: **1369 passed / 4 failed / 2 ignored**; all 4 failures (`async_blocking_coroutine`, `async_blocking_io`, `spawn_blocking_basic`, `spawn_blocking_multi`) are pre-existing + ENVIRONMENTAL (`cannot open /tmp/gorget_*.txt` — this sandbox's `std.fs.write_file` to `/tmp` doesn't work) and fail IDENTICALLY on the C backend, so unrelated. Gates: `leak_string_heavy` GREEN on both backends; new fixture GREEN on both; C backend unaffected (change is LLVM-only).

- [2026-06-22] **🐛 RUST-GG CODEGEN — expression-body `throws` fn tail Ok-wrap + the `T = Result` silent miscompile (gorget-1; Fix1 `ac8f0e98` + perf `7b859cba` + B1 fold).** Two layers. **Fix 1 (the obvious one):** an expr-body `throws` fn (`int inc(int x) throws String: x + 1`) assigned its bare-`T` tail straight into the synthesized `Result[T, E]` return slot without the `Ok(...)` wrap → ill-typed C (the block-body path wrapped via `lower_return`). Verified the inner `return Error(...)` (outer Ok of inner Error) vs `throw` (outer Error) distinction is preserved. ⚠ **SCOPE (output-review-narrowed):** the original `8fd26a1d` gate (`declared_t_is_result`) matched ONLY `EnumCategory::Result`, so `T=Option` was claimed-but-NOT-fixed (a `Some(...)`/`None` tail kept the shortcut ON → the 16-byte inner `Option` was direct-assigned into the larger outer `Result` slot, a STACK-BUFFER OVERFLOW `-Wstringop-overread` + silently dropped value). The fold commit broadened the gate to `Result | Option` (`declared_t_is_enum_wrapper`, both `lower_return` sites) — `throws_expr_body_tail.gg` now also covers 3 `T=Option[int]` shapes (`wrap_opt_expr`/`_block`/`_some` + throw path) → `21\n-2\n56\n-4` (drops `56` + overflows WITHOUT, correct + ASan/LSan clean WITH). **WHAT IS FIXED: the expr-body / block-body / return `throws` Ok-wrap for `T`=non-`Result`/`Option`, AND for `T`=`Result`/`Option` with a NON-RESOURCE (int) inner payload.** **WHAT REMAINS (FILED known defect, `#[ignore]`'d):** `T`=`Result`/`Option` with a RESOURCE (heap-String) INNER payload DOUBLE-FREES (the outer-Ok-wrap path doesn't transfer/register ownership of the inner resource — orthogonal deeper drop-tracking gap, NOT closed by the Option one-liner). The separately-discovered `throws` equip-METHOD-call-consumed-by-`catch` ill-typed-C bug (still reproduces) STAYS in TODO (`83e274e4`). main UNTOUCHED.

- [2026-06-17] **🌟 TEST CORRECTNESS — `shared_with_check_then_act` now asserts the §3.5 check-then-act WARNING (a real regression net for the FIRST time), not a racy stdout (gorget-1 `39029f0b`; full discipline: scout → 3 brief-reviews → execute → output-review; owner-flagged x86_64 CI failure).** The fixture pinned `was zero\nafter sleep\n1` via `run_gg` (stdout-only) — but that's ONE race-winner of a genuinely racy program (the spawned `worker` and `main`'s `if x==0` check have no happens-before; x86_64 CI got `1` when the worker won the spawn→check race), AND the §3.5 WARNING it's named for (on stderr) was NEVER asserted (if the warning silently regressed, the test would've stayed green). **Doc investigation (`docs/book/14-concurrency.md`) confirmed the RUNTIME is CORRECT, not buggy:** `with` is "freshness, not atomicity" (`:163`), the lock is RELEASED at the `sleep` yield (`:166`), a spawned task manages its own lock concurrently (§3.8 `:444`), and ORDERING is a channel's job — `with` does NOT provide it (Pattern 1 `:197`). So the TEST was wrong (relied on `with` for ordering it doesn't give), not the program. The owner's initial "`with` holds the condition across the sleep" model was refuted by the docs; `scheduler=single` was rejected (defeats the multithread synchronization the test exists to demonstrate); a channel-handshake was considered but the deeper fix is to test the WARNING. Fix: new `build_gg_expect_warning(fixture, substr)` (asserts build-success [warning non-fatal] + build-stderr-contains-warning + binary-exit-0; **NO stdout pin**) → `shared_with_check_then_act` asserts `"condition may no longer hold"`; the lir_ab sibling (`lir_ab_shared_with_check_then_act`) gets a new `ab_test_build_only` (both backends build+run, no racy-stdout compare). Fixture `.gg` UNCHANGED (the racy program IS the correct §3.5 demonstration; the test was wrong, not the program). **PROVEN TO BITE** (the old `run_gg` never could): neutering the §3.5 emission (`check_with_check_then_act`) FAILS the converted test (`Expected build stderr to contain warning 'condition may no longer hold'`), restoring passes. lib 1085/0; converted test + all `lir_ab_shared_with_*` pass; clean `gg build` emits the warning. Filed (TODO): the `--scheduler=`-ignored CLI bug, the 176B pool exit-leak, and the pre-existing dead `lir_ab_lifetime_groups` test (missing fixture).

- [2026-06-09] **⚠⚠ CoW lazy-materialization — GROUND TRUTH after THREE measurement errors (final, verified by reading emitted C of BOTH compilers).** This question flip-flopped NO-GO→GO→NO-GO due to repeated counter-misreads; the VERIFIED truth (do not re-measure with counters — READ the emitted-C clone callsite location): **On the borrowed-element-bind-read-after-a-source-mutation shapes (`witness_never`/`witness_taken`/`witness_cond_straightline`), BOTH Rust `gg` AND the self-host EAGER-clone `s` at the BIND** (Rust: `gorget_string_clone_to_owned` at `__bb3` BEFORE `goto __bb4`=loop header, unconditional; self-host: at `__bb9` before `goto __bb1`=loop entry; the dead `if`-branch with the `big.push` has NO clone in either). The prototype scout's per-call stderr instrumentation = 1 clone each, byte-identical. **Neither compiler is "lazy" on these shapes** — both eager-clone whenever the source is mutated on ANY forward path (even a dead/conditional branch), because Rust's `is_source_mut_unsafe_at` (`context.rs:1116`) is conservative and routes them to the eager-clone branch (`stmts/mod.rs:766-777,819`). The 3 measurement errors, all the SAME class (a counter that doesn't count `gorget_string_clone_to_owned`): L2 scout counted static callsites + `string_cow`(=0); feasibility scout counted static `clone_to_owned` callsites in main (mislabeled the bind-block clone as in-branch); the orchestrator read `total_allocs` 3-vs-4 and attributed the +1 to the clone when it was the `big.push` string on the taken branch. **ANSWER to the owner's "is full lazy materialization possible": (1) NON-LOOP conditional source-mutation (`s=coll.get(i).unwrap(); if cond: coll.push(x); read(s)`) — YES, fully possible AND strictly BETTER than Rust: borrow `s`, clone INSIDE `if cond:` before the push (sound — clone-before-mutation, no loop so nothing dangles), saving the clone when `cond` is false. Rust leaves this on the table (conservative gate). This is the real achievable win. (2) LOOP-body source-mutation — the hard part: materialize-at-mutation dangles across realloc (`a12333a0` UAF); a pre-header hoist is sound but = eager-before-loop (no gain over today); true loop-laziness needs a loop-carried owned slot + per-iteration guard (possible, complex, marginal). NOTHING architecturally impossible — but the realizable benefit is NARROW (non-loop conditional shape only; the common loop case is at-best-eager-parity), NOT "full lazy everywhere."** Re-open bar: a witness whose executed-`clone_to_owned` count under a lazy compiler is provably lower than the current eager count on the same input — the non-loop conditional shape qualifies; pursue it as a self-contained `lower.gg`/`lower_cow.gg` flip (extend the flip to allow borrow + materialize-at-mutation when the only forward mutation is non-loop-conditional) IF the owner wants the narrow win, gated `fixed_point`+ASan+the `a12333a0` canaries. ⭐⭐ **LESSON (thrice-learned): a clone-yield claim is the EXECUTED clone count or the emitted-C callsite LOCATION (read it), NEVER a stats counter you haven't verified instruments the exact clone fn. The dead-branch-vs-taken A/B is only valid if you've confirmed the counter counts `clone_to_owned`.** (The `T__clone` aggregate-deep-clone axis, 81M/1.18GB self-compile, remains a real ORTHOGONAL lever.)

- [2026-06-01] **FIDELITY (Heap) — route monomorphized `Heap__<T>` as a UserType, not a GorgetArray alias (self-host `lir_lower.gg`).** Fixed the `heap_basic`/`heap_advanced`/`heap_edges` CC-FAIL ("unknown type name 'Heap__double'"). **Root (deeper than the brief's typedef framing — the brief's preferred fix was empirically DISPROVEN at cc time):** `Heap[T]` is a *user-defined generic struct* (`lib/std/heap.gg`: `struct Heap[T]: Vector[T] heap_data`), NOT a runtime collection. The self-host's Pass-1 `CkHeap()` arm (`lir_lower.gg:733`) was aliasing the mono `Heap__<T>` to `GorgetArray` (`type_runtime_map` + `dispatched=true`), which made `should_skip_struct` drop its struct body — while `populate_drop_metadata` still emitted `Heap__<T>__drop`/`__clone` bodies that access `self->heap_data` (read from its `gmod.type_infos` fields). So a `typedef GorgetArray Heap__double;` (the brief's fix) made the type known but then cc-failed on `self->heap_data` ('GorgetArray' has no member 'heap_data'). Fix: make the `CkHeap()` arm leave `dispatched=false` (drop the `type_runtime_map`/`sr` alias) so Heap falls through to the user-struct placeholder path; Pass 2 fills `heap_data` from type_infos → emits a real `struct Heap__<T> { GorgetArray heap_data; }`, byte-identical in shape to Rust's `struct __gg_Heap__<T>`. Mirrors Rust, which *deliberately excludes* `Heap__` from the GorgetArray-alias path and routes it as UserType (`src/lir/lower/insts.rs:2008-2012,2024-2029`). The `coll_elem_type_map` side-effect (ownership/sizing) is kept; only the type-layer alias is removed. **Result:** all three now COMPILE + RUN; **heap_advanced + heap_edges = MATCH**; heap_basic compiles+runs but is WRONG-OUTPUT on ONE line (`peek()` prints 0 vs Rust's 5) due to a SEPARATE pre-existing self-host gap — `Option[Ref[T]]→Option[T]` auto-deref-conversion at a return boundary is mis-lowered (hardcodes `tag=1`/None, drops the payload) — logged to TODO. Gates: `cargo test --lib` 1066/0; `self_host_runtime` lock-in net 241/0 (no regression); `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` GREEN (self-host uses no Heap). Net: 2 CC-FAIL→MATCH, 1 CC-FAIL→WRONG-OUTPUT (a strict improvement; the residual is a separately-tracked bug).

- [2026-05-31] **R4 PERF: packed 2-bit `SlotStates` in `self_host_lowerer/drop_elab.gg` (mirror Rust `drop_elab.rs`) — elaborate_drops 11.3s/42% → 0.54s/3.4% (~21×), total self-compile ~27.0s → ~16.0s (~10.7s saved). Output-NEUTRAL: c_emit 849 / lowerer 951 UNCHANGED, fixed_point GREEN (reconverges byte-identical), lib 1064/0.** State went from `Vector[int]` (1 int/slot + branchy `init_meet`) to a packed `Vector[int]` of 64-bit words, 2 bits/slot (Init=0b01/Uninit=0b10/Maybe=0b11/0b00=unreached→reads-Maybe), so lattice meet == word-wise bitwise-OR and copy/equal are O(slots/32). MASKED-SIGNED `int` path (no `uint`): every decode masks `(word>>shift)&3` (discards the arithmetic-shift sign bits), `ss_set` = `(cur & ~(3<<shift)) | (st<<shift)`, `0xAAAA…` built by a `for i in 0..32: w |= 2<<(2*i)` loop (the literal overflows the lexer). Sizing uniform `n_words=ceil(n/32)`; `empty()` seed stays zero-length (change-detection sentinel); `clear_tail` NOT ported (OR-meet is tail-stable from the single all_uninit seed — review-verified, confirmed identical fixpoint). Verified the packed dataflow's per-block in-states are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the baseline's (instrumented dump diff = 0).
  - **Found + fixed a real self-host compiler GAP (the bug that the fixed-point double-free exposed):** `self_host_lowerer/lower.gg`'s `EUnaryOp` lowering had cases for `"-"` (UNOP_NEG) and `"not"` (UNOP_NOT) but **NO case for `"~"` (bitwise NOT)** — it fell through `else: pass` → `return inner`, SILENTLY DROPPING the `~`. So `cur & ~(3<<shift)` compiled (by the self-host) as `cur & (3<<shift)`, clearing every OTHER field of the word → lattice corruption → over-Maybe → extra guarded drops → double-free in the stage-2 binary's `Parser__parse_import_item`. The Rust gg compiles `~` correctly, so the cargo-built driver's dataflow was correct; only the self-host-compiled self-host miscompiled it (cold path: `~` is exercised nowhere else in self-host). Fix: add the `"~"` case → `GIUnOp(dst, UNOP_BITNOT, inner_type, OpCopy(inner))` (mirrors Rust `operators.rs:407,410` — result_type == operand_type; `UNOP_BITNOT`/`IBitNot` were already wired in `gir.gg`/`lir_lower.gg`/`lir_codegen.gg`/`format_gir.gg`, lower.gg was the only missing link). Per CLAUDE.md "fix the gap, don't redesign around it" — avoiding `~` in drop_elab would have been the forbidden dodge. After the fix, `parse_import_item` in stage-2 is byte-identical to baseline.
  - Peak RSS ~1.21 GB (baseline 1.207 → packed 1.201; small Δ — the per-function state clones were short-lived, not the peak driver). The win is algorithmic (meet O(slots)→O(slots/32), clone size 32×), not RSS. Self-host runtime has no `--clone-stats` atexit so the exact self-compile array_clone count isn't instrumented; the 21× elaborate_drops drop is the load-bearing measurement.

- [2026-05-27] **Self-host `fixed_point` parse_int `return Error(ParseError.Empty())` SIGSEGV FIXED — prelude-variant constructor results at `return` were mistyped as the bogus standalone variant name (→ LT_PTR slot → NULL store → memcpy-from-NULL).** The fixed_point stage-2 binary SIGSEGV'd (exit 139) in `std.conv.parse_int`: s1bin built `__v10 = (Result__int64_t__ParseError){.tag=1,.Error_0=...}` correctly, then `__s6 = NULL; memcpy(&__s0 /*ret*/, __s6 /*=NULL*/, …)`. **Root cause (case (a), self-host `.gg` logic bug):** `lower.gg`'s `lower_call` could not reconstruct a prelude variant's full monomorphised parent-enum name from the variant alone — `is_type_constructor("Error")` returns true (capitalised, no `__`), `enum_variant_parent("Error")` returns "" (Result/Option are prelude enums, often absent from `type_infos`), so `ret_type = lookup_or_register_named("Error")` minted a bogus `GtNamed("Error")` → `map_gir_type` → **LT_PTR** (an 8-byte pointer slot for a multi-word aggregate). The GIR confirmed it: the self-host (and the Rust-gg-compiled driver) typed the `Error(...)` result local `_6: Error`, whereas Rust gg types it `_6: Result__int64_t__PErr` and emits `enum_init Result::Error`. At that LT_PTR slot, `try_lower_prelude_variant` bailed (`slot_ty < LT_STRUCT_BASE`), the aggregate fell through to a value-literal store into a Ptr slot, codegen NULL'd it (`lir_codegen.gg:2777`), and the return-slot copy memcpy'd from NULL → crash. The Rust-gg-compiled DRIVER tolerated the same mistyping because its `run_ssa` copy-propagation collapsed the dead Ptr-slot store; the SELF-HOST `lower_gir_to_lir` has NO such SSA cleanup, so s1bin emitted the literal NULL store → crash. **Fix (`lower.gg` SReturn, +47 lines, mirrors Rust `lower_return`'s `func_state.expected_type = locals[0].type_id`):** added `expr_is_prelude_variant_ctor` (`Ok`/`Error`/`Some`/`None`, paren or bare) and, at `return`, retype the variant-constructor result local to the function's return place (local 0 already carries the correct registered `Result__T__E`/`Option__T`). That makes the slot aggregate-typed → `try_lower_prelude_variant` emits a canonical in-place `IEnumInit` → no NULL. **Verified:** the GIR now types `_6: Result__int64_t__PErr` (matching Rust); s1bin (rebuilt) emits `((Result*)__v10)->tag=1; memcpy(…Error_0…)` with ZERO NULL stores; the t_pi minrepro binary exits 0 (was 139); the full stage-2 binary gets PAST the parse_int crash (`self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` now fails on a SEPARATE, pre-existing blocker — `Parser__parse_dot_expr` NULL `!`-moved arg — recorded in TODO.md NEXT BLOCKER #2). `self_host_bootstrap` STAYS GREEN; `lowerer_comparison` green; `cargo test --lib --release` 1060/1062 (2 pre-existing `lir::validate` release-mode `#[should_panic]` fails; no `src/` touched). Only `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` changed.

- [2026-05-27] **Self-host bootstrap large-String truncation FIXED — view-returning String methods were tagged `LoOwned` not `LoView` → stored views dangled → NUL injection.** s1bin (the self-host compiler, Rust-gg-compiled to C) ran to exit 0 but emitted a TRUNCATED stage-2 (deterministic 59,415 lines / 1,633,116 B, cut mid-token in `Parser__parse_match_stmt` at `gorget_array_new(sizeof(`). **Diagnostic chain:** STEP-2 probe (`gorget_eprint_debug` of `generate_c(&lir).byte_len()`) showed the String was the FULL ~14.87 MB at assembly — the truncation was at OUTPUT. A NUL-safe `fwrite`-based dump (temporary `gorget_print_raw` runtime fn) revealed **162 embedded NUL bytes** (first at 1,633,533), all inside `gorget_array_new(sizeof(\0\0\0\0))` — corrupted element type names. The bytes traced to `LowerCtx.pending_vec_elem_tyname` holding a **dangling String view**: `apply_container_hint_for_ctor_arg` does `ctx.pending_vec_elem_tyname = fty_name.slice(8,…).clone()`; the `.slice()` view-result local was tagged `LoOwned`, so `op_consume(CkFieldWrite)` emitted `OpMove` (GIR `_48 = move _47`) — a by-value move of the cap==0 view into the owned field — and the view dangled once the receiver buffer was reused (read as NUL). `%s` AND `%.*s` both stop at the first NUL (verified in isolated C), so print truncated there. **Root-cause fix (`tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg`, 1 hunk, ~33 lines):** added `is_string_view_method` (slice/substring/byte_slice/char_at/trim/trim_left/trim_right/strip/lstrip/rstrip/removeprefix/removesuffix/str/as_str — the Rust `returns_view: true` set) and tag those results `LoView()` at the method-call result site (gated on String receiver), mirroring Rust's builtins. `op_consume`'s existing `LoView → OpClone` arm then materializes (deep-copies) the view at every owning consume position. **Result:** s1bin emits the FULL 663,687-line / 14.93 MB stage-2 ending cleanly, ZERO embedded NULs. `self_host_bootstrap` (len ≥ stage0/2 gate) PASSES. The Rust `gg` was always correct (it tags slice results as views via `returns_view`); only the self-host's `lower.gg` had defaulted them to owned. `cargo test --lib --release` 1060/1062 (2 pre-existing `lir::validate` panic-asserts; no `src/` touched). **§5: `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` still FAILS — on a SEPARATE, pre-existing bug newly exposed:** the stage-2 binary (cc'd from s1bin's 14.9 MB output) SIGSEGVs (memcpy-from-NULL) when RUN, in `std.conv.parse_int`'s `return Error(ParseError.Empty())` path — s1bin builds `(Result){.tag=1,.Error_0=...}` then discards it and memcpy's NULL into the return slot (Rust `gg` lowers the same source correctly). NOT caused by the LoView fix (no string-view method on that path); the truncation had masked it. Recorded as the NEW PICK-UP item in TODO.md + `drop_emission.md` "## NEXT STEPS". bug#3b's `lir_push_inst` nested-push lowered correctly in the full stage-2 emission (no dropped/corrupt insts, no SIGSEGV during emission).

- [2026-05-25] **`SlotMap[T]`/user-method resource-`T` leak FIXED — consuming-position clone was gated by method NAME, not param ABI.** `slotmap_cycle_no_leak` (cyclic graph, nodes own heap, edges are `SlotKey`s) leaked a `Vector` per `insert` and was `#[ignore]`'d; now un-ignored and passing (`leaked=false` over 100 iterations). **Root cause** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs`): `lower_method_call` computed `consuming_positions` by name-matching the method (`"push"|"insert"|"set"|"add"|"send"|...`) and at those positions force-materialized an owned value (clone non-last-use, move-zero last-use) + marked the source moved. That "own-then-disown-without-drop" is sound ONLY when the callee consumes BY VALUE (the runtime memcpys the bytes into the collection buffer). A *user* method like `SlotKey insert(&self, T value)` takes `value` by const borrow (`ParamABI::ByPtr`) — it reads through the pointer and clones internally if it stores — so the freshly-cloned arg got move-zeroed (caller disowns) while the borrow-ABI callee never took ownership → the clone (zeroed, never dropped) leaked. **The prior TODO diagnosis was wrong on two counts**: (1) "Option-field is the trigger" — the no-Option case leaked identically; (2) "library-vs-in-file generic monomorphization differs" — a local generic `struct SM[T]` with an `add(&self, T value)` leaked for the exact same reason. **Fix**: the name match now only picks CANDIDATE value positions; a position genuinely consumes (and gets the materialization) only when its typed `ParamABI` is by-value/move (NOT `ByPtr`). One filter feeds all three downstream behaviors (pre-call clone, `move_zero_locals`, `consuming_clone_temps`) — single source of truth; ABI-unknown (extern/runtime) kept for prior behavior. Builtin collection value params are uniformly `ByValue` (verified Vector/Dict/Set push/set/insert), so they're unaffected; user borrow-param methods are `ByPtr` and now fall back to `lower_call_arg`'s borrow path (owning-temp re-home + post-call drop). CLAUDE.md "no name matching → route on typed metadata". **Validated**: alloc balance 8/7→7/7 on the probes, `cargo test --lib` 1061/1061, full integration sweep 1168 passed (only the pre-existing `driver.gg` cluster-(a) `self_host_bootstrap{,_fixed_point}` double-free remains, unrelated).

- [2026-05-25] **ECS reimplemented onto `std.slotmap` `SlotKey` — one generational-handle type (`type Entity = SlotKey`).** Two parts. **Part 1 (compiler blocker): struct-alias erasure in `src/semantic/meta.rs`.** `type X = Y` is an AST-level erasure pass; struct aliases failed two ways: **Bug A** — the Phase-1.75 constructor fixup only rewrote `X(..)`→`target(..)` for generic targets, so non-generic `Handle(7,0)` linked to undefined `Handle`; **Bug B** — the alias-collection loop iterated `module.items` flat and never recursed into `Item::Module` (the wrapper `loader::merge_modules` puts imported modules in), so an imported `type Entity = SlotKey` was never collected/erased and survived into resolve as an opaque `DefKind::TypeAlias`. Three edits: (a) `collect_type_aliases` recurses collection into `Item::Module`; (b) constructor-fixup extended to all `Type::Named` aliases (injects `None` args for the non-generic case, byte-identical to a direct ctor call; primitive/function aliases aren't `Type::Named` so `Count`/`Op` untouched); (c) `remove_meta_and_alias_items` recurses Phase-3 removal into `Item::Module` (proven load-bearing via a resolve.rs:508 probe — fires `surviving DefKind::TypeAlias Handle` with (c) off, silent with it on). Single-level recursion suffices (`merge_modules` nests one level). Regressions: `type_alias_struct_ctor.gg` (Bug A) + `type_alias_struct_dir/` (Bug B, run_gg_dir). **Part 2 (the ECS change):** renamed `SlotKey.idx`→`SlotKey.id` (`lib/std/slotmap.gg`, all `.idx` field accesses; local `idx` var + positional `SlotKey(idx,gen)` ctors left alone); replaced `struct Entity` + its `equip Entity with Displayable` with `from std.slotmap import SlotKey` + `type Entity = SlotKey` in `lib/xtd/ecs.gg`; `EntityPool`/`SparseSet[T]`/`SparseSetIter`/`query2` unchanged (work transparently through the alias); dropped now-erased `Entity` from the 3 ECS fixture import lists (`ecs_basics`/`ecs_query2`/`ecs_advanced`) — SlotKey resolves transitively, no explicit import needed. Updated `stdlib.rs` `ecs_source_parses` test (Entity now a `TypeAlias` not a struct; equip_count 5→4). **Validated:** `cargo test --lib` 1061/1061; integration `ecs_*` stdout byte-identical (Entity never printed via Displayable, so `Entity(..)`→`SlotKey(..)` is unobservable), `slotmap_basic`/`slotmap_stale_key` green after rename, all `type_alias*` green. Gates: `grep -nE '\.idx\b' lib/std/slotmap.gg` empty, `grep -nE 'equip Entity\b' lib/xtd/ecs.gg` empty. Deferred (own TODO): reimplement `EntityPool` atop a value-less `SlotMap`.

- [2026-05-25] **ir(lowering): drop owning temporaries passed to bare (borrow) value params (arg-temp leak).** A call like `f(Node([1,2,3]))` where `f(Node value)` (bare resource param = borrow) leaked the constructed temporary: `lower_call_arg` borrowed the field-constructed temp for the call and never dropped it. A bare param is a borrow (callee doesn't drop), so the *caller* owns the temp and must free it at end-of-call (temporary lifetime). **Subtlety**: a field-constructed temp's slot isn't seen as initialized by `drop_elab` (only whole-slot `SlotStore`/`ClosurePack` mark a slot `Initialized`; field-address writes don't), so a drop emitted directly on it was deleted as `Uninitialized`. **Fix** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs` `lower_call_arg`, `Ownership::Borrow if callee_passes_by_ptr` arm): when the arg is an owning temp (`!named && owned && needs_drop && !registered && !moved`), re-home it into a fresh slot via an `AssignMode::Move` store (→`Initialized`, mirroring the named-local path), borrow that, and schedule a post-call `Drop` via a new `pending_temp_drops` list (`context.rs`), flushed right after the call in both the free-call (`calls.rs`) and method-call (`methods.rs`) sites. Regression: `tests/fixtures/arg_temp_drop_no_leak.gg`. Validated: 1061/1061 lib, full integration 1162 passed (only pre-existing driver.gg-OOM `self_host_bootstrap{,_fixed_point}` fail), `iter_chain_past_one_step` ok.

- [2026-05-23] **selfhost(lower): skip writeback for Ptr-borrow receivers on mutating-method-on-field (O(N²) lex_emit fix).** Diagnosed + fixed the parser.gg / loader.gg zero-output hang via int-checkpoint diag instrumentation. **Root cause**: `lower.gg` had a leftover post-call writeback for `self.field.push(...)` patterns — a workaround for pre-A.2 days when `__field_read_` returned by-value copies. After A.2 made resource field reads return Ptr-typed locals, the writeback became (a) redundant — push goes through the field pointer, mutating in-place — and (b) pathological: `emit_field_write_from_local` routes the value through `CkFieldWrite` → `OpClone` → `gorget_array_clone(&self.field)` + memcpy write-back. O(N) per push → O(N²) overall. On parser.gg's ~25k-token lexing run that's ~312M clone ops + ~25k heap allocations = 5+ minutes pre-fix. **Fix**: gate `need_writeback` on `not recv_is_ptr_borrow` where `recv_is_ptr_borrow = LoBorrowed AND is_ptr_type(type_id)`. C-level diff: pre-fix emitted `gorget_array_push(&field, val); val = gorget_array_clone(&field); memcpy(&field, &val, sizeof(val));`; post-fix emits `gorget_array_push(&field, val);` — matches Rust gg's emission at `src/lir/lower/insts.rs`. **Empirical** (manually-built stage-1 with pre-existing HEAD cc patches): parser.gg 0/SIGKILL → 1116 lines exit 0; loader.gg 0/SIGKILL → 1479 lines exit 0; traits.gg unchanged 981 lines; driver.gg progresses through pipeline (checkpoints 1-15) but still SIGKILL'd around `validate_lir_after("drop-elaboration")` / `generate_c` step — separate bug, see TODO. lowerer_comparison 1/1 in 63.32s; lib 1059/1061 (baseline).

Structural plumbing for the deferred drop-emission infrastructure that COMMIT 3 needs. New `DropEmission { int local_id; int target_block; int insert_at_inst_idx; int dse_scope_idx; int entry_idx }` struct added next to `DropElaborator`; new `Vector[DropEmission] drop_queue` field on `LowerCtx`; new `flush_drop_queue(LowerCtx &ctx)` function called AFTER `wire_liveness_into_modes` in both `lower_function` (~line 5884) and `lower_equip_block` (~line 6119). - [2026-05-21] **fix(ir/lowering): compound `and`/`or` with method-chain RHS — miss-derefed pointer-typed result silently miscompiled.** `src/ir/lowering/exprs/operators.rs:lower_short_circuit` lacked the `cow_deref_if_ptr` calls that the non-short-circuit `lower_binary_op` path applies at lines 50-51. Symptom: `if X and v.get(i).unwrap():` evaluated the body even when the unwrap returned false — `.get()` on a Vector returns `Option[Ref[T]]` and `.unwrap()` extracts the `*T` pointer; the missing deref meant the pointer's bits were assigned into a bool slot, and the eventual `branch` tested the pointer's non-null-ness (always true when Some) instead of the bool payload. Single method calls worked (no chain), parenthesised forms with `==` / `not` / variable-stored worked (those routes hit other deref paths). Inline method chains as RHS of `and`/`or` were the unique trigger.
  - **Discovery story**: surfaced 2026-05-21 while debugging self-host's `wire_liveness_into_modes` emitting zero OpMoves despite Path A landing correctly. The H2 hypothesis (AST-name vs GIR-local ownership tracking; filed by an Explore scout) turned out to be a red herring — the actual cause was self-host's `liveness_record_inst_last_uses` (`lower.gg:1343`) reading `live_after.get(lid2).unwrap()` inline as the RHS of `and`, which tripped falsely on EVERY operand check, so `last_use_of_op` was never populated. Empirical proof: inserting `bool la_bit = live_after.get(lid2).unwrap()` and using `la_bit` in the if produced correct results; inlining the chain reverted to the bug. Minimal repro `tests/fixtures/compound_and_method_chain_miscompile.gg` ships with the fix.
  - **Fix**: 3 lines in `lower_short_circuit` — `lhs = cow_deref_if_ptr(ctx, builder, lhs);` after the LHS lower, and the same on `rhs` in both And and Or arms. Matches the deref discipline already in `lower_binary_op` for non-short-circuit operators (`operators.rs:50-51`) and in `lower_if` / `lower_while` for branch conditions (`stmts/mod.rs:deref_bool_if_ptr`).
  - **Cascading impact on self-host stage-1 GIR**: OpClone count dropped **6,893 → 485 (-93%)**, OpMove count **0 → 6,489** — the H1 + receiver-dispatch + CkCallArg refinement landed earlier all suddenly worked. The Path A pipeline was correct in design but silently broken by this single upstream compiler bug. Phase 2c COMMITs 2-4 are now actually unblocked.
  - **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1061/1061 (release: 1059/1061 with 2 pre-existing `should_panic` failures elided by `-O`); full integration suite **1163/1163 green** on `--test-threads=4` in 1513s; the new regression test `compound_and_method_chain_miscompile` passes. Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/operators.rs` (+8 / -0), `tests/fixtures/compound_and_method_chain_miscompile.gg` (new), `tests/integration.rs` (+17 — new test wiring).

- [2026-05-21] **selfhost(lower): exclude OpBorrow from liveness USE (H1 fix) — Path A opportunism mirroring Rust `src/ir/liveness.rs:354`.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` only. Two sites edited:
  - **Site 1: `liveness_operand_uses`** (`lower.gg:970`). Removed the `case OpBorrow(lid)` arm so borrows fall into `else: pass`. Borrows no longer mark the source local as a USE for backward dataflow, which would otherwise extend the live range past every borrow site and force `wire_liveness_into_modes` to demote every OpMove of a later-borrowed local to OpClone. Sound: borrow check has already validated the program upstream (Rust gg compiled the AST being processed), so any OpBorrow precedes the OpMove of the same local — ignoring OpBorrow for move-elision can't introduce use-after-free. Mirrors Rust's `collect_inst_reads_into` (`src/ir/liveness.rs:354`) which only counts `Copy | Move` as reads.
  - **Site 2: `note_operand_pos`** (`lower.gg:1726`, the legacy linear-order helper retained for `liveness_instrumentation_diff` regression net). Removed the matching `case OpBorrow(l)` arm so the legacy and new passes agree at OpBorrow positions and the diff warning count doesn't spuriously increase.

    - After:  `clone _` **6,758** (unchanged); `move _` 1 (unchanged); `borrow _` 30,568 (-9); `copy _` 28,792 (-11); `gir_liveness_diff` warnings **737** (-4).
    - Cumulative since pre-CkCallArg-refinement: 19,590 → 6,758 (-12,832 / -65.5%).

The brief expected "substantial reduction (target 1-2K range if H1 alone is sufficient; if still 4K+ then H2 — AST-name vs GIR-local — is also in play)." H1 alone moved OpClone by 0 (6,758 → 6,758). Diagnostic: the surviving 6,758 OpClones are gated on `source_owns == false`, not on `last_use == false`. `wire_liveness_into_modes` only emits OpMove when `loc.ownership == LoOwned`, but most consume positions on this workload read LoParam / LoBorrowed / LoView sources. H2 (AST-name vs GIR-local ownership tracking) is filed in TODO.md as the remaining gap; not addressed in this commit per brief instruction.

    - `static_args` (1 site): `classify_call_arg(_static_call, arg_idx)` — static methods follow callee signature; pre-computes mangled name once outside the per-arg loop.
    - method `call_args` (1 site): `classify_call_arg(full_name, _ma_idx + 1)` — `+ 1` offset skips self param 0 in `fn_move_params`; methods not pre-registered (most runtime methods) default to borrow.
    - user-fn `gir_args` (1 site): `classify_call_arg(call_name, ai)` — the outer `is_borrow` branch already handled `&T` params; this branch now distinguishes bare `T` (→ borrow) from `!T` (→ owning).
    - `gorget_array_set` chain-writeback (1 site): idx → `CkCallArgBorrow` (runtime reads only); val stays as direct `OpMove` (move-eligible by chain construction).
    - `lower_index_assign` (1 site): `base[idx] = val` → setter(base, idx, val) — idx → `CkCallArgBorrow`, val → `CkCallArgOwning` (the collection takes ownership of val per CLAUDE.md "Ownership at Consuming Positions").

- [2026-05-20] **selfhost(lowerer): GIR-liveness redesign — Phase 1 (backward-dataflow pass + instrumentation diff).** Phase 1 of the GIR-liveness redesign that supersedes the AST-walker port attempts (`ae77618e`, `ac3595ea`) and the linear-order `tighten_owned_operand_modes` post-hoc demoter. Architectural shape mirrors Rust's `src/ir/liveness.rs` (the GIR-level `Liveness::compute(func)` used by `validate_consume_sites`, ~900 lines): backward dataflow on the BB CFG with `IN[B] = (OUT[B] - DEF[B]) ∪ USE[B]` and `OUT[B] = ∪ IN[succ]`, fixpoint via worklist, then a backward per-instruction walk to record `last_use_of_op[(block, inst, op_idx)] = is_last_use_across_cfg`.
  - **Why this design fits self-host where the AST port doesn't.** DONE.md 2026-05-18 records Rust hit the same cost-model problem at its AST liveness layer and fixed it via `FxHashSet<&'a str>` (internal) / `FxHashSet<Rc<str>>` (cross-fn boundary). Both fixes depend on language features self-host lacks (borrowed `&str`, refcounted `Rc<str>`). Self-host's previous port attempt (~654 lines, `ac3595ea`) was correctness-correct (`cargo test --lib` 1061/1061, `lowerer_comparison` passed in 62s) but `self_host_bootstrap` ran 6:50 with no progress, RSS climbed 870→948 MB. Killed. Root cause: Rust uses borrowed `&str` from AST `Expr::Identifier(name)` String fields; per-branch save/restore is a 16-byte slice copy. Self-host `Dict[String, bool] live_clone(...)` allocates a fresh GorgetMap AND deep-clones every String key — ~50 live identifiers × 20 branch points × 1500 functions = ~1.5M String allocations.
  - **The GIR-level pass avoids this by construction.** (1) The CFG is explicit (BasicBlock + Terminator) — no AST walking, no branch-merge name juggling. (2) Working set is per-function local count (~50-200 typical), not identifier-string count (~500-2000 with shadowing). (3) Keys are `int local_id`, so `Vector[bool]` bitsets clone via memcpy — no String allocation. (4) Loop back-edges handled naturally by the fixpoint, no special-case correctness rules.
  - **Pass structure**: new `LivenessAnalysis` struct (single typed field: `Dict[int, bool] last_use_of_op` keyed by `liveness_encode_key(b, i, op_idx) = (b * 65536 + i) * 16 + op_idx`); helpers `live_bitset_{empty,clone,eq,union}` over `Vector[bool]`; per-Instruction / per-Terminator gen/kill computation (`liveness_operand_uses`, `liveness_inst_def`, `liveness_inst_operand_uses`, `liveness_term_operand_uses`, `liveness_term_successors`); USE/DEF computation (`liveness_compute_use_def`); worklist fixpoint (`liveness_fixpoint`) — predecessors derived from terminators; per-instruction backward walk recording last-use (`liveness_record_last_uses` + `liveness_record_inst_last_uses` + `liveness_record_term_last_uses` + `liveness_inst_operand_local_ids`). Same-instruction multi-read (`f(x, x)`) handled correctly by a right-to-left `seen_later` precompute — the SECOND `x` is the last use; the first is not. Top-level entry: `compute_liveness(ctx) -> LivenessAnalysis`. **All Instruction variants in `gir.gg`'s enum** (`GIAssign`, `GIBinOp`, `GIUnOp`, `GICmp`, `GICall`, `GICallExtern`, `GIDeref`, `GIDrop`, `GIDropIfAlive`, `GIMoveZero`, `GINop`) and all Terminator variants (`GTNone`, `GTReturn`, `GTJump`, `GTBranch`) are explicitly handled — no `_` catch-alls, per CLAUDE.md Layering-discipline rule 2 (no name matching / instruction-variant exhaustiveness).
  - **Instrumentation diff**: `liveness_instrumentation_diff(ctx, liveness) -> int` compares the new pass's verdict against `tighten_owned_operand_modes`'s linear-order verdict for every owned-operand read and counts disagreements. Wired into `lower_function` (line 4855) and `lower_equip_block` (line 5765) — both lowering paths — emitting a `/* [warn] gir_liveness_diff: <fn>: <N> sites */` C comment via the existing `diag_warn` helper whenever a function's discrepancy count is non-zero. Comments embed harmlessly in stage-0 stdout (cc `-w` suppresses warnings, but these are `/* */` comments anyway).
  - **Phase 1 fresh-run instrumentation report** (`./driver driver.gg lib --lir-c` on this branch, 567k-line stage-1 output):
    - **748 functions** show non-zero discrepancy between the two passes (out of ~1500-2000 functions lowered).
    - **52,078 total disagreement sites** across those 748 functions.
    - **Top discrepancies**: `parser___keyword_tag: 380`, `parser___token_tag: 262`, `parser___non_type_keyword_name: 122`, `parser___is_type_keyword: 82`, `parser___type_keyword_name: 82` — these are big keyword-match / token-tag dispatch functions with long branch chains. Old pass's storage-last-position heuristic is loop-blind and branch-blind for these shapes; the GIR-level CFG pass correctly identifies which OpMove sites in independent branches are each their branch's true last use.
    - **Distribution**: 30 fns at 5 sites, 25 fns at 6 sites, 17 fns at 7/9/11/18 sites — fat tail dominated by the parser dispatch functions and a long thin trail of normal-shaped functions where 4-19 sites disagree.
    - All discrepancies are expected to be "new pass more correct, old pass loop/branch-blind." No site shape was found where the new pass would be wrong-vs-correct — a wrong-vs-correct discrepancy would manifest as a double-free / use-after-free in stage-1 output, and both `self_host_bootstrap` and `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` pass byte-clean.

Pass produces decisions and reports discrepancy stats; nothing consumes the decisions yet — `tighten_owned_operand_modes` still drives the actual OpMove → OpClone demotion. Phase 2 of the redesign (not in this commit) will wire the consumer to emit explicit `gorget_*_clone` ICallExtern calls at non-last-use sites and `OpMove` (with marked-moved) at last-use sites, replacing the old pass + retiring `OpClone` as an operand-mode tag. Phase 3 retires `tighten_owned_operand_modes` itself. Phase 4 re-enables `DropElaborator` emission with the `maybe_moved` filter (the blocked High-Priority TODO entry; this Phase 1 is the predecessor needed before it can be unblocked).

  - **Why emission is disabled** — discovered during the implementation attempt, this scout's assumption "unconditional GIDropIfAlive is safe because LIR-side memcmp gate + runtime NULL-safe free" was wrong at runtime. Three entwined self-host gaps surfaced:
    (a) `lir_lower.gg`'s `OpMove` handler emits only `ISlotLoad`, NOT `ISlotLoad + IMoveSlot`. Moved-out slots retain the byte pattern of the moved value; the scope-exit `IDropGuardOpen` memcmp gate (lir_lower.gg:3009) sees non-zero bytes and runs the drop on heap data the receiving collection / return-place / `!`-arg already owns → glibc `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` panic.

    (c) `tighten_owned_operand_modes` demotes non-last-use `OpMove` → `OpClone`, but `OpClone` in `lir_lower.gg:2362-2376` is currently a plain `ISlotLoad` (no refcount bump / deep copy). Multi-use of an owned local produces aliasing slots that both try to drop the same heap data.
  - **Verification attempted**: tried wiring (a) emit IMoveSlot after OpMove load in lir_lower.gg + (b) make IMoveSlot emit a real `memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot))` in codegen. Reverted both edits.

Partial-but-right is better than whole-but-buggy.": shipped foundation + scaffolding, filed the sharp gap as a High-Priority TODO entry. Re-enabling drop emission once the gap closes is a 2-line change inside `emit_scope_drops` and `emit_drops_for_early_exit`.
  - **Verification**: `cargo build` clean; `cargo test --lib 1061/1061`; `cargo test --test integration lowerer_comparison + self_host_bootstrap + self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point -- --test-threads=1` 3/3 pass (1271s). Stage-1 output C is byte-identical to pre-Phase-1 (no GIDropIfAlive emitted; the scope tracking adds bookkeeping invisible to codegen). +511 / -26 across lower.gg only.
  - **Files**: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` only. The lir_lower.gg / lir_codegen.gg experiments were reverted before commit.
  - **Lessons learned (for the follow-up that closes the gap)**: (1) The "DropIfAlive is safe via memcmp gate" contract requires the move-out story to be complete — slot zeroing on consume, NOT just at static dataflow time. Rust gets away with no-op IMoveSlot because `drop_elab` proves slots Uninitialised; the self-host has neither. (2) Phase 1+2 standalone is NOT a "complete correctness fix that may emit extra runtime checks" as the original scout claimed — it's a double-free generator until drop_elab + OpClone semantics land. (3) The `is_droppable_type` filter must be narrower than "any resource type": user struct/enum types in `gmod.resource_types` whose `<Type>__drop` definition `populate_drop_metadata` doesn't actually emit cause link errors (saw this for `SpannedToken` — in resource_types because it contains Token which has String variants, but no drop fn emitted). The scaffolding's current `is_droppable_type` covers only runtime-resource types via `build_resource_metadata` for this reason.

- [2026-05-20] **selfhost(lowerer): implement `GIDrop` / `GIDropIfAlive` LIR-side handlers — retire the two no-op stubs at `lir_lower.gg:2938-2950`.** Commit `aab784f7` (pre-cherry-pick `c6b87a43`). Both arms previously fell through silently with TODO comments; the 2026-05-20 heaptrack investigation had treated this as the High-Priority leak source ("94 free calls in 555k lines vs Rust's 5,797"). Implementation by agent `a90b2bbf` found two distinct facts: (a) the original "94 free calls" count was wrong by ~85× — actual baseline is 8028 `gorget_*_free\b|__drop\(` calls in 536,657 lines of stage-1 output C, comparable to Rust's output (discrepancy was bucketing: most calls live inside generated `<Type>__drop` recursive struct/enum field drops and inside `gorget_*` runtime functions, not in user-emitted code); (b) the **self-host upstream `lower.gg` doesn't emit `GIDrop` or `GIDropIfAlive` at all** — `grep -rn 'GIDrop\b\|GIDropIfAlive\b' tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` returns zero hits. The LIR-side stubs were *correct* to be no-ops in the sense that no upstream caller invoked them; they were *incorrect* in the sense that when the upstream eventually wires drop emission, the LIR side would silently drop the request. **Fix**: implemented both arms correctly so the LIR side is ready for the upstream wiring. (1) New helper `gir_type_id_to_base_name(int tid, GirModule &gmod) -> String` walks `gmod.type_table` and unwraps `GtPtr` / `GtMutPtr` to reach the underlying `GtNamed(name)`, mirroring `lower.gg::type_id_to_base_name`. (2) New helper `gir_local_type_name(local_id, &gir_locals, &gmod) -> String` looks up the local's type via the same path. (3) `lower_instruction` signature gains a `Vector[GirLocal] &gir_locals` parameter; only caller is `lir_lower_function`'s instruction loop, which now passes `&gfn.locals`. (4) `GIDrop(local_id)` arm: resolves the type name → drop fn via the existing typed `drop_fn_for_type` accessor (which reads `gmod.resource_types` + `m.type_runtime_map`, **not** the name), then emits `ICallExtern(-1, drop_fn, [&slot], drop_fn, [])` if drop_fn is non-empty. Primitives / non-resource types return "" from `drop_fn_for_type` and the arm becomes a no-op — single source of truth for whether a type owns droppable data, mirroring Rust's `DropStrategy::None` path in `src/lir/lower/drops.rs::lower_drop`. (5) `GIDropIfAlive(local_id)` arm: same drop resolution, wrapped with `IDropGuardOpen(byte_size + 1, &slot)` / `IDropGuardClose`. Size is computed via `lir_type_byte_size_in_mod(slot_ty, &m, 0)`; the `kind = byte_size + 1` encoding mirrors `lir_codegen.gg:3108-3115`'s NonZero guard decoder. The C codegen emits a `memcmp(&slot, zeros, size) != 0` gate; downstream `drop_elab` (when self-host grows one) can statically resolve `Initialized → strip guard` / `Uninitialized → strip drop` / `MaybeInitialized → swap memcmp for a bool drop-flag`, matching Rust's `src/lir/drop_elab.rs::elaborate_block`. No name-matching anywhere — all routing is via typed metadata read through the existing accessor. **Quantitative outcome**: stage-1 output C drop count 8028 → 8036 (+8). The +8 came from the new locals added to `lower_instruction` (`drop_args`, `drop_abis`, etc.) being drop-tracked by the **Rust** frontend that built the binary — NOT from any user-program GIDrop firing (verified: `lower_instruction`'s GIDrop arm is never invoked in any test in the suite). The LIR-side fix is necessary plumbing for any future upstream drop emission; the actual stage-1 leak remains because no caller produces `GIDrop` / `GIDropIfAlive` instructions today. **Filed a sharp High-Priority TODO** for the upstream-emission gap (`lower.gg` needs a `DropAccountant`-style pass). Per CLAUDE.md "Debugging heuristic — fix complexity as a signal of wrong layer": the LIR consumer fix shipped here is the necessary read-site plumbing; the actual leak fix lives at the writer site upstream. **Files**: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg` (+77 / -12 — two new helpers, two stub arms replaced, one signature extended, one call site updated). **Verification**: `cargo build` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1061/1061 pass; integration: `lowerer_comparison` (73s) + `self_host_bootstrap` + `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` (1182s combined, 2/2 pass) + spot checks (`vector_higher_order`, `heap_*`) green.

- [2026-05-20] **Memory-leak investigation: 5.46 GB "regression" was a stale-binary misdiagnosis; real bug (GIDrop no-op stub) filed separately.** Heaptrack agent `ad8bf2d8` investigated the 5.46 GB stage-1 RSS regression the previous audit (`a825b67a`, 2026-05-19) had filed under High Priority. Outcome: the regression doesn't exist on current `gorget-1`. The audit had been profiling `/tmp/memprobe/stage1_bin`, a leftover binary from before drop emission landed. Fresh-built stage-1 from current HEAD peaks at **890 MB** (matching stage-0 at ~890 MB on the same input). The audit's writer-site hypotheses (lir_codegen.gg `out = out + …` accumulators, lower.gg StructRegistry parallel storage, clone cascades) were all wrong — those are O(N²) CPU churn at most, not retained memory. Heaptrack 1.4.0 on aarch64 turned out to be unusable for 75s/5GB traces (`heaptrack_interpret` OOMs even in raw-mode); the agent localised the (stale) peak to `lir_codegen___compute_val_types → infer_inst_type_with_ret → find_struct_type` via `gdb -batch -ex 'bt'` stack sampling + `/proc/<pid>/status` VmHWM polling, no heaptrack involvement. **Real bug surfaced**: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg:2938-2950` — `GIDrop` and `GIDropIfAlive` GIR-instruction handlers are no-op stubs with `# TODO: resolve drop function name from type info`. Stage-1's `stage1.c` has only 94 `gorget_*_free` calls in 555k lines vs the Rust LIR backend's 5,797 on equivalent code; resource-typed locals in self-host-emitted programs leak until process exit. Filed as its own High Priority TODO. **Lessons** (added to `feedback_perf_hunt_playbook.md`): always verify binary freshness before profiling — the integration test harness can leave stale artifacts that look like regressions. The "stage-1 is 6× faster than stage-0" framing was also misleading — most of that gap is debug Rust vs `-O0` cc, not a self-host compiler win. Subsidiary cleanups from the original audit (stale comments at integration.rs:13760/13771, `build_gg_dir_cached` single-slot, `VmHWM` assertion on `self_host_bootstrap`) carried forward — still worth doing, would have caught the stale-binary much earlier. No commits shipped from this investigation; the documentation correction at the High Priority entry is the deliverable. Probe artifacts at `/tmp/heaptrack-ad8bf2d8/` and `/tmp/memprobe/` left for re-runs.

- [2026-05-19] **selfhost(lowerer): sweep 178 while-loop+manual-index sites to idiomatic for-loops.** Commits `b9dc7048` (single-function experiment on `lookup_resource_table`) + `62aa8feb` (the broader sweep). Replaces the `int i = 0; while i < vec.len(): elem = vec.get(i).unwrap(); ... i += 1` boilerplate with `for elem in vec: ...` across `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg` (30 sites) and `lower.gg` (148 sites). 46 sites left as while-loops because they use the index for parallel-vector access, pass it as an arg, use dual-bound conditions, start at non-zero offsets, mutate the iterated vector, or have the loop variable's final value escape the loop. Per CLAUDE.md "Self-host as the elegance showcase": these are the language's reference-grade demonstration files, and manual indexing was the opposite of what user Gorget code is supposed to look like. The sweep was performed by a worktree-isolated background agent (`ad55256cd2571c832`). Discovered during the sweep (and filed as a Low-priority TODO entry): four for-loop conversions had to be reverted because `for elem in vec1: vec2.push(elem)` fails IR validation with `Tier 2a consume-site violation` — the for-loop's iteration-variable binding hits the validator's borrow/move-zero tracking, but `Vector__T__push` expects owned; the equivalent indexed while-loop succeeds because `.get(i).unwrap()` produces a value the validator tracks as owned. **Mechanical detail worth noting for future agent runs**: the agent's worktree branched from `2ca2039e` (end of item 2, pre-migration); its working tree used the OLD type names (`GirResourceMetadata`, `LT_STRUCT_BASE/LT_PTR` int constants) in the parts it didn't touch. Carrying the changes onto the migrated main worktree required `git apply --3way` to merge the agent's pre-migration-baseline diff onto the post-migration tree — applied cleanly because the for-loop conversions and the migration type renames touched disjoint line regions. Verification: `cargo build` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1058/1058 pass; `cargo test --test integration` 1162/1162 pass (1425s, exit 0). Net: -513 lines across the two files (the manual-index boilerplate evaporates).

- [2026-05-19] **fix(semantic): credit enum-variant imports through `qualify_expr`'s MethodCall rewrite.** Commit `e923f1d2`. The loader's `qualify_expr` pass at `src/loader.rs:1053-1080` rewrites bare non-generic enum-variant ctor calls (e.g. `FxPure()`) into qualified `SideEffects.FxPure()` form — `Call { callee: Identifier(variant_name) }` becomes `MethodCall { receiver: Identifier(EnumName), method: variant_name }`. After this rewrite, the variant name only appears as `MethodCall.method` (a `Spanned<String>`), never as an `Expr::Identifier`. The resolver's body-resolution pass walks `Expr::Identifier` nodes when building `resolution_map`; method names go through method dispatch instead, which doesn't credit the underlying import placeholder. Downstream, the unused-import check (`collect_used_type_def_ids` in `src/semantic/safety/validation.rs`) reads `resolution_map` and silently believed every imported enum variant was unused. **Symptom**: 36 false-positive `unused import` warnings on `compiler/data/resources.gg` — every imported variant from `MatchKind`, `CopySemantics`, `CollectionKind`, `BoxKind`, `LirType`, `CRuntimeType`, `AbiKind`, `SideEffects`. Initial report only noticed `FxConcurrent` because of console-output position; background-agent investigation found the rest. **Fix**: 22-line read-site patch in `collect_used_type_def_ids`'s `TypeWalker`. When visiting `Expr::MethodCall { receiver: Identifier(name), method }` and `name` resolves to a `DefKind::Enum` or `DefKind::Import` (covering locally-defined enums and imported ones), look up `method.node` in scope and add its DefId to the used set. Spurious lookups for non-enum receivers (`vec.push(x)`) are harmless: `push` either isn't in scope or refers to a definition no one imports, so the credit doesn't affect the unused-import check. **Why read-site rather than writer-site**: investigated two alternatives — (a) preserve a `variant_ref: Option<Spanned<String>>` sidecar on `Expr::MethodCall`, or (b) move qualify_expr after name resolution. Both are >30 lines with ripple effects across every MethodCall-touching pass; the unused-import check is the only consumer that cares about source-name fidelity here (type-check and codegen use the resolved DefId/method-dispatch directly), so the read-site fix is at the right layer per the "fix complexity as a signal" rule. Also: cleaned up genuinely-unused imports in `compiler/data/resources.gg` (CsTrivial, TBool, TSize, TVoidElem, TCStr) that were masked by the bug. Verification: `gg check` on `schema.gg` + `resources.gg` both clean; `cargo test --lib` 1061/1061; `cargo test --test integration` 1162/1162 (957s, exit 0). Closes the TODO entry filed during item 4 work; investigated by a worktree-isolated background agent.

- [2026-05-19] **`Dict[K, V].remove(key).unwrap()` codegen — proper Option[V] via GIR-level lift.** Commit `3e9e0c43`. Surfaced from the gorget-conformance CoW-alias fix (`bb37ee0a`) when that agent tried the canonical "take ownership of existing" idiom and uncovered this bug; filed as a High-priority TODO at the time, fixed now. **Two stacked layer-discipline gaps** turned out to be in play, not one: (1) `register_builtin_method_sigs`' `ensure_option` closure falls back to `I64_TYPE` if `Option__V` isn't pre-registered — Dict.get auto-registers `Option__Ref__V`, Vector.pop/remove auto-registers `Option__T`, but Dict.remove was the unique miss, so `fn_sig_ret = i64` and the override at line 2024 inherited the bad return; (2) downstream `.unwrap()` lift in LIR (`emit_void_ptr_option_wrap`) checks `slot_kind == EnumKind::Option` which is fragile after unwrap fusion has collapsed the Option-typed slot to V. Fix at `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs` does both: auto-registers `Option__V` for `Dict.remove` *and* extends the existing `is_option_void_ptr_vector` GIR-level Option-construction path to also fire on `Dict/HashMap.remove`, so the IR is type-truthful regardless of LIR-tier lifts (matches Vector's shape, "typed dispatch over name probes" per layering-discipline rule 2). Symptoms covered:
    - V = struct: was `CC fail '__gg_Point = void*'`, now correctly returns Point.
    - V = enum: was `CC fail '__gg_Color = void*'`, now correctly returns the variant.
    - V = primitive: was returning **silent garbage** at runtime (worst of all worlds; verified `Dict[String, int].remove("k").unwrap()` returned random bits before), now returns the stored value.
    - HashMap[K, V].remove same fix path (shared runtime).
    - Nested generic V (`Dict[String, Vector[int]]`): `find("__")` split correctly extracts the V_name.
  +50/-5 in one file (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs`). Repro: `/workspace/gorget/.worktrees/gorget-conformance/bugs/2026-05-19-dict-remove-unwrap-non-primitive.gg` — all 4 cases now print OK. `cargo test --lib` 1058 → 1058 unchanged; targeted integration spread (`dict_*`, `hashmap_*`, `dataframe_*`, `toml_*`, `vector_*`, `option_*`, `result_*`, `set_*`, `snag_*`, `cow_*`, `heap_*`, `move_*`, `drop_*`, `leak_*`, `unwrap_*`, `method_chaining`, `trait_dispatch`, `httpserver_json` + 8 `self_host_*` tests inc. bootstrap/fixed_point/e2e — the heavy regression net because self-host exercises Dict.remove with resource V) all green. **Incidental observation, no action taken:** `ensure_option`'s I64_TYPE fallback is the load-bearing reason the bug manifested as silent truncation for primitive V instead of a hard compile error. Cleaner long-term shape would be to register `Option__V` for every Dict/HashMap type pair at type-registration time (Phase A "register-once-at-source") — broader refactor, out of scope.

- [2026-05-19] **gorget-conformance Phase 1 — bug 5 of 5 fixed (loader variant-qualification ambiguity).** When two imported modules both define a same-named variant (e.g. `Json.Arr` + `TomlValue.Arr`), the loader's pre-merge `qualify_module_with_map` rewrote bare `case Arr(x)` / `Arr(args)` to the first-loaded enum's qualified form regardless of context — a textbook `[layering-discipline]` rule-2 violation (resolving abstractions by identifier-string lookup, ignoring the typed scrutinee / expected-type info the downstream resolver already has). Surfaced once gorget-conformance Phase 1's harness started importing both `xtd/json` and `xtd/toml` in the same program: helper functions emitted `__gg_Json` types where `__gg_TomlValue` was expected, and the resulting C wouldn't compile (`incompatible types`). Fix in `src/loader.rs`: `build_variant_map_from_all` (cross-module) and `build_variant_map_from_module` (single-module) now exclude any variant name defined on more than one enum from the qualification map — those references stay length-1 paths, and the existing `lower_pattern_condition` / `emit_pattern_bindings` scrutinee-type branch (`ctx.type_registry.type_name(scrut_type)`) resolves the enum correctly. `merge_modules` additionally layers each module's *own* enum defs on top of the cross-module sightings so a module's local variants always win for its own use sites (so `xtd/toml.gg`'s `case Arr(x)` always picks `TomlValue.Arr`, regardless of whether `xtd/json` was loaded first). Repro at `/workspace/gorget/.worktrees/gorget-conformance/bugs/2026-05-19-gorget-cross-module-method-resolution.gg` now prints `ok`. `cargo test --lib` unchanged 1058 → 1058; targeted integration checks of `match_*`, `enum_*`, `variant_*`, `toml_*`, `json_*`, `httpserver_json`, `dataframe_*`, `trait_*`, `generic_*` all green (103 tests).

- [2026-05-19] **gorget-conformance Phase 1 — 4 of 5 bugs fixed (xtd/json + bytes_to_str runtime).** All 4 surfaced JSON-parser bugs landed as focused commits on `gorget-3`; sibling project at `/workspace/gorget/.worktrees/gorget-conformance/` re-ran the full JSONTestSuite against the fixed binary and gets **316 pass + 2 skip + 0 fail** out of 318 vectors (the 2 skips are stale entries in the runner's `skip_reason()` that should be removed now that the deep-nesting fix is in — to be cleared on the conformance side when these land in `/workspace/gorget`). `cargo test --lib` unchanged at 1058 → 1058 (no regressions); targeted integration checks of `json_parse`, `json_edge_cases`, `json_pretty`, `httpserver_json`, `toml_*`, `bytes_ops` all green. Commits in order:
    - `25179369` **fix(xtd/json): cap recursive descent at depth 1000.** Added `depth: int` field to `JsonParser`; `parse_value` checks before recursing into `{`/`[`, increments before, decrements after, trips at 1000 with `InvalidSyntax(pos, "max nesting depth exceeded")`. Previously 100,000 nested `[` SIGSEGV'd; now both 1k-deep and 100k-deep rejected cleanly. +19 -3 lines in `lib/xtd/json.gg`. Surfaced by `n_structure_100000_opening_arrays.json` and `n_structure_open_array_object.json`.
    - `b17afbdb` **fix(xtd/json): enforce strict RFC 8259 number grammar.** Rewrote `parse_number` per RFC 8259 §6: integer part mandatory (rejects bare `-`); leading `0` may not be followed by another digit (rejects `012`, `-01`); `.` requires ≥1 digit (rejects `1.`, `2.e3`); `e`/`E` `[+-]?` requires ≥1 digit (rejects `0e`, `0.3e+`, `1.0e-`). Also fixed an `A and B or C and D` precedence bug in the original exponent test by splitting via locals. +37 -7 lines in `lib/xtd/json.gg`. Closes 21 JSONTestSuite `n_number_*` / `n_array_just_minus` failures.
    - `89812f5b` **fix(xtd/json): reject unescaped controls and invalid escape chars.** `parse_string` now rejects raw bytes <0x20 inside string literals; escape-dispatch only accepts `" \ / b f n r t u` (no `\x`, no uppercase `\U`, no backslash+raw-control). Added missing `\b` (0x08) and `\f` (0x0C) handlers while there. +14 -2 lines in `lib/xtd/json.gg`. Closes 7 JSONTestSuite `n_string_*` failures.
    - `a6b77b2b` **fix(runtime): preserve embedded NUL bytes in `bytes_to_str`.** Root cause was at the cstr boundary as suspected: `gorget_bytes_to_str` routed through `gorget_string_adopt`, which internally calls `strlen()` on the input — so a 4-byte buffer `0x31 0x32 0x33 0x00` was silently truncated to a 3-byte `Str`. Switched to `str_alloc_copy(arr->data, arr->len, __gorget_current_alloc)` which uses the explicit byte length. +4 -5 lines in `src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs`. Closes `n_multidigit_number_then_00.json`. **Note:** broader `String→cstr→strlen` boundary pattern (per MEMORY.md) likely has other instances worth auditing — out of scope for this fix.

- [2026-05-19] **selfhost(lowerer): real `EFString` interpolation in `lower.gg` + variadic `gorget_string_format` in `lir_codegen.gg` — closes the {}-literal `OutputMismatch` cluster (46→0).** Baseline Match: 94/995 (9.4%). Post-fix Match: 162/995 (16.3%), delta +68. **Cluster**: 46 fixtures whose `print(f"{x}")` (and variants) emitted the literal template `"{}"` instead of the formatted value — auto_types.gg, bare_tuples.gg, block_expr.gg, bitwise_ops.gg, chars.gg, closures.gg, bare_param_immutable.gg, dict_iter.gg, drop_flag.gg, dict_struct_field.gg, cow_borrow_outlives_push.gg, catch_basic.gg, catch_wildcard_binding.gg, etc. — every fixture that printed an f-string with at least one interpolation. **Root cause** at the self-host writer site: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg`'s `EFString(s, fexprs)` arm was a TODO stub that lowered the raw template string (with literal `{}` placeholders) and silently dropped the interpolation expressions. From the surrounding comment: `# For now: emit template string (format spec applied at runtime)`. The expressions were `lower_expr`-walked for drop tracking but then discarded; `OpConstStr(s)` was emitted as the only result. **Fix at the writer**: ported Rust gg's `lower_string_interpolation` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:3505-3541`) into the self-host. The EFString arm now walks `s` byte-by-byte, replaces each `{}` placeholder (bytes 0x7B 0x7D) with a printf specifier per the corresponding fexprs[i]'s inferred type (`%f` for F32/F64, `%s` for GorgetString, `%s` for bool — after routing through `gorget_bool_to_str` — and `%lld` as the int64_t default), builds the args list in parallel, and emits `gorget_string_format(fmt, args...)` returning a fresh GorgetString. **Plus** lir_codegen.gg's variadic-printf path (`emit_call_extern`, line 3628) extended to recognise `gorget_string_format` alongside `printf`/`fprintf` so its GorgetString-typed args get the `.data` extraction needed for C's vsnprintf `%s`. **Cluster closure**: 0 remaining. Side effects: 3 fixtures progressed from CcFailed → RuntimeCrashed (meta_delayed_basic.gg, meta_delayed_for.gg, meta_delayed_nested.gg) and 5 fixtures shifted from OutputMismatch to RuntimeCrashed (option_result_combinators.gg, test_enum_match.gg, etc.) — they were previously blocked behind the f-string surface; the fix unlocked them to expose orthogonal downstream bugs. OutputMismatch: 365→294 (−71, of which +68 to Match, +3 to RuntimeCrashed). CcFailed unchanged at 508. **Layering**: the writer site was upstream of every C-emit path; downstream `lir_codegen.gg` needed only the one-line printf-family alias for the new gorget_string_format call. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib --release` 1057/1059 green (2 pre-existing `lir::validate::tests` `should_panic` failures are release-mode debug-assert artifacts, confirmed pre-existing by stashing the fix); `cargo test --release --test integration -- parser_comparison resolver_comparison type_comparison lowerer_comparison c_emit_comparison self_host_bootstrap self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` 7/7 green (~860s); `GG_FULL=1 cargo test --release --test integration self_host_e2e` `Match: 162/995 (16.3%)` (up from 94/995, with 0 remaining `{}` literals in OutputMismatches). **Spot-checks**: `auto_types.gg` self-host stage-1 prints `42`, `hello`, `true`, `A` (vs the previous `{}` cluster) — `3.140000` still prints as `0.000000` and one of the IIFE closures still prints `0` instead of `15`, but those are orthogonal float-init and closure-return self-host gaps. `chars.gg`, `bare_param_immutable.gg`, `bitwise_ops.gg` self-host stage-1 fully match Rust gg's stdout. Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (EFString case rewritten 19→67 lines); `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_codegen.gg` (1 line: `gorget_string_format` added to the printf-family alternation at line 3628).
