- [2026-05-19] **selfhost(lowerer): add `eliminate_dead_globals` LIR pass + strip dead preamble `__lir_g<N>` decls — closes 96 `__lir_g` collisions in `self_host_e2e`.** Baseline Match: 84/995 (8.4%). Post-fix Match: 85/995 (8.5%). **Cluster fixed** (96 fixtures total): the top two CC-failure clusters were collisions on the `__lir_g<N>` C-identifier namespace between the e2e harness's runtime preamble (built from `_self_host_e2e_preamble.gg`) and the stage-1 body emitted by `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/driver`. Two failure modes: (a) **67 fixtures** `error: conflicting types for '__lir_g0'; have 'GorgetFile'` — preamble had `double __lir_g0 = INFINITY` (dead, init-in-main excluded by the cut), stage-1 had `GorgetFile __lir_g0 = stdin`; (b) **29 fixtures** `error: redefinition of '__lir_g0'` — same name, types coincide (both emit INFINITY/NAN). **Root cause + fix**: self-host's `lower_gir_to_lir` unconditionally lowers every `gmod.statics` entry, including stdin/stdout/stderr handles from `lib/std/io.gg` even when the fixture never touches them. Rust gg has `eliminate_dead_globals` in `src/lir/optimize.rs:410` that prunes unreferenced globals before codegen. Self-host was missing the parity pass. **Fix at the writer site**: ported the pass into `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg` (new `eliminate_dead_globals` function; 3-pass: collect referenced gids from `IGlobalAddr` instructions, build old→new index map, rewrite all `IGlobalAddr` to use new gids), wired into `driver.gg` between `lower_gir_to_lir` and `run_ssa`. **Plus** `tests/integration.rs:strip_user_struct_defs` now also strips dead `<type> __lir_g<N> = ...;` declarations from the preamble (the cut excludes the in-main init code so they're unreachable). Both fixes are complementary: self-host pass reduces stage-1 emission to only the globals the fixture actually uses; harness strip handles the residual case where stage-1 legitimately emits the same global the preamble also has (INFINITY/NAN). Net cluster: 67 `conflicting types` → 0, 29 `redefinition` → 0. Match +1 (the rest of the freed fixtures hit other downstream bugs and progressed from CcFailed → OutputMismatch / RuntimeCrashed). Rust gg analog: `src/lir/optimize.rs:410` (`eliminate_dead_globals`). **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059; `lowerer_comparison`, `parser_comparison`, `type_comparison`, `resolver_comparison`, `lexer_comparison` all green; `c_emit_comparison` green; `self_host_bootstrap` and `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` both green; `GG_FULL=1 self_host_e2e` reports `Match: 85/995 (8.5%)` (up from 84/995, with 0 remaining `__lir_g` collisions in the CC failure cluster). Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg`, `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/driver.gg`, `tests/integration.rs`.

- [2026-05-18] **fix(typecheck): allow Result→T auto-prop in non-generic enum variant constructor args (snag #46 ↔ #8 reconciliation).** Snag #8's writer-site fix (commit `7ba60e1c`, 2026-05-18) closed a typecheck hole where the non-generic-variant fast-path in `infer_variant_constructor` skipped arg-type unification entirely — silently accepting `Outer.StrV(int_x)` and feeding garbage to the runtime. But its strict `unify` call also false-positived against the **principled** snag #46 behaviour (commit `c80e58a4`-ish from 2026-05-14, `[2026-05-14] Snag #46`): a `throws`-fn call returning `Result[T, E]` passed inline to a constructor at `T`-typed position is **legal** when the enclosing function can propagate — the IR-lowering's `maybe_auto_propagate` unwraps the Result at consumption. Two correct fixes collided. **Failure surface**: `tests/fixtures/snag46_throws_inline_in_ctor.gg:64` (case A: `Tagged.BoolV(fn_bool_throws())` inside `throws MyException` ctx) reported `error: type mismatch: expected bool, found Result[bool, MyException]` after `7ba60e1c`. **Fix at the same writer**: route the new unify check through the existing throws-sugar compatibility helpers — `is_auto_propagation_compatible(declared, value)` (line 3829, the Result[T, E]→T propagating-context unwrap) and `is_result_capture_compatible(declared, value)` (line 3976, the dual `Result[T, E] r = call()` capture form). This is the same pattern the call-arg / var-decl / return / if-cond sites already use (e.g. typecheck.rs:1361, :2763, :2815, :2855, :2987, :3014). The carve-out applies symmetrically at the generic-variant branch too — `Some(throws_call())` / user-generic `Outer.A(call())` had the same hole; both branches now skip `unify` when auto-prop OR Result-capture covers the apparent mismatch. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green; `cargo test --release --test integration snag46_throws_inline_in_ctor` PASSES (cases A through F all "got true" / "got (true, 42)"); `cargo test --release --test integration gorget_js_snag_8_nongeneric_enum_arg_typecheck` PASSES (snag #8 regression sentinel still rejects `Outer.StrV(int_x)`); targeted spot-check `snag throws result enum` 91/91 green (no regressions). **Layering**: both fixes live at the same writer site (`infer_variant_constructor`), so the discipline is "the strict check must respect the same throws-sugar carve-outs the rest of the typechecker uses." Per CLAUDE.md "complexity = wrong layer": the fix is a one-call-site routing change at the writer, not a multi-case patch at any downstream reader. Files: `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (non-generic and generic branches of `infer_variant_constructor` both route through `is_auto_propagation_compatible` + `is_result_capture_compatible`).

- [2026-05-18] **fix(selfhost): restore `self_host_check/driver.gg` ctx plumbing (regression from c52f5c7b).** `check_comparison` integration test was failing to even build the self-host driver since commit `c52f5c7b` (2026-05-18 typechecker port of 5 control-flow checks), with `error: ownership mismatch for ctx: expected mutable borrow (&), found borrow (bare)` at `self_host_check/driver.gg:69`. **Root cause**: `c52f5c7b` widened `type_check_module`'s signature to take `ResolveContext &ctx` (mutable borrow) and threaded `&ctx` through 113 caller sites in `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/`, but missed the parallel `self_host_check/driver.gg`. The dir is a sister fixture set: 16 of its 17 `.gg` files are SYMLINKS to `self_host_typechecker/` (so the signature change auto-propagated), but `driver.gg` is an independent copy (loader-aware vs analyze-only) and stayed at the old bare-`ctx` call site. **Why it slipped**: `c52f5c7b`'s verification step ran `type_comparison` + `lowerer_comparison` + `resolver_comparison` + `parser_comparison` + `lexer_comparison` (5 of the 6 comparison tests) but NOT `check_comparison` — the only one whose driver dir has an independent `driver.gg`. **Fix**: one-character edit at `self_host_check/driver.gg:69` — `type_check_module(m, &scopes, &types, ctx)` → `type_check_module(m, &scopes, &types, &ctx)`. The signature is already correct via the symlinked `typecheck.gg`. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1057/1059 green (2 pre-existing failures in `lir::validate::tests` unrelated, confirmed pre-existing by stashing the fix and re-running); `cargo test --release --test integration -- --test-threads=4 type_comparison lowerer_comparison resolver_comparison parser_comparison lexer_comparison check_comparison` 6/6 green in 69s. **Lesson**: the introducing commit's verification step should have run ALL comparison tests when touching ANY `self_host_*` driver dir — `check_comparison` is the regression-net for `gg check` against the self-host implementation and is the only comparison test with an independent driver. Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_check/driver.gg` (line 69: `ctx` → `&ctx`).

- [2026-05-18] **selfhost(typecheck): port 5 control-flow check sites from Rust analog (first batch from the 47-site queue).** Builds on the 2026-05-18 typed-Diagnostic infrastructure commit `6fedd333` — that commit shipped the `Vector[Diagnostic] diagnostics` field on `ResolveContext`, the `&ctx` plumbing through 19 fn signatures, and ONE exemplar push site (`MainThrowsNonInt`); this commit adds the first batch of REAL check-site ports, which means porting the corresponding **check logic** (not just the diagnostic call). **Ported sites** (5 total): (a) `BreakOutsideLoop` — `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:2875` (SemanticErrorKind::BreakOutsideLoop), `break` in a position where no enclosing loop is active; (b) `ContinueOutsideLoop` — `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:2898` (SemanticErrorKind::ContinueOutsideLoop), same shape; (c) `ThrowInNonThrowingFunction` — `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:2866` (SemanticErrorKind::ThrowInNonThrowingFunction), `throw` in a fn that doesn't declare `throws T`; (d) `DoubleAwait` — `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:2075` (SemanticErrorKind::DoubleAwait), `await await x` where the inner await already unwrapped Task[T]→T; (e) `ReturnOutsideFunction` — `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:2833` (SemanticErrorKind::ReturnOutsideFunction), wired against `ctx.in_function_body` (parser rejects truly module-scope `return` upfront, so the check is rarely exercised in practice but matches the Rust semantics). **Infrastructure**: added new `DkControlFlow` variant to all four per-dir `diagnostic.gg` copies (`self_host_typechecker` + `self_host_parser` + `self_host_resolver` + `self_host_lexer`, with `self_host_lowerer/diagnostic.gg` inheriting via the existing symlink) — cross-stage parity. All four copies now have identical 8-variant `DiagKind` enums. Added 3 fields to `ResolveContext` (in `resolve.gg`): `int loop_depth`, `bool current_function_throws`, `bool in_function_body`. `type_check_function` save-resets-restores them around the body walk (mirroring Rust's `check_function` per-function context save). `walk_expr_closures_with_type`'s `EClosure` case save-resets-restores them around the closure body walk (closures have their own throws/loop scope). `SFor` / `SWhile` / `SLoop` cases bump+drop `loop_depth` around their body walks. The Break/Continue/Throw/Return checks fire on the `Stmt`'s embedded expression span when the stmt has a payload (the AST has no spans on bare statements); `SContinue` falls back to `Span(0,0)`. The DoubleAwait check is driven from a new `EAwait` arm in `walk_expr_closures_inner` (NOT from `infer.gg`'s `EAwait` — that path is driven by VarDecl init AND by the new walk arm, so pushing the diag there would double-fire). The walk arm fires for both VarDecl init (`auto v = await await x`) AND return-position (`return await await x`); `infer.gg`'s comment notes the choice. **Fixture**: `tests/fixtures/typecheck_control_flow_diagnostics.gg` (new) — covers all 4 active checks; type_comparison reads only stdout so the DIAG-on-stderr output is invisible to the matched/mismatched accounting (fixture lands in "exact"). **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean. `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green. `cargo test --release --test integration type_comparison` ok (Fixtures compared: 1115, exact: 1023, superset: 40, total: 1063, mismatched: 52, crashed: 0 — mismatched IDENTICAL to pre-port baseline; no regression). `lowerer_comparison` / `resolver_comparison` / `parser_comparison` / `lexer_comparison` 4/4 ok. End-to-end smoke: running the rebuilt self-host typechecker driver on the new fixture emits the expected 4 `DIAG error control-flow` lines on stderr; running on `void foo() throws int: throw 42` is silent (no false positive on legal throw). **42 of 47 Rust-side `self.error(...)` sites remain** — TypeMismatch / WrongArgCount / NoFieldFound / RethrowInNonThrowingFunction / OnErrorInNonThrowingFunction / SelectOutsideAsync / AwaitOutsideAsync / SpawnNonFuture / AwaitNonFuture / NonExhaustiveMatch / PositionalAfterNamed / etc. Each is a separate follow-up — TODO entry sharpened. Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_{lexer,parser,resolver,typechecker}/diagnostic.gg` (DkControlFlow variant added); `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/{resolve.gg (3 fields), typecheck.gg (function entry save/restore + closure entry save/restore + SFor/SWhile/SLoop loop_depth bump + SReturn/SBreak/SContinue/SThrow check sites + EAwait DoubleAwait check in walk_expr_closures_inner), infer.gg (comment about DoubleAwait dispatch site)}`; `tests/fixtures/typecheck_control_flow_diagnostics.gg` (new fixture).

- [2026-05-18] **perf(ir/lowering): bundle of 4 follow-ups — `meta_expand` block.clone elision (−97%) + `lower_if` sub-bucket instrumentation + `is_source_mut_unsafe_at` format! retire + `lower_var_decl` get_type_def coalesce.** (Commit `5579bd66`.) Bundles the four cheap-win follow-ups filed by the `91af0eb1` and `177388b0` instrumentation commits. **Items**:

  **(1) Coalesce redundant `get_type_def(&tn)` in `lower_var_decl`** (filed by `177388b0`). The opt/result enum-droppability branch did two FxHashMap-by-name lookups on the same `tn`. Coalesced into one. Added `TypeRegistry::is_closure_runtime_type(type_id) -> bool` in `src/ir/types.rs` and folded three independent `match get(...) { Named(n) => get_type_def(n).c_runtime_alias == Some("GorgetClosure") }` chains in `lower_var_decl` into typed accessor calls. Layering rule 2 win: name-match on `"GorgetClosure"` literal → typed boolean. Measured: no isolated perf delta (sub-ms regime); code quality is the win.

  **(2) Instrument `lower_if` into sub-sub-phases** (filed by `177388b0`). `lower_if` was a single ~11ms bucket; split into 5 named sub-phases using the same `stmt_nested_dur` checkpoint trick. On the lowerer driver (median-of-5): `then_branch` 5.19ms (47%) / `cond_eval` 4.06ms (37%) / `elif_branches` 1.47ms (13%) / `else_branch` 0.46ms (4%) / `phi_merge` 0.07ms (1%). Sum 11.25ms matches the parent `stmt::if` ~11.0ms. Finding: dominant is `then_branch` (structural per-Stmt::If); no one-line cheap win surfaces.

  **(3) Retire residual `format!` in `is_source_mut_unsafe_at`** (filed by `91af0eb1`). Three `format!("@mut:{}", path)` allocations per call → single `String::with_capacity(...)` buffer with `truncate(PREFIX.len())` + incremental `push_str` rebuild. 3+ allocs/call → 1 alloc/call. **Note**: shipped on disk as part of commit `982c853e` (gorget-js snag #7) when the parallel agent's `git commit -a` swept up my staged context.rs edits. Same fix on disk, mixed commit attribution.

  **(4) `meta_expand` block.clone elision** (filed by `91af0eb1`). New `meta::block_has_delayed_meta(&Block) -> bool` recursive scanner walks all nested blocks looking for any `Stmt::Meta*` or `MatchItem::MetaFor`. Read-only AST walk with early exit. Gates the three `evaluate_delayed_meta_block` call sites in `src/ir/lowering/functions.rs` — if no delayed-meta node is reachable, skip the `block.clone()` + walk entirely. **Measured: `body::meta_expand` 3.4ms → 0.10ms on the lowerer driver (−97%); same drop ratio across all 4 workloads.** Headline-visible perf win of the bundle.

  **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green; targeted integration `self_host_lexer self_host_parser self_host_resolver_comparison self_host_e2e lowerer_comparison type_comparison resolver_comparison` 6/6 green. Profile snapshot post-bundle (median-of-5 on `self_host_lowerer/driver.gg`): total ≈ 597ms, `gir_lower` 103.5ms, `lower_functions` 52.7ms, `body::lower_block` 43.2ms, `meta_expand` 0.1ms. Files: `src/ir/types.rs` (+`is_closure_runtime_type`), `src/ir/lowering/context.rs` (`is_source_mut_unsafe_at` rewrite — shipped via `982c853e` co-commit), `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs` (var_decl coalesce + 3 `is_closure_runtime_type` call sites + `lower_if` instrumentation), `src/ir/lowering/functions.rs` (3 elision gates), `src/semantic/meta.rs` (+`block_has_delayed_meta`).

- [2026-05-18] **fix(ir/lowering): tag view-returning String methods in the builtin protocol — close gorget-js snag #7.** Regression from this week's StructLiteral liveness work (`0872feeb` "isolate StructLiteral as snag #3 culprit" + `1af25de0` "enable StructLiteral liveness arm"). Once `uses_expr` walked StructLiteral args, a last-use string local bound to `byte_slice` (or another view-returning method) got `AssignMode::Move` at struct-init — but the view bytes (cap=0 Str pointing into the receiver's buffer) flowed into the struct field verbatim instead of materializing through clone-to-owned. The struct field then held a dangling alias once the receiver dropped. Real-world site: `src/lexer.gg` in gorget-js — `lex.source.byte_slice(start, end)` stored into `Tok.text` — 38/59 lexer unit tests failing + every downstream JS parse failing on garbage tokens. **Root cause at the writer**, per CLAUDE.md "complexity = wrong layer" + "typed metadata, not name-matched": `byte_slice` (along with `char_at`, `trim_left`, `trim_right`, `lstrip`, `rstrip`, `removeprefix`, `removesuffix`) was NOT declared in the `GORGET_STRING_VIEW` protocol in `src/ir/lowering/builtins.rs`. The protocol's `returns_view: true` flag is what tags the call's result local as `LocalOwnership::View` at the call-site tagger in `methods.rs` (`builtin_returns_view` queries the protocol). Without the entry, the result was treated as Owned, no view-tag was set, and the consume-site clone path in `ensure_owned_at_boundary` / `clone_multi_use_resource_args` saw a regular owned local — no clone-to-owned was emitted. The adjacent `substring` method WAS in the protocol and worked correctly. **Fix**: register the missing methods in the protocol with the correct `returns_view`/`runtime_callee`/params. Required a small typed-metadata extension — the `params` callback signature was `fn(&BuiltinTypeArgs) -> Vec<TypeId>`, which couldn't produce a `String`-typed param (needed for `lstrip(chars)` / `rstrip(chars)` / `removeprefix(p)` / `removesuffix(s)`) because `owned_string_type` is dynamic. Mirror of the existing `return_type: fn(&BuiltinTypeArgs, &LookupCtx) -> TypeId` shape — `params` now takes `&LookupCtx` too. Adds a `string_param` helper alongside the existing `no_params` / `int_param` / `two_ints` / etc. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green; targeted integration sweep `cow view byte_slice struct_literal ownership` 32/32 green (including new `gorget_js_snag_7_view_through_struct_literal`); `string char_at strip slice trim lstrip rstrip removeprefix removesuffix` 89/89; `self_host_lexer self_host_parser` 2/2; `lexer_comparison parser_comparison resolver_comparison type_comparison` 4/4; all snag tests (`snag_1 snag_3 snag_4 snag_5 snag_6 snag_7 snag_8`) 8/8. Snag #3's fixture (`gorget_js_snag_3_match_struct_literal_use`) remains green — the fix is purely additive at the protocol layer, doesn't undo the liveness arm. Files: `src/ir/lowering/builtins.rs` (8 new view methods + `string_param` helper + `params` signature widened to `(&BuiltinTypeArgs, &LookupCtx)` + 21 closure/helper bodies updated to the new arity), `src/ir/lowering/context.rs` (2 call sites pass `&lookup_ctx`), `tests/fixtures/gorget_js_snag_7_view_through_struct_literal.gg` (new), `tests/integration.rs` (new test).

- [2026-05-18] **fix(typecheck): check arg types for non-generic enum variant constructors (gorget-js snag #8).** `infer_variant_constructor` in `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` had a non-generic fast-path (`if generic_params.is_empty()`) that walked args via `infer_expr` for side-effects but skipped the arg-type unification step entirely. Repro: `enum Outer: StrV(String); NumV(int)` and `Outer.StrV(int_x)` passed `gg check` silently, then the runtime reinterpreted int bytes as a String header and printed garbage. The generic branch worked correctly because its substitution path inherently unifies each arg against the variant's declared field type (so `Some(x: int)` instantiates `?T → int`); non-generic variants have no type-vars to bind, and the author of the fast-path forgot they still need the plain type check. **Fix at the writer**: resolve `variant_field_types` with an empty `subst` map and unify each arg's inferred type against the field type, mirroring the generic path minus the substitution step. Diagnostic surface unchanged — uses the same `SemanticErrorKind::TypeMismatch` the rest of the typechecker emits. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green; targeted `cargo test --release --test integration enum` 32/32 green (including new `gorget_js_snag_8_nongeneric_enum_arg_typecheck`); `cargo test --release --test integration typecheck match variant` 61/61 green. The new fixture `tests/fixtures/gorget_js_snag_8_nongeneric_enum_arg_typecheck.gg` is a negative test asserting the diagnostic surfaces. Generic-enum constructor paths (`Some(42)`, `Ok("x")`, `MyResult.Bad(...)`) verified intact via a smoke fixture. **gorget-js eval.gg surface**: task description anticipated 4 snag #2 sites would appear after this fix (vs the 2 it already flagged); observed 0 — gorget-js's `addf7ee [cleanup-H]` refactor retired the `host_error(JsValue.StringV(msg))` pattern entirely, so the snag #2 surface is closed by gorget-js's own work, not regressed by it. TODO entry sharpened to reflect the closure. Files: `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (writer-site fix in `infer_variant_constructor`), `tests/fixtures/gorget_js_snag_8_nongeneric_enum_arg_typecheck.gg` (new), `tests/integration.rs` (new negative test wiring).

- [2026-05-18] **perf(ir/lowering): instrument `lower_block` per-statement-kind + O(1) builder-index lookup cleanup in `infer_operand_type_*`.** Step 2 follow-up to `91af0eb1` — extends the `lower_function` instrumentation one more layer deeper into `body::lower_block`, exposing EXCLUSIVE (self) time per statement kind so the next round can target the dominant sub-sub-pass. **Instrumentation**: `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs::lower_stmt` now records each dispatch's wall time minus nested-`lower_stmt` time into `ctx.lower_fn_sub_times` under keys `lower_function::body::lower_block::stmt::<kind>` (var_decl / shared_var_decl / assign / compound_assign / return / expr / if / while / for / loop / match / throw / assert / assert_return / snapshot / with / unsafe / named_scope / select / break_continue / item_or_meta / on_error / pass). The exclusive-time math uses a new `LoweringContext::stmt_nested_dur: Duration` running total: each call saves it on entry, adds its own `elapsed` on exit so the parent subtracts it back out — the per-kind buckets sum to `body::lower_block` total with no double-counting from `Stmt::If`/`Stmt::Match`/`Stmt::For` recursing through their bodies. **Findings**: on the 695-function self-host lowerer (median-of-15 lightest-5 runs), `body::lower_block` ≈ 40ms breaks down as `var_decl` 11.7ms (29%) / `if` 9.1ms (23%) / `expr` 6.2ms (16%) / `match` 3.9ms (10%) / `return` 3.3ms (8%) / `assign` 2.3ms (6%) / `while` 1.4ms (4%) / rest <1ms. **The dominant kind `var_decl` is structural** — `lower_var_decl` (stmts/mod.rs:308-948, ~640 LOC) does ~6 typed registry checks (`is_box`, `type_name_for_id`, `get_type_def(c_runtime_alias)`, `is_resource_type`, `needs_drop`, `is_collection_type_name`) + 2-3 `infer_operand_type_with_builder` calls + 2-3 drop registration calls per var decl. Every individual op is a single FxHashMap lookup; the 12ms is genuinely 1500+ var-decls × ~8μs of typed bookkeeping. No O(N²) or per-call alloc to attack. Per the "ship instrumentation if cheap-fix isn't there" rule, no perf claim attached. **Quality cleanup landed alongside**: `infer_operand_type_with_builder` (stmts/mod.rs:2985), `infer_operand_type_full` (exprs/type_reg.rs:218), and `infer_type_name_from_operand_full` (exprs/methods.rs:3254) all linear-scanned `ctx.locals_iter()` BEFORE the O(1) `builder.locals[idx]` fallback. Swapped the order — in-range builder index first (authoritative for normal locals since `lower_var_decl` writes both maps with the same `type_id`), ctx scan only as fallback for closure-param sentinel `LocalId(u32::MAX - i)` IDs registered by `closures.rs:203`. Per CLAUDE.md "fix complexity as a signal of wrong layer": the 3-way duplicated linear-scan-before-O(1)-index pattern was the smell; the structurally-correct fix swaps the two arms with a comment explaining the sentinel-ID case. **Measured perf delta**: 0ms — the ctx.locals map is small enough (~30-50 entries per function) that the scan was already fast. The win is code quality, not throughput. **TODO follow-ups filed**: (A) coalesce the ~6 redundant `type_registry.get_type_def(type_name)` lookups in `lower_var_decl` into one cached read, speculative 1-2ms shave; (B) `lower_if`'s 9ms — would need its own sub-pass timer to identify dominant sub-work; (C) `lower_expr` (exprs/mod.rs, 4331 LOC) is the structural target for the `expr`-kind work — requires a refactor tour, not a one-line fix. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean. `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green. Targeted integration: `cargo test --release --test integration -- self_host_lexer self_host_parser self_host_e2e lowerer_comparison` 4/4 green; `resolver_comparison lexer_comparison` 2/2; `parser_comparison type_comparison` 2/2. Files: `src/ir/lowering/{context.rs (+1 field + 1 init), stmts/mod.rs (instrumentation + infer fix), exprs/type_reg.rs (infer fix), exprs/methods.rs (infer fix)}`.

- [2026-05-18] **perf(ir/lowering): instrument `lower_function` sub-passes + Rc<str>/&str fix on prescan, −10ms on lowerer `lower_functions` (−15%).** Extends the `3dfc9916` per-pass instrumentation pattern one layer deeper. **Step 1**: split `lower_function` (`src/ir/lowering/functions.rs`) into `setup` / `prescan` / `body` / `finalize` Duration accumulators on a new `LoweringContext::lower_fn_sub_times: HashMap<&'static str, Duration>` field, folded into `pass_times` by `lower_module` so they surface under `gir_lower::pass_times_ms` in `gg profile` JSON. `body` further split into `body::meta_expand` (the block.clone + delayed-meta walk) + `body::lower_block` (the dominant inner statement+expression walk). `prescan` split into the four AST walks: `cow_unsafe` / `cow_after` / `name_use_counts` / `liveness`. The `unaccounted` residual computation in `lower_module` filters out `lower_function::*` entries to avoid double-counting (they're already inside `lower_functions`). **Step 2**: writer-side fix at the two dominant prescan sub-passes. (a) `src/ir/lowering/liveness.rs` `FxHashSet<String>` → `FxHashSet<&'a str>` borrowed directly from AST `Expr::Identifier(name)` String fields. The live set is cloned at every branch (if/elif/else, match arm, while body, for body, Expr::If, Expr::Match) — with `String` each clone reallocated every entry (~9ms on the 695-function lowerer); with `&str` each clone rehashes 16-byte slice headers, no allocation. (b) `src/ir/lowering/functions.rs::compute_cow_reassigned_after` and helpers `FxHashSet<String>` → `FxHashSet<Rc<str>>` with a per-function `String→Rc<str>` interner. `cow_after_block` clones the live "future" set at every statement (`result.insert(stmt.span.start, future.clone())`) plus at every branch save/restore — with `String` each clone reallocated every entry (~7ms); with `Rc<str>` each clone is per-entry refcount bumps. `ctx.func_state.cow_reassigned_after` type updated to match. `is_source_mut_unsafe_at` queries unchanged at the API surface — `Rc<str>: Borrow<str>` lets `set.contains(s as &str)` work. The two analyses had structurally identical "reverse AST walk with branch union" patterns; `&str`-borrow is the cleaner fix for the analysis that produces internal-only state (liveness); `Rc<str>`-interning is the localized fix for the analysis that produces cross-function-boundary state (the result map lives in `FunctionState` and is queried across many body-lowering call sites).

  **Lowerer (`tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/driver.gg`, median-of-5)**:

  | Sub-pass                          | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Δ |
  |-----------------------------------|------------:|-----------:|---:|
  | `lower_functions` (parent total)  |        65.0 |       55.0 | **−15%** |
  | `lower_function::body`            |          ~50 |       45.8 | tail (dominant remainder) |
  | `lower_function::prescan`         |        18.0 |        7.8 | **−57%** |
  | &nbsp;&nbsp;`prescan::liveness`   |         9.0 |        3.0 | **−66%** |
  | &nbsp;&nbsp;`prescan::cow_after`  |         7.3 |        3.0 | **−59%** |
  | `gir_lower` (parent phase)        |       116.0 |      104.5 | **−10%** |
  | `total`                           |       581.0 |      570.0 | −2% |

  **Typechecker** (`self_host_typechecker/driver.gg`, median-of-5): `lower_functions` 12.3 → 11.3ms (−1ms, −8%); proportional but smaller absolute win because fewer functions and shorter bodies. **Parser**: tiny absolute, in noise.

  **The fix illustrates CLAUDE.md "Debugging heuristic — fix complexity as a signal of wrong layer" obliquely** — the writer site (`future.clone()` at every statement boundary plus union sites in if/match) was paying full per-`String` alloc cost; the cheap fix is changing the cell type to make clones cheap. The 9ms body-side speedup (~50ms → 45ms) is a downstream effect: body lowering reads `cow_reassigned_after` via `is_source_mut_unsafe_at` (one call per CoW-borrow site), and those calls used to allocate `format!("@mut:{}", path)` `String`s as map keys. Lingering follow-ups filed in TODO.md (residual `format!` in `is_source_mut_unsafe_at`, structural body sub-pass `lower_block` at 41ms which is the new dominant sub-pass and needs a tour of `exprs/mod.rs` + `stmts/mod.rs`).

  **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean. `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green. Targeted integration `cargo test --release --test integration -- self_host_lexer self_host_parser self_host_e2e` 3/3, `parser_comparison resolver_comparison type_comparison` 3/3, `cow_*` 21/21, `match_ for_loop` 51/51, `liveness move_ auto_move` 27/27 — all green. The prescan analyses are the load-bearing pieces of CoW + auto-move correctness, so this set is the targeted regression net for behavior-equivalence under the type change. Files: `src/ir/lowering/{liveness.rs,functions.rs,context.rs,mod.rs}`.

- [2026-05-18] **selfhost(lexer): migrate to typed `Diagnostic`, mirror resolver POC + parser migration patterns.** Final stage in the Diagnostic sweep for stages with low push-site counts (typechecker + lowerer remain; both have 50+ sites and warrant their own session). The old `String lex_error` field on `Lexer` was write-only — set at four error sites in `lex_scan_string` / `lex_scan_char_lit`, never read by any consumer; effectively dead state that masked the diagnostic as "handled." Replaced with `Vector[Diagnostic] lex_diagnostics`. **Migrated 5 push sites** at malformed-literal / unexpected-char paths: (a) `lex_scan_string:580` newline in non-triple string; (b) `lex_scan_string:592` escape parse failure; (c) `lex_scan_char_lit:677` mid-char escape failure; (d) `lex_scan_char_lit:685` EOL before closing quote; (e) `lex_scan_single_char:885` unrecognised character. Each pushes `Diagnostic.error(Span(start, self.lex_pos), DkLexError(), "msg")` using the scan function's pre-existing `int start = self.lex_pos` as the span start. The TkError-token emissions at (c) (d) (e) stay alongside the diagnostic push — TkError is the downstream-visible token contract (parser sees it via the token stream), diagnostic is the surfaced error stream. **Public API**: new `LexResult { Vector[SpannedToken] tokens; Vector[Diagnostic] diagnostics }` + `lex_with_diagnostics(source)` entry point. The existing `lex_tokenize(source) -> Vector[SpannedToken]` stays as a tokens-only convenience wrapper for callers (main.gg's inline tests; the parser dir's `parse_source`, which has its own lexer.gg copy at md5sum-identical bits and stays on the old shape per the per-dir migration policy) that don't need diagnostics. **Driver**: drains diagnostics to stderr (sorted by span start via insertion-sort for determinism), same shape as the parser driver from 2026-05-17. lexer_comparison reads only stdout so the line-by-line comparison contract stays byte-stable — none of the 996 fixtures actually trigger any of the migrated sites in practice (all parse cleanly through the lexer; the diagnostics are reserved for the upcoming malformed-input fixture sweep). **DkLexError variant added to all three diagnostic.gg copies** (`self_host_lexer/diagnostic.gg` new + `self_host_parser/diagnostic.gg` + `self_host_resolver/diagnostic.gg` for cross-stage parity). Span is defined inline in the lexer's diagnostic.gg (the lexer driver dir has no `ast.gg`; trivially identical to `ast.Span` in the parser/resolver dirs). **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, `cargo test --release --test integration lexer` 2/2 green (`self_host_lexer` main.gg inline tests + `lexer_comparison` 996-fixture sweep — byte-identical stdout to baseline), `cargo test --release --test integration parser_comparison resolver_comparison` 2/2 green (no regression from adding DkLexError to those dirs' diagnostic.gg). Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lexer/diagnostic.gg` (new, 115 lines), `tests/fixtures/self_host_lexer/lexer.gg` (struct field swap + 5 push sites + new `LexResult` + `lex_with_diagnostics` + `lex_tokenize` thinned to a one-line wrapper), `tests/fixtures/self_host_lexer/driver.gg` (rewired to `lex_with_diagnostics` + insertion-sort drain to stderr), `tests/fixtures/self_host_{parser,resolver}/diagnostic.gg` (+1 enum variant + 1 case arm each).

- [2026-05-18] **semantic(typecheck): push equip scope unconditionally in `register_signatures_recursive` — closes the latent footgun sibling of commit `27230b43`.** At `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:5898-5923`, the equip-block branch in `register_signatures_recursive` pushed a fresh `EquipBlock` scope only when `impl_block.generic_params.is_some()`. For non-generic equips, `register_function_signature` for the method ran with the root scope active. Today this was correct because commit `27230b43` (2026-05-17, the arena `gg check` regression fix) inverted the def-lookup order to span-first — so the scope-active-during-registration doesn't matter for the signature-write path. But the resolve-pass / typecheck-pass asymmetry was a latent footgun: any future code reading `scopes.current()` or `scopes.lookup_within_function(scopes.current_fn_scope(), ...)` inside `register_function_signature` would silently see the root scope for non-generic equip methods, picking up the wrong def for trait/equip-method generics or `Self` resolution. **Fix**: drop the `if impl_block.generic_params.is_some()` gate and push the `EquipBlock` scope unconditionally; the generic-param defines (when present) stay inside the scope; the matching `pop_scope()` runs after `register_function_signature` for all methods. Mirrors `src/semantic/resolve.rs:539`'s symmetric shape (unconditional push at the equip-block branch). Per CLAUDE.md "Layering Discipline rule 3 — one source of truth per axis": the scope-active-during-equip-method-registration is now consistent across the resolve and typecheck passes; no more "register a method without entering its equip scope" path. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, `cargo test --release --test integration -- --test-threads=4 equip trait method generic shadow` 109/109 green (`equip_method_no_shadow_extern` regression sentinel from 2026-05-17 commit `27230b43` still passes), `gg check target/gorget-arena/src/main.gg` clean (only the expected CoW auto-clone warning, zero errors). Diff: `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` ~5 line net change at lines 5898-5923.

- [2026-05-17] **fix(typecheck): equip method signature no longer clobbers same-named extern's signature — closes gorget-arena `gg check` regression surfaced by snag #2.** Symptom: 9× `expected VFS, found String` errors at `file_exists(...)` call sites in `target/gorget-arena/` after the post-2026-05-17 batch. Self-host comparison tests unaffected because no comparison-test parser/typechecker/resolver self-host module pairs a same-named equip method with a same-named extern. Root cause (writer site, per CLAUDE.md "fix complexity as a signal of wrong layer"): `register_function_signature` at `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:5099` looked up the def by NAME first (`scopes.lookup(func.name.node)`) and fell back to span lookup only if name lookup returned None. For an equip method `bool file_exists(self, String)` defined in vfs.gg, `register_signatures_recursive` recurses through `Item::Module → Item::Equip → method` without pushing the equip scope onto the scope stack (push happens only when the equip block has explicit generic params). At the equip method's `register_function_signature` call, the current scope is therefore the root module scope, so `scopes.lookup("file_exists")` returns whichever same-named def is visible there — for arena: the `gorget_file_exists` extern that `std.fs::file_exists` re-exports to the root via `export_non_private`. The function then writes the equip method's `(VFS, String) -> bool` signature into the EXTERN's `DefInfo.type_id`, silently corrupting every `file_exists(path: String)` call site across the importing module. Hidden by the imported-module truncate until snag #2 fix (commit `547a9abd`) routed concrete-vs-concrete call-arg mismatches through `hard_errors`. **Fix**: invert the lookup order — `lookup_def_by_span` first (name + span pair is documented as uniquely identifying), `scopes.lookup` removed entirely (span lookup is always correct; the fallback path was load-bearing-by-accident for the equip-not-on-stack case). Added regression fixture `tests/fixtures/equip_method_no_shadow_extern/` (vfs.gg + main.gg) and integration test `equip_method_no_shadow_extern`. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, `cargo test --release --test integration -- modules equip method trait_ imported shadow self_host_typechecker resolver_comparison parser_comparison type_comparison` green (105 tests across the touched surface, no regressions), `gg check target/gorget-arena/src/main.gg` now clean (was 9 errors), `gg build` succeeds and emits the arena binary cleanly.

Investigation under `--sanitize` (AddressSanitizer + UBSan) across four repro shapes failed to reproduce: (a) `Vector[Item]` where `Item` owns a `String`, push 3, pop into named `Option[Item]`, read `.name` field on the Some payload; (b) drain-via-pop `while items.len() > 0: Option[Item] tail = items.pop()` loop holding the Option past iterations; (c) parser-mirroring `Diagnostic { Span span, Severity sev, DiagKind kind, String message }` with `try_parse_with_rollback` + `while diagnostics.len() > saved: Option[Diagnostic] _d = diagnostics.pop()`; (d) tight 10-iteration speculation loop with truncate-by-pop rollback after pushing 1+ diagnostics. All ASAN-clean. **Why the contract is sound today**: `Vector.pop()` routes to `gorget_array_safe_pop` (`src/lir/runtime.rs:402` — `ArraySafePop`); the runtime decrements `arr->len` and returns a ptr to the now-past-len slot — `elem_drop` is NOT called (caller owns now). The LIR lift at `src/lir/lower/lifts.rs:emit_void_ptr_option_wrap` recognises `safe_pop` via `is_consuming_method` (line 65-70), skips the `resource_clone_fn_for_payload` path, and Memcpys the slot bytes directly into the Option's Some payload via `EnumInit` (aggregate-payload Memcpy expansion at line 172-175). The array's eventual drop iterates `0..len` (`gorget_array_clear`/`gorget_array_free` in `src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs`) so the popped slot — past len — is never re-dropped. Resource fields end up owned exactly by the popped Option, freed exactly once at Option drop. **Note**: a separate latent leak (`gorget_string_copy_cow` allocation orphaned by f-string `{}` interpolation when reading a String through `Vector[Vector[String]].pop().unwrap().get(0).unwrap()`) surfaced during the investigation; it is unrelated to pop and manifests even without pop (3-byte leak when the inner vector is read with one element, no leak when read with zero elements or via direct binding). Not in scope for this agent. **Outcome**: shipped `tests/fixtures/vector_pop_resource_element_no_double_free.gg` as a positive regression sentinel covering the truncate-by-pop shape + named-Option binding + named-payload field-read post-pop. Wired into `tests/integration.rs::vector_pop_resource_element_no_double_free` (passes; ASAN-clean under `--sanitize`). The `speculation_depth` gate in parser.gg stays — it remains the right design (semantic distinction speculative-vs-real parse, not a workaround). The doc-comment claim in `enter_speculation` is now overstated relative to ground truth; updating it is out of scope for this agent (parser.gg is the associated-type-alias agent's zone in this round). **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, `cargo test --release --test integration vector pop drop` 69/69 green (includes the new fixture), `gorget_js_snag_3_match_struct_literal_use` green, related vector/ownership/enum tests (`ownership_vector_elements`, `vector_struct_loop`, `enum_variant_clone_loop`) green.

- [2026-05-17] **ir(lowering): fix `lower_assign` to clear stale `maybe_moved` on reassignment — closes gorget-js snag #3 (the lone `StructLiteral` liveness culprit from commit `0872feeb`).** Commit `0872feeb` shipped 7 of 8 `uses_expr` variants from the reverted 9-variant fix (`2fddacdc`/`cc8dd42f`); `StructLiteral` was held back as a `#[ignore]`d fixture because adding it deterministically corrupted the self-host stage-0 driver with `malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`. ASAN traced the UAF to `Parser__parse_function_def`'s `bb26` regular-return path: `ret_ty` (a `SpannedType` local) was both memcpy'd into the returned `FunctionDef.return_type` AND dropped immediately after, producing a dangling `String` pointer that `derive___expand_derives::Item__clone` later memcpy'd from. The GIR showed `move_zero _2` correctly emitted in the other three return branches (which all cloned `_2`) but missing in `bb26` where `_2` was last-used and routed straight into the struct. **Root cause** (the "complexity = wrong layer" tell): `move_zero_consumed_args` queries `ctx.drops.is_moved(local)` to skip already-moved sources. `_2` was marked `maybe_moved=true` by an earlier `vec.push(move _2); move_zero _2` (inside the `if check_tok COMMA:` branch's tuple-types loop). The subsequent `[Mv] _2 = copy _13` (the `ret_ty = SpannedType(TTuple(...), Span(0,0))` re-bind) at `lower_assign` in `src/ir/lowering/stmts/assigns.rs:350` correctly emitted the Move assignment AND propagated ownership via `set_owned(local_id)` — but never **reset** the stale `maybe_moved` flag in `drops`. With the old liveness (no `StructLiteral` arm), the tail return always cloned `_2`, so the missing reset stayed latent. With the arm added, `_2` was correctly recognised as last-use → no clone → `move_zero_consumed_args` saw `is_moved=true` → skipped the required post-consume `move_zero` → the unconditional scope-exit `drop_if_alive _2` freed data the returned struct also owned. **Fix** (writer site, mirrors the existing `set_owned` propagation): new `DropElaborator::clear_moved(local)` helper in `src/ir/lowering/drops.rs` (1 method, ~10 lines); `lower_assign` calls it right after `builder.assign_mode(...)` so the slot's drop-state and ownership-state agree on "this slot has a live value here." Layering note per CLAUDE.md rule 3 (one source of truth): drop-state and ownership-state were diverging at this writer site — fixed by making the reset symmetric with the existing `set_owned`. **Retired**: `#[ignore]` removed from `gorget_js_snag_3_match_struct_literal_use` in `tests/integration.rs`. **Verification**: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, the snag #3 fixture now passes outputting `true`, all 4 self-host bootstrap tests green in 743s (`phase_c_closed_classes_remain_at_zero_self_host`, `self_host_bootstrap`, `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point`, `validate_passes_passes_self_host`), self-host driver compiles `dataframe_groupby.gg`/`json_parse.gg`/`httpserver_router.gg` cleanly with `GG_VALIDATE_PASSES=1` (zero `# validate_passes (FATAL):` headers). Diff: `src/ir/lowering/drops.rs` +24, `src/ir/lowering/stmts/assigns.rs` +14, `src/ir/lowering/liveness.rs` +6 (StructLiteral arm), `tests/integration.rs` ~12 (removed `#[ignore]` + refreshed comment).

- [2026-05-17] **backend(c_lir): forward-declare static-inline drop fns + extern clone fns at the top of `emit_recursive_struct_drops` / `emit_recursive_struct_clones` (closes parser POC out-param workaround).** Recursive-struct `{Name}__drop` fns are emitted in LIR-struct iteration order, which is *not* a topological order over the drop-call graph. When a parent `A { B field }` is iterated before `B`, `A__drop`'s body calls `B__drop` before `B__drop` is declared; with `static inline`, GCC promotes that to an *implicit declaration with `int()` linkage*, then errors at the real definition (`static declaration of 'B__drop' follows non-static declaration`). Same hazard for the per-type `{Name}__clone` fns (extern, not static, but same forward-reference shape — implicit declaration with `int()` return type collides with the later real declaration). Fix: at the top of each emitter, walk `module.structs` once and emit a forward declaration for every entry that will get a body (`static inline void X__drop(void*);` for drops; `T X__clone(void*);` for clones). Emission-order then doesn't matter. Minimal repro shape that failed before this fix and passes after: `struct ParseResult { Module module; Vector[Diagnostic] diagnostics }` where `Module` is declared *after* `ParseResult` — exactly the shape the self-host parser POC wanted in lieu of the `&out_diagnostics` out-parameter. Verification: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, drop-related integration tests (`box_in_recursive_struct`, `option_box_enum`, `drop_collections`, `recursive_enum_tree`, …) stay green. The retirement (parser `parse_source_into(source, &out_diagnostics) -> Module` → `parse_source(source) -> ParseResult`) was unblocked by the concurrent snag #3 finisher's `clear_moved` fix on reassignment-after-prior-consume (the field-of-result-struct passed-by-value path was hitting the snag #3 double-free until that landed) and got folded into commit `8103afeb` by the parser-noise agent's hand-merge; matched 1089/1107 — byte-identical to baseline. Per CLAUDE.md "when you fix a compiler gap, also retire the workarounds": both halves of the cited TODO sub-bullet now closed.

- [2026-05-17] **selfhost(parser): fix `parse_type` speculative-call diagnostic noise (98 fixtures → 1).** Closes the spurious-"expected type" follow-up filed in the parser typed-Diagnostic migration (DONE 2026-05-17). Root cause: the self-host parser has 6 speculative call sites that disambiguate generic-call-vs-index, method-level turbofish, generic-constructor, and function-type-vs-primitive — they save `self.pos`, call into `parse_type` / `parse_type_args` / `parse_function_type`, and roll the position back on failure. But `parse_type`'s fallback (`expected type`) **pushed unconditionally** to `Vector[Diagnostic]`, and the position rollback never undid the push. The drained-to-stderr migration made the noise visible at 98 fixtures × ~5 diagnostics each (474 spurious "expected type" entries at HEAD-baseline). **Fix at the writer site** (per CLAUDE.md "Layering Discipline" / "complexity = wrong layer"): new `int speculation_depth` field on `Parser` + `enter_speculation` / `exit_speculation` helpers around each of the 6 speculative call sites. `parse_type`'s fallback now gates its `self.diagnostics.push(...)` on `self.speculation_depth == 0` — mirrors Rust's design where speculative `parse_generic_type_args` returns `Err` (silent) and `try_parse(... .ok()?)` drops it without ever touching the parser's error stream. The 6 sites cover: postfix `expr[...]` (line 1613), method-level turbofish `.method[T](args)` (line 1825), generic constructor `Option[T](args)` for smart-pointer keywords (line 2326), primitive-keyword-followed-by-`(` function-type detection inside `parse_type` (line 1219), NamedType-followed-by-`(` function-type detection at two paths (lines 1294 / 1306). Non-speculative callers (var-decls, function return types, type aliases, etc.) still surface real "expected type" — the fallback push is **gated, not removed**. Naive `truncate-by-pop` rollback was tried first but trips a separate double-free bug — `gorget_array_pop` on a resource-typed-element vector doesn't transfer ownership cleanly (filed as latent in the doc-comment of `enter_speculation`). Verification: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, `cargo test --release --test integration parser_comparison` matched **1089/1107, mismatched 18, crashed 0** — byte-identical to baseline. **Diagnostic noise: spurious "expected type" 474 → 2** (the 2 remaining are real, in `sigil_type_args.gg` — `type Limit: Comparable = T` associated-type-alias inside trait, separate residual bug). Fixtures with spurious "expected type": 98 → 1. Scope discipline: `tests/fixtures/self_host_parser/parser.gg` only; the typechecker / lowerer / lexer copies are independent and stay on the old shape (md5sum confirms — typechecker's parser is unrelated to parser's parser). Co-Authored-By: C-backend drop-fn forward-decl agent (concurrent commit `5168d24e` migrated `parse_source_into → parse_source/ParseResult`; clean hand-merge in the same parser.gg).

Three sites in `src/lir/optimize.rs`:

Remaining stdlib uses in `optimize.rs` are all cold-path: `OptStats.pass_times` (tiny, static-string keys), `spawned_names`/`hot_reload_roots` in `find_live_functions` (small `&str` sets built once), `find_hashable_key_types` (one-shot String set), and the `HashSet<ValueId>`/`HashSet<usize>` *values* inside the already-FxHashMap'd `param_sources`/`removed_params` (matching the 2026-05-16 author's choice — small inner sets, not the dominant hash cost). Pure type swap, zero semantic change. Verification: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green. Scope strictly `src/lir/optimize.rs` per agent prompt.

- [2026-05-17] **selfhost(parser): typed `Diagnostic` migration — drains 8 push sites to typed records, surfaces 100+ previously-silent parse errors.** Mirrors the resolver POC pattern (DONE 2026-05-17, commit `e052606e`-ish ancestor): new `tests/fixtures/self_host_parser/diagnostic.gg` defines `Diagnostic { Span span; Severity sev; DiagKind kind; String message }` + `Severity { SevError, SevWarning, SevSuggestion }` + `DiagKind { DkUndefinedName, DkDuplicateDefinition, DkParseError, DkNotAType, DkTypeMismatch, DkUnreachable }` (DkParseError newly active; rest reserved for upcoming typechecker / lowerer / lexer stages). The `Parser` struct's `Vector[String] errors` field is replaced by `Vector[Diagnostic] diagnostics`; all 8 push sites (`expect_tok` + `expect_kw` + the 6 inline "expected type/pattern/field name/expression/case-or-else" sites) now construct typed records via `Diagnostic.error(self.current_span(), DkParseError(), msg)`. New `parse_source_into(source, &out_diagnostics) -> Module` entry point drains the parser-internal diagnostics into a caller-owned vector; the legacy `parse_source(source) -> Module` wraps it for back-compat. Driver renders diagnostics to **stderr** as `DIAG <severity> <kind> <span_start>:<span_end> <message>` lines (sorted by span start for determinism). **No regression**: `parser_comparison` matched 1088/1106 — identical to pre-migration. stdout comparison stays line-by-line stable because diagnostics go off-band. **Real bugs exposed**: ~97 fixtures fire spurious "expected type" diagnostics during parsing (the parser's `parse_type` fallback path hits at e.g. `print(v[0])` where Rust uses different expression/type-context lookahead). All pre-existing — masked by the write-only `errors` accumulator until this migration drained them — filed as a follow-up bullet in the same TODO entry. Out-param shape (`&Vector[Diagnostic]`) used in lieu of a `ParseResult` struct due to a C-backend gap: `ParseResult__drop` is emitted before `Module__drop` (non-topo struct-iteration order), causing a `static inline` forward-decl error. The proper fix at `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs::emit_recursive_struct_drops` is a 4-line forward-decl prelude; filed as a separate TODO sub-bullet. Verification: `cargo build --release` clean, `cargo test --lib` 1059/1059 green, `cargo test --release --test integration parser_comparison` green. Scope discipline: ONLY `self_host_parser/` touched — other dirs' `parser.gg` copies (independent per `md5sum`) untouched.

- [2026-05-17] **perf(lir,backend): retire stack-traces v1 fixpoint allocation churn + per-inst filename re-escape (~22ms per heavy fixture).** Profile-driven hotspot hunt on the stack-traces v1 regression. Two layers fixed at the writer site:

  **Layer 1 — LIR fixpoint alloc churn.** `eliminate_dead_code` was the 2nd-largest LIR opt sub-pass on `self_host_lowerer/driver.gg` (28ms post-v1, up from 12ms baseline), called inside the fixpoint loop ~10× per function × 695 functions × ~20 blocks. Per call it ran `mem::take` on `block.insts` + `block.span_map`, allocated two fresh `Vec::with_capacity` vecs, and re-pushed the kept entries. Replaced with: (a) an early-exit fast path that skips the whole block when no inst is dead (the dominant case after the first iteration); (b) in-place `Vec::retain` on `insts` and `span_map` lockstep-indexed via a tracking counter inside each closure. Same fix applied to `remove_companion_memsets`, `elaborate_block`'s deletion sweep, and `elaborate_drops` Phase 4 MoveSlot removal. Result on LW driver: `eliminate_dead_code` 28.1ms → 12.5ms (**-55%**), `post_elab_dce` 9.8ms → 5.4ms (**-45%**), `drop_elaboration` 138.1ms → 128.1ms (-7%).

  **Layer 2 — Codegen per-inst filename re-escape.** `resolve_panic_loc` was called per panic-emit-eligible LIR inst (~10% of ~200k insts on LW). Each call ran `escape_c_string(filename)` — a fresh `Vec<char>` of every filename character + a per-char match + a `String` of equivalent size, dropped on return. Pre-baked the C-escaped filename inside `FileInfo` at construction (one walk per file at load) and added `offset_to_location_full` so the codegen path reads the pre-baked field instead of re-escaping. Result on LW codegen: 102.9ms → 96.2ms-ish (∼-13ms in cleaner runs; noisy due to overall codegen variance).

  **End-to-end speedup** (`self_host_lowerer/driver.gg`, median of 5 release runs):
  - HEAD before fix: 647.8ms total / 227.6ms `lir_optimize` / 102.9ms `codegen`
  - HEAD after fix: 640.8ms total / 207.6ms `lir_optimize` / 101.5ms `codegen`
  - Baseline (`e4e1f6a3` pre-stack-traces): 637.1ms total / 202.4ms `lir_optimize` / 96.2ms `codegen`
  - Net: regression closed from +44.2ms (lowerer) / +20.2ms (typechecker) to **+3.7ms / +3.8ms** — within the small-fixture flat tax band that's unavoidable from filling span_map at every push site. Sum across 9 heavy fixtures: +86.8ms → +29.4ms.

  **Layering note**: span_map's parallel-array shape vs `insts` survives because every mutation site is now either an in-place `retain` lockstep walk or carries a defensive reseed (`if span_map.len() != insts.len()`). Per CLAUDE.md Layering Discipline rule 1, the invariant doesn't drop. Per rule 2, `filename_c_escaped` is typed metadata on `FileInfo` (not a sidecar map) — the source of truth is the `FileInfo::new` constructor; consumers read through a typed accessor.

  Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1059/1059 green, all targeted critical fixtures (yaml_parse, test_set_all, regex_basic, etc., 11 tests) green, self_host_lexer/parser/e2e/snag5 green (152s for those 4). Diff: `src/lir/optimize.rs` +27/-13, `src/lir/drop_elab.rs` +93/-50, `src/span.rs` +60/-3 (escape helper + `offset_to_location_full`), `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs` +9/-3 (read `fi.filename_c_escaped.clone()`).

- [2026-05-17] **perf(semantic): pre-allocate primitive IDs + name-keyed trait impl index + single-pass trait method resolve.** Three-item Low-priority cluster from the 2026-05-16 semantic perf hunt, shipped as one bundle. (1) `TypeTable::primitive_id` (`src/semantic/types.rs:222`): the fast-path cached IDs for `Bool/Int/Float/CStr/StringType/Void` in O(1), but `Int8/16/32/64`, `Uint8/16/32/64`, `Float32/64` fell through to a linear scan over `self.types` (which grows to thousands of entries at self-host scale, and is hit on every typed annotation via `ast_type_to_resolved` plus every `byte_at`/`to_upper`/`to_lower` call via `builtin_method_type`). Fix: pre-allocate all 17 `PrimitiveType` variants in `TypeTable::new`, store in a fixed-size `[TypeId; 17]` array indexed by `PrimitiveType as usize`. `primitive_id` is now an unconditional array lookup — **O(N_types) → O(1)** on every variant. (2) `TraitRegistry::resolve_method` (`src/semantic/traits.rs:155`): after the 2026-05-16 `trait_impls_by_type` index shipped, the lookup still did two passes over the same impl-indices bucket (overrides then default fallback). Combined into one pass that records `default_hit: Option<&TraitInfo>` and falls through to it on a second miss — **2 × N_bucket → N_bucket** (sub-microsecond win since typical buckets are 1-5 entries, but free cleanup). (3) `TraitRegistry` five-method name-keyed scans (`has_any_impl_by_name`, `has_inherent_only_impls`, `has_trait_impl_by_name`, `trait_generic_args_by_name`, `has_method_for_type`): all five walked every impl in the registry filtering by `self_type_name: String` — used from the typecheck cross-module-equip fallback and from meta `implements(T, Trait)`. Added a parallel `impls_by_name: FxHashMap<String, Vec<usize>>` index populated at the single `registry.impls.push(...)` write site (mirrors the existing `trait_impls_by_type` pattern); all five methods now hit the bucket directly — **O(N_impls) → O(N_bucket)**. Layering note: name-keyed lookup is fine here because the underlying data (`self_type_name: String`) is *already* name-keyed at the source — this is not new name-matching, it's an index over an existing string axis. Per CLAUDE.md Layering Discipline rule 3 (one source of truth per axis), the linear-scan code is *replaced*, not retained as a fallback; the source of truth remains `registry.impls`. Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1059/1059 green, targeted integration set (`trait method_resolve generic primitive`, 64 tests) all green in 2.47s. Continues the established playbook (recent `ScopeTable` and `trait_impls_by_type` wins). Diff: `src/semantic/types.rs` +37/-15, `src/semantic/traits.rs` +60/-30.

- [2026-05-17] **fix(typecheck): surface concrete-vs-concrete call-arg mismatches in imported modules (gorget-js snag #2).** Symptom: in gorget-js's 6094-line `eval.gg`, the call `int new_len = to_uint32(raw)` where `raw: float` and the function signature is `int to_uint32(JsValue v) throws RuntimeException` **silently compiled** — no type error from `gg check`, just a broken binary that reinterpreted the float's bit pattern as a JsValue enum tag and returned 0. The same call in a 25-line standalone file correctly errored. **Root cause**: `check_items_recursive_tc` in `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` truncated ALL type-check errors emitted while processing `Item::Module` (imported modules) — the truncate was added 2026-03-14 to swallow library-foreign-scope false positives, but the sledgehammer also ate real, concrete-vs-concrete call-argument type mismatches at user-imported module boundaries. **Fix** (surgical, doesn't widen the false-positive surface): added `hard_errors: Vec<SemanticError>` sidecar on `TypeChecker` + an `is_fully_concrete(TypeId)` helper that returns true only when neither side carries `Var`, `Error`, or `Never` (recurses through Generic/Tuple/Array/Slice/Ref/Owned args). At the `Expr::Call` arg-unify site (line ~1378), run `unify(param_type, arg_type, arg.span)` normally; if `unify` pushes a new error AND both types are fully concrete, mirror the pushed error into `hard_errors`. The imported-module truncate now does `errors.truncate(N)` then re-appends `hard_errors[hard_N..]` — known-real call-arg mismatches survive, foreign-scope auto-prop and unbound-Var noise still gets eaten. Verified: snag #2's `to_uint32(raw)` now errors at `eval.gg:4781:29 type mismatch: expected JsValue, found float`; self-host typechecker comparison test (`driver.gg`) stays clean (the 184 byte-literal `int → uint8` mismatches still hidden — they involve non-concrete inference paths and would need a separate writer-site fix at the byte-literal lexer); two additional pre-existing bugs in gorget-js `eval.gg` (lines 4266, 5185: `host_error(&realm, msg, ...)` where `msg: RuntimeException` not `String`) now also surface (real bugs, gorget-js will fix). New fixture: `tests/fixtures/imported_call_arg_type_check/{main,impl,lib}.gg` — main.gg imports impl.gg which imports lib.gg; the wrong-typed call (`unwrap_tagged(float_arg)`) lives in impl.gg so it's processed under the truncate path. Integration test `imported_call_arg_type_check_errors` (post-`modules_basic`) asserts `gg check` reports the mismatch. Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1059/1059 green, narrow fixture check confirms broken case fires and good case is unaffected. Touches `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (+58/-2), `tests/integration.rs` (+13), new fixture dir (3 files).

- [2026-05-17] **lint(typecheck): suggest `throws E` for match-unwrap-or-rethrow Result patterns.** Closes the discoverability gap surfaced by the gorget-js critique (2026-05-12): an LLM with docs access built a 4500-line interpreter, then realised in hindsight that `throws E` + auto-propagation would have eliminated ~40% of its `match Result: case Ok(v): v; case Error(e): return Error(e)` boilerplate. New module `src/semantic/lint_suggest_throws.rs` runs as Pass 4.6 (between typecheck and safety, consuming `expr_types`). For each function whose return type is `Result[T, E]` AND that is NOT already declared `throws`, the lint walks every `Stmt::VarDecl` / `Stmt::Assign` whose RHS is `Expr::Match` over a Result-typed scrutinee with exactly two arms — `Ok(v)` unwrapping `v` and `Error(e)` rethrowing via `return Error(e)`, `return e`, or `throw e` (single-statement Block bodies accepted; multi-stmt arms rejected as ambiguous). Variant identification goes through typed `EnumVariantInfo` DefIds (`Ok`/`Error` DefIds resolved once at entry), NOT string-compares on path names — per CLAUDE.md "No name matching". One `SuggestThrowsRefactor { fn_name, error_type, occurrence_count }` warning per function (not per site) — keeps signal high when a function has 5 of these in a row. Threaded into the existing `result.warnings: Vec<SemanticWarning>` channel, rendered through the unchanged `report_semantic_warning` path. Side improvement: typecheck now records `expr_types[scrutinee.span] = scrutinee_type` for both `Expr::Match` and `Stmt::Match`, closing a gap that previously left match scrutinees outside the typed-expr map. Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/lint_suggest_throws_{basic,negative_nonresult,already_throws}.gg` + 3 integration tests (`check_gg_warns` / `check_gg_silent_for` helpers). Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1059/1059 green, cargo test --test integration -- lint_suggest 3/3 green, `match_*` / `throws_*` / `catch_*` test families unchanged (~56 + 25 tests). Diff: +650 (new lint module + helpers + fixtures + tests), -1 (one TODO move).

Idiomatic constructor helpers via `equip Diagnostic: Diagnostic error(span, kind, msg) / .warn(...) / .suggest(...)` — call sites read `Diagnostic.error(expr.span, DkUndefinedName(), msg)` instead of verbose struct literals. Migration scope: `ResolveContext` gained `Vector[Diagnostic] diagnostics` field; previously-silent error sites in `resolve.gg` (`EIdentifier` + `EStructLiteral` undefined-name lookups, lines 645–651 / 829–839) now push real diagnostics with the use-site span. Driver renders them as `DIAG <severity> <kind> <span_start>:<span_end> <message>` lines after the existing DEF / SCOPE / RES output, sorted by span start for determinism. Dead `errors.gg` stub (defined `SemanticErrorKind` enum that no one ever imported — pre-existing fossil) deleted. **No regression**: `resolver_comparison` integration test still green — the normalizer at `tests/integration.rs:12308-12324` only extracts DEF + RES lines, so new DIAG lines slot in cleanly. Scope discipline: ONLY the resolver migrated — parser / typechecker / lowerer / lexer remain on the free-form `Vector[String] errors` accumulator; per-stage push-site counts + migration order filed in TODO.md follow-up entry (the original entry on line 168 was rewritten to reflect "POC done, remaining stages").

Modes: `sites` (default, == legacy --show-clones), `verbose` (sites + size_bytes + runtime_fn columns — subsumes the entire --trace-cow TODO scope), `stats` (== legacy --clone-stats), `all` (alias verbose,stats). - [2026-05-17] **backend(llvm): file:line:col panic format parity with C backend.** Mirrors commit `86c08373`'s C-backend pattern in `src/backend/llvm/mod.rs`. Per-instruction `loc` resolved from `block.span_map[idx]` + `module.file_infos` via a local `resolve_panic_loc` helper (kept LLVM-side; C-backend version pre-escapes filenames for C-source interpolation, LLVM version escapes lazily through `llvm_escape_string` at intern time — 10-line difference didn't justify shared abstraction). Sites updated: `Inst::Add/Sub/Mul` overflow trap (via `emit_overflow_check`), `Inst::Div/Rem` signed+unsigned div-by-zero, `Inst::BoundsCheck`, `Inst::DivCheck`, `Inst::Trap`, `Inst::CallExtern` for `gorget_panic` → rewrites to `gorget_panic_at(file, line, col, msg)` with GorgetString → const char* conversion. Pre-interned `"gorget: integer overflow\n"` etc. globals removed (strings now per-callsite, interned lazily via `str_globals.intern`). `@gorget_panic_at(ptr, i32, i32, ptr)` added to `LIBC_BUILTINS` declarations. **Out-of-scope (pre-existing LLVM gaps, NOT stack-traces parity):** LLVM `Shl/Shr` has no shift-count check (poison on overflow), `Div/Rem` signed paths have no INT_MIN/-1 check, `__result_unwrap_error` reads err field without tag check. These mean the two backends differ on *what* panics they emit, not on *how* they format the ones they do — parity for the latter only. Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1058/1058 green. Diff: `src/backend/llvm/mod.rs` +109/-35. Commit `f1d54193`.

- [2026-05-17] **perf(ir/validate): collapse 5 resource-site walks into one (Phase D5 follow-up).** Per Agent A's gir_lower instrumentation findings (commit `3dfc9916`): `lower_module` was running 5 separate resource-site validators (`validate_resource_moves`, `validate_resource_call_args`, `validate_resource_index_reads`, `validate_resource_enum_reads`, `validate_resource_field_reads`) back-to-back, each independently walking every function / block / instruction. All 5 share the unified `validate_read` rule, return the same `ResourceMoveWarning` type, and differ only in their per-instruction extractor — the existing typed `ReadSiteClass` discriminant gives free per-bucket dispatch. New `ResourceSiteFindings` struct + `validate_resource_sites_all` function in `src/ir/validate.rs`, single `time_pass!` block in `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs`. Per-class diagnostic labels (`[resource-moves]`, `[resource-call-args]`, etc.) preserved byte-identically, in the same order as the legacy split-walk path (first-failing panic byte-identical). **Note**: the original task brief said "several validators recompute `Liveness::compute`"; verification showed only `validate_consume_sites` actually does that. The 5 resource-site validators weren't redundantly computing liveness; the consolidation win is from walking once instead of 5 times. **Validator smell flagged for future TODO** (not addressed): `validate_no_null_assign_to_option_slot` (validate.rs:2110) uses name-matching (`name.starts_with("Option__")` etc.) to detect tagged enums — comment acknowledges this is a fallback "until the IR-layer Option/Result wrapper migration in Cluster 1 lands". Per CLAUDE.md "No name matching", layering smell. Plus `validate_move_follow_through` + `validate_drop_pre_rebind` both call `collect_drop_registered_locals(func)` — ~1ms duplicated work, sharable. Speedup measured on LW driver (median of 5 release-profile runs): 5 resource-site walks summed ~7.8ms before → `validate_resource_sites_all` ~1.7ms after (**~75% reduction in this family**, ~15ms total gir_lower phase saving). Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1058/1058 green. Diff: `src/ir/validate.rs` +95, `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs` reshape. Commit `4b529742`.

- [2026-05-17] **loader: parallelise sibling read+parse with rayon.** Per Agent B's profile snapshot, `load_imports` was the top non-forbidden-zone hotspot at 67ms / 8% of LW total compile time. New `ModuleLoader::load_imports_batch` (in `src/loader.rs`) reshapes the per-import iteration: (1) plan serially (resolve path → canonicalize → check `self.loaded` / `self.load_stack`), (2) read sources in PARALLEL via `par_iter`, (3) assign `module_base_offset` serially to keep the offset chain deterministic, (4) parse in PARALLEL with the per-task baked-in offset, (5) post-process serially in plan order so per-child recursion preserves post-order. Recursive serial `load_recursive` stays as the fallback path for builtins (`std.*` / `gg.*`), already-loaded paths, cycle hits, and canonicalize failures. **Key dedup subtlety**: canonicals are inserted into `self.loaded` at *planning* time (not after parsing), so descendants recursed from earlier siblings' subtrees and in-batch duplicate imports both see the canonical as already loaded and don't re-batch it. Order preserved end-to-end (parsed AST spans match the merged source buffer's offsets). Measured (median of 9 runs, post-warm-up): on `self_host_lowerer/driver.gg` (26 imports) baseline 44.6ms → parallel 30.7ms (**~31% saving**); on `self_host_typechecker/driver.gg` 14.9ms → 12.6ms (~16%). Caveat: less than the predicted 40-50ms saving — Docker container with limited CPU count plus the in-batch overhead (planning + serial offset assignment) bound the win. Cargo: rayon 1.10 added. Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1058/1058 green. Diff: `src/loader.rs` +234/-50, `Cargo.toml` +1, `Cargo.lock` +52. Commit `107ab8dc`.

- [2026-05-17] **perf(lir): HashMap→FxHashMap in `propagate_copies` (~20% faster).** Pure type-swap per Agent B's profile snapshot. 6 stdlib HashMap → `rustc_hash::FxHashMap` conversions in `src/lir/optimize.rs::propagate_copies` and its helpers (`param_sources`, `subst`, `removed_params` decls + inits, plus `subst_inst_uses` / `subst_term_uses` / `remove_jump_args_for_removed_params` signatures). Used fully-qualified `rustc_hash::FxHashMap` (matching the existing scoped usage at line 269) to avoid touching top-level imports. Scope discipline: untouched stdlib maps elsewhere in optimize.rs (`OptStats.pass_times`, `find_live_functions` HashSet, `eliminate_common_subexpressions`, HashSets inside `propagate_copies` itself) — flagged as separate larger swaps. Measured on LW driver (3 runs each, median): `propagate_copies` 20.765ms → 16.589ms (**~20%**). Verification: cargo build clean, cargo test --lib 1058/1058 green. Diff: 8 lines, 1 file. Commit `469d7942`.

- [2026-05-17] **perf(lir,backend): retire integration-sweep regression from stack-traces v1 (~46× codegen speedup on LW).** Profile-driven hotspot hunt confirmed the suspect from the stack-traces v1 TODO: `resolve_panic_loc` was called *per LIR instruction* during C emission, doing a linear walk over `file_infos` plus a linear walk over the file's source bytes counting `\n` for every call. On `self_host_lowerer/driver.gg`: 197,119 LIR instructions × ~30 KB source × ~30 files compounded to **6075 ms of codegen** (91% of total compile time), up from ~136 ms pre-regression — a clean +6 s regression on a single heavy fixture. Multiplied across ~600 fixtures the integration sweep paid roughly the +8 min the TODO documented.

  **Two cheap wins, shipped together (~100 LOC across three files):**
  1. **`FileInfo::line_starts`** precomputed at construction (`src/span.rs`). One pass over each file's source at load (~one `Vec<usize>` push per `\n`), then `offset_to_location` binary-searches via `partition_point` instead of a per-call linear walk. O(log n) per lookup, asymptotic win on large files.
  2. **`inst_needs_loc` predicate** in `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs`. The emit loop now skips `resolve_panic_loc` entirely for the 60–70% of instructions that don't emit any inline panic site. Only overflow-checked arithmetic (`Add`/`Sub`/`Mul` with `Overflow::Trap` on signed-int types), integer `Div`/`Rem`/`Mod` (zero / signed-overflow guards), `Shl`/`Shr` (shift-count guards), `BoundsCheck`, `DivCheck`, `Trap`, and `CallExtern` (conservatively included for `gorget_panic` + `unwrap_err` combinator) resolve a loc. Predicate is one typed match — no name matching on instruction names, no sidecar registry, no shape heuristics.

  **Measured speedup on `self_host_lowerer/driver.gg`** (median of 5 release-profile runs):
  - codegen: 6075 ms → **108 ms (~56×)**
  - total compile: 6687 ms → **706 ms (~9.5×)**
  - `hello.gg` (small workload sanity check): no regression — codegen stays sub-1 ms.

  **Estimated saving on full integration sweep**: ~5–8 minutes off the 20-min current → back to roughly the historical 12-min baseline. The bigger codegen savings on LW-class fixtures (~6 s each) compound across the ~10 self-host comparison tests and similar self-host workloads; smaller fixtures save proportionally less but every panic_loc skipped is a `String::clone()` + linear scan avoided.

  **Verification.** Release `cargo build` clean (zero warnings), `cargo test --lib` 1058/1058 green, `cargo test --test integration -- panic_location overflow bounds_check numeric_division panic_builtin test_should_panic coroutine_result_combinators` 14/14 green (proves every `loc`-using inst variant — overflow trap, bounds, div-by-zero, compiler-`gorget_panic`, HOF `unwrap_err`, etc. — still emits a correct `file:line:col` panic message), and `lowerer_comparison` integration test passes (105 s). Parent agent runs the full sweep.

  **Surprises:** the suspect from the TODO was right. The TODO had three candidate wins (1: gate `Block::push_inst` on `span: None`; 2: line-starts; 3: per-block emit-time loc cache). The profile said #1 wasn't the dominant cost — push_inst overhead is amortised inside other phases and didn't show up as a top-N regression target. #2 was a clean win at the function level. #3 wasn't needed because the predicate gate sidestepped the cache: if 95%+ of instructions never look at the loc, caching what you don't compute is free. Ships only #2 + a sharper version of #3 (skip vs cache); skips #1.

- [2026-05-17] **Stack traces on runtime panics v1 shipped.** Runtime panics now print `path/file.gg:LINE:COL: <msg>` instead of the location-less `gorget: <msg>`. Six commits on `gorget-1`:
  - `833ead88` lir(keystone): add `span_map: Vec<Option<Span>>` + `terminator_span: Option<Span>` to `lir::Block` (Stage 1a — 10 LOC, default-init at the sole construction site)
  - `a0343dbe` lir(writer): fill `span_map` at GIR→LIR push sites (Stage 1b — 327 `push_inst` sites, 23 terminator sites, debug-assert in `lower_module` enforces `span_map.len() == insts.len()`)
  - `68cf58de` lir(preserve): keep `span_map` parallel through ssa/drop_elab/optimize/types/split_edges/bir-lower (Stage 1c — 21 mutation sites in `bir/lower.rs` HOF expansion, 5 in `drop_elab`, plus ssa/optimize/types; 3 helpers `push_inst`/`push_synthetic`/`insert_inst` on `Block`)
  - `81c16375` lir,backend: thread `file_infos` for span→loc lookup (Phase 2 — `LirModule.file_infos: Vec<span::FileInfo>` populated by `main.rs`, `span::offset_to_location` helper returns 1-based `(file, line, col)`)
  - `86c08373` backend,runtime: file:line:col on runtime panics (Phase 3 — 14 compiler-side panic emit sites updated: Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Mod/Rem/Shl/Shr overflow + BoundsCheck/DivCheck/Trap + unwrap_err combinator + `__unwrap_err` generated body; `gorget_panic` grown to `gorget_panic_at(file, line, col, msg)` with the old 1-arg wrapper kept for runtime-internal callers that fall back to `<unknown>:0:0`)
  - Plus the scoping commit `a35ea90d` (TODO refile with concrete plumbing inventory after an exploratory agent run)

  **Surprises along the way:**
  - Phase 3 needed **zero existing-fixture updates**. Sweep was 1150/1150 pass on the first try (1149 pre-existing + 1 new `panic_location_overflow.gg`). Fixture assertions on panic stderr were already substring-tolerant (`integer overflow` matches both old and new formats); no fixture asserted on the literal `gorget:` prefix that would have broken.
  - Phase 3 agent went above scope and caught **Inst::Mod (signed + unsigned), Inst::Shl, Inst::Shr** panic sites that weren't in the original 9-site inventory. Right call — same panic class, mechanical to add together.
  - **Four consecutive agents stalled on the integration-test wait** during this work (Agent K Stage 1a, Stage 1c, Phase 2+3 combined, Phase 2 alone). Pattern: agent runs `cargo test --test integration` itself, the ~20-min sweep, then loses the monitor wait → never commits → worktree auto-cleaned. **The revised contract that finally worked: agent commits after `cargo build` + `cargo test --lib` green only, parent drives the integration sweep + fixture loop.** Phase 3 shipped on the first attempt under this rule.
  - Confirmed memory `feedback_multi_agent_worktree_isolation.md` — `isolation: "worktree"` is advisory in this project; agents often write to `/workspace/gorget-1` directly. Pattern was: salvage diffs from the working tree even when the worktree branch was auto-cleaned.

  **Out-of-scope follow-ons filed to TODO.md:**
  - Integration sweep slowdown (~12 min historical → ~20 min current). Phase 1's per-instruction `span_map` plumbing is the suspect. Cheap wins available (specialize `push_inst` for `span: None`, precompute line-start indices in FileInfo, cache `resolve_panic_loc` per block).
  - Runtime-side panic locations (~50+ sites in `c_runtime.rs`). Today fall back to `<unknown>:0:0:` via the `gorget_panic` wrapper. Proper fix needs per-runtime-function span plumbing.
  - LLVM backend parity (LLVM emit path at `src/backend/llvm/mod.rs:6402` et al. still uses the legacy `"gorget: integer overflow\n"` string globals).
  - `caller_location()` builtin + multi-frame stack walking (multi-week, deferred to a future round).

  **Total LOC**: roughly +1100 across LIR plumbing + backend emit + runtime helpers + 1 new fixture. Verification: full integration sweep 1150/1150 pass (1195.90s).

Audited the Vector HOF block per TODO entry: the cited dead `each` entry had already been deleted in commit 1b0e7022 (2026-04-21), making the TODO partly stale. - [2026-05-16] **Gorget-js snag #1 — `&xs.get(i).unwrap()` in a `while` loop silently zeroed the cloned payload.** Pattern `out.push(clone_v(&xs.get(i).unwrap()))` inside a `while` body produced empty `StringV()` for every iteration; the named-local form `JsVal local = xs.get(j).unwrap(); out.push(clone_v(&local))` worked.
