  **Root cause (one writer site, layering rule 2 violation).** `.unwrap()` on `Option__Ref__T` returns `Ptr(T)` (a borrow into the collection element — `_20: *JsVal` in GIR). When that result flows into a `&`-sigil call argument, `lower_call_arg` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs:152`) unconditionally emitted `borrow_mut <local: *T>` → producing `*mut *T`. The callee then reads pointer bits as the payload — for page-aligned pointers, the low int32 bits are zero, so the enum tag reads `StringV(0)` with empty string field. The standalone `Expr::MutableBorrow` handler (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:362`) already had the `is_already_ptr` check that forwards when the inner expression already yields a pointer — but the `lower_call_arg` sibling site (drift-prone duplicate) was missing it.

  Pattern B worked because `&local` where `local: *JsVal` hits the *Identifier* fast-path at `calls.rs:55-75`, which has the `is_already_ptr` check; through copy-propagation the `&local` became a direct forward of the unwrap result pointer. Pattern A had no Identifier — the inner is a method-chain expression — so it fell through to the general MutableBorrow arm, which lacked the check.

  **Fix.** Mirror the `is_already_ptr` check inside `lower_call_arg`'s `Ownership::MutableBorrow` arm (8 LOC). When the inner operand is a plain local (no projections) whose type is already `Ptr`/`MutPtr`, forward the pointer directly instead of taking its address. Matches the standalone `Expr::MutableBorrow` handler — the two sibling sites are now in sync. Filed under "writer-site missing a check" per CLAUDE.md "Debugging heuristic — fix complexity as a signal of wrong layer."

  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/gorget_js_snag_1_unwrap_borrow_in_loop.gg` (the original 4-case minimised repro). Test: `gorget_js_snag_1_unwrap_borrow_in_loop` appended at the end of `tests/integration.rs`. Pattern A and Pattern B now produce identical output. Bootstrap fixed-point unaffected.

- [2026-05-16] **Self-host snag #6 — DictIter / DictDrain `next` failed Tier 2a on resource-typed K or V.** `return Some((!k, !v))` in `DictIter[K, V] with Iterator[(K, V)]` and `DictDrain[K, V] with Iterator[(K, V)]` (lib/std/iter.gg) panicked at consume-site validation when monomorphized to `Dict[String, _]` / `Dict[_, String]` / `Dict[String, String]` — `StructInit(<tuple>, arg #N) of _N : GorgetString : borrowed source consumed at consuming position`. The original hypothesis (writer-tagging miss for generic-extern `T &out` writers) turned out to be wrong: those locals (`_16`, the String slot written by `__dict_iter_value`) were correctly tagged Owned. The actual bug was downstream — `Expr::Move`'s lowering of `!v` creates a fresh Owned temp (`_27 = [Mv] copy _16; move_zero _16`), and then the immediately-following `_28 = tuple_init(copy _26, copy _27)` calls `set_tuple_element_borrow(_27, _28, 1)`, which unconditionally overwrote `_27`'s ownership to `Borrowed { TupleElement }`. The consume validator at the very same `TupleInit` then read the post-overwrite Borrowed state and fired.

  **Root cause (one writer site, layering-discipline rule 1 violation).** `set_tuple_element_borrow` in `src/ir/lowering/context.rs:2124` was lossy on the Owned/FreshOwned/SharedHeap invariant: the upstream `Expr::Move` (exprs/mod.rs:286-287) called `ctx.set_owned` on the move-temp, then `lower_tuple_literal` (exprs/mod.rs:516-521) iterated every droppable elem and clobbered that ownership state to Borrowed. The `BorrowOrigin::TupleElement` tag was meant only as a back-reference for return-path readers (`tuple_element_sources` MoveZero loop in stmts/mod.rs:1741); preserving the Owned tag for already-owned source locals doesn't break that reader (the unconditional `drops.unregister(local)` side effect still transfers drop responsibility to the tuple). Per CLAUDE.md "Debugging heuristic — fix complexity as a signal of wrong layer": this was a five-line writer-side guard, not a multi-case read-side rule.

  **Fix.** `set_tuple_element_borrow` now checks the source's existing ownership and skips the Borrowed-overwrite when it's already Owned / FreshOwned / SharedHeap. `drops.unregister(local)` still runs unconditionally (the tuple takes drop responsibility regardless of source provenance).

  **Workarounds retired.** `dict_keys_lazy.gg` and `dict_values_lazy.gg` lost their "uses Dict[int,int] to dodge the bug" disclaimers; three new resource-typed fixtures exercise the previously-blocked shape directly: `dict_drain_resource.gg` (Dict[String, String] + Dict[int, String]), `dict_keys_lazy_resource.gg` (Dict[String, int]), `dict_values_lazy_resource.gg` (Dict[int, String]). The minimum-repro fixture `snag_6_dict_iter_resource_value.gg` iterates a Dict[int, String] via the `for (k, v)` driver. All four new tests appended at the end of `tests/integration.rs`. Bootstrap fixed-point unaffected.
- [2026-05-16] **Cross-module global initialiser now executes for stdlib-imported `static`/`public` declarations.** `lib/std/math.gg`'s `public float INFINITY = _math_infinity()` was lowered to `GlobalInit::Zeroed` and the underlying global stayed `__lir_g0 = {0}` at module load. The visible behaviour (`INFINITY` reading as `inf`) was masked by a hardcoded `module_constants.insert("INFINITY", F64::INFINITY)` holdout in `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs`; removing the hardcoding revealed the bug as `INFINITY` reading `0.000000`. Two root causes, both upstream of the apparent skip site at the StaticDecl-lowering loop:

  1. **`eval_static_init` returned `Zeroed` for primitive-typed statics with an extern-call initialiser.** The function's dispatch matched literal initialisers and `Named` types only — primitive-typed statics like `float INFINITY = _math_infinity()` short-circuited to `Zeroed`. Fix at the writer: pass `ctx.extern_bindings` into `eval_static_init`, add a primitive-typed extern-call arm that resolves the Gorget callee name to its C symbol (`_math_infinity` → `gorget_math_infinity`) and emits `GlobalInit::Extern { name, args }`. The C backend then emits `__lir_g0 = gorget_math_infinity()` in main()'s init prologue.

  2. **Conditional runtime gate ignored globals.** `emit_runtime_modules` in `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs` scanned `externs` and `CallExtern` instructions for runtime-module inclusion but never looked at `Global::init` Extern names — so `RUNTIME_MATH` wasn't pulled in for programs that only used `gorget_math_infinity` via a global initialiser. Fix: include global Extern init names in the scan; add `gorget_math_` prefix to the math-runtime gate.

  Diagnostic bonus: the `decl.span.start == decl.span.end` skip predicate at the StaticDecl-lowering loop was a sentinel-shape heuristic (CLAUDE.md "no name matching") referencing a long-gone synthetic-stdlib code path. Every stdlib StaticDecl flows through `Parser::new_with_offset` and gets a real span — the predicate is dead and removed. The original TODO description ("the dummy-span shape produced when stdlib statics enter via the import path") was based on stale theory: the real bug is in `eval_static_init`, not the loop predicate.

  Cleanup follow-on: the `INFINITY`/`NAN` hardcoding in `module_constants` (the residual auto-injection holdout from the Snag #29 PI/E/TAU removal) is now gone — `from std.math import INFINITY, NAN` is the single source of truth, completing the Layering rule 3 cleanup. Files touched: `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs` (fix at writer, hardcoding removed, dead span-shape predicate removed), `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs` (conditional runtime gate widened). Fixture: `tests/fixtures/static_init_imported.gg`.

Fix: incremental `name_index: FxHashMap<String, Vec<DefId>>` on `ScopeTable`, maintained alongside `definitions` via the existing `alloc_def` / `define_with_mutability` write sites (2 pushes total). Results: LW semantic 375→190 ms (1.97×), TC 50→24 ms (2.08×), parser_driver 20→11 ms (1.82×), resolver_driver 22→12 ms (1.83×). Total compile time: LW 1033→813 ms (-21%), TC 228→184 ms (-19%). Typecheck on LW also benefited (58→25 ms; it calls `lookup_within_function` too). Architectural cleanup: retired three linear scans over `definitions`. Net diff ~120 LOC across `src/semantic/{mod,scope,safety/mod}.rs` + `src/main.rs` (profile JSON surfacing). Mirrors the drop_elab fix shape exactly: typed sidecar at the right write site, not a downstream cache. Validates: 1054 unit tests + bootstrap_fixed_point + 5 comparison tests (parser/resolver/type/lowerer/check).

- [2026-05-16] **Snag #51 — multi-statement closure body whose last statement is a `match`/`if` used as a tail value silently returned the closure's return-type zero-init default.** Reported by gorget-js with a minimized 4-case repro (`/tmp/snag51/snag51.gg`): int-returning closures returned 0, String-returning closures hit C type mismatch at compile, non-Copy enum-returning closures SIGSEGV'd or hit the type mismatch. The single-stmt closure form (`auto f = (): match x: case _: 1`) worked because it routed through the bare-expression branch that already called `emit_implicit_return`; the multi-stmt form fell into a stale block-tail dispatcher that recognised only `Stmt::Expr` as a tail value.

  **Root cause (three sibling dispatchers had drifted from `lower_block_expr`).** `lower_block_expr` in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:3220` already recognised three tail-value shapes — `Stmt::Expr`, `Stmt::If`, `Stmt::Match` — so regular function bodies were fine. Three sister sites only recognised `Stmt::Expr`:

  1. **Closure body lowering** (`src/ir/lowering/closures.rs::emit_closure_call_function`, the `Expr::Block` arm at line 472). For multi-stmt closure bodies, the trailing match/if got lowered as a regular statement (no tail value), so `LocalId(0)` never received the closure's return value and the function returned its return-slot's zero-init default.

  2. **Closure return-type inference** (`src/ir/lowering/closures.rs::infer_closure_return_type`, the `Expr::Block` arm at line 1013). Mirrored the same gap — registered the closure as `UNIT_TYPE`-returning. The caller's `auto x = mk()` slot landed at unit size, so even when the body did write `LocalId(0)`, the cross-call boundary lost the value.

  3. **If-chain expression result sizing** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs::build_if_chain_expr`). Sized `result_id` at hardcoded `I64_TYPE` with no refinement from branch bodies — the exact bug Snag #29b fixed for `lower_match_stmt_as_expr`. The if-chain version was latent because the only writers of `Stmt::If`-as-tail were `lower_block_expr` (where outer destinations refined naturally) and the snag-#51-broken closure path; with that path fixed, a String-returning closure tail of `if true: "yes" else: "no"` started producing `Str = int64_t` C errors.

  **Also closed: poisoned `expected_type` capture.** `lower_closure` snapshotted `ctx.func_state.expected_type` into `LiftedClosure.expected_type` for Ok/Some-constructor resolution inside the body. For `auto`-typed VarDecls like `auto mk = (...)`, the auto path's `infer_type_from_expr` falls through to `I64_TYPE` for `Expr::Closure` (the closure's concrete type isn't inferable without lowering it first). That polluted I64 propagated to `expected_type` at the VarDecl site, was captured on the LiftedClosure, and at body-lowering time was restored as the body's `expected_type`. `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` then sized its result_local from I64 AND set `result_type_refined = true` (because `expected_type.is_some() && !is_result_wrapper`), short-circuiting refinement from the arm body's actual type. Fix: body-level `expected_type = Some(closure.return_type)` — the closure's own inferred return type, free of outer-context pollution. That makes match-result-local sizing track the closure's body contract, and Ok/Some constructors still resolve correctly when `return_type` is a Result/Option (inferred via existing arms in `infer_closure_return_type`).

  **Structural fix to prevent regression.** The recognised-tail-shapes list now lives in `lower_stmt_as_tail_value` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`, factored out of `lower_block_expr`). Both `lower_block_expr` and the closure-body lowerer dispatch through it. New tail-value shapes touch one site; the two dispatchers can't drift again. The companion `infer_stmt_tail_type` in `closures.rs` plays the same role for the type-inference walker — handles `Stmt::Expr` directly and recurses into `Stmt::Match`/`Stmt::If` branch bodies via existing `infer_closure_return_type`.

  **Family.** Snag #46 / #48 / #49 / #50 were all "value-flow holes at match-as-expression boundaries" with different mechanisms (auto-propagation gaps, sibling-arm name-map leaks). Snag #51 is the closure-body-tail boundary, which none of those reached. The shared shape — block-tail dispatchers must recognise all tail-value shapes — is now enforced by a single helper so a future fourth dispatcher can't silently regress this family of zero-init-default symptoms again. Reporter's "widen the check" instinct was correct in spirit; the fix lives in `closures.rs` + a shared dispatcher, not where #46/#48/#50 patched.

  **Additional MethodCall→enum-variant inference.** Surfaced as a follow-on: `Box.A(...)` parses as `Expr::MethodCall { receiver: Identifier("Box"), method: "A" }`, and `infer_closure_return_type`'s MethodCall arm only handled method calls on values. Added a pre-check: if the receiver is a bare identifier matching a registered named type and isn't a local, treat as qualified enum-variant constructor and return that type. Without this, closure bodies returning `Box.A("payload")` typed as I64 and produced `__gg_Box = int64_t` even after the tail-value fix.

  **Fixture.** `tests/fixtures/snag51_closure_block_tail_value.gg` — 9 cases covering int / String / non-Copy-enum tails via both match and if, plus elif-chain and a control single-stmt case. Wired as `snag51_closure_block_tail_value` in `tests/integration.rs`.

  **Files.** `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` (factor out `lower_stmt_as_tail_value`, fix `build_if_chain_expr` sizing + clone-discipline via `assign_match_arm_to_result`), `src/ir/lowering/closures.rs` (route closure body through shared helper, mirror tail-value inference, drop polluted `expected_type` capture, add MethodCall→enum-variant inference), `tests/fixtures/snag51_closure_block_tail_value.gg` (new), `tests/integration.rs` (+~30 lines).
- [2026-05-16] **stdlib/iter: `Drainable[(K, V)]` / `Drainable[T]` for `Dict[K, V]` / `Set[T]` + lazy `DictKeysIter` / `DictValuesIter`.** Two TODOs closed in one commit. Drain ships via a new runtime helper `gorget_map_drain_entry(map, phys_idx, out_key, out_val)` in `src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs` (+ `gorget_set_drain_entry` thin wrapper): walks the same `order` array as the iter accessors, memcpys K/V out of the bucket at `phys_idx`, tombstones the slot (`states[idx] = 2`, `count--`, `tombstones++`) so the source's normal `gorget_map_free` drop sees `states[i] != 1` and skips the drained entries — no double-free. Returns `int64_t` (1 = drained, 0 = empty / already-tombstoned) so user-space drain iterators can skip empty slots without a separate state lookup. Signature: `const void* m` to match Gorget's `Ref[Dict[K, V]]` / `Ref[Set[T]]` extern-parameter convention; the helper casts to non-const internally (same pattern as `gorget_map_iter_key` which writes through the map's `key_clone` hook). Wired via `collection_void_param_indices` in `src/backend/c_lir/helpers.rs` (`gorget_map_drain_entry` → `&[2, 3]`, `gorget_set_drain_entry` → `&[2]`).

  User-space additions in `lib/std/iter.gg`:
  - `struct DictDrain[K, V] { Dict[K, V] source; int cursor }` + `equip with Iterator[(K, V)]` walking the order array, calling `__dict_drain_entry`, returning `Some((!k, !v))`.
  - `struct SetDrain[T] { Set[T] source; int cursor }` + `equip with Iterator[T]` mirroring the same pattern with `__set_drain_entry`.
  - `equip [K, V] Dict[K, V] with Drainable[(K, V)]: drain(!self) -> DictDrain[K, V]` — consumes via `!self`, drain owns the dict.
  - `equip [T] Set[T] with Drainable[T]: drain(!self) -> SetDrain[T]` — same shape.
  - `struct DictKeysIter[K, V]` / `struct DictValuesIter[K, V]` with `Ref[Dict[K, V]]` borrow fields (same plumbing as `DictIter`), yielding `Option[K]` / `Option[V]`.

Migrating the eager forms would break ~19 fixtures (`Vector[K] ks = d.keys()` pattern); deferred as follow-up.

- [2026-05-16] **Gorget-arena snag #1: `String s = expr as String; s = s + ...` panicked at lowering.** The repro `String s = "x" as String; s = s + "y"; print(s)` failed in two stages: (1) a Tier 2a consume-site violation `AssignIntoOwnedSlot(dst: GorgetString) — untracked source consumed` at the bare-assign Move; (2) once (1) was fixed, the C backend mis-routed the literal cast through `gorget_int_to_str(Str)` and cc rejected the type mismatch.
  **Root cause — two writer-site oversights, one per layer.** (a) `src/ir/tag_ownership.rs::infer_func` didn't tag `Instruction::Cast` destinations as `Owned`. Every other producer (HeapAlloc / Call / CallExtern / FieldLoad / EnumFieldLoad / StructInit / EnumInit / TupleInit / BinOp / UnOp / IndexLoad-Clone / Assign of Str-constant) is listed; `Cast` was missed. The Cast result for `expr as String` is structurally owned (the LIR backend emits a `gorget_str_from_cstr` / `gorget_string_clone` / `gorget_int_to_str` call producing fresh heap data), but the dst stayed `Untracked` and the very next `s = s + …` re-assign Move's source then tripped the AssignIntoOwnedSlot validator. (b) `src/lir/lower/insts.rs`'s Cast-to-String handler computed `src_gir_ty` by matching only scalar `Constant` variants — `Constant::Str(_)` fell through to `None`, so `is_str_source=false`, `is_ptr=false`, and the path took the `gorget_int_to_str(__v0)` fallback. The literal's value at that point IS a `Str` struct (the `Inst::StrLit` lowering shipped during the thin-pointer-string redesign), so the correct route is the `is_str_source` branch (calls `gorget_string_clone(&Str)`).
  **Fix — two writer-site one-liners.** (a) Add `Instruction::Cast { dst, .. } => decisions.push((*dst, LocalOwnership::Owned))` to the producer-walk match in `tag_ownership.rs:245-247`. The `apply_decision` `needs_drop` gate filters scalar casts (int→float etc.) so this is sound by construction. (b) Add `let is_str_literal = matches!(value, Operand::Constant(Constant::Str(_))); let is_str_source = is_str_source || is_str_literal;` to `insts.rs:277-279` so string-literal sources take the existing `gorget_string_clone(&Str)` branch.
  **Per CLAUDE.md "Debugging heuristic — fix complexity as a signal of wrong layer":** both were classic write-site oversights. Diagnosis was localised by tracing the data the validator read (Untracked → produced by Cast → producer-walk doesn't tag Cast) and the C emit error (gorget_int_to_str(Str) → Constant-arm doesn't list Str → fallback path).
  **Fixture.** `tests/fixtures/arena_snag_1_as_string_owned.gg` — the user's minimal repro (4 lines), expected stdout `xy`. Wired in `tests/integration.rs::arena_snag_1_as_string_owned`.
  Files: `src/ir/tag_ownership.rs` (+12 lines incl. comment), `src/lir/lower/insts.rs` (+13 lines incl. comment), `tests/fixtures/arena_snag_1_as_string_owned.gg{,.expected}`, `tests/integration.rs` (+24 lines wire + comment). Test status: 1050 lib pass; full integration sweep below.

- [2026-05-16] **`drop_elab` SlotStates switched from `HashMap<SlotId, InitState>` to dense `Vec<InitState>` — 18-21× speedup, 64% off total compile on Lowerer.** After per-pass timing in `OptStats` (commit `8a4d7623`) revealed `drop_elaboration` consuming 92-98% of `lir_optimize` wall time across self-host driver workloads, the suspect was the hashmap dataflow state cloned per block-visit in `forward_dataflow`'s worklist + once more in `elaborate_block`. `InitState` is a 3-variant enum (1 byte with `#[repr(u8)]`), slot counts run 20-100, so the storage shape was pure constant-factor cost — `HashMap` allocator/hasher dance vs `Vec<u8>` memcpy.
  **Change.** `type SlotStates = HashMap<SlotId, InitState>` → `Vec<InitState>` indexed by `SlotId.0 as usize`. Pre-sized once per function to `func.slots.len()` (slot count is stable through phases 1+2; phase 3's `add_slot` only adds AFTER dataflow has finished and only writes to the pre-captured `bb0_in_state` Vec, never re-runs dataflow). `meet_states` becomes a linear scan over two byte slices (auto-vectorizable; equality is `Vec::eq`). `Option<SlotStates>` retained at the outer layer to keep "unreachable block / no predecessor processed yet" Top semantics 1:1. New `slot_state(&SlotStates, SlotId) -> InitState` helper preserves the `MaybeInitialized` fallback for out-of-bounds reads (matches prior `HashMap::get(...).unwrap_or(MaybeInitialized)`).
  **Measurement** (3-run median, release):

  | Workload | Before drop_elab | After drop_elab | Speedup | Total compile |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | self_host_typechecker driver | 253 ms | 14 ms | 18× | 591 ms → 212 ms (−64%) |
  | self_host_lowerer driver | 2751 ms | 130 ms | 21× | 3647 ms → 956 ms (−74%) |

  **Validation.** `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --lib` 1050/1050 pass; `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` pass (270s); smoke set (`drop_ ownership_ resource_ closure_ collection_`) 69/69 pass; full integration 1117 pass + 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (`fstring_cross_module_callee`, fixture from commit `d1cae03d` not in this branch's lineage; verified failing identically on stashed baseline).
  Files: `src/lir/drop_elab.rs` (+62/−32 lines, well within the 150-LOC budget the task spec called out).

- [2026-05-16] **Self-host: lowerer reads typechecker-inferred method-call return types via `gmod.tc_types.expr_types` side-table (Gap #2 Phase 3).** Closes the explicit-targs half of gap #2: `iter_lazy_adapters.gg` (uses `.take_while[bool(int)]`, `.drop_while[bool(int)]`, `.filter_map[…]`, `.inspect[…]`) and `iter_chain_past_one_step.gg` now emit zero diagnostics in stage-1 output (previously 4 and ≥1 respectively). The remaining 5 iter-family fixtures with diagnostics are composite generics with Tuple type args — they need discovery extension to `EMethodCall.targs`, filed as a follow-on TODO.

  **Architecture.** Three coordinated pieces on top of Phase 1+2 (the side-table + ResolvedType translator):

  - **`GirModule.tc_types` and `.tc_scopes`** (in `gir.gg`): read-only references stashed at lower_module entry so downstream lowering passes that hold `&gmod` can query per-expression resolved types without threading two extra args through every signature in the call chain.
  - **`infer_expr_type` writes to `types.expr_types` at the trait-registry-resolved EMethodCall arm** (in `infer.gg` line ~352): targeted recording, not a global wrapper — the wrapper-based variant I prototyped cost ~100s on self-host's own source (≈1M expression nodes × Dict.put). Self-host today writes at ONE site; Rust gg writes at ~10 sites (`src/semantic/typecheck.rs`). Extend recording per new lowerer query site.
  - **EMethodCall in `lower_expr` consults the side-table** (in `lower.gg` line ~2427): ordered (1) fn_sigs (Option B's pre-pass — fast, authoritative); (2) `lookup_expr_gir_type(sexpr, &gmod)` (Phase 3 — covers method-generic calls); (3) `infer_method_return_type` (name-based heuristic last resort). The (2)-before-(3) ordering is architecturally correct: the typechecker is the single source of truth for resolved expression types (Layering rule 3).

  **Why a sidecar Dict instead of a typed field on SpannedExpr.** This faithfully mirrors Rust gg's `expr_types: FxHashMap<Span, TypeId>` (`src/semantic/mod.rs:51`, `src/semantic/typecheck.rs:407`). The architecturally cleaner shape would put `int resolved_type` on `SpannedExpr` itself — see TODO entry "extend tc_types.expr_types write-through … consider span-keyed-sidecar replacement". Span-keyed lookups are fragile in principle (we've been bitten by span-collision bugs in `resolution_map`); they're protected today by per-module offset shifting in `loader.gg`. Worth pioneering a typed-field replacement if a collision bug surfaces or Rust agrees to migrate in lockstep.

  **The `RTRef` translator rule.** `resolved_to_gir_type` translates the typechecker's `RTRef(T)` to bare `T` (not `Ptr[T]`). The typechecker models borrow-vs-owned in the ResolvedType; self-host's GIR models the same distinction on `GirLocal.ownership` (`LoBorrowed` / `LoOwned`). Wrapping in a GIR pointer here would double-encode and break the existing name-based heuristic for `.get(i).unwrap()`-style collection getters (caught the first try — bootstrap regressed; fix landed before commit).

  **Test deadlines bumped 300s → 600s** (`tests/integration.rs`: 4 sites — stage-0 driver in both bootstrap tests + stage-1→2 + stage-2→3). The 300s deadline was already flaky under parallel cargo-test load; Phase 3's added cost is negligible (262s solo user-time, same as baseline) but pushed wall-clock past 300s when 4 tests share CPU.

  **Verified.** `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` → 1124/1124 passing in 1207s. All 5 self-host comparisons green. Bootstrap_fixed_point + self_host_bootstrap green.

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/gir.gg` (+~15 lines). `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (+~50 lines). `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/infer.gg` (+~10 lines). `tests/integration.rs` (+~10 lines: deadline bumps).

- [2026-05-16] **Snag #50 — outer-match scrutinee reads as zero-init default inside an inner-match arm when a sibling un-taken arm borrows it.** Match-as-expression lowering paths (`lower_match_expr` and `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`) iterated over arm bodies WITHOUT per-arm save/restore of `func_state.locals` — unlike `lower_match_stmt` (statement-match in `stmts/patterns.rs`) which has had it since the original Snag #8 / #41 fixes. When an arm body contained `&v` on a non-Copy bare-Ptr param, the CoW `cow_before_mutation` materialized a fresh owned clone and rebound the name `v` to the new local. The rebind leaked into the SIBLING arm's body lowering — that arm's `v` reference resolved to the dead arm's materialized local (only initialized along the un-taken path), which read back as the type's zero-init default (`Undefined`, tag=0 in the reporter's `JsValue` enum).

  **Original site.** gorget-js's `src/eval.gg::stringify_thrown` (the uncaught-throw formatter). Observable symptom: every uncaught `Test262Error` printed as "Test262Error: undefined" regardless of the actual message — because `this` inside `Error.prototype.toString` was Undefined instead of the Error object. Minimized to `/tmp/snag49/snag49.gg` by the gorget-js agent (under that name — the snag was then renumbered to #50 since it's not in the auto-propagation family).

  **Trigger.** Seven distinct conditions; removing any one makes the bug disappear. (1) Enum has a non-Copy variant — makes the enum non-Copy. (2) Function parameter `v` of that enum type. (3) Outer `match v: case Variant(_):` wildcard. (4) Inside the arm: throws-fn call bound via match-on-Result. (5) Inner match has ≥ 2 arms. (6) Un-taken sibling arm declares `<T> c = clone_fn(&v)`. (7) Taken arm reads `v` by-value. The throws-call requirement is incidental — it's the typical shape that puts the inner match inside an arm body block where the trailing match becomes the block's tail expression, routing through `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` instead of `lower_match_stmt`.

  **Why the bug doesn't fire in statement-form match.** `lower_match_stmt` in `stmts/patterns.rs` uses `ctx.save_locals(...)` / `ctx.restore_locals(...)` around each arm body. `lower_match_expr` and `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` in `exprs/mod.rs` didn't, because the expression-match was originally added without the snapshot/restore discipline that the statement form already had for Snag #8 (drop-flag leak) and Snag #41 (mark_moved leak). Same architectural shape, three different leaks; this one specifically about the name-binding map.

  **Fix.** Add per-arm snapshot/restore of `ctx.func_state.locals` (the name→local map) in both expression-match paths and in the `else` branch. Mirrors the statement-match form but DOESN'T use the full `save_locals` / `restore_locals` pair — that would also rewind `builder.locals[i].ownership`, clobbering the `set_owned(result_local)` that `assign_match_arm_to_result` performs (Snag #31's invariant — `result_local`'s `Owned` tag must survive the arm boundary for the merge-bb's downstream `[Mv] user_var = copy result_local` to pass the AssignIntoOwnedSlot validator). Only the name map is snapshotted; ownership state stays.

  **Regression fixture.** `tests/fixtures/snag50_match_as_expr_arm_locals_leak.gg` — verbatim from the reporter's minimization, expecting `v=object` in the Function arm body.

  **Tests.** 1051 unit tests pass. snag50 + all 15 sibling snag fixtures pass (`cargo test --test integration snag` returns 16/16). Full integration suite passes — the c_emit_comparison / self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point timeouts observed during the full-run validation were under heavy multi-agent host contention; both pass in isolation (`self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` clocks ~512s alone vs ~200s nominal per CLAUDE.md).

- [2026-05-15] **Snag #49 family closed — Result→T auto-propagation centralized at the `lower_expr` exit (producer-side).** The "consumer-site whack-a-mole" class that produced Snag #43 (call args), Snag #46 (constructor args), and Snag #48 (match scrutinees) had a non-empty remaining surface (for-loop iter, if/while conditions, index expressions). The principled fix from the TODO entry — plumb `expr_types` through monomorphization — is a deeper change deferred to a future session. Took the partial-fix path the TODO calls out: **producer-side centralization at `lower_expr`**, gated to `Call` / `MethodCall` expressions only.

  **Mechanism.** New one-shot `FunctionState::suppress_auto_prop` flag (`src/ir/lowering/context.rs`). `lower_expr` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`) consumes the flag at entry, lowers the expression, and — when the expression is a `Call` or `MethodCall` and suppression wasn't requested — applies `maybe_auto_propagate` at the tail. The `is_producer` filter is the key bit: firing the hook on every `lower_expr` would over-fire on method receivers like `body_r.unwrap()` (the receiver MUST stay `Result` for the `.unwrap()` to dispatch correctly). Restricting to Call/MethodCall mirrors the existing call-only auto-prop pattern.

  **Why "only Call / MethodCall."** Auto-propagation is a *producer* transformation: the throws-sugar is what synthesizes the unwrap. An `Identifier` whose binding happens to be `Result[T,E]`, or a field-access whose object is `Result`-typed, are not candidates — they're not "fresh out of a call." Reaching those cases requires the typechecker's `expr_types` plumbing (the deferred principled fix). For now the seven residual consumer-side `maybe_auto_propagate` calls (`stmts/assigns.rs:112`, `stmts/mod.rs:129/317/1422`, `calls.rs:151/1030/1065/1206`, `methods.rs:224`, `exprs/mod.rs:1788/1823/1854`, and the match-scrutinee non-call fallback) stay as safety nets for the `Identifier`-of-Result case. The match-scrutinee site also keeps `arms_match_result_or_option_*` because user-written `Ok/Error/Some/None` discrimination is now signaled to the centralized hook by setting `suppress_auto_prop = true` before `lower_expr`.

  **Suppression sites.** Three callers of `lower_expr` set the one-shot before invoking it: (a) `lower_match_expr` / `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` / `lower_match_stmt` when arm patterns are `Ok/Error/Some/None`; (b) `lower_rethrow_expr`'s inner expression (operates on the raw `Result`); (c) `lower_catch_expr`'s inner expression (extracts Ok/binds Error from the raw `Result`). The flag is one-shot — consumed at the next `lower_expr` entry — so nested sub-expressions auto-prop normally.

  **Typechecker companions.** Three new auto-prop gates so the new producer-side cases actually surface to IR-lowering (without them the typechecker rejects `if throws_fn():` etc. with a type mismatch before IR ever sees the expression): `Stmt::If` / `Stmt::While` condition (`Result[bool, E]` → `bool`), `Stmt::If` elif condition (same), `Expr::Index` index (`Result[K, E]` → `K` for str/Vector/Dict/HashMap indexing). Each skips the strict `unify` step when `is_auto_propagation_compatible(expected, found)` returns true — mirroring the existing call-arg / VarDecl / Return gates.

  **Index-expression boundary clear.** `lower_index_access` now `take()`s `expected_type` before lowering object / index. Without this, the outer destination type (e.g. `Result[int, E]` from `return v[throws_fn()]`) would leak through, the hook would see a Result destination, and the index slot would hold the bytes of the unwrapped Result struct rather than an int — the runtime symptom that broke `snag49c_throws_index` at first.

  **Fixtures.** Four new fixtures cover the holdouts named in the TODO: `snag49a_throws_for_iter` (for-loop iterable), `snag49b_throws_if_cond` (if condition), `snag49c_throws_index` (index expression), `snag49d_throws_while_cond` (while condition).

  **Litmus test status (`grep -r maybe_auto_propagate src/ir/lowering/`).** Goal: (a) one at `lower_expr` exit, (b) zero elsewhere. Achieved: (a) yes, plus the suppression flag plumbing. (b) seven residual calls remain as Identifier-of-Result safety nets. The TODO entry is demoted to track that retirement work pending the `expr_types` plumbing.

  **Tests.** 1051 unit tests pass. Integration suite passes 1124/1124 (deterministic run); 1119/1120 with one flaky `vector_task_get` race that passes in isolation — unrelated to this change (shared-counter timing under contended multi-agent host).

- [2026-05-15] **Import aliasing: `from X import Y as Z`.** Parser extends the `from X import …` list to accept optional `as Z` after each name. AST: `ImportName { name: Spanned<String>, alias: Option<Spanned<String>> }` replaces the prior bare `Spanned<String>` element type of `ImportStmt::From.names`. Resolver registers the alias-or-source name as the `DefKind::Import` placeholder, then a post-merge fixup pass rebinds `Z` to the `Y`-DefId once `Y`'s real def is in scope. A new `rewrite_import_aliases` pass walks the entry-file AST and renames `Expr::Identifier(Z)` / `Expr::Path { head: Z }` / `Type::Named { Z }` back to `Y` so the IR backend (which lowers calls by surface name) emits references to the real C symbol. Symmetric collision check still fires when a user-written def collides with the alias placeholder. Closes the gorget-js critique gap: `from std.math import sin as msin` lets a user keep `int my_sin()` (or even just a `sin` local) without globally renaming. Commit `12451e39`.

- [2026-05-15] **Module-level wildcard imports: `from X import *`.** Parser accepts bare `*` after `import` (must be the only item — no mixing with named or glob imports). New `wildcard: bool` field on `ImportStmt::From`. Resolver adds a fourth top-level pass that, for each wildcard import, looks up the source module's `FileModule` scope and rebinds each name into the importing scope via the new `bind_wildcard` method. The existing `export_non_private` pass already hoists public names from imported modules to the parent (Module) scope as a side effect of loading, so the wildcard pass is mostly a no-op semantically today — but it's there so the unused-import check treats wildcards as exercised and so the rule still works if `export_non_private` ever gets tightened. The path-based loader already loads the target module from the `path` field, no loader changes needed. Closes the prerequisite for self-host unification (the five self-host programs use symlinks today because every shared symbol previously needed an explicit name). Commit `0cc1b1a8`.

- [2026-05-15] **`borrowed` qualifier for extern return types (parser + AST + IR metadata; auto-clone consumer split off).** Original TODO from 2026-04-03; the original entry's intent is now half-shipped — see the live TODO entry filed today for the remaining work. What landed: `extern borrowed T f(...)` parses, `FunctionDef.returns_borrowed: bool` threads through `finish_function_def`, `ExternDecl.returns_borrowed: bool` is on the IR struct, and the lowering pass populates a typed `Module.fn_returns_borrowed: FxHashSet<String>` sidecar keyed by both Gorget name and bound C symbol (rule 3 — single source of truth; rule 2 — typed sidecar, not name matching). `borrowed` is parsed as a contextual identifier only in extern-fn-decl position, so it's still a valid regular identifier everywhere else. What's split off: the call-site auto-clone insertion in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs` was out of scope for this branch (parallel agent work on the same file), filed as a follow-on TODO. Until that lands, `borrowed`-tagged externs parse and the metadata flows, but the runtime behaviour matches a bare `extern T f(...)` — the buffer's lifetime is still the FFI's responsibility at the call site. Fixture exercises the parser path with a primitive `int` return so the test doesn't depend on the auto-clone being wired. Commit `7faf63b6`.

- [2026-05-15] **LIR value origin metadata — Phase D6 complete.** All five origin bitmaps the C backend used to maintain locally (`str_lit_vals`, `null_vals`, `cstr_vals` / `extern_cstr_return_vals`, `func_addr_targets`, `spawn_source_fn`) are retired. The replacement is a single typed sidecar `LirFunction.value_origins: Vec<Option<ValueOrigin>>` populated by `compute_module_value_origins` in `src/lir/types.rs`. The `ValueOrigin` enum carries `StrLit`, `NullPtr`, `CStr { from_extern }`, `FuncAddr(FuncId)`, `SpawnSource(String)`. Producer sites: `Inst::StrLit` → `StrLit`; `Inst::NullPtr` → `NullPtr`; `Inst::FuncAddr { func }` → `FuncAddr(func)`; `Inst::CallExtern` with `ret_abi == AbiKind::CStr` → `CStr { from_extern: true }`; `Inst::CallExtern { name: "__gorget_spawn_X" }` whose return got reshaped from Task struct → `SpawnSource("X")`. Consumer sites: `EmitContext::is_str_lit / is_null / is_cstr / is_cstr_extern / spawn_source` typed accessors read the sidecar via `match`. Used at 70+ emit-decision sites across `src/backend/c_lir/{mod,emit_types,emit_call_extern,helpers}.rs`. The lifts that the typed metadata unblocked (Store routing for null-fill vs aggregate-memcpy, SlotStore Str/GorgetString/cstr coercion, Call/CallPtr ABI coercion) are all done. Shipped across commits `ee8d1662` (LIR producer), `fabdd13e` (C backend consumer migration), `7bcf53c7` (retirement of parallel bitmaps from EmitContext). The doc references to bitmap names that remain in `src/lir/mod.rs:418-420` and `src/lir/mod.rs:1254-1256` are descriptive history of what was replaced, not live state.

- [2026-05-15] **C backend: seed val_types / ptr_pointee from func.value_types / func.pointee_types (partial closure of "migrate val_types to func.value_types").** The LIR-canonical typed sidecars (`func.value_types`, `func.pointee_types`, populated by `compute_module_value_types` / `compute_module_pointee_types` in `src/lir/types.rs`) are now the single source of truth for these axes. The C backend reads them as the seed for its local `val_types` and `ptr_pointee` tables; backend-specific fixups (CallExtern→SlotStore mismatch, guard accessor inference from consumers, cross-type combinator, consumer-driven back-propagation, InlineC→SlotStore) layer on top of the seed rather than re-deriving from instructions. Two companion changes shipped to make the seed sound:

  1. **Compute order: pointee_types FIRST, value_types SECOND.** Previously `compute_module_value_types` ran before `compute_module_pointee_types`, so the shared `infer_inst_type` couldn't consult the pointee table for the `Inst::Load { ty: Void }` fallback the C backend's local pass had. Switching the order lets the shared inference fall back through pointee_types exactly like the local pass did, eliminating one of the reasons the C backend kept its own pass. `infer_inst_type` gained a `pointee_types: &[Option<LirType>]` parameter.

  2. **C backend `Inst::Store` routing: separate `FuncRef` from `Ptr`.** Before this work the C backend's local `infer_inst_type` (in `c_lir/helpers.rs`) had no case for `Inst::NamedFuncAddr`, so values from those instructions were typed `None` and the Store routing fell through to the struct-by-value branch (`memcpy(p, &val, sizeof(val))`). Once the shared seed started tagging them as `FuncRef` (the shared `infer_inst_type` has the case), the Ptr branch grabbed them and emitted `memcpy(p, val, sizeof(*(val)))` — UB for void* source. Added a dedicated FuncRef branch upstream of the Ptr one in the C backend's Store handler. Per CLAUDE.md's debugging heuristic, the fix is at the reader, not at the writer — but it was unblocked by the writer (shared seed) becoming richer.

  Files touched: `src/lir/types.rs` (infer_inst_type signature + Load Void fallback), `src/main.rs` (5 call sites: pre-BIR + post-BIR, lex/parse/check/build/run paths), `src/lir/integration.rs` (test pipeline), `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs` (seed + Store FuncRef routing). Commit `7ee48098`. Tested: `cargo test --test integration -- --test-threads=4` — 1127/1127.

  Remaining work in the original TODO entry: the C backend still maintains the local pass (post-seed) because it does several things the shared inference cannot — CallExtern→SlotStore slot-type override, guard accessor inference from consumers (looks at next 10 instructions for the consumer that reveals the type), cross-type Option/Result map combinator override, consumer-driven Add/Cmp peer-type back-propagation, InlineC→SlotStore inference, Ret-from-function backfill. These are genuinely backend-specific augmentations and they don't yet have a clean upstream home. Pushing them upstream is a separate cluster of work — each augmentation involves cross-instruction reasoning that the shared pass would have to grow capability for.

- [2026-05-15] **Snag #48 — `match <throws-fn-call>(): case Variant(x): x …` read the variant payload as the enum's discriminant tag.** Same family as Snag #46 (constructor-arg position): the call's `Result[T, E]` operand wasn't auto-propagated at the match-scrutinee boundary, so pattern condition / extraction read Result's layout as if it were T. With variant-carries-int → returns 0; variant-carries-bool → returns false; variant-carries-String → compile error (int64_t → Str type clash that the C compiler catches). Discovered by gorget-js's `eval.gg` native_call nid 7 (Object.prototype.toString reading [[Class]]) after Phase 9 made `member_lookup` itself `throws RuntimeException`.

  **Root cause.** Three match-lowering sites all lowered the scrutinee via `lower_expr` without calling `maybe_auto_propagate`: `lower_match_expr` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`), `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` (same file), `lower_match_stmt` (`src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs`). The sibling call-arg / constructor-arg paths do call `maybe_auto_propagate`. Same gap shape as Snag #43 / Snag #46.

  **First-try over-fired**. Naive "auto-propagate every Result-typed scrutinee in throws context" broke 3 fixtures: `snag31_match_arm_move_into_owned`, `snag41_match_scrutinee_consume`, `nested_match_return_from_inner_arm`. All three are the canonical `Completion c = match risky_call(): case Ok(x): … case Error(e): return Error(e)` shape — user-written Result discrimination, NOT throws-sugar. Auto-prop would discard the very Ok/Error split the user wrote arms for.

  **Gate**. Added `arms_match_result_or_option_arm` / `arms_match_result_or_option_item` helpers (`src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs`) that detect when any arm pattern is `Ok(...)` / `Error(...)` / `Some(...)` / `None` (or the fully-qualified `Result.Ok` / `Option.Some` forms). When set, the scrutinee stays as-is (no auto-prop) so the explicit Result/Option discrimination works. Otherwise (e.g. `case Tagged.NumberV(n):` — patterns against a user-defined enum's variants), apply `maybe_auto_propagate` after `lower_expr`. The check is name-based on the prelude variants because the typechecker's resolved `expr_types` map isn't plumbed to IR-lowering — same pragmatic shape as elsewhere in IR-lowering when the typed signal hasn't been wired.

  **expected_type handling**. Match scrutinee's surrounding `expected_type` (e.g. `int x = match …`) describes the MATCH RESULT slot, not the scrutinee. Without clearing it, a Result-typed surrounding context (`Result[T,E] r = match …`) would block auto-prop via `maybe_auto_propagate`'s skip-on-Result-destination heuristic. Save+clear `expected_type` around the `maybe_auto_propagate` call, restore after. Only applies on the non-Result-pattern path.

  **Three sites patched** (same shape, different AST signatures for `MatchArm` vs `MatchItem`):
  - `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs::lower_match_expr` (path for `T x = match …`)
  - `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs::lower_match_stmt_as_expr` (path for nested `match …:` inside an arm-body block)
  - `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs::lower_match_stmt` (statement form; only non-identifier scrutinee branch — identifier scrutinees bind an already-named local where auto-prop already fired at the VarDecl boundary, which is the `Tagged t = throws_fn(); match t:` workaround that always worked)

  **Regression fixture.** `tests/fixtures/snag48_throws_match_scrutinee.gg` wired in `tests/integration.rs::snag48_throws_match_scrutinee`. Cases A (inline String) + B (inline int) + C (inline bool) + D/E/F (local-bound workaround) all pass.

  **Architectural follow-up.** Producer-side centralization (apply auto-prop at `lower_call` instead of N consumer sites) would eliminate ~80% of the mole-whacking but the match-scrutinee gate would still be needed (the consumer's typed context is what differentiates `case Ok(x)` from `case Tagged.X(x)`). The principled fix is plumbing the typechecker's `expr_types` to IR-lowering so every consumer can read the semantic-type-vs-IR-type delta and auto-prop accordingly. See TODO entry.

  Files: `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs` (+50 lines: 2 helper fns + `pattern_is_result_or_option` private + gate in `lower_match_stmt`), `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` (+30 lines: gate in `lower_match_expr` + `lower_match_stmt_as_expr`), `tests/fixtures/snag48_throws_match_scrutinee.gg` (new, ~130 lines from gorget-js's repro), `tests/integration.rs` (+45 lines). Verified post-rebase on main: 1051 unit + 1124 integration tests pass (was 1123; +1 for the new regression).

- [2026-05-15] **Self-host: generic struct templates from imported modules are now merged into the lowerer's view, closing the `[bug] EFieldAccess` on mono'd iter structs.** Closes iter-chain gap #1. `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg`'s IStruct case previously gated merging on `sdef.type_params.len() == 0`, so `struct VectorIter[T]`, `struct VectorDrain[T]`, `struct TakeIter[Iter, T]`, etc. from `lib/std/iter.gg` never reached `m.items`. The downstream `lower_module` struct_templates collector (already iterating m.items for type_params > 0) consequently missed them, and the mono'd-fields pass at line ~6100 had nothing to monomorphize — so `VectorIter__int64_t.source` / `.idx` field access fell into the `[bug] EFieldAccess: unknown field` placeholder.

  **Fix.** A `else:` branch in the loader's IStruct match arm: merge generic struct templates into `m.items` without the `__imported_type__` flag (since the Rust preamble doesn't emit mono'd struct bodies — self-host has to emit them itself). The existing `lower_module` machinery does the rest unchanged: struct_templates collector picks up the templates, generic discovery finds the type instances (via Option B's transitive-equip walk), and the mono-fields pass registers `VectorIter__int64_t.source: Vector__int64_t`, `.idx: int64_t`, etc. into `type_infos`.

  **Verified end-to-end.** `auto_iter_test.gg` (zero imports, uses `for x in v.drain():`) now emits zero `[bug] EFieldAccess` diagnostics in stage-1 output (previously 10+ across VectorIter/VectorDrain/ChainIter). `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` → 1123/1123 passing in 1208s. All 5 self-host comparisons green.

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg` (+10/-0).

- [2026-05-15] **Self-host snag #5: `Type it = expr` parser ambiguity fixed — `it` now accepted as a binding name in var-decl position.** The original framing (Rust-stage codegen miscompile of `Vector[Item]` match) traced to a parser-level misparse: `Item it = m.items.get(i).unwrap()` silently split into two statements (an expr stmt `Item` + an assignment `it = …`) because `it` is the implicit-closure-parameter keyword (`Token::Keyword(Keyword::It)`), and `parse_decl_or_expr_stmt` (in `src/parser/stmt.rs:649`) gated the binding name on `matches!(p.peek(), Token::Identifier(_))`. The downstream lowerer then emitted a unit-typed local with elided initializer — `_6: unit; _6 = const unit` — and the match's `enum_field_load _6, IStruct, 0` read garbage offsets out of the unit slot, producing `__s8 = items.cap` storing an int64 into a `__gg_StructDef`-typed slot. The "called from `load_imports`" / "compiles when not called" framing was misleading: the call activation only mattered because dead-code elimination kept the broken helper alive when reachable. Fix in `src/parser/stmt.rs`: accept `Token::Keyword(Keyword::It)` as a binding name once a type has been parsed (unambiguous in this position). With the parser fix, `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg` now factors the auto-load check into `should_auto_load_std_iter(m)` + three top-level-match-on-Item helpers as the idiomatic shape demands, retiring the inlined workaround in `load_imports`. Verified: cargo test --test integration --release 1123/1123 passing in 1057s. Self-host bootstrap_fixed_point green. New parser regression test `test_var_decl_with_it_binding` in `src/parser/tests.rs`.

- [2026-05-15] **Self-host: `std.iter` auto-import shipped — zero-import iter-chain fixtures now reach the lowerer with stdlib equips visible.** Closes gap #1 from the post-Option-B iter-chain work. Mirrors `src/loader.rs:115` (`module_should_auto_load_std_iter`). With this in `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg::load_imports`, a fixture like `stdlib_iter_drain.gg` (zero imports — relies on auto-load) now triggers `std.iter` load, populating `equip_templates` / `equip_generic_names` so the Option B fn_sigs + transitive-discovery foundation actually fires. Verified end-to-end: a `for x in v.drain():` fixture now monomorphizes `VectorIter[int]` / `VectorDrain[int]` / their `next()` / `iter()` cascades AND `ChainIter[VectorIter, VectorIter, int]` (chain of iter()s) discovered transitively.

  **Implementation shape.** Three pieces in `loader.gg`: (1) `name_is_iter_marker(String)` — the marker-name list (`Iterator`, `Iterable`, `VectorIter`, `MapIter`, …); (2) recursive AST mention-detectors (`type_mentions_iter` / `expr_mentions_iter` / `stmt_mentions_iter` / `block_mentions_iter` / `function_mentions_iter`); (3) an **inlined** check at the top of `load_imports` that walks `m.items`, sets three flags (`already_imports_iter`, `shadows_vec_iter`, `mentions_iter`), and pushes `"std.iter"` into `import_paths` when the auto-load conditions are met.

  **Why inlined.** Factoring the entry-point check into `bool should_auto_load_std_iter(Module m)` triggered a Rust-stage codegen miscompile of the helper's `Vector[Item]` match: in the called function's C, `__s8 = items.cap` (length read) gets stored into a `__gg_StructDef`-typed slot, producing the C type-mismatch error chain. The bug requires the full `loader.gg` context — a standalone `.gg` file with the same pattern compiles fine. Filed as Self-host snag #5 in TODO.md with full repro instructions. The factored helpers that don't top-level-match-on-Item (the type/expr/stmt mention detectors) DO compile correctly when called transitively from inlined code, so they stay factored.

  **What this unblocks vs what's still gated.** Auto-import now fires for any module mentioning `Iterator` / `.iter()` / `.drain()` / `VectorIter` / etc., as long as `std.iter` isn't already imported and `VectorIter` isn't user-shadowed. The mono'd iter structs (`VectorIter__int64_t`, `VectorDrain__int64_t`, `ChainIter__…`) now get discovered transitively (Option B's machinery). Remaining gap: their **field metadata** isn't registered because the loader's IStruct case still skips generic struct templates — `self.source` / `self.idx` field access on those mono'd structs emits `[bug] EFieldAccess: unknown field`. That's TODO gap #1 (now sole remaining iter-chain gap).

  **Verified.** `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` → 1123/1123 passing in 1064s. All 5 self-host comparisons green. Bootstrap_fixed_point green. The change is purely additive: existing fixtures get an extra `std.iter` load when they mention iter-related names but didn't before; no semantics change for fixtures that already imported it.

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg` (+~380 lines: helpers + inlined auto-load block; one import-list extension to bring in `SpannedExpr` / `SpannedType` / `Stmt` / `Expr` / etc.).

- [2026-05-15] **Self-host: mono'd generic-equip methods now register in `fn_sigs`, and transitive discovery follows their return types + bodies.** Closes the foundational half of "Option B — register trait-equipped methods in fn_sigs so iter-chain return types resolve correctly." Two coordinated additions in `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg::lower_module`:

  **Part 1 — fn_sigs pre-pass for mono'd generic equip methods.** Inserted right after the existing mono'd-function fn_sigs registration (lines ~6121-6135). For each `GenericInstance` whose `base_name` is in `equip_generic_names`, find the matching `equip_templates` entries and write each method's mono'd return type into `gmod.fn_sigs` under the `<MonoTarget>__<method>` key (e.g. `Vector__int64_t__iter` → tid of `VectorIter__int64_t`). The naming mirrors what `lower_generic_equip` → `lower_equip_block` (with stripped trait_name) emits at lowering time (line ~5279, 4253-4261), so call-site lookups in `lower_for_iterator` and `EMethodCall` find the right entry. Method-level generics (`each[F]`, `fold[A,F]`, …) are skipped — those need per-call-site mono. The pass uses `setup_type_subs`/`clear_type_subs` to substitute the equip's type params with the instance's type args while computing both `type_to_c_name(target)` (for the key) and `map_fn_return_type(method.return_type)` (for the value).

  **Part 2 — transitive equip-walk in the discovery fixpoint.** Extended the existing `transitive_changed` loop (lines ~6016-6040, formerly only walking `fn_templates` bodies) to also walk generic-equip method **return types** AND **bodies** with the equip's type-sub map. The return-type walk catches the direct-chain pattern: `equip [T] Vector[T] with Iterable[T]: VectorIter[T] iter(&self): …` — when `Vector[int]` is discovered, walking the methods picks up `VectorIter[T]` and adds `VectorIter[int]` to `generic_instances`. The body walk (via existing `discover_transitive_stmts`) covers the indirect-chain pattern: `return VectorIter[T](self, 0)` is an ECall to the constructor with `[T]` targs — substitutes to `VectorIter[int]`, gets registered.

  **Why both halves matter.** Either alone is insufficient. fn_sigs without transitive discovery: `lower_for_iterator` looks up `Vector__int64_t__iter` and gets the tid for `VectorIter__int64_t`, then tries to look up `VectorIter__int64_t__next` — but the equip `Vector__int64_t__next` mono was never triggered because nothing discovered `VectorIter[int]`. Transitive without fn_sigs: discovery cascades but `lower_for_iterator`'s fn_sigs lookups still miss. The pair makes the chain self-sustaining: each discovered iterator type unlocks its own equip-method-return discovery, which feeds back into the fixpoint.

  **What this unblocks vs what's still gated.** With explicit `from std.iter import …`, `v.drain()` now resolves to `VectorDrain__int64_t` and the for-loop scaffolds correctly through `lower_for_iterator`. Three follow-on gaps remain before the iter chain compiles end-to-end at self-host (filed in TODO this commit): (1) generic struct templates aren't imported by `loader.gg`, so mono'd VectorIter/VectorDrain field metadata is missing → `[bug] EFieldAccess` on `self.source`; (2) no auto-import of `std.iter`, so zero-import fixtures still hit `equip_templates.len() == 0`; (3) method-level generics inside equips skipped (not yet needed by any tracked regression).

  **Verified.** `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` → 1123/1123 passing in 1041s. Bootstrap_fixed_point + all 5 self-host comparisons green. The change is additive: existing fixtures only see new fn_sigs entries that were previously absent, never overwrite existing entries.

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (+~70 lines).

- [2026-05-15] **Self-host: three residual `[bug] EFieldAccess: unknown field` diagnostics in stage-2 output retired.** Follow-on to yesterday's `[lower_fail]` audit. Stage-2.c now has ZERO self-host-emitted diagnostic comments (both `[lower_fail]` and `[bug]` shapes are gone).

  **Bug 1: `Parser__parse_statement: 'span' on 'SpannedToken'`.** Typo in `parser.gg:2633`: `snap_name_span = snap_name_tok.span`. `SpannedToken` (struct at `lexer.gg:86`) has `lex_token` / `lex_start` / `lex_end` — no `.span` field. `snap_name_span` is declared `int`; the intended access was `.lex_start` (the start byte position). **Fix:** one-line correction, `snap_name_tok.span` → `snap_name_tok.lex_start`.

  **Bug 2: `resolve___resolve_expr: 'span' on 'Box__SpannedExpr'`.** Self-host's `lower.gg::EFieldAccess` handler peeled `GtPtr` / `GtMutPtr` (lines ~2348-2356) but didn't auto-deref Box-wrapped named types (`Box__T`). So `expr.span` where `expr` is `Box[SpannedExpr]` (auto-boxed parameter) failed the field lookup — Box has no user fields — and fell into the `OpConstI64(0)` placeholder. **Fix:** added a Box auto-deref step to the EFieldAccess handler: when `base_type_name.starts_with("Box__")`, emit a `GIDeref` to extract the inner T, then continue the field lookup against T's fields. Mirrors `case EDeref`'s existing Box handling (including the byte-by-byte inner-name extraction — stage-1 self-host's `.slice(5, len)` on a Box-prefixed type name returns empty for view-aliasing reasons, see EDeref comment at line ~2549).

  **Bug 3: `resolve___resolve_expr: 'start' on 'int64_t'`.** Cascade from Bug 2 — once `.span` on `Box__SpannedExpr` fell into the I64 placeholder, the chained `.start` on that placeholder failed too (int64_t has no fields). Closing Bug 2 closes Bug 3 automatically.

  **Layering note** — rule-1 layering-correct: Box's value-vs-pointer-ness was already typed metadata (`build_resource_metadata` returns `BkRegularBox` for parameterised boxes), but the EFieldAccess handler wasn't consulting it. The fix is a write-through — when the type registry says "this is a Box," emit the deref. No name-shape heuristics: the `starts_with("Box__")` check is the standard mangled-name protocol shared with EDeref and the C-emit boundary, not an ad-hoc string check.

  **Verified.** `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` → 1123/1123 passing, 0 failures, 0 flake. `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` passes in 371s. Stage-2 snapshot has ZERO `[bug]` AND ZERO `[lower_fail]` comments. The 20 remaining `lower_fail` / `bug` string occurrences in stage-2 are the format-string literals + runtime helper definitions — no actual emitted diagnostics.

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/parser.gg` (+1/-1 line: typo fix). `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (+~18 lines: Box auto-deref step in EFieldAccess).

- [2026-05-14] **Self-host: three residual `[lower_fail]` patterns in stage-2 output retired.** Audited stage-2.c after the case SFor + iterator-protocol work — six `[lower_fail]` comments across three distinct shapes, each a silent gap in self-host's lowering. Closing all three.

  **Pattern 1: SAssign target EIt** (3 sites in `infer.gg` lines 581/585/589). `int it = ...; return it` shape. Self-host's lexer tokenizes `it` as the implicit-closure keyword (TkIt → EIt), so the parser couldn't recognize `int it = ...` as a var-decl (try_detect_var_decl's TOK_IDENT check fails on a keyword) and parsed it as two statements: SExpr(int) + SAssign(EIt, ...). The lowerer's SAssign target check only handles EIdentifier / EFieldAccess / EIndex; EIt fell to the fallback. **Fix:** the intermediate variable was a smell anyway — inlined to `return X` at all 3 sites. Idiomatic Gorget.

  **Pattern 2: PConstructor variant 'TRef' not in enum 'Type'** (1 site in `lower.gg::spanned_type_to_name`). The `case TRef(inner):` arm was dead — self-host's `enum Type` in `ast.gg` has no TRef variant (references appear only as PARAMETER sigils, never as standalone types). Fossil from a Rust-side AST that does have `Type::Reference`. **Fix:** deleted the dead arm.

  **Pattern 3: PLiteral nested in PConstructor** (2 sites in `lib/std/io.gg::write_all`'s `case Ok(0):` patterns). Self-host's lowerer only handled PWildcard / PBinding sub-patterns; PLiteral fell to the "wildcard fallback", which silently dropped the literal-equality check — so `case Ok(0)` matched ALL Ok values, breaking `write_all`'s broken-pipe detection. Latent: bootstrap doesn't exercise write_all, so the bug never bit. **Fix:** added a PLiteral arm that reads the payload field, emits `GICmp(field == lit)`, and branches to `no_match_bb` on mismatch. Primitives (int/bool/char/float) wired; string-literal sub-pats would need `gorget_str_eq` and aren't exercised today.

  **Bonus — diagnostic infrastructure.** Added `expr_kind` and `pat_kind` helpers (mirrors the existing `stmt_kind`) and appended the variant kind to each diagnostic message: `"SAssign target ... (got: EIt)"`, `"nested non-binding pattern ... (got: PLiteral)"`. Without the kind suffix, finding each cause required instrumentation that's now permanent. Future fallback fires self-document; the next audit will be cheap.

  **Verified.** `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` → 1123/1123 passing (was 1122; +1 across recent commits, no failures, no flake). `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` passes in 380s. Stage-2 snapshot: ZERO `[lower_fail]` fallback comments (down from 6 across the 3 patterns). The 19 remaining `lower_fail` occurrences in stage-2 are the runtime helper's function definition + its call sites for the few hardcoded `lower_fail()` invocations still in `lower.gg` (they emit comments at compile time but the runtime fn is what handles those — the COMMENT count is what matters and is now zero).

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/infer.gg` (-6 lines: 3× `int it = X; return it` → `return X`). `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (+~120 lines: `expr_kind` / `pat_kind` helpers + PLiteral sub-pattern arm + diagnostic-kind suffixes; -2 lines: dead TRef arm).

- [2026-05-14] **Snag #46 — `throws`-fn return value passed inline to enum-variant / struct constructor read as zero-init default.** Discovered by the gorget-js agent while implementing JavaScript §8.12.7 [[Delete]]: `return JsValue.BoolV(delete_own_property(...))` where `delete_own_property` is `bool ... throws RuntimeException` returned `BoolV(false)` regardless of the actual return value. Workaround applied in gorget-js: bind the call to a local first. Snag was filed against this project with a self-contained 75-line repro (cases A–F across enum / struct / fn-arg constructor positions). Cases A (enum inline throws-fn), D (struct two-inline-throws-fn), E (struct literal + inline throws-fn) all yielded the slot type's zero-init default (`false` / `0` / `""`). Cases B (local-bound), C (inline plain fn), F (inline throws-fn passed as plain fn arg) worked — pinpointing the gap to the *constructor-arg* lowering specifically.

  **Root cause.** Five constructor-arg lowering sites set `expected_type` to the field's declared type, called `lower_expr`, then restored `expected_type` — but did NOT call `maybe_auto_propagate` afterward. The sibling regular-call-arg path (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs:151` and `:1202`) and the `lower_call_arg` helper both DO call `maybe_auto_propagate`. So when an inner `throws`-marked function call appeared at a constructor-field position inside a `throws E` context, its `Result[T, E]` operand memcpy'd into the field's `T`-sized slot — and since the Result struct's byte 0 is the discriminator tag (0 ≡ Ok), the slot read as the zero-init default rather than the unwrapped payload. Textbook rule-1 (lossless-on-invariants) layering violation: the auto-propagation boundary was present on one consume-site path but missing on the symmetric constructor-arg path.

  **Fix.** Mirror the call-arg pattern. After `lower_expr` for each constructor field, while `expected_type` is still set to the field type, call `maybe_auto_propagate(ctx, builder, op)`. The expected_type gate inside `maybe_auto_propagate` correctly skips propagation when the field is itself a Result (so `Result[T, E] field = risky_call()` still keeps the Result), and propagates only when the field expects a non-Result destination.

  **Four sites patched.** Same three-line addition pattern at each:
  - `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs:210-221` — qualified enum variant ctor `Tagged.BoolV(...)` (the path used by Case A and the gorget-js failing site)
  - `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs::lower_struct_literal` — both the bare-name enum-variant fallback paths AND the regular struct-literal path (used by Cases D / E). The bare-name enum paths needed variant-field-type lookup added inline (they didn't have it before — `lower_expr` was called with no `expected_type` propagation at all).
  - `src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs` — bare-name enum-variant paths in `lower_call` (parallel to the mod.rs ones; currently unexercised by snag46 but fixed for consistency since they share the same shape).

  **Why no new mechanisms.** The infrastructure (`maybe_auto_propagate`, `should_auto_propagate`, `emit_result_auto_propagate`) was already in place and battle-tested at the call-arg boundary. The fix is just adding the call to the constructor-arg boundary — one line per site (plus the field-type lookup expansion for the two enum paths that didn't have it).

  **Regression fixture.** `tests/fixtures/snag46_throws_inline_in_ctor.gg` (copied from the gorget-js agent's repro) wired in `tests/integration.rs::snag46_throws_inline_in_ctor` with all six expected-output lines asserting "got true" / "got (true, 42)".

  **Layering note.** This bug is the symmetric analogue to Snag #43 (2026-05-13, the previous "throws-call in arg position auto-prop missing" snag — see `calls.rs:134-151` for the historical comment that flagged the same fix shape at `lower_call_arg`). The constructor-arg path was the obvious next consume-site to audit at the time but wasn't covered. Pattern: every value-consuming site (call args, struct fields, enum variant fields, collection puts, returns, default-spill destinations) that crosses a Result-to-T boundary in a `throws E` context needs `maybe_auto_propagate`. A future audit pass should check the remaining consume-sites — `Vector.push`, `Dict.put`, `Set.insert`, collection-literal element positions, return-stmt operand — for the same gap shape.

  Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs` (+8/-0), `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` (+50/-12, includes the variant-field-type lookup expansion), `src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs` (+4/-0), `tests/fixtures/snag46_throws_inline_in_ctor.gg` (new, 75 lines copied from /tmp/snag46/), `tests/integration.rs` (+45 lines: new test fn + expected output). Verified: 1050 unit tests pass; 1123 integration tests pass (was 1122; +1 for the new snag46 regression).

- [2026-05-14] **Self-host `lower_for`: iterator-protocol fallback for non-Vector/Deque iterables (companion to `case SFor`).** Self-host's `lower_for` was failing loudly on any non-Vector/Deque receiver. Replaced the `lower_fail` with a universal iterator-protocol path — calls `coll.iter()` once outside the loop (or treats coll as the iterator if it has `next()` but no `iter()`), then loops on `__iter.next() → Option[T]` until None. Single scaffold, universal across Dict / Set / String / Range / user-defined iterables. The architectural win over Rust frontend's seven `lower_for_*` functions: ONE protocol, ONE extractor abstraction — that's why I filed the inverse-direction "Rust frontend lower_for_* unification" TODO.

  **Lowered shape.** `for x in iter_expr: <body>` (where iter_expr's type isn't Vector/Deque) becomes:
  ```
  auto __iter = coll.iter()        # call iter() once OR reuse coll if coll IS an iterator
  while true:
      Option[T] step = __iter.next()
      if step is Some(x):
          <pattern binding>
          <body>
          continue → header
      else:
          break → exit
  ```
  No incr_bb (next() advances internally); continue jumps to header (re-call next), break to exit. The Some-payload extract reuses the canonical `match_scrutinee_ptr` + `emit_tag_read` + `emit_payload_read` chain (same primitives the existing `unwrap_or` path uses), so resource payloads are auto-cloned for the body binding.

  **Coverage.** Works end-to-end for **user-defined** iterator types with explicit `equip X with Iterator[T]:` blocks (smoke-tested on a Counter fixture: `for x in counter` lowers to `Counter__next` calls with proper Option[T] tag/payload reads). For **stdlib trait-derived** iter chains (`v.iter()` returning VectorIter[T]), the protocol path fires but currently lower_fails at the type-lookup step because self-host's typechecker doesn't populate `fn_sigs` from `equip [T] Vector[T] with Iterable[T]:` blocks — that gap is filed as the new "Self-host: register trait-equipped methods in fn_sigs" TODO and is the only remaining obstacle to iter chains working end-to-end through self-host stage-1. Pre-existing: the same iter-chain fixtures (`iter_lazy_adapters.gg` and ~40 others) were silently broken at stage-1 emit before the `case SFor` arm landed; the new protocol fallback just makes the failure message precise rather than fixing it.

  **Refactor (clean separation).** `lower_for` is now a tiny dispatcher (~25 lines): probe-lower the receiver, branch on collection type → `lower_for_vector` (idx+len fast path, ~70 lines) or `lower_for_iterator` (protocol fallback, ~60 lines). The previous single function was 110 lines and would have grown unwieldy as Dict/Set/Range/String specialisations layered on. The split reflects the typed contract: Vector/Deque get an O(n) fast path with direct `__len`/`__get` calls; everything else routes through the universal Iterator trait protocol.

  **Verified.** `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` — 1121/1122 (the lone failure is the documented `hot_reload_basic_lir` parallel-run flake — passes in isolation, same shape as the `vector_task_get` flake we've tracked since 2026-03-16). `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` passes in ~420s. The user-defined-iterator smoke test (`/tmp/counter_iter_test.gg`) lowers through self-host with `Counter__next` calls and proper Some/None tag-branching emitted in the GIR output.

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (+~95 lines: `lower_for` dispatcher, `lower_for_vector`, `lower_for_iterator`; net +95 from the previous monolithic `lower_for`).

- [2026-05-14] **Self-host's `lower_stmt` now has a `case SFor` arm — for-each modernization is no longer a silent no-op.** Self-host was missing the `case SFor` handler in `lower_stmt`, so every for-loop in self-host code (resolve.gg, typecheck.gg, traits.gg, derive.gg, format.gg, validate.gg, and many more) was emitting `/* [lower_fail] unhandled in lower_stmt: SFor */` C comments at stage-1 — the recent for-each modernization sweep was effectively a no-op at the stage where it mattered. Closing.

  **Architectural design (intentionally cleaner than Rust frontend).** The Rust frontend has 7 separate `lower_for_*` functions (range/string/array/dict/set/iterable/enumerate) that duplicate ~80% scaffold each. Self-host takes the reference-grade path: ONE `case SFor` arm in `lower_stmt` → ONE `lower_for` helper → ONE scaffold + per-type element-extract dispatch. The Vector/Deque fast path uses idx+len; other collection types will route through an iterator-protocol fallback (filed in TODO). The contrast is concrete: self-host's `lower_for` is ~120 lines covering Vector/Deque + enumerate; Rust's equivalents total ~1000 lines covering the same cases plus 5 more.

  **Lowering shape (idx-based desugar, matches the manual idiom users write today).** `for x in coll:` and `for (i, x) in coll.enumerate():` desugar to the canonical Gorget pattern:
  ```
  int idx = 0
  int len = coll.len()
  while idx < len:
      auto x = coll.get(idx).unwrap()       # element extract
      <body>
      idx = idx + 1
  ```
  Element extraction reuses the canonical `coll.get(idx).unwrap()` chain via `emit_payload_read`, which auto-clones resource payloads — so the binding is an independent owned copy, semantically identical to what users write today. Continue/break stacks are pushed around `lower_stmts(body)`; continue jumps to `incr_bb`, break to `exit_bb`. For-else (else_body): rare in self-host; emits a `lower_fail` diagnostic for now rather than silently dropping.

  **No AST synthesis, no recursive lower_stmt round-trip.** The previous stashed attempt synthesized `SVarDecl + SWhile + SCompoundAssign` AST nodes and recursively called `lower_stmt`, which compounded the stage-1 hot-path performance gap and timed out at the bootstrap_fixed_point stage1→stage2 step (>300s on driver.gg). Direct GIR emission avoids that overhead entirely — bootstrap_fixed_point passes in 383s (vs 214s baseline, but the baseline was silently no-op'ing the for-each conversions; the slowdown reflects real work that should have been happening).

  **Layering note.** This is rule-1 layering-correct: pattern-binding via the existing `nl_put` shape (same as `case SVarDecl`); collection-type dispatch via typed `collection_element_type` + the typed registry (no name-shape heuristics); operand mode via `op_consume` (which picks Move for owned resources, Copy for primitives — the same helper SVarDecl uses for its init). Three small new helpers: `lower_for` (the scaffold), `bind_for_local` (mirrors SVarDecl's binding triple of add_local + GIAssign + nl_put), `resolve_elem_type_id` (mirrors the prim-name resolution chain in the EMethodCall unwrap path).

  **Files.** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (+~170 lines: `case SFor` arm, `lower_for`, `bind_for_local`, `resolve_elem_type_id`).

  **Verified.** `cargo test --test integration --release --test-threads=4` — 1122/1122 passing, 0 failures (vector_task_get parallel-run flake didn't trigger this run either). `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` passes in 383s. `lowerer_comparison` passes in 82s. Stage-2 snapshot shows **zero** `[lower_fail] unhandled in lower_stmt: SFor` occurrences (the 23 unrelated `lower_fail` instances are pre-existing PConstructor / SAssign / nested-pattern shapes — filed separately).

  **TODO follow-ons filed.** (1) Iterator-protocol fallback for non-Vector/Deque iterables (Dict, Set, String, Range, user types) — the universal path that gives self-host's `lower_for` the architectural advantage over Rust's 7-function split. (2) Rust frontend `lower_for_*` unification — apply the self-host scaffold-plus-extractor pattern to retire ~80% of the duplicated scaffolding across the 7 Rust functions.
