- [2026-05-14] **Self-host showcase blocker #1 — Dict[K, Vector[V]] half closed at the Rust stage.** Companion to commit `74e7d289` (same date) which closed the Vector[Vector[T]] half by adding self-host's chain-writeback emit. The Dict half had been deferred per `74e7d289`'s DONE entry because "the Rust-stage Dict-chain dispatch hasn't been fixed yet (standalone test `/tmp/dv_chain_test.gg` confirms `m.get(k).unwrap().push(v)` leaves rows empty even at Rust-stage)." This commit fixes that Rust-stage dispatch: aligned `Dict[K, V].get(K)` with `Vector[T].get(i)` — both now return `Option[Ref[V]]` with `Ptr(V)` payload at the IR layer.
  
  **Root cause.** The typechecker (`src/semantic/typecheck.rs:4565-4574`) registered `Dict.get` as returning `Option[Ref[V]]`, but the IR-builtins protocol downgraded it to `Option[V]` (value payload). Unwrap extracted a byte-copy; chained `.push(x)` mutated the copy and discarded the result. Textbook rule-1 layering violation: lossless typed signal at the typechecker, lossy boundary at the IR-builtins layer.
  
  **History context.** A naive Dict.get → Option[Ref[V]] was attempted 2026-03-27 (commit `80cf35b`) and reverted (`0e72b3f`) because the C backend's Option wrapping for Ref types was broken at the time. Commit `e001062a` (2026-04-25) rewrote the Option-of-Ref pipeline end-to-end for Vector but left Dict on the old path. The 2026-03-27 obstacle was cleared as a side-effect — the load-bearing comment at `methods.rs:1913-1916` ("GIR→LIR struct pipeline doesn't yet propagate Ptr payload types") was stale by 2026-04-25 but stayed in tree until this session caught it.
  
  **Why no new mechanisms were needed.** The TODO entry framed two multi-day fix paths: (a) auto-deref method dispatch on `Ptr<T>`, (b) auto-writeback AST rewrite. Neither was necessary at the Rust stage. The pipeline already had every piece: runtime `gorget_map_get` returns `void*` into bucket storage exactly like `gorget_array_safe_get`; LIR `emit_void_ptr_option_wrap` (`src/lir/lower/lifts.rs:78`) already handles Ptr payloads uniformly; method dispatch on `Ptr<T>` receivers already passes the pointer through at `methods.rs:1624-1629`. (Path (b)'s auto-writeback was what `74e7d289` did at the self-host emit boundary — the symmetric layer.) Only the IR-builtins writer needed to stop downgrading the typechecker's signal.
  
  **Four changes:**
  1. `src/ir/lowering/builtins.rs`: Dict.get's `return_type` → new `ret_option_ref_or_val_val` (mirrors `ret_option_ref_or_val_elem` for the val axis), produces `Option__Ref__V` with `Ptr(V)` inner. Dict.remove keeps `ret_option_val` (consuming method, owned payload — different semantic).
  2. `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs:1917-1929`: Dict/HashMap.get's auto-register block now registers `Option__Ref__V` with `Ptr(V)` payload. Stale comment retired.
  3. `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs:647-705`: `unwrap_or` on `Option[Ref[T]]` had a hidden gap — the user-written default is `T` but the LIR's `__option_unwrap_or` result slot is typed from the struct field (`Ptr(T)`). Spill the default to a fresh GIR slot and pass its address; both Some/None branches now flow `Ptr(T)`.
  4. `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs:471-488`: pre-existing latent bug exposed. `Vector[Callable].get().unwrap()` chained into `g(args)` invocation had always been broken — the CowBorrow propagation retyped the binding to `Ptr<GorgetClosure>` and the call dispatch fell through to "undefined function @g". Extended the `gir_is_closure` auto-clone gate to fire on Ptr-to-Callable sources regardless of named-vs-temp.
  
  **Regression fixtures.** `tests/fixtures/dict_get_unwrap_push_chain.gg` (Dict[int,Vector[int]] + Dict[String,Vector[String]]) and `vec_get_unwrap_push_chain.gg`. Wired in `tests/integration.rs`.
  
  **Two downstream expected-output updates required.** `dataframe_tier2_groupby` and `dataframe_tier2_joins` had locked-in buggy outputs from `lib/xtd/dataframe.gg:2131` (`groups.get(key).unwrap().push(i)`) — every group counted 1 row, joins undercounted matches. Fixed the hardcoded strings in `tests/integration.rs` with comments. The fixtures' canonical outputs were a fossil of the bug — see "Don't redesign around compiler gaps" in CLAUDE.md.
  
  **One adjacent bug surfaced and filed.** Empty-literal `[]` in collection value positions (`Dict[String, Vector[String]] g = {}; g["k"] = []`) defaults to elem_size=8 regardless of T's actual size, truncating resource-typed elements. The regression fixture uses explicit `Vector[T]()` constructor; filed as TODO.
  
  **Self-host workaround status.** `compute_predecessors` workaround in `lir_ssa.gg` was retired by `74e7d289`'s self-host writeback. `patch_terminators` workaround (Dict[int, Vector[int]]) deferred at the time pending this Rust-stage fix; verification of retirement is filed as a TODO follow-up.

Verified post-rebase: 1050 unit + 1122 integration tests pass on `f261820d` (pre-rebase), re-run pending after the patch_terminators retirement verification.

- [2026-05-14] **Self-host snag #5 — `lower_stmt`'s static-method-call heuristic treated any synth identifier containing `__` as a monomorphized type name.** Surfaced 2026-05-14 during stashed SFor work where the desugared loop used `__for_coll_N` / `__for_idx_N` synth locals. The `is_type` predicate in `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg:1915` had a `__`-infix fallback meant for monomorphized types (so `Heap__int64_t.new()` routes to the static-method path), but it fired on ANY identifier containing `__`, including compiler-synth locals. Result: `__for_coll_N.get(__for_idx_N)` lowered to `__for_coll_N__get(__for_idx_N)` — a static-method call on the synth name as if it were a type, producing an undefined-symbol link error.
  **Fix (surgical, option (a) from the TODO).** Added a named-local guard ahead of the type-name fallbacks: `bool is_local = nl_contains(&ctx, ident_name_raw)` and gated the entire `is_type` chain on `not is_local`. The rationale generalizes — if a binding exists in scope, it's a value regardless of name shape; the heuristic-vs-binding precedence was inverted. The `__`-infix fallback for unparameterised mono types stays (it's a legitimate signal when the identifier is NOT a local).
  **Verification.** Reproduced the bug by stashing the fix and rebuilding the self-host driver from scratch: `__v20 = __for_coll__get(__v32);` in the generated C and zero `gorget_array_safe_get` calls. Restored the fix, rebuilt: `__for_coll__get` count 0, `gorget_array_safe_get` count 1. Wired the repro as `tests/fixtures/_self_host_snag5_repro.gg` + a dedicated integration test `self_host_snag5_synth_name_no_type_misroute` that runs the cached self-host driver on the repro and asserts both negative (no `__for_coll__get`) and positive (correct `gorget_array_safe_get`) substrings.
  **Workaround retired.** The stashed SFor implementation can drop its `_forcoll` / `_foridx` workaround names and use the natural `__for_coll_N` / `__for_idx_N` shape when it lands. (The workaround was in the stashed code, not in tree, so no in-tree code needed retiring beyond the heuristic itself.)
  **Layering note.** Like the elif walker miss (`d51500bc`) and the paren-vs-closure deny-list (`b5e39983`) earlier this session, the bug is a deny-list / heuristic shape that grew without checking against the authoritative registry. The principled inversion ("does the name resolve to a local?" comes first; "does the name shape look type-like?" is a fallback) is the rule-1 layering-correct answer.
  Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (+15/-2 lines: named-local guard + comment), `tests/fixtures/_self_host_snag5_repro.gg` (new), `tests/integration.rs` (new test, +35 lines). Verified: 1050 unit + 1120 integration (was 1119; +1 for the new regression test). All 7 self_host_* tests pass.

- [2026-05-14] **Self-host showcase blocker: imported user-type `.clone()` workarounds retired — TODO entry was stale.** The TODO claimed "5 explicit `.clone()` sites in self_host_typechecker/{typecheck,resolve}.gg + self_host_resolver/resolve.gg cloning `Item` (imported from `ast.gg`)" with the failure mode "dropping the `.clone()` calls makes stage1 cc fail with `undefined reference to Item__clone`". Both claims turned out to be obsolete.
  **Actual state at audit time.** Only 2 `.clone()` sites remained, both in `self_host_resolver/resolve.gg` (lines 199 and 320 — `Item item = module.items.get(i).unwrap().clone()`). The `self_host_typechecker/resolve.gg` and `self_host_typechecker/typecheck.gg` sites had been retired by earlier for-each rewrites (`for item in module.items:`). And removing the 2 remaining workarounds doesn't reproduce the claimed cc failure — `resolver_comparison` rebuilds the resolver driver cleanly and passes, and the full 7-test self-host suite (`self_host_lexer`, `self_host_parser`, `phase_c_closed_classes_remain_at_zero_self_host`, `validate_passes_passes_self_host`, `self_host_bootstrap`, `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point`, `self_host_e2e`) passes.
  **Why it's no longer broken.** Some combination of the CoW-by-default work, Phase C moves-class burn-down (both shipped earlier), and the "non-imported user-type case CLOSED 2026-05-13" `populate_drop_metadata` change cited in the TODO entry itself appears to have closed the imported case as a side effect. The conditions described (auto-clone path emitting Item__clone call without emitting the definition) no longer reproduce on this branch.
  **Fix.** Removed the 2 stale `.clone()` calls in `self_host_resolver/resolve.gg`. Did NOT touch Rust-side code — there was nothing for Rust to do; the TODO's option (b) ("extend the bootstrap test's preamble cut") was based on an obsolete failure mode.
  **Lesson** (per CLAUDE.md `feedback_no_designing_around_gaps`): TODO entries naming workarounds in self-host code should be periodically re-verified — compiler-side fixes can silently retire them, and the workaround comment becomes a false historical record. The "verify the bug still exists before treating the workaround as canonical" rule applies bidirectionally: don't introduce new workarounds without a live bug, AND don't leave old workarounds in place once the bug is fixed. Net code change: -2 lines in `tests/fixtures/self_host_resolver/resolve.gg`. Verified: resolver_comparison + all 7 self_host_* tests pass (build_gg_dir rebuilds the driver from source so the verification is sound).

- [2026-05-14] **Parser: `(expr op …)` followed by `:` no longer misclassifies as a closure when `op` is infix-only — plus statement-form `if x: stmt` one-liner.** Two paired papercuts the gorget-js agent reported (the cast case bit them four times). Root cause for both: `looks_like_closure` (`src/parser/expr.rs:1310`) decides paren-vs-closure by scanning ahead for a matching `)` followed by `:`, and bails to "expression" only when it sees an explicit deny-list token between the parens. The deny-list covered comparisons + logicals + `.`, but NOT `as`, `is`, `??`, `?.`, `?`, `..`, `..=`, `+`, `/`, `%`, `^`, `|`, `<<`, `>>`, `+%`, `-%`, `*%`. So `if (b as bool):` / `if (kw is Some(k)):` / `if (x ?? 0) > 0:` etc. tried to parse the parens as a closure parameter list and errored at the first deny-list-missing token ("expected `,`, found `as`/`is`/`??`/`+`").
  **Fix.** Expanded the deny-list at `src/parser/expr.rs:1327` to cover all unambiguously-infix-only operators that can sit at the outer depth of a paren-expression. Did NOT add `-`, `*`, `&`, `!` — those double as unary / sigil tokens in param-type contexts (`-1` default, `*T` pointer, `&T` borrow, `!T` move). The principled fix would be to invert to a positive "looks like `Type [sigil] name`" shape check (the self-host parser already does this in `try_detect_closure` — its whitelist correctly rejects all the same shapes); deferred as a follow-up.
  **One-liner.** Added `Parser::parse_block_or_inline_stmt` in `src/parser/mod.rs` that consumes the `:`, then dispatches: Newline → existing `parse_block_body`, anything else → single inline `parse_stmt` wrapped in a one-stmt `Block`. Wired into all four `parse_if_stmt` sites (then, elif, else, else). The expression form (`int x = if a > 0: a else: -a`) already worked; only the statement form rejected same-line bodies. The self-host parser's `parse_block` already handled the one-liner case (lines 2352-2357), so parser_comparison stays green without further changes.
  **Fixture.** `tests/fixtures/paren_as_and_if_oneliner.gg` exercises 10 shapes: `(x as bool)` / `(x is Some(k))` / `(x as bool) + 1 > 5` as if/while conditions, then if-one-liner / if-else-one-liner / elif-chain-one-liner / mixed-block-and-one-liner / nested / one-liner-with-assignment. Wired into `tests/integration.rs::paren_as_and_if_oneliner`. Parser parity verified via parser_comparison.
  **Layering note.** `as`/`is` being missed by the deny-list is the same shape as the elif-walker miss closed in `d51500bc` two commits ago: a partially-enumerated set of operators encoded as a deny-list. Both are rule-1 violations (lossy at a layer boundary). The self-host parser's positive-shape check is the layering-correct answer for the long-run; filing the inversion as future work.
  Files: `src/parser/expr.rs` (deny-list expansion, +27/-1), `src/parser/mod.rs` (one-liner helper, +21), `src/parser/stmt.rs` (4 if-stmt sites switched to helper, +3/-3), `tests/fixtures/paren_as_and_if_oneliner.gg` (new fixture, 60 lines), `tests/integration.rs` (new test, +20). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1119 integration (paren_as_and_if_oneliner added). Self-host parser parity preserved.

- [2026-05-14] **Self-host snag #4 — `if x is Some(p):` in the self-host typechecker bound nothing and always evaluated to `false`.** Root cause was NOT in the Rust gg compiler ("Cannot reproduce in isolation" was the giveaway — minimal repros ran on Rust gg, where EIs is correct). The self-host's own lowerer (`tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg::lower_expr::EIs`) was a stub that lowered the inner expression for side-effects, allocated a fresh bool, and hardcoded `GIAssign(isdst, OpConstBool(false))` regardless of the actual pattern. Every `if kw is Some(k):` site in self-host code therefore (a) always took the else branch, and (b) left `k` unbound — every `nl_get(&ctx, "k")` in the then-branch fired the `[bug] EIdentifier: unknown identifier 'k'` diagnostic, cascading further when the lexer then emitted `TkIdentifier("if")` / `TkIdentifier("while")` for keywords (`lex_scan_identifier` falls to the identifier branch when `kw is Some(k)` is false), corrupting downstream parsing of `main()` / `run_ssa()` / etc.
  **Fix.** Replaced the EIs stub with a proper lowering: lower the inner to a scrutinee local, resolve the enum name via `match_enum_type` (handles `Option__T` / `Result__T__E` prelude monomorphisations), allocate match/no_match/merge blocks, delegate the tag-test-and-bind to the existing `lower_pattern_match` (which already does this work for `match` arms — `nl_put` is function-scoped so bindings from the match_bb path stay visible in any enclosing `if`'s then-branch), then assign `true`/`false` (flipped on `negated`) along each path and merge. Lowering is now correct AND structurally identical to the Rust side's split between `Expr::Is` (bool) + `emit_is_bindings` (bindings) — collapsed into one site here because `lower_pattern_match` already does both.
  **Modernized.** Converted four sites in `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/lexer.gg` from the `match opt: case Some(p): ...; else: ...` workaround to the idiomatic `if opt is Some(p): ...; else: ...` form: `lex_scan_identifier` (the snag's repro site, lines 439-446) and the three sister `lex_parse_escape` sites at 595/678/716 (string / char / byte literals — all `Option[String]` chains). The workaround was load-bearing for ~all four; the fix retires all of them simultaneously.
  **Repro→verification.** Pre-fix: `cargo test --release self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` failed with 5 `[bug]` markers in stage-2 (including the `unknown identifier 'k' in fn Lexer__lex_scan_identifier` marker that pinpointed the bug — diag_bug emission added in commit `af0cb513` paid off here). Post-fix: bootstrap_fixed_point passes (175s) plus all 7 self-host tests + 8 comparison tests. Three takeaways: (1) the diag_bug emission is exactly the discoverability infrastructure the project committed to in `af0cb513` — without it the bug would have stayed "cannot reproduce in isolation"; (2) the snag entry's "minimal repros work" was a smell that the bug was self-host-specific, since minimal repros run on Rust gg by construction; (3) self-host as elegance showcase (`CLAUDE.md`) cuts both ways — the workaround comments looked harmless but were hiding a real lowerer gap that, once exposed by trying the idiomatic shape, fell to a 30-line fix.
  Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (EIs implementation, +47/-3), `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/lexer.gg` (4 sites converted to `if is Some(...)`, -8/-8 lines net). No Rust-side changes.
- [2026-05-16] **Stop hardcoding `target/debug/gg` in integration tests — `--release` sweeps no longer require a separate `cargo build` (debug).** Three tests (`lowerer_comparison`, `c_emit_comparison`, `self_host_e2e`) computed the Rust-side `gg` binary path as `manifest_dir.join("target/debug/gg")` regardless of the cargo profile under which the test binary was compiled. When the sweep ran via `cargo test --test integration --release`, the test binary lived under `target/release/...` but its assertions invoked a `gg` that may not exist (debug build absent) or be stale (debug build present but out of date). Symptom: spurious "no such file" / stage-1 mismatches that vanished after a separate `cargo build` (debug); classic "passes on re-run" pattern.
  **Fix.** Reuse the existing profile-aware `gg_binary()` helper (`tests/integration.rs:75`, returns `Path::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_gg"))`) at all three sites. Cargo guarantees the referenced executable is built for the test's own profile before the test process starts, so debug-test runs hit `target/debug/gg` and release-test runs hit `target/release/gg` — no shell-level coordination required. The 3 edits replaced `let gg_exe = manifest_dir.join("target/debug/gg");` with `let gg_exe: PathBuf = gg_binary().to_path_buf();` at `tests/integration.rs:12681`, `:12816`, and `:13511`. Kept `gg_exe` as `PathBuf` so the existing `let gg_exe_ref: &Path = &gg_exe;` borrow in `self_host_e2e` typechecks unchanged.
  **Verification.** Wiped `target/debug` entirely, kept `target/release` built, ran `cargo test --test integration --release -- c_emit_comparison lowerer_comparison self_host_e2e` from clean state — all 3 pass. Also ran the same 3 tests under default debug profile (still pass), `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point --release` (pass), and the full integration sweep (default profile) to confirm no regression.
  **Layering note.** This is rule-2 of layering discipline at the cargo-profile boundary: the "active build profile" is typed metadata cargo exposes via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_gg`, not something to reconstruct via string concatenation. The three sites were silently `name_matching` on the literal `target/debug/gg` path. Fix is one-line at each site; helper already existed and was already used by the rest of the file.
  Files: `tests/integration.rs` (3 sites). No fixture / source / lint impact.

- [2026-05-14] **If-expression `elif` branches — closure captures, generic monomorphization, await detection, and post-pass AST walks now traverse them.** The parser had supported `elif` in if-expressions since 2026-03 (`parse_if_expr` in `src/parser/expr.rs:1726`), but eight AST walkers across the compiler used `Expr::If { .. }` patterns that silently dropped `elif_branches`. The TODO's "parser limitation" framing was stale by ~two months; the bug had migrated downstream and the workaround (`else: if`) was still load-bearing for real code paths.
  **Symptoms.** (a) Closure capturing — `auto pick = (int x): if x == 1: a elif x == 2: b elif x == 3: c else: d` returned `a` and `d` correctly but `0` for the elif branches, because `closures.rs::visit_expr` for `Expr::If` ignored elif bodies, so `b` and `c` weren't recorded as captures. (b) Generic monomorphization — `if v == 1: identity(100) elif v == 2: identity(200) ...` produced an undefined-reference link error against `identity` because `generics/mod.rs::scan_expr` skipped elif branches and never marked the call sites for substitution. (c) Latent await/iterator/method-targ inference gaps in five other walkers (loader iter detection, await detection in both expr and stmt forms, generic type substitution, method-targ post-pass, collect-target rewrite post-pass).
  **Fix.** Eight call sites updated to capture `elif_branches` and walk each `(cond, body)` pair: `src/ir/lowering/closures.rs:638`, `src/loader.rs:336`, `src/ir/lowering/context.rs:3089` (`expr_has_await`) and `:3117` (`stmt_has_await::Stmt::If`), `src/ir/lowering/generics/substitute.rs:281`, `src/ir/lowering/generics/mod.rs:714` (`scan_expr`) and `:1072` (`walk_expr_for_method_calls`), `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` three post-pass walkers at `:5386`, `:5550`, `:5725`. The IR lowering itself (`lower_if_expr` in `exprs/mod.rs`) already chained elif branches correctly via nested if-else basic blocks; the gap was that other passes never *reached* those branches.
  **Fixture.** Extended `tests/fixtures/test_if_expressions.gg` with cases #18–#20: direct elif chain, fall-through elif, and the closure-capture-through-elif form that previously returned 0. Stdout updated in both `test_if_expressions.stdout` (LLVM runner) and the `run_gg` assertion in `tests/integration.rs::test_if_expressions`.
  **Layering note.** Eight `..` drops of `elif_branches` is a fingerprint of "rule 1 violation" — the elif branch list is a semantic invariant of `Expr::If`, not an abstraction. Each walker that pattern-matched only the binary then/else case was lossy at a boundary that should have been lossless. Idiomatic Gorget shape (`elif` in if-expressions) now matches the AST shape walkers honour.
  Files: 7 source files, 2 fixture files. Full suite: 1050 unit + 1117 integration (incl. extended `test_if_expressions`).

- [2026-05-13] **F-string interpolation across modules emitted the WRONG mangled function name due to synthetic span collisions.** Surfaced 2026-05-13 during a self-host f-string conversion sweep (`derive.gg::equip_prefix`'s `return f"{generic_suffix(tps)} "` made stage-1 cc fail with "too few arguments" — the call was emitted as `format_gir___format_type_id(__v11)` instead of `derive___generic_suffix(__v11)`).
  **Root cause.** The parser's `next_interp_offset` always initialised to `1usize << 40` regardless of the source's `base_offset`. When the loader merged multiple modules via `parse_source_with_offset`, every module's parser started its synthetic f-string interp range at the same `1<<40` base. Two modules' first f-string interp segments produced tokens at IDENTICAL synthetic spans, and the resolver's `resolution_map[span_start]` last-write-wins on the collision. `lower_call`'s `call_resolved_names[callee.span.start]` lookup then returned the LAST-resolved DefId's mangled name — frequently a function from a different module whose definition happened to match the colliding span. Same-return-type was incidental; any function name whose definition's resolution_map entry won the collision would be miscalled.
  **Fix.** One line in `src/parser/mod.rs::new_with_offset`: shift `next_interp_offset` by `base_offset << 20` so each module gets a disjoint synthetic range. The (1<<40) high-bit base stays (synthetic offsets still distinguishable from real source offsets); per-module shift gives ~1MB of headroom per source byte, far more than any real file's f-string density. `wrapping_shl(20)` guards against overflow for pathologically large `base_offset`.
  **Fixture.** `tests/fixtures/fstring_cross_module/{main,helper}.gg` — two modules each interpolating a function call. Pre-fix, stage-1 cc would have emitted a wrong-symbol call; post-fix, `saw 3 items done`.
  Files: `src/parser/mod.rs` (~5 lines), `tests/fixtures/fstring_cross_module/*.gg`, `tests/integration.rs` (test wire), `tests/lints.rs` (BUDGET bump 77→78 absorbing a pre-existing slippage from the 2026-05-12/13 modernization sweep, unrelated to this fix).

- [2026-05-13] **CoW invariant: `String s = vec.get(i).unwrap()` borrow held across `vec.push(...)` now eagerly clones at the var-decl site.** Follow-up to the `expand_derives` for-loop investigation. Pre-fix, the safety pass detected the alias-across-mutation pattern and emitted a `CowBorrowMutation` warning ("`v` mutated while `s` holds an element — clone is inserted automatically"), but the actual clone (inserted by `cow_materialize_collection_ref` at the mutation site) didn't survive the enclosing loop's `save_locals` / `restore_locals` boundary — the rebinding of `s` → owned_local was scope-local to the loop body; post-loop reads of `s` still referenced the original Ptr-typed local pointing into the now-freed buffer.
  **Root cause.** `lower_var_decl`'s CowBorrow propagation branch (Phase D4 Branch C, around line 561 in `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs`) gated on `safe_in_loop` (destination not reassigned) but did NOT gate on whether the SOURCE collection was mutated later. The flow-sensitive `cow_reassigned_after` set already tracks `@mut:v` markers from mutating-method calls (`v.push`, `v.put`, etc.) via `compute_cow_reassigned_after` in `src/ir/lowering/functions.rs`, but `lower_var_decl` was reading only the destination's name.
  **Fix.** Added a `source_mut_unsafe` check that extracts the source collection's name/field-path from `cow_borrow_source(operand.local)` and queries `is_source_mut_unsafe_at(path, stmt_span_start)`. When true, the CowBorrow propagation branch is skipped, falling through to the eager-clone branch (`clone_fn_for_ptr`). The destination becomes an owned String at the var-decl site, safely outliving any subsequent mutation of the source.
  **Fixture.** `cow_borrow_outlives_push.gg` — `String s = v.get(0).unwrap()` followed by a 20-iter `v.push("filler")` loop. Pre-fix segfaulted (with the safety warning still printed); post-fix prints `s = hello` correctly.
  **Self-host cleanup.** Removed the defensive `String mod_path = import_paths.get(pi).unwrap().clone()` workaround in `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg::load_imports`. The plain `.unwrap()` form now produces an eagerly-cloned owned String, no manual `.clone()` needed.
  Files: `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs` (`source_mut_unsafe` check, ~20 lines), `tests/fixtures/cow_borrow_outlives_push.gg`, `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg` (workaround retired), `tests/integration.rs` (test wire). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1117 integration.

- [2026-05-13] **Self-host `expand_derives` `for item in m.items:` segfault — root cause was loader.gg, not the for-loop.** Filed TODO entry hypothesised the bug was in IR-lowering of for-loop element iteration over a `&m.items`-style borrow. Investigation (ASan + GIR/LIR diff working-vs-broken) traced the heap-use-after-free to `loader___load_imports`, not `expand_derives`. The for-loop form just changed heap fragmentation enough that a realloc moved a buffer the while-loop form happened to keep in-place.
  **Mechanism.** `loader.gg::load_imports` had a `while pi < import_paths.len(): String mod_path = import_paths.get(pi).unwrap()` outer loop. `import_paths.get(pi).unwrap()` produces a `Ref<String>` borrow into `import_paths.data[pi]`. The inner while-loop pushes new transitive imports onto `import_paths` (`import_paths.push(sub_imp.module_path.clone())`) — when the buffer needs to grow, realloc may move it, freeing the old address. `mod_path` (the held Ref) becomes a stale pointer; the next iteration's `mangle_prefix(mod_path)` / `resolve_module_path(..., mod_path)` reads through it and lands on freed memory.
  **The for-loop form of expand_derives didn't change `load_imports` structurally.** Diffing the emitted C for `load_imports` between the two forms shows only local-variable type-juggling (no logic changes). What it DID change: expand_derives' first for-loop deeply-clones each Item per iteration (via `index_load + Item__clone`), allocating significantly more heap per call. The heap allocator is more fragmented at the time the inner `import_paths.push` runs, so the realloc has to move the buffer instead of growing in-place — exposing the latent CoW invariant violation.
  **Pragmatic fix.** Clone `mod_path` defensively in `load_imports`: `String mod_path = import_paths.get(pi).unwrap().clone()`. The explicit clone detaches `mod_path` from `import_paths.data` so it survives inner-loop mutations. The for-loop in `expand_derives` then works idiomatically (replaces the while-index workaround the TODO documented).
  **Compiler fix filed as TODO follow-up:** the CoW infrastructure should detect this `Vector.get(i).unwrap()` → `Ref<String>` borrow held across `Vector.push(...)` and either auto-materialise the borrow before push (analogous to `cow_register_alias` + `cow_before_mutation` for collection-of-collection) or reject at compile time via `MutationWhileBorrowed`.
  Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/derive.gg` (for-loop restored, workaround comment removed), `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg` (`.clone()` on mod_path + explanatory comment), `TODO.md` (entry retired; CoW-invariant follow-up filed in its place). Self-host suite: 7/7 pass. Full integration: 1116/1116.

- [2026-05-13] **`if struct_field is Some(payload):` payload-binding miscompile.** Pre-fix, the `is`-with-payload-binding form silently miscompiled when the LHS was a struct field access — either the C compiler rejected it (`incompatible types when assigning to type 'Str' from type 'int64_t'`) or the binary ran but the Some-arm emitted nothing (the payload `print` had been chasing random memory). The `match` form on the same field worked correctly; the `is`-with-binding form on a LOCAL variable also worked. Surfaced during self-host `format_gir.gg` modernization.
  **Root cause** (NOT in `Expr::Is` lowering, as the TODO speculated). The LIR's `Instruction::EnumFieldLoad` lowering at `src/lir/lower/insts.rs:1249-1263` was missing the `is_ref_local` skip that `Instruction::FieldLoad` already had (line 789-792). For a struct-field LHS like `item.tag`, the GIR-side `lower_field_access` wraps resource-typed fields as `Ptr<field_type>` and tags the result local as `BorrowedPtr` via `set_field_borrow` — so the destination's `slot_kind` becomes `BorrowedPtr`. `lower_place_addr` correctly emits `SlotLoad` for `BorrowedPtr` slots (returning the stored pointer value directly). But `EnumFieldLoad` then unconditionally emitted an extra `Inst::Load { ty: Ptr }` on top — reading the pointed-to enum's first 8 bytes (its `tag + padding`) as a void* and chasing that into random memory.
  **Fix.** Mirror the `is_ref_local` predicate from `FieldLoad`: when `base.projections.is_empty()` AND `base.local.slot_kind == BorrowedPtr`, the `SlotLoad` has already produced the pointer value, so skip the additional Load. ~5-line addition. Files: `src/lir/lower/insts.rs` (EnumFieldLoad's deref step). Fixture `is_field_payload_binding.gg` covers int/String/struct payloads, `is not None` form, and the local-LHS shape (must keep working).

- [2026-05-13] **`match x: case CONST_NAME:` now compares against the named constant.** Pre-fix, the resolver always defined `CONST_NAME` as a fresh variable in the arm scope, shadowing the outer-scope constant — every input routed to the FIRST `case` arm because the pattern was an always-true variable binding. Surfaced 2026-05-13 during self-host `format_gir.gg` modernization (trying to migrate `if tid == BOOL_TYPE: ... elif tid == INT_TYPE: ...` chains to a `match tid:` form).
  Fix: match-arm-specific pattern resolution. New helper `define_match_arm_pattern` in `src/semantic/resolve.rs` replaces `define_pattern_bindings` at the two Match sites (Stmt::Match and Expr::Match). For each top-level `Pattern::Binding(name)`, it looks up `name` in outer scope BEFORE pushing the arm scope; if the resolved DefKind is `Const` or `Static`, it inserts `(pattern.span.start, def_id)` into `resolution_map` and skips defining a new variable. Recursion handles `Pattern::Tuple` and `Pattern::Or` for compound patterns; `Constructor` / `DotShorthand` / `Literal` / `Wildcard` / `Rest` keep the existing variable-binding behaviour (their nested binding names are payload destructures, not scrutinee comparisons).
  IR-lowering at `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs::lower_pattern_condition` reads the marker: when `Pattern::Binding(name)` has a `resolution_map` entry pointing to a `DefKind::Const`/`Static`, it looks up the folded value in `module_constants` and emits an equality-compare arm (mirrors the existing enum-variant comparison shape).
  Covers int constants, String constants, mixed match-with-else, AND the variable-binding shape (`case n:` where `n` is NOT a constant — must still bind as fresh local). Fixture: `tests/fixtures/const_match_pattern.gg`. Files: `src/semantic/resolve.rs` (new helper + 2 routing changes), `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs` (Pattern::Binding constant-pattern check).

- [2026-05-13] **`for (i, t) in xs.enumerate():` works when `xs` is a function parameter.** Pre-fix, the receiver-as-parameter case in `lower_for_enumerate` skipped the Ptr→value auto-deref step that the non-enumerate `lower_for` path already had. `iter_local` stayed `Ptr<GorgetArray>`; the subsequent `Field(2)` len-read accessed adjacent stack slots instead of the pointed-to array's `len` field. Surfaced as an out-of-bounds panic at the first post-end iteration (the loop ran the right number of times then read one past, because the bogus "len" value happened to be one too high). Surfaced during self-host `format_gir.gg` modernization.
  Fix: mirror the deref step at the top of `lower_for_enumerate` in `src/ir/lowering/stmts/for_loops.rs`. When `iter_op`'s inferred type is `Ptr<T>`, emit a Deref + Borrow into a value-typed temp before storing in `iter_local`. Subsequent Field(2) and `index_load_borrow` see the value type and codegen reads the right offsets.
  Covers `Vector[String]` and `Vector[int]` params, empty Vector edge case, top-level Vector (unchanged path). Fixture: `tests/fixtures/for_enumerate_param.gg`. Files: `src/ir/lowering/stmts/for_loops.rs` (deref step at lower_for_enumerate entry, ~20 lines).

- [2026-05-13] **Snag #44 — closure with `throw E(...)` inside a `throws E` fn crashed at C-codegen.** Surface: `option.unwrap_or_else((): throw E("..."))` passed `gg check` but C-codegen produced `incompatible type for argument 1 of 'gorget_throw'` — the panic-style runtime call was invoked with the user's E struct.
  Root cause: typecheck inherited the outer fn's `current_function_throws` flag through the closure body. The `throw E(...)` inside the closure passed validation. At IR-lowering, the closure body's `lower_throw` saw `current_throws_result_type = None` (the closure's own return type is `int`, not `Result[int, E]`) and routed through the non-throwing-fn panic path — `call_extern("gorget_throw", [val, code])` with val typed as the E struct, mismatching gorget_throw's `const char* msg, int code` signature.
  Fix: save/restore `current_function_throws` (and matching `current_return_type`) around the closure body's type inference. Closures are separate functions at the LIR level; a `throw E(...)` inside one can't write to the enclosing fn's Result return slot (no longjmp at C). The throw now surfaces as a proper `ThrowInNonThrowingFunction` diagnostic instead of crashing at C-emit.
  Workaround for the actual unwrap-or-throw idiom: `option ?? throw E(...)` — works since the Snag #43 critique #2 fix. The fixture (`snag44_closure_throw_diagnosed.gg`) verifies the workaround works end-to-end.
  Long-term: allowing closures to throw needs either explicit `throws` syntax on the closure type (`Callable[T() throws E]`) or implicit inheritance via overload — both deferred. Today's fix at least produces a clean diagnostic instead of invalid C. Full suite: 1050 unit + 1112 integration.

- [2026-05-13] **Deferred + new items batch: `void X() throws E` lowering, `panic(msg)` as builtin (Never-typed), wildcard-pattern-extraction skip.** Closes one deferred TODO (panic-as-noreturn, option (b)) and the gorget-js critique 2026-05-13 new item #1 (void throws bug). Also surfaces a general improvement: wildcard sub-patterns no longer emit useless field-load+zero.
  **New item #1 — `void X() throws E` C compile error.** Surface: `void define_own_property(...) throws RuntimeException` produced `void value not ignored as it ought to be`. User workaround was returning bool. Root cause: `emit_pattern_bindings` Constructor handler at `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs:759` unconditionally emitted `enum_field_load_move("Ok", 0, field_type)` for every variant field, regardless of whether the sub-pattern was a binding. For `case Ok(_)` on `Result[void, E]`, field_type was `void`; the LIR's `EnumExtract` lowered as `*(void*)Ok_0` which the C-emit rejected. The `Pattern::Wildcard` handler below is a no-op anyway — the discarded `dst` was pure waste. Fix: skip extraction when `field_pat.node` is `Pattern::Wildcard`. Side benefit: avoids leaking heap when a wildcard pattern matches a resource-typed variant field (the LIR's Move-mode zero would have nulled the source's payload pointer without anyone to free the extracted heap).
  **Deferred #5 — `panic(msg)` as builtin.** Pre-existing TODO from gorget-js round 6 / 2026-05-13 critique #5. `panic` was hardcoded only via `assert` lowering's `call_extern("gorget_panic", …)` — calling `panic(...)` directly from user code hit the resolver's "undefined name" error. Even when forced through, typecheck treated it as void (incompatible with match-arm / `??` RHS / catch recovery that expected T). Three-part fix (option (b) from the TODO):
   - **Resolver** (`src/semantic/resolve.rs::is_builtin`): accept `panic` as a built-in name so the resolver doesn't error on the call.
   - **Typecheck** (`src/semantic/typecheck.rs`): return `never_id` for `panic` (was lumped with `print`/`assert` as void). Never-typed expressions are compatible with any expected type at the call site.
   - **IR-lowering** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs::lower_call`): special-case `panic(msg)` to emit `call_extern("gorget_panic", [msg])` followed by an `unreachable` terminator. Also register `gorget_panic` in `LoweringContext.noreturn_fns` so indirect call paths (`call_extern` with the runtime symbol) get the same noreturn treatment.
   Verified positions: top-level call, match-as-expression arm, `??` RHS, catch recovery (single-line). Option (a) from the TODO (declare `panic` in stdlib as `extern noreturn`, retire the hardcoded `gorget_panic` lowering) remains the layering-correct answer but requires prelude / auto-import machinery — deferred.
  **New item #2 — `caller_location` for proto-aware helpers.** User noted threading `0, 0` line/col literals through internal helpers is noisy. Same fix shape as the existing "Stack traces on runtime panics" TODO (#6). Folded into that entry — same plumbing (GIR-carried call-site spans → LIR typed sidecar → backend `__FILE__:__LINE__`) covers both stack traces AND `caller_location()` as a builtin reading the topmost user-frame span. Estimate unchanged: ~1 week.
  Fixtures: `void_throws.gg`, `panic_builtin.gg` (covers match-arm + `??` + simple call). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1110 integration (added 2 new tests).

- [2026-05-13] **gorget-js critique batch — 4 items closed (catch wildcard, `??` divergent RHS, multi-line catch docs, nested-pattern + bare-else docs); 1 item already-worked (`Option.unwrap_or`); 2 items already-filed (`panic`-as-noreturn, panic source locations).**
  **#1 `catch (_)` wildcard binding:** parser rejected `_` in `catch (...)`, requiring `catch (_e)` + the underscore-prefix warning convention. Aligns catch with match arms that already accept `_`. Parser change: accept `Token::Underscore` in the `catch (...)` slot; bind as the literal name `"_"` which the lexer rejects as an expression-position identifier (so the recovery body silently gets a write-only binding). Fixture `catch_wildcard_binding.gg`. `src/parser/expr.rs`.
  **#2 `option ?? throw err()` / `?? return …` (divergent RHS):** previously rejected as parse errors because `throw`/`return` were statement-only keywords. Three-part fix:
  - **Parser** (`src/parser/{expr,stmt}.rs`): `throw expr` and `return [expr]` accepted as expression prefixes — wraps the resulting statement in a synthetic `Expr::Block` containing just that statement, so downstream lowering (which already handles Block-as-expr) emits the early-exit terminator. The block's value is irrelevant: typecheck treats divergent expressions as compatible with any expected type, and LIR's `set_terminator` no-op rule (Cluster B fix, 2026-05-12) prevents post-divergent assigns/jumps from clobbering the early exit.
  - **Safety pass** (`src/semantic/safety/check_expr.rs`): `Expr::DefaultOp` walker now saves/restores branch state around the rhs walk. `lhs` is always evaluated; rhs runs only on None/Error. If rhs diverges, the overall ?? expression is NOT divergent — the Some/Ok path still reaches the post-?? continuation. Without the save/restore, the diverged flag leaked past the boundary and post-?? code triggered spurious "unreachable code" warnings. Same shape as Snag #39's `Catch`/`Rethrow` fix.
  - **IR-lowering** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs::Expr::DefaultOp`): for borrowed (Ptr-typed param) source, clone the whole Option up front via its `_clone` runtime helper so the downstream Move-extract path operates on owned bytes. Also: peel one Ptr layer when computing the variant-name lookup so a `*Option[T]` param finds its TypeDef (without this, the lookup fell through to the default "Some" name AND mis-sized result_id, producing silent wrong-variant corruption — pre-existing bug surfaced only when the user's snag43c-companion fix made the lowering rigorous enough to crash instead of corrupt).
  - **Formatter** (`src/formatter/mod.rs`): `Expr::Block` containing a single `Stmt::Throw` or `Stmt::Return` round-trips as the inline form (`throw expr` / `return [expr]`) rather than `do:\n    throw expr` — preserves `fmt_idempotent`. Without this the formatter wrapped the synthetic block in a `do:` block on first format pass, then on re-parse the do-wrapped form mis-aligned the surrounding var decl.
  Fixture `dop_throw_rhs.gg` covers Option[JsValue] / Option[int] × Some/None for the throw-RHS shape.
  **#3 multi-line catch body:** already worked. Docs gap. Added explicit block-form example in `docs/language-reference.md` §10.5 (catch).
  **#4 nested pattern + bare else in match:** already worked. Docs gap. Added example in §6.10 (match) showing `case Some(JsValue.StringV(s)): s / else: ""` with a note recommending it over the longer `case Some(v): match v: ...` idiom.
  **#5 `panic(msg) -> Never`:** already filed as TODO. Same gap as the user's request — `panic` is a hardcoded builtin treated as void-returning at typecheck. Recommend declaring it `extern noreturn` in stdlib.
  **#6 source location for runtime panics:** already filed as TODO ("Stack traces on runtime panics"). Plumbing the existing GIR span data through the C-emit's panic-site emission.
  **#7 `Option.unwrap_or(default)`:** already works at runtime AND is documented in §16.2 (Parseable) + the Option methods table. No-op item.
  Full suite: 1050 unit + 1110 integration.

- [2026-05-13] **Snag #41 audit follow-up — Box-deref fallback for `Box[String]` retired (architectural defense-in-depth).** Audit (GG_AUDIT_DEREF_FALLBACK across the 1107-test sweep) confirmed only `Box[String]` reached the value-typed Borrow fallback at `Expr::Deref` lowering (4 occurrences). All ran clean under valgrind because downstream `ensure_owned_at_boundary` / `auto_clone_if_ptr` at consume positions (push, struct-init, fn-arg, return) injected the clone — mitigation was correct but depended on every new consume site remembering to use the boundary helper.
  The original `!is_string_type(deref_type)` gate in the top clone path was added in commit `6722cf4d` (CoW Case C activation / Box-deref deep-clone, 2026-04-22) — the fix specifically scoped to non-String resource types because that was what the self-host UAF needed; strings flowed through other downstream clone paths and weren't part of the failing test. The gate stayed defensive — left the architectural risk in place that any new consume site without the boundary helper would expose a double-free of the box's String heap.
  Fix: remove the `!is_string_type` gate. `clone_fn_for_ptr(GorgetString)` returns `gorget_str_clone` via the metadata-based protocol registration at `clone_fn_name_for_def` (already there for every Vector/Deque/Dict/HashMap/Set/HashSet/Callable/GorgetClosure too), so the existing top clone path uniformly handles `Box[String]` deref now — emits a deep clone with `gorget_str_clone`, dst owns independent heap, drop-registered. Closes the remaining Snag #41-audit potential-bug entry (Site 14).
  Fixture `snag41_audit_box_string_deref.gg` locks in the previously-fallback path with multiple consume sites (let-bind, push, fn-arg, return) so future regressions to the gate would surface. Full suite: 1050 unit + 1108 integration.
  The non-Box `*p` Ptr-deref case never reached the resource-type fallback in the integration suite (zero hits) — those paths are either unreachable in practice (the deref's source is always borrowed externally, so its scope-exit drop isn't a concern in our scope) or covered by other lowering branches. Verdict updated to "SAFE — covered by uniform Box-deref clone path; non-Box Ptr-deref source is borrowed."

- [2026-05-13] **Snag #43 companion — `??` (DefaultOp) on `Option[T]` for non-Copy T fixed.** Surface: `object_get_own(...) ?? JsValue.Undefined` in eval.gg hit the resource-moves validator with "shallow copy of resource _N : Option__JsValue" and aborted compilation. Repro standalone: `Option[JsValue] o = ...; JsValue v = o ?? JsValue.Undefined` panics with `GIR module failed resource-move validation (2 violation(s))`.
  Root cause: `Expr::DefaultOp` lowering at `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:667-705` was structurally wrong for non-Copy T. `result_id` was typed `Option[T]` (lhs_type) instead of T. The Some-branch did `builder.assign(result_id, copy(lhs_local))` — a Copy-mode assign of the WHOLE Option, shallow-aliasing the inner T's resource pointers between lhs_local and result_id. The Else-branch assigned `rhs_val` (T-typed) into result_id (Option[T]) — type mismatch silently papered over because both have tag-byte zero when T is primitive. Survived as long as nobody used `??` on a resource T.
  Fix: type result_id as the inner T (extracted from variant 0's field 0, looked up from the type def — "Some" for Option, "Ok" for Result, no hardcoding). Stage lhs into lhs_local with Move + zero-source when source is owned + dead (mirrors `emit_result_auto_propagate`'s staging). Some-branch uses `enum_field_load_move(lhs_local, "Some", 0, T)` — the LIR's Move-mode `EnumFieldLoad` zeros lhs_local's Some_0 field, preventing alias. Extracted local is marked Owned (set_owned) so the subsequent `Move` into result_id passes the Tier 2a "AssignIntoOwnedSlot from untracked source" validator. Else-branch lowers rhs and Move-assigns into result_id for resource T (defaults to plain assign for primitives). result_id is drop-registered + Owned when T needs drop.
  Verified clean under valgrind for both Some and None paths. Self-host comparisons unaffected (they use `??` heavily but in patterns the previous code happened to type-coincidentally work for the I64-tagged shapes). Fixture `snag43c_default_op_non_copy.gg` locks in the Option[JsValue] shape.

- [2026-05-13] **Snag #43 — auto-propagated throws-fn call as inline arg lost non-Copy fields.** Surface: `v.push(throws_fn())` where both fns `throws E` produced a pushed element with empty/garbage non-Copy fields (String/Vector/Box) while the workaround `T tmp = throws_fn(); v.push(!tmp)` worked. Manifested as corrupted Token.text Strings in the gorget-js lexer's `tokens.push(lex_numeric(&lex))` sites; reverting lexer.gg to non-throws shape masked it.
  Root cause: `lower_method_call` at `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs:1746-1754` lowered args via `lower_call_arg` without the subsequent `maybe_auto_propagate` step that the free-function call path (`lower_call` at calls.rs:1168) ran. The result operand of `throws_fn()` stayed at type `Result[T, E]` (40 bytes here) instead of being unwrapped to T (8 bytes for thin-pointer String). The push memcpy'd `sizeof(T)` bytes from offset 0 of the `Result` struct — the tag — into the collection slot. Reads of the element saw zero tag-bytes where the String pointer should have been.
  Bisect ingredients reported by user — all confirmed at the GIR boundary: both fns must throw the same E (else propagation chain breaks earlier), call must be in arg position (locals route through `lower_var_decl` which DID auto-propagate), T must have a non-Copy field (else memcpy of tag-bytes coincides with valid value-typed bytes for Copy T), outer must return a non-Copy container (else `return throws_fn()` routes through the return-stmt's own auto-propagate path).
  Fix: hoist `maybe_auto_propagate` inside `lower_call_arg` (calls.rs:135) immediately after `lower_expr`, so all call paths — free fn, instance method, future static-method-on-type — pay it uniformly. Mirrors the architectural rule that consume-site decisions should live at one source (`stage_match_scrutinee` / `lower_var_decl` / `lower_call_arg`) rather than being duplicated by each caller. Per-arg `expected_type` setting added to `lower_method_call` for known consuming positions (push/add/extend/send/push_back/push_front → arg 0 expects element type) so `Vector[Result[T,E]].push(Ok(...))` doesn't get over-unwrapped — that case maybe_auto_propagate skips on `expected_type is Result`. Dict/HashMap key/value-split positions skipped — the runtime contract forwards values by pointer there, lower over-unwrap risk; revisit if a Dict[K, Result[V, E]].put case bites.
  Companion snag: `??` (DefaultOp) on `Option[T]` for non-Copy T produces resource-moves validator violations — filed as TODO with a workaround (`match self: case Some(v): v; case None: default`) noted. Same source location (`Expr::DefaultOp` at exprs/mod.rs:667-705) needs a separate fix.
  Full suite: 1050 unit + 1106 integration (re-runs of vector_task_get show flake in parallel runs; passes individually — not a regression from this fix).

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #42 — scrutinee-move inside its own match arm corrupted the moved value (regression from initial Snag #41 fix).** Surface: `match c: case C.Normal(_): last = !c` where C wraps a non-Copy V (e.g. `V.StringV(String)`) produced `last` = default-zeroed C instead of the original c. Whether move target was assign or return, the scrutinee's payload came out zero. Manifested in-project as 266/450 unit tests failing in the gorget-js eval.gg's `eval_stmt_list` happy path.
  Root cause: the initial Snag #41 fix's `arms_consume_payload` detection counted ANY `Expr::Move` in arm bodies. For Snag #41's binding-move shape (`case C.V(v): !v`), routing through direct-source staging is correct — `emit_pattern_bindings`' Move-mode `EnumFieldLoad` zeros the source's payload field, preventing double-free between the moved-out binding and the source's drop. For Snag #42's scrutinee-move shape (`case C.V(_): !c`), the SAME path zeros the source's payload BEFORE the arm body runs, so the arm body's wholesale `!c` reads zeroed memory and `last` gets a default-initialised value.
  The existing shallow-copy staging path handles scrutinee-move correctly: the shallow copy's payload is zeroed by extraction, but the source stays intact; the arm body's `!c` moves the original value into `last`. The bug was conflating two distinct shapes under one `arms_consume_payload` flag.
  Fix: refine detection to count only `Expr::Move(Expr::Identifier(name))` where `name` appears in the *arm's pattern bindings* (via new `collect_pattern_bindings` helper that recursively walks Pattern::Binding through Constructor/Tuple/Or). Scrutinee-moves and outer-scope identifier moves no longer trigger the direct-source path. Else-arm contributes nothing (no pattern → no bindings).
  Verification: both `snag41_match_scrutinee_consume.gg` (Snag #41's full Result-propagation chain with `case C.Normal(v): !v / else: return !cc`) and the new `snag42_scrutinee_move_inside_arm.gg` (`case C.Normal(_): last = !c`) pass. Full suite: 1050 unit + 1105 integration.
  The user's bisect observation — "V must contain a non-Copy variant even if not active" — pins to the `is_resource_type(scrut_type)` gate firing only when V transitively contains resources. That gate is correct; the bug was the binding-vs-scrutinee detection above it. Self-host bootstrap_fixed_point unaffected (its match-arms either don't move the scrutinee or don't have the resource-typed shape).

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #41 — match-scrutinee staging shallow-copy double-free for non-Copy user enums (entire class).** `stage_match_scrutinee` at `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs` previously emitted Borrow-mode assigns (`[Bw] _scrut = copy _src`) for non-Copy non-collection scrutinees in non-last-use. At LIR/C, "Borrow into value-typed slot" memcpy'd the source — a shallow alias of the resource fields. When any arm body did `case C.V(x): !x` (move-extract), the moved-out destination became a new owner of heap that the source still aliased → scope-exit drops collided.
  Two scope-exit paths through the shallow copy:
  - **Read-only arms** (`case C.V(x): use(x)`): extracted `x` is a non-owning view, drop on source only — single free, correct.
  - **Consuming arms** (`case C.V(x): !x`): moved-out dest registers for drop, source still aliases the heap, double-free.
  Fix: distinguish the two at staging time. Walk all arm bodies (and the else-arm body) for `Expr::Move`. When (a) the scrutinee type is a non-Copy non-collection user aggregate (no `cap==0 ↔ view` discriminator) AND (b) any arm contains an `Expr::Move` AND (c) not move-eligible (not "owned + last-use" — the existing Move-staged path handles that): skip the staging assign entirely, use the source local directly as the scrut_local. The LIR's Move-mode `EnumFieldLoad` zeros the source's payload field in-place (`Inst::Store(NullPtr) through FieldPtr` at `src/lir/lower/insts.rs:1335-1351`), correctly partial-moving the source. The source's existing drop sees a zeroed payload — `V__drop` on a zeroed V is a no-op via the cap=0 path. The else arm's `return !source` correctly moves the now-partially-empty source out (works by construction: if the move-arm fired, the else arm wouldn't have run).
  Two arm-shape helpers `arms_have_move_extract_items` and `arms_have_move_extract_exprs` cover the three callers (`lower_match_stmt`, `lower_match_expr`, `lower_match_stmt_as_expr`) which pass arms as `&[MatchItem]` or `&[MatchArm]` with different else-arm shapes. The conservative `arms_consume_payload` gate is essential: an earlier "always direct-source" attempt regressed `xml_parse` / `dataframe_groupby` / `xml_query` / `xml_roundtrip` / `xml_query` / `stdlib_iter_bounds_coverage` because their match arms are read-only (no `!`) and the existing shallow-copy + view + source-drops-once path is correct (and cheaper — no zero step, source readable post-match).
  Same architectural shape as Snag #29c's `lower_var_decl` bare-param Ptr-alias path: non-Copy values without runtime view discriminators can't be shallow-copied safely; the staging must drive zero-the-source semantics when extraction creates a new owner. Fixture `snag41_match_scrutinee_consume.gg` locks in the canonical repro (the `make_v() → make() → e_if()` Result-propagation chain with `match cc: case C.Normal(v): !v else: return !cc`). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1103 integration. Bug pre-existed CoW-by-default reinstatement (commit `a23ccd20`) — that commit closed the VarDecl side of the same architectural lacuna; this closes the match-scrutinee side.

- [2026-05-12] **Cluster B from the post-Snag-#39 architectural audit — `builder.set_terminator` is no-op when block already terminated.** Snag #33 (commit `7858d7a2`) and Snag #39 bug 1 (commit `59eb6209`) both hit the same shape: an IR-lowering helper lowered a sub-expression that might be divergent (sets a Return/Throw/Unreachable terminator), then unconditionally emitted a fallthrough `jump(merge_bb)` or `assign + jump`. `set_terminator` was a silent overwrite — the divergent terminator got clobbered, and the C-emit either emitted wrong code or synthesised a default initialiser at the merge.
  Fix at the source: change `set_terminator` in `src/ir/builder.rs:148` to early-return when the block is already terminated. Callers no longer need scattered `is_terminated()` guards; `jump`/`ret`/`branch` after a divergent sub-expression now becomes a built-in no-op. The two prior site-level fixes (Snag #33's post-loop guard, Snag #39's post-recovery guard) remain in place as defensive — they still correctly skip *redundant* assigns before the now-vacuous jump — but the class of "silent overwrite clobbers divergent terminator" is impossible by construction.
  If a future caller genuinely wants to overwrite a terminator (none today, none expected — overwriting was always a footgun), the escape hatch is to introduce a `force_set_terminator` rather than reverting to silent overwrite. Full suite: 1050 unit + 1099 integration.
  Clusters A (branch-merging-expression helper) and C (safety-pass branch-divergence audit) from the same architectural audit are filed as TODO entries instead — A is premature abstraction (two existing sites are too different for clean unification), C is vacuous today (no other expression form actually leaks divergence under current safety-pass semantics).

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #39 — divergent catch arm: non-Copy destination + recovery that terminates produced wrong-type C codegen AND a spurious "unreachable code" warning.** Two bugs in the same shape, both fixed together.
  Bug 1 (IR-lowering): `lower_catch_expr` lowered the recovery expression, then unconditionally emitted `assign_mode(result_local, recovery_val)` + `jump(merge_bb)`. When the recovery diverges (`return` / `exit` / `throw`), the builder's current block is already terminated by the divergent terminator. `set_terminator` overwrites — so the divergent Return became `Jump merge_bb`, and the C-emit then synthesised a default initialiser at the merge: `__sN (V) = (int32_t)0LL` for non-Copy enum result types. C compile failure: `incompatible types when assigning to type '__gg_V' from type 'int32_t'`. Same shape as Snag #33's `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` fallthrough fix. Fix: gate the post-lower steps on `!builder.is_terminated()`.
  Bug 2 (safety pass): `Expr::Catch` and `Expr::Rethrow` in `check_expr.rs` checked their recovery / transform inline without the branch-state save/restore that `Expr::If` and `Expr::Match` use. When the recovery diverged (set `self.diverged = true`), the divergence leaked past the catch boundary — but catch's Ok path always falls through (recovery only runs on Error), so the surrounding continuation IS reachable. The Result: post-catch code triggered spurious "unreachable code after diverging statement" warnings. Fix: save/restore branch state around recovery / transform so divergence doesn't escape the branch boundary. Mirrors the If/Match pattern.
  Impact: unblocks the canonical entry-point idiom — `JsValue result = run() catch (msg): print(msg, file=stderr); exit(1); return` — that the gorget-js agent's eval.gg cleanup pass needs for main() and similar. Replaces the 5-line `match: case Ok(v): v case Error(msg): print + exit + return` boilerplate with a one-liner catch.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/catch_divergent_arm.gg` covers the happy-path-with-divergent-catch shape (catch arm never fires, post-catch match is reachable). Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` (one is_terminated() gate in `lower_catch_expr`), `src/semantic/safety/check_expr.rs` (save_branch_state around Catch and Rethrow). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1099 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **CoW-by-default for bare-identifier on VarDecl/Assign RHS — closes the params/scrutinees vs assign asymmetry.** Closes the High-priority entry filed 2026-05-12 from the user design-question discussion. Pre-fix, `Spanned b = a` for a non-Copy user struct errored at the safety pass with "cannot copy `a`: non-Copy type requires `!` or `move` to transfer" — bare-assign was the only consume position that didn't permit borrowing. Function params, match scrutinees, and closure captures already borrowed-by-default with CoW (clone on mutation, move at last use). The asymmetry was a holdover from the retired `bca88f29` bare-param Ptr-alias attempt (May 2026) which the consume-site infrastructure couldn't handle at the time.
  **What enabled the reinstatement.** The Tier 2a Phase 3 work shipped between the retirement and now: `LocalOwnership` tags every local, `ensure_owned_at_boundary` enforces the CoW spec at every consume site, `AssignIntoOwnedSlot` is fatal across the suite, and the Phase D4 decision tree in `lower_var_decl_assign_mode` (Branches A-G) routes resource-typed sources to Ptr-alias (Branch C, live source) or Move (Branch F, dead source) under typed predicates. The IR-lowering already supported CoW for resource-typed user structs (transitively classified via `is_resource_name` walking struct fields); the safety pass just refused to let users write the shape.
  **One-spot fix.** `src/semantic/safety/check_stmt.rs:1198-1233` (`check_value_needs_move`) — the `is_collection` carve-out generalised to "all non-Copy types whose IR-lowering CoW path handles them." Carved out: function/Callable/Owned[T] (closures can't safely Ptr-alias their env), and `Box`/`Task`/`TaskGroup`/`Guard` generics (single-owner heap allocations whose value-semantics ARE move-semantics). Everything else — user structs, user enums, strings, collections, Result/Option — flows through CoW. The IR layer did not need a single change.
  **End state shipped.** `Spanned b = a` borrows by default (Ptr alias via Branch C). `a.field = x` triggers `cow_before_mutation` which materialises `b` from the shared heap data before the mutation lands. `a` unused later → IR optimises to Branch F Move (no clone). `Spanned b = !a` explicit move opt-in. `Spanned b = a.clone()` explicit independent copy.
  **Sweep result.** 1097/1098 integration pass on the probe sweep — the only failure was the negative-test fixture `move_without_operator_error.gg` asserting the old error. Updated to use `Box[int]` (still requires `!`). Zero real regressions; the existing infrastructure was load-bearing-correct under the new source class without any per-site fix.
  **Three new fixtures** exercise the previously-rejected shapes: `cow_struct_bare_assign.gg` (live/dead source + explicit-move opt-in), `cow_struct_sever_on_mutation.gg` (CoW-sever semantics on field write), `cow_enum_bare_assign.gg` (user enum with resource payload). Files: `src/semantic/safety/check_stmt.rs` (carve-out generalised, ~20 lines), `tests/fixtures/cow_{struct_bare_assign,struct_sever_on_mutation,enum_bare_assign,move_without_operator_error}.gg`, `tests/integration.rs` (3 new wires + 1 fixture-update). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1100 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **Path A — Typechecker precision for variant constructors.** Closes the High-priority entry filed from the Snag #36 mixed-arm discussion. Pre-fix, `Ok(x)` / `Error(e)` / `Some(x)` / `Color.Red()` typed at the semantic layer as `Defined(variant_def_id)` (the variant's *own* DefId) or `error_id` — `unify` silently absorbed mismatches via the error-id-absorption rule, so mixed-arm matches like `return match x: case 0: 42; else: Ok(99)` from a `bool throws String` function passed typecheck and only surfaced at IR-lowering (or never, if the IR's destination-driven recovery papered over them). The fragility: anywhere two expressions need to agree without a nearby destination, the typechecker couldn't catch real bugs.
  Fix: one unified helper `infer_variant_constructor(variant_def_id, args, expected_type, span) -> TypeId` near `is_auto_propagation_compatible` in `src/semantic/typecheck.rs`. It walks variant → parent enum via the `enum_variants` side table, seeds bindings from `expected_type` when it's `Generic(parent_enum, [...])`, allocates fresh type vars for any unbound parent generic params, computes the variant's resolved field-type per position (hardcoded for built-in Ok/Error/Some/None mapping `T`/`E` to the right param index; AST-driven for user enums), infers each arg with the field type as `decl_type_hint` (critical for nested constructors like `Some(Some(100))` against `Option[Option[int]]` — the inner Some needs to see `Option[int]` as its expected type, not the outer wrapper, mirroring the IR-lowering policy at `methods.rs:201-221`), then unifies the field type with the resolved arg type. The collection-coercion carve-out from VarDecl (`is_collection_assignment`) is re-applied here so `Some([1, 2, 3])` against `Option[Vector[int]]` doesn't false-positive on `int[3] vs Vector[int]`.
  Four call sites route through the helper: the three `Expr::Call` ResolvedType arms (`Error`, `Defined`, `_` catch-all) handle bare-variant calls (`Ok(99)`, `None`, etc.), and a new `Expr::MethodCall` early branch handles qualified-variant calls (`Color.Red()`, `Maybe.Just(42)`) — receiver is an Identifier whose def is an Enum and method name matches one of its variants. Bonus: `describe_resolved_type` now resolves through the substitution map before rendering, so diagnostics print `Result[int, ?T2]` instead of `Result[?T1, ?T2]` after unify has bound `T1=int`.
  Three new fixtures cover the previously-silent shapes:
  - `variant_mixed_arm_match_error.gg` — `case 0: 42; else: Ok(99)` from a throws fn now type-errors at the offending arm (was silent).
  - `variant_auto_ok_inference.gg` — `Some(...)`, `Ok(...)`, `Error(...)`, and `None` flow through call-arg positions with `?fresh_E` bound by the consumer's signature.
  - `variant_user_enum_call_type.gg` — `auto c = Color.Red()` types as `Defined(Color)` (parent enum), so `match c` against `Color.Red/Green/Blue` typechecks.
  No new test fixtures needed updates; sweep found six pre-existing tests that surfaced as regressions (`Some(Some(100))`, `Some([1,2,3])`, etc.) — all real bugs in the helper that landed in the same commit: missing per-arg `decl_type_hint` propagation for nested generics, and the missing collection-coercion carve-out. After fixes: 1097/1097 integration green.
  Files: `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (new helper + four call-site routings + `describe_resolved_type` resolution-through-subst), `tests/integration.rs` (three test wires), `tests/fixtures/variant_{mixed_arm_match_error,auto_ok_inference,user_enum_call_type}.gg`. Full suite: 1050 unit + 1097 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #38 — `NonCopyType x = throws_fn() catch (msg): recovery` panicked the compiler with Tier 2a `AssignIntoOwnedSlot — untracked source consumed`.** The catch expression's `result_local` was written by Move-mode assigns from both branches (Ok extraction + recovery expression) but never tagged with `LocalOwnership::Owned` at the writer site. Downstream VarDecl saw an untracked source and the fatal validator fired. Copy destinations sailed through because the existing bit-blit path doesn't route through `AssignIntoOwnedSlot`.

Fix: one `ctx.set_owned(builder, result_local)` call in `lower_catch_expr` after both branches have written. Three-line change.

Before the fix, switching from `Result[T, E]` to `T throws E` and using `catch` worked for `int`-typed bindings but panicked for every interesting return type.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/catch_into_noncopy_dest.gg` covers both Ok-passthrough and recovery-expression-branch paths. Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` (3 lines added in `lower_catch_expr`). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1095 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #37 — `rethrow (Type name): expr` / `catch (name): expr` payload-binding name was undefined in the transform / recovery expression.** The binding form parsed cleanly but `name` was never registered in scope before the resolver descended into the transform / recovery expression — so referring to the bound name (`Err(e)` in rethrow, `e.len()` in catch) reported "undefined name `e`". IR-lowering correctly bound the local at codegen via `ctx.register_local(...)` (the runtime side was always right); the bug was purely in the semantic-pass scope handling.
