  1. **Resolver**: `Expr::Rethrow` and `Expr::Catch` now push a Block scope, define the binding name as `DefKind::Variable`, recurse into transform/recovery, then pop. Mirrors how if/loop/match-arm bindings already register themselves.
  2. **Typechecker**: set the binding's `def.type_id` so references to the name resolve to a proper type instead of `<error>`. For Rethrow, the user-declared `Type` in `(Type name)` provides the type. For Catch, the error type is extracted from the inner expression's `Result[T, E]` (which Snag #35 made the call's typecheck-level return type).
  Three shapes verified in the regression fixture: `rethrow (String e): Err(f"transformed: {e}")` (payload re-wrap with bound name interpolated), `catch (e): e.len()` (recovery references binding), and `catch (_e): default` (binding unused — regression-pin since the bare-binding-no-reference shape may have appeared to work before because the resolver didn't fault on the unused name).
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/rethrow_catch_binding.gg`. Files: `src/semantic/resolve.rs` (Rethrow/Catch scope+define), `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (Rethrow/Catch type_id set on binding). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1094 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **Phase C self-host validator burn-down — moves class closed, 100,170 → 0.** Final step of `docs/internals/self-host-resource-model.md` §5 — the third (and last) Phase C class. All three validators (`validate_resource_field_reads`, `validate_resource_call_args`, `validate_resource_moves`) now run unconditionally and panic on the first violation; the `GG_VALIDATE_RESOURCE_MOVES` env gate stays for diagnostic per-fixture logging but is no longer load-bearing.

  **The mechanism.** Added a single `op_consume(LowerCtx &ctx, GirModule &gmod, int lid)` dispatcher to `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` that picks the right operand mode from the source local's typed ownership:
  - Non-resource source → `OpCopy` (byte-copy is sound for scalars / pointer aliases — both filtered by the validator anyway).
  - `LoBorrowed` / `LoView` resource source → `OpBorrow` (alias propagates; no transfer).
  - `LoOwned` / `LoParam` / `LoMaybeOwned` resource source → `OpMove` (matches the convention established by the closed `validate_resource_call_args` migration at the EMethodCall receiver / EFieldAccess base / lower_field_write base / lower_index_assign base sites — last-use is assumed at the consume point).

  Migrated ~25 OpCopy emit sites in lower.gg to route through the helper: string concat args, var-decl init, return value, cstr coercion, printf, ECall positional, EMethodCall non-self args, closure call args, static method args, field write value, index-assign key+value, pattern match scrutinee binding, enum payload extraction, compound binop sites, GICmp fall-through, GIBinOp fall-through, scrutinee_ptr threading through `emit_tag_read` / `emit_payload_read`.

  **Single source of truth for resource classification.** `is_resource_type_name` in lower.gg now delegates to `build_resource_metadata` in lir_lower.gg (layering rule 3 — one source of truth per axis), covering runtime types GorgetString/Array/Map/Set/Closure, parameterised Vector__/Dict__/Set__/HashMap__/HashSet__/Box__/Heap__/Deque__, and opaque handles Mutex__/RWLock__/Channel__/Shared__/Weak__/AtomicInt__/AtomicBool__/Semaphore__/OnceFlag__/etc. The previous hand-coded list was missing GorgetArray/GorgetMap/GorgetSet/GorgetClosure and all the opaque-handle families.

  **Validator-side skip aligned with Rust.** Added the view-awareness skip (`src/ir/validate.rs:1080-1088` analog) to `check_operand_for_copy` in validate.gg: OpCopy on `LoBorrowed/LoView` sources is sound (both copies are aliases). Phase D step-2's tagging of collection-getter destinations and field-access results as LoBorrowed now flows correctly through the validator.

  **Runtime-behaviour parity.** All four operand modes lower to the same `ISlotLoad` at the LIR layer (lir_lower.gg:2349-2394) in self-host today; this burn-down produces correct GIR ownership labels without changing emitted code. When Phase 5 codegen lands real OpClone / OpMove emission (drop-tracking + move-zero), the labels written here become the contract.

  **Sweep results.** 1,048 / 1,049 integration fixtures: 0 violations (1 unrelated crash). Bootstrap fixed-point passes (221s, unchanged). The closed-class regression test `phase_c_closed_classes_remain_at_zero_self_host` now covers all three classes and uses a tightened FATAL detector (`^# validate_resource_.*(FATAL):` header) so it doesn't false-positive on string-literal occurrences inside the driver's own emitted GIR.

  Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` (op_consume helper + 25 migrations + is_resource_type_name delegation), `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/validate.gg` (LoBorrowed/LoView skip + moves promoted to fatal), `tests/integration.rs` (closed-class regression test updated).

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #36 follow-up — `return match v: case A(b): b ...` from a throws function.** The recursive-match-arm shape that surfaced while writing the Snag #36 regression fixture: when an outer `return match v: ...` is in a throws function AND any non-divergent arm produces a bare `T` value rather than `Result[T, E]` (e.g. `case BoolV(b): b`), the IR-lowering wrote a bare `T` into a `Result[T, E]` result_local slot. The Tier 2a validator caught it as `untracked source consumed`, and the user's gorget-js agent had been working around it by binding `bool r = match ...; return r`.
  Root cause: `lower_match_expr` / `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` size the match's result_local from `expected_type`. For `return match v: ...` in a throws function, `lower_return` had set `expected_type` to the function's `Result[T, E]` return type — but the typecheck-level match expression's natural type is the arms' unified type (bare `T` for bare-T arms). The IR layer was overriding the typecheck-level decision via `expected_type`.
  Fix (Option A from the discussion): when `expected_type` is a `Result[T, E]` wrapper, *defer* the result_local's final type to the first non-divergent arm — the existing refinement mechanism already in place for the no-expected-type case. Arms producing bare `T` (the throws-sugar case) refine to `T`; the outer `lower_return` then wraps once at the `throws` boundary via its existing Ok-wrap path. Arms producing explicit `Ok(...)` / `Error(...)` refine to `Result` — same end state, just discovered arm-by-arm. The asymmetry (Result-wrapper triggers deferral, Option-wrapper doesn't) is principled: auto-wrap is a property of the `throws E` *signature sugar*, not of Result the wrapper type — Option has no analogous signature sugar so its `expected_type` propagation stays uniform.
  Three options were considered (per-arm Ok-wrap; `lower_return` adjusts expected_type to bare T; defer refinement). Option B (lower_return adjusts) was rejected because `Ok(true)` at expr position needs `expected_type = Result` to disambiguate Result-vs-Option in the variant-constructor inference. Option C (per-arm wrap) duplicates logic at distributed sites — `lower_return` already owns the wrap. Option A keeps the wrap concentrated at `lower_return` and aligns the IR layer with the typecheck-level match type.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/throws_call_in_tail_return.gg` extended with three recursive-match cases (BoolV bare arm + NumberV positive + NumberV negative — both arms exercised across the three calls). Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` (both `lower_match_expr` and `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` get the same `expected_is_result_wrapper` deferral). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1093 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **Set literal lowering + container-literal discipline ratchet.** Closes the (b) work from the earlier (a)+(b) audit. Two issues shipped together:

  **1. Set literal silent-UB bug (`Set[int] s = {1, 2, 3}`).** Pre-fix produced garbage memory-address-like values at runtime. Surfaced during the post-Tier-2a container-literal hint-propagation audit.

  Root cause: the parser produces `Expr::ArrayLiteral` for BOTH `[a, b, c]` AND `{a, b, c}` (shared AST node, "set vs array distinguished by context" — `src/parser/expr.rs:1663`). But the IR lowering only built GorgetArray — when decl_type_hint was Set/HashSet, the C-emit memcpyed GorgetArray bytes into a Set[T] slot. Different layouts → undefined values returned for `s.len()`.

  Fix: `lower_array_literal` now checks `ctx.func_state.expected_type` at entry; if `CollectionKind::Set | OrderedSet`, dispatches to new `lower_set_literal_from_array` helper that calls `gorget_set_new` + `gorget_set_add` with per-element Move + MoveZero discipline (parallel to `lower_array_literal`). Regression fixture `set_literal_basic.gg` covers `Set[int]`, `Set[String]` (with deduplication), and the explicit constructor empty case.

  **2. Container-literal discipline ratchet (`tests/lints.rs::container_literal_arms_count`).** New one-way ratchet asserting the number of `Expr::*Literal(...)` / `*Comprehension { ... }` arms in `infer_expr` (`src/semantic/typecheck.rs`) stays at the expected baseline (5: ArrayLiteral, TupleLiteral, DictLiteral, DictComprehension, SetComprehension). Adding a new container-literal arm requires bumping the count with a justification — forces the author to audit decl_type_hint propagation for nested collection literals (DictLiteral/TupleLiteral propagate; ArrayLiteral relies on `is_collection_assignment` permissiveness at the var-decl unify site).

  Closes the (b) ratchet that was outlined when the user picked "Both — (a) first, then (b)" earlier in the session.

  **Why this matters.** The set-literal bug is the third in a class surfaced over this session: dict-literal-with-resource-value (Snag #25b symmetric), tuple-literal-resource-element, and now set-literal-silent-UB. All three were latent because no existing test exercised the shape AND no validator caught the class structurally. The ratchet locks the discipline so future container-literal arms can't silently slip through.

  Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/collections.rs` (~95 lines: dispatch + `lower_set_literal_from_array` helper), `tests/fixtures/set_literal_basic.gg`, `tests/integration.rs` (regression wire), `tests/lints.rs` (new ratchet + Phase D BUDGET bump for new proxy reads).

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #36 — `return throws_fn(...)` from inside a throws function.** After Snag #35 made throws functions type as `Result[T, E]`-returning at the call boundary, the tail-return path missed two updates: (a) `Stmt::Return` in typecheck called `unify(ret_type, expr_type)` directly without the auto-prop / capture-compat skip the VarDecl and arg-passing paths now share — so `return helper(x)` (where both functions are `T throws E`) failed typecheck with "expected `T`, found `Result[T, E]`"; (b) `lower_return` in IR-lowering treated only syntactic `return Ok(...)` / `return Error(...)` as "already a Result" — so even with (a) fixed, the Ok-wrap path would have re-wrapped the call's Result-typed operand, producing `Result[Result[T, E], E]` bytes in the `Result[T, E]` return slot at the C layer (Ok(true) returning as Ok(false)).
  Fix:
  1. **typecheck `Stmt::Return`**: mirror the `Stmt::VarDecl` / `Stmt::Assign` policy — skip unify when the destination type matches the value's Ok type (auto-prop) OR when the destination IS the wrapping `Result[T, E]` (capture). Routes through the existing `is_auto_propagation_compatible` / `is_result_capture_compatible` helpers; no new predicate needed.
  2. **IR-lowering `lower_return`**: after `lower_expr`, check whether the operand's type matches the function's `current_throws_result_type`. If yes, treat it as `is_explicit_result_variant = true` so the direct-assign path fires instead of the Ok-wrap. Falls back to the existing Ok-wrap for non-Result operands (so `return bare_T` from a throws fn still gets wrapped exactly once).
  Repro: `bool helper(int x) throws String: ...; bool caller(int x) throws String: return helper(x)` now compiles and propagates both Ok and Error correctly across the tail-return boundary. Match-arm tail-return shape (`case A: return throws_fn(...)`) also works for the *flat* case; the *recursive-with-mixed-arm-types* case (where one arm produces bare T and another does its own return) surfaced a pre-existing IR-lowering bug — `lower_match_expr` sizes the match's `result_local` from `expected_type` which `lower_return` set to the Result type, so the bare-T arm assigns bool into a Result slot and trips Tier 2a's `AssignIntoOwnedSlot` validator. Filed as a separate TODO at the top of TODO.md; workaround is to bind to a local first.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/throws_call_in_tail_return.gg` covers happy path, success-with-different-value path, and error-propagation path.
  Files: `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (Stmt::Return auto-prop/capture-compat skip), `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs` (lower_return type-match → direct-assign). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1092 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **Snag #35 — `int n = throws_fn()` from non-throws context now compile-errors, plus arg-position fix.** Surface symptom: calling a `T throws E` function from a non-throws context and binding to plain `T` (instead of `Result[T, E]`) typechecked silently and produced C-level pointer/int garbage at runtime — the IR-lowering coerced a Result handle into the bare-T slot. Same bug bit the arg-position case (`unwrap_or_zero(might(5))` where `unwrap_or_zero` takes `Result[T, E]`). Per `docs/book/10-errors.md:121-122`: "Without the `Result` type on the destination, calling a `throws` function from a non-`throws` function is a compile error."
  Root cause: the typechecker's Call inference returned the bare declared return type `T`, ignoring the `throws E` annotation. The `throws` was tracked as a side-channel `FunctionInfo::throws: bool` flag with no `Result[T, E]` shape exposed at the type-system level — so unify treated `int n = might(5)` as `int = int` and no error fired. The IR-lowering then wrapped the call's runtime return as `Result[T, E]` and memcpy'd it into the int slot.
  Fix per option (1) of the snag report (hard error, matching the docs):
  1. **Add `throws_type_id: Option<TypeId>` to `FunctionInfo`** (resolve.rs). Populated at the three function-registration sites by resolving `f.throws.as_ref()`'s AST type.
  2. **Call inference returns `Result[T, E]` for throws callees** (typecheck.rs's `Expr::Call` arm). When `func_info.throws_type_id` is `Some(E)`, the inferred return type is wrapped as `Result[T, E]` via `intern_generic`. Unification then fails naturally for `int n = might(5)` in non-propagating contexts.
  3. **Skip unify when auto-propagation or capture is compatible** at the arg-passing sites (positional and named-arg paths). Same policy already used at `Stmt::VarDecl`: skip unify when the destination type matches the OK type (auto-prop, requires enclosing fn to be throws/returns-Result) OR is itself the wrapping `Result[T, E]` (capture). Without this, every legitimate auto-prop call-arg (`f(might(5))` from inside a throws fn) would false-positive.
  4. **`maybe_auto_propagate` at call-arg lowering** (calls.rs). Runtime side of (3): when the arg is a `Result[T, E]` operand bound for a `T`-typed param, emit the unwrap-or-return chain at the call site. The capture form (param IS `Result[T, E]`) returns the operand unchanged.
  5. **`Expr::Catch` returns the OK type** (typecheck.rs). With (2) in place, `try_parse(s) catch (e): -1` has inner_type `Result[int, String]`; the catch resolves to `int`. Without this fix, 14 existing `catch`/`rethrow` fixtures regressed because their typed result became `Result[T, E]` instead of `T`.
  Four supported shapes verified: explicit capture (`Result[int, String] r = might(5)`), VarDecl auto-prop inside throws fn (`int v = might(x)`), arg-position auto-prop inside throws fn (`double_it(might(x))`), and capture into Result-typed param (`unwrap_or_zero(might(5))`). The two error shapes fail at typecheck with `expected 'int', found 'Result[int, String]'`.
  Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/throws_call_into_bare_t_error.gg`, `throws_call_arg_into_bare_t_error.gg`, `throws_call_capture_and_propagate.gg`.
  Files: `src/semantic/resolve.rs` (FunctionInfo field + 3 init sites), `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (Call inference + arg unify + catch type), `src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs` (arg auto-prop). Full suite: 1050 unit + 1091 integration.

- [2026-05-12] **Tier 2a `consume_externs` burn-down COMPLETE — validator promoted to fatal.** Closes the 27-violation latent class surfaced by the 2026-05-11 infrastructure ship (commit `31250be5`). The typed registry's `is_consume_extern(module, name)` is now live at the two callsites in `validate_consume_sites`; `is_runtime_collection_mutator` stays as runtime-symbol fallback only.

  **Three writer-side fixes that landed together:**

  1. **var-decl Callable auto-clone** (`src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs:425`). `Callable[T(...)] h = hook` pre-fix shallow-Copy'd the 16-byte GorgetClosure handle, aliasing hook's env with h. Subsequent `push(h)` then double-freed at scope exit. Fix: detect the destination's `gir_type` as a closure shape (FnPtr or Named-with-`c_runtime_alias = "GorgetClosure"`) and auto-clone via `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned` to FreshOwned. Keys on destination because source's `inferred` is unreliable — Callable params resolve to `UNIT_TYPE` at the immutable `map_ast_type` path (intentional design for the void* `__callable_N` ABI).

     **Narrow gate** to avoid spurious clones: only fire when source is a NAMED local that's NOT already Owned/FreshOwned. Closure literals (`!(n): n * 2`) are unnamed temps that lower to user-`__Closure_N` struct types — passing those to `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned` ABI-mismatches (the runtime wants `const GorgetClosure*`, not a user struct by value). Closure literals are fresh-by-construction and skip the auto-clone.

  2. **for-loop string-iter `set_owned_fresh`** (`src/ir/lowering/stmts/for_loops.rs:270`). `for ch in s:` calls `gorget_str_codepoint_at` which allocates a fresh owned String per codepoint. The loop var was `drops.register_local`'d but missing the ownership tag, so the validator saw Untracked at `stack.push(ch)` in `string_algorithms::is_balanced`. One-line `ctx.set_owned_fresh(builder, ch_local)` after register.

  3. **Validator promotion** (`src/ir/validate.rs`). Swap `is_runtime_collection_mutator(callee)` → `is_consume_extern(module, callee)` at the two consume-site callsites in `validate_consume_sites`. Retire `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `is_consume_extern` and update its doc-comment to reflect live status.

  **Probe sequence (full transparency).** Three iterations refined the diagnosis before landing on the fix:
  - Iter 1: extended `lower_function`'s string-only `set_owned` to all resource Move params. 27→25, hypothesis incomplete (dominant class is Borrow not Move). Reverted.
  - Iter 2: added var-decl FnPtr branch keyed on source `inferred`. Worked on `Callable[int(int)]` repro; failed on httpserver `Callable[UserType(...)]`. Debug print → source `inferred=Unit` for Callable params (by design — void* ABI signal).
  - Iter 3: re-keyed the var-decl branch on destination `gir_type`. Narrow gate excluding closure literals. 27→4. Investigated the 4 — 3 were closure-literal C-ABI mismatches (fixed by gate), 1 was the for-loop char-iter ownership tag gap (separate fix #2 above). Final: **27 → 0**.

  **What's locked in.** The Tier 2a typed registry now sees mangled-name collection mutators (`Dict__K__V__put`, `Vector__Callable__GorgetClosure__push`, etc.). Any future writer that emits a consume-shape mangled extern without proper move/clone discipline halts the build — same fatal-panic shape as the existing Phase C / Tier 2a coverage. Per CLAUDE.md "No name matching": registry-driven, not pattern-matched.

  **Self-host parallel.** The self-host frontend uses Callable params (e.g., parser combinators) — its lowering may have analogous gaps. Not surfaced by this sweep (self-host fixtures pass) but the structural class exists. Future audit work, not a session blocker.

  Files: `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs` (var-decl branch, ~50 lines), `src/ir/lowering/stmts/for_loops.rs` (1-line `set_owned_fresh`), `src/ir/validate.rs` (promotion + doc update). Full integration: 1088/1088 PASS in 662s.

- [2026-05-11] **Tier 2a typed `consume_externs` registry shipped as infrastructure; TupleLiteral hint propagation + parallel typecheck fixes; validator promotion deferred pending Callable-param ownership burn-down.** Follow-up to the dict-literal investigation answering the architectural question "is this an isolated gap or a class?".

  **What's structural.** The runtime double-free fix at `lower_dict_literal` (commit `077f756e`) was a writer-side correctness fix. The validator that SHOULD have caught the class — Tier 2a's `validate_consume_sites` — was looking at the wrong name: `is_runtime_collection_mutator` is a name allowlist of post-mono runtime symbols (`gorget_map_put`), but the IR-stage call uses the mangled name (`Dict__K__V__put`).   1. **`Module::consume_externs: FxHashSet<String>`** — typed registry of consume-shape extern fn names. Populated at module finalization from two sources: (a) writer-site direct registrations (e.g., `lower_dict_literal` inserts the mangled `Dict__K__V__put` at the call emission point), (b) derivation from `LoweringContext::fn_param_ownerships` — any registered fn with at least one `Ownership::Move` param is consume-shape by definition (covers Vector__push, Set__add, etc. registered via `register_collection_method_sigs`).

  2. **`is_consume_extern(module, name)` helper** in `src/ir/validate.rs` — ORs the typed registry with the existing `is_runtime_collection_mutator` runtime-symbol allowlist. Currently UNUSED (commented as future-path) — the helper exists for the burn-down session that promotes it.

  3. **TupleLiteral typecheck hint propagation** — `(Vector[int], int) p = ([1, 2, 3], 42)` pre-fix failed typecheck with `expected Vector[int], found int[3]`. Parallel to the DictLiteral hint propagation (commit `077f756e`); container literals must propagate per-element type hints from `decl_type_hint` to nested positions so collection-literal coercion works inside Tuple slots. Fixture `tuple_literal_resource_value.gg` locks in the regression. ArrayLiteral works via the existing `is_collection_assignment` permissiveness path (no fix needed for nested Vector cases).

  **Probe sweep deferred via TODO.** Promoting `is_consume_extern` (replacing `is_runtime_collection_mutator` at its two callsites in `validate_consume_sites`) surfaces 27 latent violations across 25 fixtures, dominated by `Vector__Callable__GorgetClosure__push` at Router::use / Router::before / gorget-js eval_* sites. Pattern: Callable parameters at fn entry are `LocalOwnership::Untracked`, then the push consumes them without tracked ownership. Root cause: `src/ir/lowering/functions.rs:632` tags string `!` (Move) params as `Owned` but the analogous tagging is missing for other resource Move params (Callable, Vector, etc.). Burn-down requires extending the writer-side param tagging — estimated 1-2 sessions. Sharp TODO filed.

  **Honest framing.** The dict-literal class IS architectural — same root cause shape as Tier 2c (Snag #23) and the broader Tier 2a (consume-without-MoveZero). The typed registry is the right structural fix; the validator promotion just waits on the burn-down of the latent violations the strengthening surfaces. Per the structural-guards.md framework, this is the standard pattern: register, gate, log, burn down, promote.

- [2026-05-11] **Dict literal with resource value type — double-free + bare-init expected-type propagation fixed together.** Two coupled issues from TODO 2026-05-09:

  **Issue (a) — runtime double-free.** `Option[Dict[String, Vector[int]]] x = Some({"a": [1,2,3], "b": [4,5,6]})` produced `free(): double free detected in tcache 2` at scope exit. Symmetric class to Snag #25b (array literal, fixed 2026-05-09) but at the dict-put boundary.

  Root cause: `lower_dict_literal` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/collections.rs:166`) emitted raw `Copy` operands for key/value arguments to `gorget_map_put`. The put memcpys the value struct into the dict slot, but the temp's drop registration stayed live — both the temp's scope-exit drop and the dict's `val_drop` freed the same heap allocation. For `GorgetString` values, `val_materialize = gorget_string_materialize_inplace` papered over the aliasing; for other resource values (Vector/Map/Set), no materialize hook existed.

  Fix: mirror `lower_array_literal`'s per-element discipline. New `stage_dict_arg` helper: for resource-typed key/value operands, stage through a fresh per-elem local with Move-mode assign + `move_zero_and_mark` on the source; the staged local is intentionally NOT drop-registered (the dict's `val_drop` / `key_drop` hooks own the slot lifecycle from here). Non-resource operands pass through unchanged. The mode picker matches array-literal's: Move when source is owned-by-Phase-D or an unnamed temp that needs drop, Copy otherwise.

  Why this approach over `val_materialize = clone_inplace`: zero-cost when temps transfer ownership (no clone unless the source is named/non-temp, which the existing method-call `.put()` path already handles via `clone_resource_args_for_init`), and structural symmetry with `lower_array_literal` (single source of truth for "consume position at a collection literal").

  **Issue (b) — bare-init expected-type propagation gap.** Surfaced while writing the regression fixture: `Dict[String, Vector[int]] d = {"a": [1,2,3]}` failed typecheck with `expected Vector[int], found int[3]`. The `Some({...})` wrapper happened to propagate the value-type, masking the issue at the wrapped boundary.

  Per CLAUDE.md "Don't redesign around compiler gaps", the regression fixture must use idiomatic Gorget — not reshape around the gap. Initial pass reshaped to `Dict[K,V] d = Dict[K,V](); d.put(...)` (workaround); after user flagged it, fix shipped instead.

  Root cause: `Expr::DictLiteral` typechecker (`src/semantic/typecheck.rs:2230`) inferred K/V from the first pair's lowered types without reading the surrounding `decl_type_hint`. A nested array literal in a value position typed as `T[N]` regardless of whether the outer Dict expected `Vector[T]`.

  Fix: extract K/V hints from `decl_type_hint` when it's a `Generic(Dict|HashMap, [K, V])`. Set `decl_type_hint = K` while inferring keys, `= V` while inferring values. Final dict type uses K/V from the hint when available (so the literal types as `Dict[K, Vector[T]]` even when nested values inferred as `T[N]` — the `is_collection_assignment` coercion at var-decl unify time then accepts).

  **Coverage.** Two regression fixtures, valgrind-verified clean:
  - `dict_literal_resource_value.gg` — idiomatic bare-init `Dict[String, Vector[int]] d = {...}`. Locks in BOTH the typecheck (issue b) and the runtime double-free (issue a) classes — the test fails the build if either regresses.
  - `dict_literal_some_resource.gg` — `Some({...})` wrapper for the same shape; pre-fix only the (a) issue fired here, because Some's lowering pre-propagated V.

  Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/collections.rs` (stage_dict_arg helper + value-type expected_type override for the IR-lowering side), `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (DictLiteral decl_type_hint propagation for typechecker), `tests/fixtures/dict_literal_resource_value.gg` + `dict_literal_some_resource.gg` (new), `tests/integration.rs` (regression wires).

- [2026-05-11] **Tier 2b (match-scrutinee discipline) documented as subsumed by Phase C + Tier 1c.** No separate validator needed; backlog entry retired.

  **Why subsumed.** Tier 2b's invariant — "match scrutinee staging assigns of resource-typed scrutinees use `AssignMode::Borrow` or `AssignMode::Move`, never `Copy`" — is structurally enforced by the combination of:

  1. **Writer-side rule** in `stage_match_scrutinee` (`src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs:49-70`): for resource scrutinees, the mode is unconditionally `Move` (last-use + owned) or `Borrow` (otherwise). `Copy` is reserved for non-resource scrutinees where it is correct.
  2. **Phase C `validate_resource_moves`** (already fatal) walks every `Inst::Assign { mode: Copy }` with resource-typed dst. The match-scrutinee staging assign IS one of those — if the writer-side rule ever mis-classified, this validator catches it.
  3. **Tier 1c closure** of the original motivating gap: pre-Tier-1c, `Option/Result-of-resource` TypeDefs carried stale `(None, Trivial)` metadata, so `is_resource_type` returned false at match-staging time and the writer-side picker fell into the Copy branch. With metadata coherent at construction, the resource branch fires correctly.

  Empirical confirmation: the full 1084-fixture sweep runs `validate_resource_moves` as fatal and stays green — no match-scrutinee staging assign produces `Copy` mode on a resource scrutinee today. A separate Tier 2b validator would be redundant-and-more-specific with no marginal soundness benefit.

  Files: `docs/internals/structural-guards.md` (§2b rewritten as SUBSUMED). No code changes required.

- [2026-05-11] **Tier 1a + 1d inverse-direction validators shipped; Tier 1b inverse attempted and retracted.** Two inverse validators close coverage gaps in the existing forward validators; a third was attempted and withdrawn after the integration sweep revealed the bug class doesn't have a clean syntactic signature.

  **Shipped:**

  1. **`validate_drop_fn_presence` (Tier 1a inverse)** at `src/lir/validate.rs`. Forward `validate_drop_completeness` walks entries IN `module.type_drop_fns`; it can't see structs that should have an entry but don't. New typed `expects_drop_fn: bool` field on LIR `StructDef`, set at the writer site by `populate_type_drop_fns` when the GIR strategy is `Recursive | Custom`. Validator asserts every `expects_drop_fn: true` struct has a matching `type_drop_fns` entry. Catches the populator-skip class: a Recursive struct whose field walk emerged empty because every field fell into a `_ => continue` arm (non-`Named`/non-`FnPtr` types: pre-mono `Tuple`, fixed-size `Array`, bare `Generic`) produces no drop fn at all — silent leak. Today no known violations (Tuple monomorphises to Named; fixed-size Array and bare Generic don't appear as TypeDef fields post-monomorphization). Future-proofs the populator. 3 unit tests + ~30 StructDef literal sites updated for the new field.

  2. **`validate_box_inner_type_consistency` (Tier 1d inverse)** at `src/lir/validate.rs`. Forward `validate_box_inner_type` walks `Box__`-named structs and asserts `box_inner_type: Some(suffix)`. The inverse: any struct carrying `box_inner_type: Some(_)` MUST have a `Box__` name prefix. Catches stray metadata on a non-Box struct — e.g., a future copy-bug in the `c_runtime_alias` clone path that accidentally propagates the field across registrations. The per-type Box emitter scans `box_inner_type` and would emit `Box__<inner>__drop` / `__gorget_box_alloc_<inner>` for the wrong type. No known violations today. 3 unit tests.

  **Retracted — Tier 1b inverse (`validate_movezero_provenance`).** The premise was: every `MoveZero` on a drop-registered bare local must have a Move-style consumer (Move-mode `Inst::Assign` source, or `Operand::Move(p)` anywhere) somewhere in the function. The integration sweep produced 315 failures on the first run; investigation showed the bug class doesn't have a clean syntactic signature.

  **Why it failed.** `Shared[T](v)` / `Mutex[T](v)` / similar smart-pointer constructors lower to `Call(...new, [Operand::Copy(v_place)])` followed by `MoveZero(v_place)`. The lowering pass emits the MoveZero because the call semantically consumes `v` — but the operand passed to the call is `Operand::Copy`, not `Operand::Move`. The validator's "Move-consumed" detection requires a syntactic `Operand::Move`, so it can't see these consume-with-Copy-operand patterns. They're widespread (Shared, Mutex, RWLock, Channel, Weak, Box.new — see also Tier 2c's `heap_alloc_consumer_externs` registry of analogous patterns).

  **Lesson.** Inverse validators only work when the writer-side transfer pattern has a clean syntactic signature in the IR. Tier 1a/1d worked because their transfer signatures are typed metadata fields. Tier 1b inverse would need a typed `consumes_its_arg_externs` registry analogous to `heap_alloc_consumer_externs` (populated at every writer site that emits MoveZero after a Copy-operand call), and that registry didn't exist. Building it would be a multi-week refactor of every consume-shape constructor's lowering path. Not motivated by a known bug class; retracted.

  **Per discipline doc framing.** Inverse validators only motivated by genuine two-failure-mode invariants with structurally-clean detection. The other ~12 existing validators don't have parallel inverse classes — their single-direction walks already enumerate every soundness shape. Audit: Tier 1a/1d are the two that ship cleanly; Tier 1b inverse would need typed-registry infrastructure first; Phase C read-site / `consume_sites` / `drop_pre_rebind` / cycle-check / cross-module-collision / etc. are already bidirectional by construction or single-shape-only.

  Files: `src/lir/mod.rs` (StructDef field + struct_def_by_name_mut accessor), `src/lir/validate.rs` (two LIR validators + 6 unit tests + VALIDATORS registry), `src/lir/lower/mod.rs` (writer-site setter in `populate_type_drop_fns` × 2 — struct + enum), `docs/internals/structural-guards.md` (table rows + Tier 1a body update), plus ~30 trailing StructDef-literal updates across `src/lir/types.rs` / `src/lir/lower/mod.rs` / `src/lir/display.rs` / `src/lir/validate.rs` / `src/bir/synth.rs` / `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs`. Full integration: 1084/1084 PASS.

- [2026-05-11] **Snag #34 — `Dict[K, NonCopyEnum]` silently dropped mutations when the read site used a nested constructor pattern.** Surface symptom: `d.put("k", v2)` after `d.put("k", v1)` left the previous value in place — `d.get("k")` returned the first value. The user discovered it via gorget-js's Array.push (`length` stored as JsValue, push reads length / writes length+1, the nested pattern read returned 0 → push stuck at 1). The bug actually fired with a *single* put + nested-pattern read too — the "overwrite" framing was a red herring; the root cause was destructive reads in the condition test *before* binding.
  Root cause: `lower_pattern_condition` for nested constructor patterns (`Some(V.Num(n))`) emitted `builder.enum_field_load_move` to inspect the inner enum's tag. At LIR, `EnumFieldLoad` unconditionally zeros the source's payload field for resource-type payloads (the shallow-copy-double-free guard). The subsequent `emit_pattern_bindings` then re-extracts from the *same* source — which is now zeroed — and binds zero values. Pure-Copy enums dodged the bug because `payload_needs_post_extract_zero` returns false for them; the LIR skips the zero step.
  Fix: split `EnumFieldLoad` into `Move` / `Borrow` modes via a new `EnumFieldLoadMode` enum. The condition test (`lower_pattern_condition`) emits `enum_field_load_borrow` (no source-zero); the binding (`emit_pattern_bindings`) keeps `enum_field_load_move` (existing destructive shallow-copy-safety semantic). The LIR emitter at `src/lir/lower/insts.rs:1310-1344` gates the zero step on `mode == Move && payload_is_resource`. Both builder helpers route through the same `Instruction::EnumFieldLoad` variant so the two surface forms can't disagree about the underlying instruction.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/dict_nested_pattern_noncopy_enum.gg` covers single-put / overwrite / read-modify-write cycle (the gorget-js Array.push trigger).
  Files: `src/ir/instructions.rs` (mode enum + field), `src/ir/builder.rs` (`enum_field_load_borrow` helper), `src/lir/lower/insts.rs` (consumer gates zero on Move), `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs` (condition site now Borrow), plus pattern-match `..` updates at the four downstream `Instruction::EnumFieldLoad` consumers (printer / validate / tag_ownership / sim).

- [2026-05-11] **Snag #33 — nested match-as-expression silently overwrites inner arm's `Return` terminator with `Jump merge_bb`.** When the inner of a nested match-as-expression contained `return X` in an arm body, the inner block's `Return` terminator was overwritten by a `Jump` to the inner match's merge block. The function never returned; control fell through to the outer merge, used a stale/zero result_local for the outer arm value, and silently produced a wrong answer. Repro: `outer(1)` (the path that triggers the inner Error → return Error(e)) returned `Ok(100)` instead of `Error("inner-error")`.
  Root cause: `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` at lines 2930-2933 in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` had a post-loop `else if !concrete_arms.is_empty() { builder.jump(merge_bb) }` branch that emitted an unconditional `Jump` on the current block. `builder.jump → set_terminator` *unconditionally overwrites* the existing terminator. After the for-loop, builder.current_block is the last arm's body block (because `next_test_bb == merge_bb` for the last arm so the post-arm `switch_to` is skipped). For the snag #33 shape, that body was already terminated by `Return` (from `lower_return` for `return X`), and the spurious jump clobbered it.
  Fix: gate the post-loop fallthrough jump on `!builder.is_terminated()`. Defensive — current code-paths don't actually hit the un-terminated case (the loop's inner `if !is_terminated() { … jump(merge_bb) }` already handles it). The sibling `lower_match_expr` doesn't have this branch at all (correct); both forms now agree. The single-match form `outer(): match inner(): …; return Ok(v+100)` routes through `lower_match_expr` and was always correct — which is why the snag required the *nested* shape to reproduce.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/nested_match_return_from_inner_arm.gg`. Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`. Full suite: 1044 unit + integration green.

- [2026-05-11] **Snag #32 — None-literal materialisation at writer boundaries (whole class plugged).** A bare `Expr::NoneLiteral` RHS at field-store / index-store / deref-store sites lowered to `Operand::Constant(Constant::Null)` and the C backend rendered the assign as `memset(slot, 0, sizeof(Option))`. Given the `Some=0 / None=1` discriminator layout, the zero-store produced a *Some(empty payload)* zombie — silently dropping the user's `r.field = None` / `vec[i] = None` / `*box = None` write. Family with Snag #26 (Box-deref write silent no-op) and Snag #29b runtime (None at call-arg position lowered to NULL).
  Per the user's request for "a generic invariant to plug the whole class": three-layer fix.
  1. **`expected_type` propagation** at each writer-site (`lower_field_assign` / `lower_assign`'s Deref arm). The bare-`NoneLiteral` arm of `lower_expr` already materialises a tagged None when `expected_type` is set to an `Option__T`; propagating it at the writer fans the Snag #29b runtime fix into the assign paths.
  2. **Chokepoint coercion `coerce_null_to_option_none`** inside `emit_field_store_with_cleanup`. Every field/deref/index store routes through this helper. If any future writer site forgets the `expected_type` propagation, the chokepoint catches the Null and rewrites it to `enum_init <T> None []` before emission. New on `LoweringContext` in `context.rs`.
  3. **Module-exit validator `validate_no_null_assign_to_option_slot`** in `src/ir/validate.rs`. Walks every `Instruction::Assign { value: Constant::Null, .. }` and resolves the dst's type through projections. Any `Constant::Null` reaching a `Option__T` / `Result__T__E` slot is a fatal violation — surfaces as "GIR module failed None-literal-materialisation validation" in the panic block at `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs`. Defence in depth: even if a new writer shape is added that skips the chokepoint, the validator halts the build.
  Three regression shapes in `tests/fixtures/none_assign_to_option_slot.gg` (field/idx/deref). Full suite: 1044 unit + integration green. NOT a Tier 1c issue (the wrapper metadata was already correct — drop_if_alive fired correctly on the field); this is a writer-side discipline gap one layer deeper.
  Files: `src/ir/lowering/context.rs` (helper), `src/ir/lowering/stmts/assigns.rs` (chokepoint + propagation), `src/ir/validate.rs` (validator), `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs` (fatal panic wiring).

Closes the same class of latent destructure bug for Resource tuples.

  3. **Closure-env validator carve-out.** Closure capture structs (`closures.rs:140`) intentionally stay `(None, Trivial)` despite holding resource-typed fields — captures are lifetime-tied aliases of outer-scope locals, not independently owned, so outer-scope drops handle cleanup (`docs/internals/closure-capture.md`). Added `is_closure_env: true` skip to `validate_type_metadata_coherence`, mirroring the smart-pointer wrapper carve-out. One new unit test `tier1c_coherence_closure_env_skipped`.

  4. **`closure_clone` clone-stats counter.** Added `__gorget_closure_clone_count` to `src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs` and instrumented `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned`. The counter covers all closure-clone paths (the recursive-struct-clone mapping I added in commit `11f1b3bf`, plus `gorget_closure_clone_inplace` which goes through `_to_owned` internally, plus the existing `lifts.rs:744` / `operands.rs:1458` / `calls.rs:569` emission sites). Now visible in `--clone-stats` / `--show-clones` output as `closure_clone=N`. Per the project rule that all implicit clones must be visible.

  **Audit: are the new clones wasteful?** No. The recursive-struct-clone mapping `gorget_closure_free → gorget_closure_clone_to_owned` (added in `11f1b3bf`) fires only when a Recursive struct holding a FnPtr field is cloned via `T__clone(void*)` — which happens at IndexLoad on `Vec[T]` or Option/Result unwrap of a borrowed parent. Iterator-chain structs (`MapIter`, `FilterIter`, …) are transient stack values, never stored in collections in practice. Probed with `clone-stats` on basic iter-chain + capturing-closure + Vec-of-closures scenarios: `closure_clone=0` in all cases. When the clone DOES fire, it's semantically necessary (deep-clone of closure env to avoid double-free at the boundary). Architectural correctness, not a quick fix.

  Files: `src/ir/lowering/types.rs`, `src/ir/lowering/exprs/type_reg.rs`, `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs`, `src/ir/validate.rs`, `src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs`. Test budget: 4 integration sweeps + 1 unit-test run. Full integration: 1082/1082 PASS in 679s.

- [2026-05-11] **Tier 1c — FnPtr-field drop emission + `monomorphize_struct` migration shipped.** Closes the second blocker behind the `monomorphize_struct` Tier 1c migration (the first — per-mono wrapper-emission — shipped earlier the same day in commit `39679d0e`).

  **The bug.** Iterator-chain structs (`MapIter`, `FilterIter`, `TakeIter`, `DropWhileIter`, `InspectIter`, `FilterMapIter`) hold a `Callable[U(T)] f` field whose GIR type is `GirType::FnPtr` but whose LIR storage is a 16-byte `GorgetClosure` struct with heap-allocated env. `populate_recursive_drop_structs` and `populate_type_drop_fns` (both at `src/lir/lower/mod.rs`) only handled `GirType::Named` fields and skipped FnPtr — silently leaking the closure env when the wrapping struct gets dropped. Tier 1a `validate_drop_completeness` (`src/lir/validate.rs:851`) correctly flagged the gap: its `is_droppable_type` predicate matches LIR struct names `"GorgetClosure"` and `c_runtime_alias` aliases, but the field never made it into `field_drops`. Layering rule 1 violation: GIR said "not droppable" (FnPtr excluded from the helper), LIR said "droppable" (via the runtime-alias check).

  **The fix.** Extended both `populate_recursive_drop_structs` (pass 1), `populate_recursive_drop_enums` (pass 2), and `populate_type_drop_fns` (pass 3 — both struct and enum branches) to handle `GirType::FnPtr` by emitting a field_drops/variant_drops entry with `drop_fn = "gorget_closure_free"` and `field_type_name = "GorgetClosure"`. The drop fn signature `void gorget_closure_free(void*)` (`c_runtime.rs:1494`) takes a pointer to the GorgetClosure struct; the existing recursive-drop emission already calls field drops as `drop_fn((void*)&self->field)` so the ABI fits. Also extended three clone-side mapping sites (`drop_fn → clone_fn`) to add `gorget_closure_free → gorget_closure_clone_to_owned`, matching the runtime's `GorgetClosure gorget_closure_clone_to_owned(const GorgetClosure* src)` signature.

  **Migration re-applied.** With FnPtr handling in place, `monomorphize_struct` (`generics/mod.rs:2342`) now calls `compute_drop_strategy_for_struct(&fields)` at construction. Per the helper's narrow predicate (mirrors `upgrade_types_from_fields`), a struct gets `(Recursive, Resource)` whenever ANY field is transitively droppable through registered Named TypeDefs — iterator-chain structs reach this via the inner-iter field, and their FnPtr field then correctly emits `gorget_closure_free`. The helper itself stays narrow (FnPtr excluded) because the construction-side predicate matches the post-hoc upgrade pass; the FnPtr handling lives at the LIR drop-fn population layer.

  **Why it's safe.** Only structs/enums with `Recursive` or `Custom` drop strategies enter the FnPtr emission paths (pass 1 + pass 3 are gated on strategy). Trait vtable structs don't go through `monomorphize_struct` and don't get promoted; their FnPtr fields stay un-dropped (correct — vtable fn pointers reference `.text`, not closures). Closure capture structs (`closures.rs:140`) use `Ptr(T)`/`MutPtr(T)` for captures, never `FnPtr`-as-field.

  Files: `src/lir/lower/mod.rs` (4 sites — pass 1 struct, pass 2 enum-variant, pass 3 struct + enum), `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs` (3 sites — struct-clone, enum-clone, enum-variant-clone mappings), `src/ir/lowering/generics/mod.rs` (re-apply migration). Test budget: 4 integration sweeps. Full integration: 1082/1082 PASS in 675s.

The validator correctly flags a **real pre-existing closure-env leak** that was silent before (the wrapping struct had no drop fn at all). Layering rule 1 violation between GIR and LIR. **Fix path:** extend `populate_type_drop_fns` + `populate_recursive_drop_structs` (`mod.rs:515-545`) to handle `GirType::FnPtr` with drop_fn = `gorget_closure_free`, field_type_name = `"GorgetClosure"`. Filed under TODO "Tier 1c — complete the Option/Result wrapper migration" sub-bullet for `monomorphize_struct`.

- [2026-05-10] **Self-host showcase blocker (3/5, root cause confirmed, deferred).** Replacing the `lir_ssa.gg` rebuild-and-set workaround with the chained `preds.get(succ).unwrap().push(bi)` form reproduces stage-2 cc errors as documented in TODO. Root cause traced via 4h time-boxed investigation: `.get(i).unwrap()` on a nested `Vector[Vector[T]]` byte-copies the inner Vector struct (data ptr + len + cap), `.push` grows the LOCAL copy, and the original `preds[succ]` stays empty. Empty predecessor sets corrupt `compute_preds`'s output, which corrupts SSA phi insertion globally, which surfaces as type-mismatch errors in UNRELATED downstream functions (e.g., `parser___token_float_val` declared `double` but body emits bare `return;` from BB1 because SSA mis-tracked types across mis-computed predecessors). This is the same compiler-level gap as blocker 2: `.get(i).unwrap()` should return either a mutable alias (`get_mut`-style) OR have an implicit `.set(i, _)` write-back, both of which fall under the Phase C moves-class burn-down work. Decision per the 4h time-box: revert to the rebuild-and-set workaround, file root-cause findings, defer the systemic fix to the moves-class burn-down. The workaround comment was upgraded with the root-cause explanation + cross-reference. Verified: bootstrap_fixed_point ok (~213s) with the workaround restored.

The chained form previously crashed stage-1 silently (SIGSEGV, no stderr) because `emit_payload_read` tags its result LoBorrowed/BoField (post-blocker-4) and the inline form byte-copied the borrow across the `type_check_item(item, ...)` value-passing boundary, aliasing module.items's interior. The destructure+dispatch inside `type_check_item` then invalidated the alias's storage. Explicit `.clone()` is the right Gorget-semantic shape for "I want an owned Item now" — the compiler should ideally insert it automatically at value-passing boundaries when source is borrowed, which is the Phase C moves-class burn-down work (~89,678 OpCopy violations baseline). Deferred until that lands; TODO entry refreshed with the systemic-fix pointer. Verified: gg check clean, lowerer_comparison ok (~53s), self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point ok (~220s).

- [2026-05-10] **Self-host showcase blocker (5/5) — parser `(method_call())` in boolean context.** `looks_like_closure` (`src/parser/expr.rs:1269`) was matching the closure shape on `if x and (d.contains("a")):` because the if-statement's trailing `:` looked like a closure-marker once the scan walked past the inner expression. Fix: add `Token::Dot` to the "tokens that cannot appear in closure parameter lists" exclusion set — closure param types are simple or generic (`int`, `Dict[K, V]`, `Vector[T]`), never dotted. A `.` inside the parens proves it's an expression. Regression fixture `tests/fixtures/paren_method_call_in_bool.gg` pins 4 canonical shapes: `flag and (d.contains("a"))`, `(d.contains("z")) or flag`, `((d.contains("a")))`, and nested method-chain `flag and (nested.get("outer").unwrap().contains("inner"))`. No self-host re-impl needed — the workaround was implicit (drop the parens at call sites). Verified: full integration suite passes (1082/1082, 643s).

- [2026-05-10] **Self-host pattern parser now accepts type-keyword tokens as binding names — IMemset destructure bug closed; lift port's ICallExtern memset workaround retired.** The Phase A.4 lift port hit a residual self-host bug where `case IMemset(ptr, byte, sz):` generated wrong destructure C: `byte` read as constant 0 instead of `IMemset_1`. Diagnosis traced through SSA value-subst instrumentation, then narrowed to substitute_inst's match arm: the trace showed `tk_name=int` for a `byte` token, which exposed that self-host's parser wasn't reading the keyword's type at all — `byte` (lexed as `KwUint8`) wasn't accepted as a binding by `parse_pattern_atom`, so `case IMemset(ptr, byte, sz)` parsed as `case IMemset(ptr, _, sz)` with the middle wildcarded. The body's `byte` reference then failed name resolution → `unknown identifier 'uint8'` → OpConstI64(0) placeholder.
  Fix: extend `parse_pattern_atom` (parser.gg, all three independent copies — typechecker which the lowerer symlinks, plus parser and resolver) to accept `TkKeyword(kw)` tokens as `PBinding`. Uses the keyword's source spelling via `type_keyword_name`/`non_type_keyword_name` so `case Foo(x, byte, z):` binds the middle position to "uint8" (matching how the expression parser already lowers a bare `byte` to `EIdentifier("uint8")`).
  Lift's ICallExtern("memset", ...) workaround retired in favour of the original `IMemset` emission. Self-host bootstrap + bootstrap_fixed_point + 1078 integration green. Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_{typechecker,parser,resolver}/parser.gg`, `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg`.

  2. `lower.gg::EMethodCall::unwrap` handler extended with the C-typedef name table (`int64_t/double/uint8_t/...` → primitive type ids) so monomorphised `Option__int64_t` etc. unwraps correctly.
  3. **LIR lift port** `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg` (~200 lines mirroring `src/lir/lower/lifts.rs::emit_void_ptr_option_wrap`): helpers `is_collection_void_return` / `is_consuming_collection_method` / `resource_clone_fn`, the `emit_void_ptr_option_wrap` function, signature change of `lower_instruction` to return `int` (new bb), lift dispatch in the GICallExtern arm, and the caller-loop bb threading.
  Bridge at `lir_lower.gg::map_gir_type` now reads through `resource_meta_for(&gmod, name)` (the typed accessor) instead of the populate-pass-bypass `build_resource_metadata(name)`. The Phase A populate pass at `lower_gir_to_lir` entry is now the sole source of truth for resource metadata reads. Bootstrap + bootstrap_fixed_point + 1078 integration green.

- [2026-05-10] **Snag #29b refinement quality — Unit-arm refinement of `result_local` was producing `void * = int32_t` warnings (13 per `gorget-js` build).** When my Snag #29b fix sized the match's `result_local` from the first non-divergent arm, it refined to `UNIT_TYPE` if the arm produced `Constant::Unit` (e.g. `case None: pass`). UNIT_TYPE lowers to `LirType::Void` → declared as `void *` in C. The next sibling arm storing `(int32_t)0LL` then triggered `assignment to 'void *' from 'int32_t'`. Pre-fix the slot was hardcoded I64 (silent miscoercion); post-fix it was structurally voided.
  Fix: skip refinement when the arm produces Unit. Unit-arm matches are statement-form; the result is unused so leaving the slot at the I64 default is harmless. Both `lower_match_expr` and `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` updated. Confirmed: 13 → 0 warnings on `gorget-js`'s main.gg build.
  This was a refinement of the Snag #29b fix (compile-error half), surfaced by user testing the gorget-js JS interpreter against the new compiler. Full suite: 1032 unit + 1078 integration. Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`. The runtime double-free in eval_try that the user also reported is a separate CoW-boundary issue at VarDecl-from-function-call-result and is filed as a TODO with the LIR diagnosis.

- [2026-05-10] **Snag #29b runtime follow-up — bare `None` literal at call-arg position lowered to `Constant::Null` and the C backend dereferenced it as `*(__gg_Option__T*)NULL` → SIGSEGV.** The compile-error half of Snag #29b shipped earlier today (commit `1b8522b8`) cleared the C type-mismatch on nested match-as-expression returning enums, but a separate, pre-existing bug masquerading as the same trigger still segfaulted at runtime: any call with a bare `None` literal as one of the arguments crashed (`f(None)`, `take_two(None, 7)`, `run(E.A, None)`). Bisection: triggers without any match — `void f(Option[int] o, int x): ...; f(None, 1)` segfaults too. The parenthesised `None()` form (`Expr::Call { callee: NoneLiteral }`) correctly read `expected_type` and materialised a tagged Option struct; the bare `Expr::NoneLiteral` arm just returned `Operand::Constant(Constant::Null)` and relied on the Assign handler to rewrite the null into a tagged struct downstream — which call args / return positions / struct-field inits don't flow through.
  Fix: extract `materialise_none_for_expected_type(ctx, builder)` from the existing Call(NoneLiteral) branch, route BOTH arms through it. The two surface forms can no longer disagree. The Constant::Null fallback remains for genuinely-no-expected-type sites (caught downstream by the Assign handler).
  Layering smell noted at the helper site: the GIR-layer Option-detection still uses `name.starts_with("Option__")`. The IR layer doesn't yet carry the typed `EnumKind::Option` flag that LIR has — a separate layering audit; tracked under the Tier 2a Phase 3 work.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/none_literal_at_call_arg.gg` (covers single-arg, multi-arg-with-int, and Option-after-enum shapes — the last being Snag #29b's reproducer). Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` (extracted helper, both arms now route through it). Full suite: 1032 unit + 1078 integration.

- [2026-05-10] **Snag #29 follow-up #2 — resolver now errors symmetrically on import-vs-user-def collisions (silent-shadow class closed).** `define_with_mutability` had an asymmetric "first one loses" rule: `from X import Y` followed by `enum Y:` silently let the user definition replace the import (the historical clause `existing.kind == Import && kind != Import`), but the reverse order — user def first, then import — already errored as `DuplicateDefinition`. The silent-shadow path was the underlying mechanism behind Snag #29: the resolver registered `enum E:` over a same-named `from std.math import E` (or hardcoded `module_constants["E"]`) without diagnostic, so qualified-path resolution at use sites silently dispatched to the wrong referent. Both orders now fail symmetrically: the user must rename one declaration or remove one. Dummy-span built-in imports (Vector, Box, Future, etc., registered with `Span::dummy()` in `collect_top_level`) remain replaceable via the surviving placeholder clause.
  Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/import_collides_with_user_def.gg` (the new error case — previously silently passed) and `tests/fixtures/user_def_collides_with_import.gg` (regression-pin for the existing reverse-order error). Files: `src/semantic/scope.rs` (one `can_replace` clause deleted, the others kept as placeholder-only). Full suite: 1032 unit + 1077 integration.

- [2026-05-10] **Snag #29b — nested match-as-expression returning a non-trivial enum miscompiled (`__gg_E = int64_t` C type mismatch).** `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` allocated `result_local` as `I64_TYPE` and never refined the type — unlike `lower_match_expr` which reads `expected_type` and refines from the first non-divergent arm. So a nested `match` returning a struct/enum got an I64-sized slot; arms wrote `&__sNN` (Ptr to the enum struct) into it via Move; the outer match's boundary path then did `__s5 = __v39` (`__gg_E = int64_t`), producing `incompatible types when assigning to type '__gg_E' from type 'int64_t'` at C-emit. Reproducer was `enum E: A; B(int)` with `match try_c: case E.B(_): match opt: case Some(_): E.A; case None: E.A; else: E.A`.
  Fix: mirror lower_match_expr — size from `expected_type` if available, otherwise refine from the first non-divergent arm. The Snag #28 boundary helper (`assign_match_arm_to_result`) was already routing arm values correctly; the bug was the slot type, not the helper.
  Side-find filed as a separate TODO: `None` literal at multi-arg call positions lowers to `__vN = NULL` followed by `*(__gg_Option__T*)__vN` (NULL deref → SIGSEGV). Single-arg form correctly constructs a tagged Option struct; multi-arg form skips the materialisation.
  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/nested_match_expr_enum_result.gg`. Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`. Full suite: 1032 unit + 1075 integration.

Removed PI/E/TAU/INT_MAX/INT_MIN — `lib/std/math.gg` already carries the correct const declarations and the const-eval path resolves them at compile time, so `from std.math import PI, E, TAU` is now the single source of truth (Layering rule 3). INT_MAX / INT_MIN had no callers outside example comments and were dropped.
  Spot-tests: `math_constants.gg` still passes all 8 assertions (PI/E/TAU come through the stdlib import); user-defined `enum PI:` now works without colliding; user `const float PI = 1.0` and stdlib import compose normally; Snag #29 repro still passes.
  **Holdout:** `INFINITY` / `NAN` remain hardcoded with explanatory comment. Their stdlib shape is `public float INFINITY = _math_infinity()` (runtime-init statics, not consts), and the import-side global initialiser does NOT execute today — `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs:1196` skips zero-length-span StaticDecls from stdlib imports, leaving `__lir_g0 = {0}`. Removing the hardcoded entries while that bug remains makes `INFINITY` read as 0. Filed as the cross-module global-init follow-up (TODO entry below).

- [2026-05-10] **Snag #29 — user-defined enum shadowed by hardcoded math constant; qualified-path resolution silently dispatched to the constant.** Symptom: `enum E: A; B(int)` followed by `E e = E.A` (or `E e = match x: case 1: E.A else: E.A`) failed C compilation with "incompatible types when assigning to type '__gg_E' from type 'int32_t'". The user reported it as a match-as-expression codegen bug; the actual root cause was name shadowing — `E` is hardcoded as a math constant in `module_constants` at lowering startup (`src/ir/lowering/mod.rs:486-493`, alongside `PI`/`TAU`/`INFINITY`/`NAN`/`INT_MAX`/`INT_MIN`). Two parallel resolution sites — `methods.rs::lower_method_call` (for `E.method(args)`) and `mod.rs::lower_field_access` (for `E.X` without parens) — gated the type/static-dispatch path on `!module_constants.contains_key(name)`, so they bailed out into method-on-value before checking `lookup_named`. `E.A` became "method `A` on the float `e = 2.718…`" → `call @double__A()` → void return assigned to `__gg_E` struct. The "any payload variant triggers it" trigger was misleading: payload-vs-no-payload didn't matter; what mattered was whether the enum's struct type happened to be a single int32 (all-unit case, where the type mismatch was masked by C's int→int compatibility) versus an actual struct (any payload variant case, where C catches the type mismatch).

  Fix per Rust-style separate type/value namespaces: in qualified-path position, type-name resolution takes priority over `module_constants`, but locals still take priority over types (matching `let MyType = …; MyType.x()` semantics). The two resolution sites now compute `is_type_name = lookup_named || resolve_enum_variant || is_primitive_type` and branch on `!is_local && (is_type_name || !module_constants.contains_key(name))`. Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs:57-72`, `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:1755-1764`. Fixture: `tests/fixtures/enum_name_collision_with_constant.gg`. Full suite: 1027 unit + 1074 integration.

  **Filed two TODOs (Layering rule 3 violations):**
  1. The hardcoded auto-injection of `PI`/`E`/`TAU`/etc. at IR-lowering startup duplicates the stdlib's `lib/std/math.gg` `const float E = 2.718…` definitions. The right shape is normal stdlib imports — users who want the constants `from std.math import PI, E, TAU`. Removing the hardcoding eliminates the collision class entirely.
  2. The resolver should detect collision at registration time: when the user defines `enum E` and `E` is already in `module_constants` (or vice versa), warn or error. Silent shadowing produced the wrong-codegen failure mode here, which is the worst possible (no diagnostic).

The existing fatal consume-site validator covered Calls/Inits/CollectionMutators but **not plain `Inst::Assign`** — exactly where Snag #28's bug shape lived (`[Mv] _result = copy _ptr` materialising as memcpy of borrowed pointee struct, double-drop at scope exit). This pair of commits closes the validator gap and drives the initial sweep down by 73%.
  - **`2846baf4` — validator + non-fatal env-gating.** New `ConsumeSiteClass::AssignIntoOwnedSlot { dst_type }` walks `Inst::Assign` whose dst is resource-typed AND the dst slot is owned-required. New `validate_assign_consume` helper, sibling of `validate_consume`. The two helpers split by which side gates resource-ness: source-type for the existing classes (correct for call args / inits where the consumer takes ownership of the value passed in), dst-type for AssignIntoOwnedSlot (correct for plain Assigns where codegen may auto-deref a Ptr<T> source into a T dst — Snag #28's shape, where source's own type is non-droppable Ptr but its ownership is Borrowed/View). Source-side ownership rules are identical. The fatal block in `lowering/mod.rs` partitions warnings: existing classes stay fatal (Phase 2A/2B/2C); the new AssignIntoOwnedSlot class is non-fatal pending sweep + migration. Sweep-of-record: 11,129 violations across 1073 fixtures (9527 untracked / 1068 borrowed / 460 owned-live / 74 maybe-owned).
  - **`2e8a38f7` — narrow validator + tag aggregate constructors (3 fixes).** (a) Validator dst-filter narrowed from `Owned|FreshOwned|Untracked|MaybeOwned` to `Owned|FreshOwned` only. The Untracked/MaybeOwned dsts are transient temps (printf-arg scratch, IndexLoad results) whose lack of drop-tracking makes the auto-deref-and-memcpy shape benign at runtime; Snag #28's bug class is specifically about NAMED result slots that DO get drop-tracked at scope exit. 11,129 → 5,234 from this filter alone. (b) `tag_ownership::infer_fresh_owned` extended to tag `EnumInit`/`StructInit`/`TupleInit` dsts as Owned. The aggregate's owned-ness is structural — fresh value built from field/element operands. Without these decisions, downstream Inst::Assign sites consuming the aggregate (e.g. `Option[T] x = Some(...)`) saw Untracked sources and tripped the validator. Collapses entire clusters: Option__ReliableStream (1,560 → 0), Option__SendSegment/RecvSegment/PeerInfo/DHTEntry (104 each → 0), Option__Task__void (40 → 0), and named-debug fns ParseError__debug (1,676 → 0), IoError__debug (554 → 0). (c) Dict-literal results tagged Owned (mirrors `lower_array_literal:61`'s `set_owned` at `gorget_array_new`). Three sites: `lower_dict_literal` empty-branch and non-empty-branch, `lower_dict_comprehension`. Combined: 5,234 → 3,052.

  - **BinOp/UnOp dsts**: binary/unary ops on resource types produce fresh values by construction (e.g. `Vector[T] + Vector[T]` lowers to a concat returning a fresh array). `apply_decision` filters non-droppable dsts via its `needs_drop` check, so blanket tagging is sound. Catches the iterator default-method `acc = acc + x` shape in `sum`/`product` over `Vector[T]`-yielding iterators (WindowsIter, ChunksIter, VectorDrain, ChainIter, etc).

Restricted to `Constant::Str` — other Constant variants don't produce heap data. Catches the empty-string-init pattern in iterator `join` default-method bodies and similar fresh-literal var-decls.

The `Borrow` mode is the zero-copy view path and stays untagged (the dst is an alias slot, not owned). Catches the `Dict[K, V][k]` shape — the Router clusters in `xtd.httpserver` were dominated by `Callable[...] h = sub.exact_routes[k]` where the IndexLoad result was Untracked, tripping the AssignIntoOwnedSlot validator at the var-decl bind. - [2026-05-10] **Snag #28 — match arm value crossing the result-slot boundary skipped the borrow→owned clone discipline.** Symptom: `match lhs.node: case Node.Ident(n): n` (where `lhs.node` is FieldLoad-derived → scrutinee is a Ptr → `n` binds as `*GorgetString`) double-freed at scope exit. The arm value flowed into the value-typed result slot via `[Mv] _result = copy _ptr`, which the codegen materialises as a memcpy of the GorgetString struct (data+cap+len+alloc) into the result. Both the result slot and the variant payload then aliased the same heap data — both fired scope-exit drops. Per the CoW spec table in `CLAUDE.md` ("Ownership at Consuming Positions"), a borrow source crossing into an owned destination requires a clone, not a memcpy.

  Fix: extract `assign_match_arm_to_result(ctx, builder, result_local, arm_val, span)` into a single helper at `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:2237` that runs the boundary discipline once: (1) `ensure_owned_at_boundary` clones if the source is a Ptr-to-resource or by-value resource borrow; (2) Move-mode assign into the result slot for Phase C; (3) move-zero-and-mark when the source is drop-registered. Three call sites — the per-arm loop and else-arm in `lower_match_expr`, plus the same shape in `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` (nested match in arm body) — now route through it. Without consolidation, each site was a parallel implementation of the same boundary rule (Layering-discipline rule 3); the arm-loop site already had the Move-mode + move-zero logic but was missing the clone gate, and the else-arm + nested-match sites had even less.

  This is a strict subset of the eventual Tier 2a fix (typed slot ownership + writer-side validator); the helper is one of the call sites the validator will pin down once it ships. Filed Tier 2a as the next item on the agenda. Fixture: `tests/fixtures/match_arm_borrow_clone.gg`. Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`. Full suite: 1027 unit + 1073 integration.

- [2026-05-10] **Snag #27 — `Option[Box[T]]` field/payload alongside another droppable field tripped the LIR drop-completeness validator (Tier 1a).** Symptom: any struct/enum combining `Option[Box[T]]` with any other droppable content panicked with `Drop completeness: struct "X" has droppable field "outer" (type "Option__Box__T") missing from type_drop_fns field_drops`. Root was Tier 1c coherence-at-construction (`docs/internals/structural-guards.md`): the wrapper got registered with `..Default::default()` metadata (`drop: None, copy: Trivial`) when its inner Box[T] resolved to `UNIT_TYPE` during pre-registration — Box had no handler in `map_ast_type_mut` and fell through. Later, `remonomorphize_enum_fields` fixed the variant field type (Some._0: Unit → Box__T) but did NOT recompute the wrapper's metadata. So Option__Box__T ended up "field is droppable" + "wrapper isn't" — the validator firing on the inconsistency. Also exposed a parallel-implementation smell: `register_builtin_option`/`register_builtin_result` inlined the TypeDef literal with default metadata instead of calling `make_option_type_def`/`make_result_type_def`, silently bypassing any centralised metadata fix.

  Architecturally-aligned fix per Tier 1c (NO name-matching at consumer boundaries):
  1. **`make_option_type_def`/`make_result_type_def`** now take `&TypeRegistry` and compute `(copy_semantics, drop_strategy)` from `registry.needs_drop` of each payload. Coherence-at-construction: the wrapper carries correct metadata at first registration; no reliance on the post-hoc upgrade pass.
  2. **`register_builtin_option`/`register_builtin_result`** — the parallel implementations — collapsed to call the helpers (Rule 3: one source of truth per axis).
  3. **`ensure_option_type_registered`** simplified — its post-hoc upgrade fix-up is no longer needed since the constructor handles it directly.
  4. **`map_ast_type_mut`** gained a Box arm with the same Box-typed metadata as `register_collection_alias` (Resource + Trivial("free") + is_box). Without this, `Box[T]` inner-type resolution at wrapper-arg recursion still returned `UNIT_TYPE`. Mirrors the existing `Box` arm in `register_collection_alias`; both paths exist because field-type pre-registration takes a different entry point than wrapper-arg recursion. Sibling consolidation (collapsing the two paths) is a separate, larger refactor.

  No `field_type_name.starts_with("Box__")` checks were added — the original sketched fix was rejected per `AGENTS.md` "no name matching" rule and Tier 3a. The whole point of the Tier 1a validator firing here is to force the upstream metadata fix.

  Fixture: `tests/fixtures/box_in_recursive_struct.gg` (the minimal repro from the snag report). Files: `src/ir/lowering/types.rs` (helper signatures + Box arm + parallel-impl consolidation), `src/ir/lowering/context.rs` (`ensure_option_type_registered` simplification), `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs` (two `map`/`map_err` Result-rebuild sites updated). Full suite: 1027 unit + 1072 integration.

- [2026-05-10] **Snag #26 — `*box` deref-write was silently dropped (compiled mode); now mutates the heap correctly.** Symptom: `(*b).field = X`, `mutate(&*b)`, and `*b = T(...)` all silently no-op'd. Read-back returned the original value with no warning. Three independent code paths missed the lvalue-through-deref shape: (1) `try_resolve_field_place` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:2024`) didn't handle `Expr::Deref` — `(*b).n = X` fell to `lower_field_assign`'s value-copy fallback, which loaded the heap value into a temp, mutated the temp's field, and discarded. Added an `Expr::Deref` arm that recurses and appends a `Deref` projection. The projection-walk loop also switched from `pointee_type` (handles `Ptr`/`MutPtr` only) to `deref_inner_type` (handles `Box[T]` Named-struct shape too) — without that change, the field lookup landed on `Box__T`'s `_0` field instead of the user's named field. (2) `lower_assign` (`src/ir/lowering/stmts/assigns.rs:393`) had no `Expr::Deref` arm at all — `*b = T(...)` hit the catch-all `_ => { /* not yet supported */ }` and was discarded silently. Added an arm that builds the deref place, computes the pointee type, and routes through `emit_field_store_with_cleanup` (so the old `T` is dropped before the new one is stored — same machinery as struct-field assigns). (3) `lower_call_arg` for `Ownership::MutableBorrow` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs:108`) lowered `&*b` by first loading the heap value into a temp, then borrowing the temp — the callee mutated the discarded copy. Added a Deref-aware fast path that builds the `borrow_mut` through a Deref-projected place so the resulting pointer addresses the heap. (Also added a parallel fast-path in `Expr::MutableBorrow` for standalone `&*b` outside call args.) Fixture `tests/fixtures/box_deref_write.gg` covers all three forms; integration test added. Full suite: 1070/1070.

- [2026-05-09] **Tier 3a name-prefix routing ratchet shipped.** Per `docs/internals/structural-guards.md` §3a. New test in `tests/lints.rs` scans `src/**/*.rs` for `starts_with("X__")` calls where X is a known mangled-type prefix (Vector/Deque/Dict/HashMap/Set/HashSet/Mutex/RWLock/Channel/Shared/Weak/Guard/ReadGuard/WriteGuard/Box/Task/Heap/Tuple/Callable/MutCallable/ConsumeCallable/Option/Result) and asserts the count never exceeds `BUDGET`. Baseline 2026-05-09 = 438 occurrences (438, not 353 — the Rust regex `find_iter` counts occurrences not lines, and several lines have multiple matches). The ratchet is one-directional: count can only DECREASE, never grow. Adding a new layering-discipline-violating `starts_with` site fails the test until the site is migrated to typed metadata OR the budget is intentionally raised with explanation. As migrations land, the budget tightens — every commit that retires a site can drop BUDGET in the same diff to lock in the new floor. Doc comment on the test enumerates the migration playbook (typed `is_trait_box`, `combinator_result_struct_id`, `enum_kind` patterns from recent commits) and the re-derivation command. Box.new is the only shallow-copy heap-allocating consumer in the codebase today. Wired as fatal in `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs:1648` next to Tier 1b's panic — the initial sweep is silent across 1070/1070 integration fixtures, locking the rule that a future shallow-copy heap-allocating consumer can't ship without a paired `move_zero_and_mark`.

- [2026-05-09] **Tier 1a drop-completeness validator shipped** — per `docs/internals/structural-guards.md` §1a. `validate_drop_completeness` in `src/lir/validate.rs:824` walks every entry in `module.type_drop_fns`; for each registered type, it checks that every droppable field of the corresponding `StructDef` appears in the entry's `field_drops` (struct case) or `enum_variants` (enum case). Droppability is determined LIR-locally (no GIR access): a `LirType::Struct(sid)` is droppable iff (a) its name has its own `type_drop_fns` entry, (b) it's a runtime resource (`GorgetString`/`GorgetArray`/`GorgetMap`/`GorgetSet`/`GorgetClosure`), (c) it has a `c_runtime_alias` to one of those, or (d) it's a `Box__T`. Primitive LIR types (I64/Bool/Ptr/...) are non-droppable. Wired into the `VALIDATORS` registry at `validate.rs:81` so it runs after every LIR pass via `assert_module_valid` (debug builds + release with `GG_VALIDATE_PASSES`). Four unit tests cover: complete struct accepted, missing struct field detected (the snag #24 class), complete enum accepted, missing variant payload detected. Full integration suite 1070/1070 — the validator is silent on every existing fixture, locking the contract that future LIR-lowering bugs which forget to register a droppable field/variant payload halt the build instead of leaking at runtime.
  Files: `src/lir/validate.rs` (validator + 4 unit tests).

- [2026-05-09] **Tier 1a unblocker — Option/Result skip in third-pass `populate_recursive_drop_structs` removed.** Lines 599 and 650 of `src/lir/lower/mod.rs` skipped `Option__/Result__` field types when populating `type_drop_fns` — the parent struct's drop fn would silently leave Option/Result fields un-dropped, requiring downstream code to compensate (or just leak). Snag #24 (commits earlier this session, in main: tag-reset on `__option_unwrap` + value-2 sentinel + Option/Result skip removal from passes 1 + 2 of `populate_recursive_drop_structs`) made Option/Result correctly drop their payloads on scope exit; Snag #25c (commit `20722a78`, expected_type propagation through enum variant constructor args) and Snag #25b (commit `cbcc7478`, array literal Owned + drop-registered) closed the type-mismatch and literal-leak issues that masked the third-pass skip; Snag #25d (commit `8583bccc`, match-scrutinee drop transfer at last-use) closed the named-scrutinee-aliasing issue. With those landed, removing the third-pass skip is now safe — every parent struct whose Option/Result fields hold resource payloads now correctly drops them. - [2026-05-09] **Snag #25d — match-scrutinee aliasing for named owned resource local at last-use: drop transferred to scrutinee.** Sharp repro: `auto r = parse(...); match r: case Ok(fm): assert fm.es5id.unwrap() == "..."` double-freed in the bind-then-match path while `match parse(...): case Ok(fm): ...` (direct, unnamed scrutinee) worked. Both forms are semantically identical at the language level — the difference was that the named `r` triggered the `is_named_local && needs_drop` skip in `stage_match_scrutinee` (`src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs:65`), leaving the source's drop registered. The match arm's `unwrap()` zeroed only the scrutinee's variant tag (LIR `Move` is memcpy-without-zero, so source and scrutinee aliased the resource fields), and the source's scope-exit drop double-freed what unwrap had already extracted. Fix: thread `source_at_last_use: bool` through `stage_match_scrutinee` (computed via `is_last_use_at(name, scrutinee.span)` at all three call sites — `stmts/patterns.rs:153`, `exprs/mod.rs:2210`, `exprs/mod.rs:2755`); when true for a named owned source, transfer drop tracking from source to scrutinee (no `move_zero` — `tag_of source` reads the source after the staging assign and needs the data intact). Also fitted test/bench/suite-setup/suite-teardown function builders with `compute_function_liveness` (they had been missing, so `is_last_use_at` returned false → conservative no-transfer → an earlier unconditional fix attempt broke `self_host_bootstrap` because it transferred even for non-last-use named locals; conditional + liveness keeps the not-at-last-use case intact for self-host's match-named-then-reuse patterns). Fixture `tests/fixtures/test_option_resource_field.gg` extended with `match_direct_arm_unwrap` + `match_bound_arm_unwrap` regression tests (both pass; before fix, the bound version crashed with `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`). Full suite: 1070/1070.

Restructured to a single `if let Some(sz) = opaque_runtime_size(type_name) { return sz; }` call between the BuiltinTypeProtocol-alias path and the recursive `Tuple__`/`Option__` paths. Two layering benefits: (1) one source of truth for runtime-struct sizes (`opaque_runtime_size`), (2) `c_runtime_alias`-tagged structs now read their alias's typed `computed_c_size` rather than hardcoded values. ~30 lines removed; behavior preserved bit-for-bit. **Out of scope:** `opaque_runtime_size` itself still has prefix-match arms for `Vector__/Dict__/Set__/Box__/Guard__/Task__/Mutex__/...` — eliminating those requires plumbing `module.struct_aliases` through `c_sizeof_with_structs`'s call chain so monomorphized alias names resolve to their target StructDef's `computed_c_size`.
