- [2026-05-09] **Snag #25c (partial) — cross-module `Option[String]` in enum variant: type mismatch / size disagreement fixed.** Symptom: `R2.A(Some(s))` (where `s: String`) lowered the inner `Some(s)` to `Option__T<n>` (a 16-byte struct with `Some_0: *GorgetString` payload) instead of `Option__GorgetString` (a 40-byte struct with `Some_0: GorgetString` payload). The outer `R2.A(...)` then memcpy'd 40 bytes from a 16-byte source — `[-Wstringop-overread]` warning + UB at runtime. Cross-module exposure made the size disagreement visible (both `Option__T<n>` and `Option__GorgetString` got registered, with different layouts), but the bug also fired in single-file code (silently overreading stack memory). Root cause: enum variant constructor lowering paths (qualified `R2.A(...)` in `methods.rs`, bare and effective-name in `calls.rs`) didn't propagate `expected_type` to per-arg lowering. `Some(s)` therefore inferred its Option type from the operand type of `s` (a `*GorgetString` borrow param) instead of the variant slot type. Fix in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs:154-169` and `src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs:923-980`: pre-resolve the variant's field types from `TypeRegistry::get_type_def(enum_name).kind == Enum`, then thread each field type as `ctx.func_state.expected_type` while lowering the corresponding arg. `Some` resolution at `mod.rs:1264` now sees `expected_type == Option__GorgetString` and registers the correct concrete type instead of falling through to `format_type_for_mangle(Ptr<String>) → T<n>`. Full suite: 1070/1070. **Residual:** the same Repro 2 (`match r: case R2.A(s): s.unwrap()`) still double-frees because the match scrutinee staging memcpy-aliases the named source's resource fields; unwrap zeros the scrutinee's tag but the source's drop frees the same payload. Filed in TODO as Snag #25d (match-scrutinee aliasing for named owned resource locals).

- [2026-05-09] **Snag #25b — `Vector` literal in `Some(...)` / struct field init silently cloned-then-leaked.** Symptoms: `Option[Vector[int]] x = Some([1, 2, 3])` allocated the literal Vector, then `clone_resource_args_for_init` saw the temp's ownership as `Untracked` and emitted `gorget_array_clone` into the Option payload, orphaning the original buffer (64 bytes leaked per literal). The same shape applied to nested literals (`[[1,2,3], ...]`) and struct field assignment from a literal. Root cause: `lower_array_literal` called `gorget_array_new` for the literal's outer `GorgetArray` but did NOT tag the resulting local as `LocalOwnership::Owned` and did NOT register it for scope-exit drop — comprehensions had this pair, array literals didn't. Fix in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/collections.rs`: (1) added `ctx.set_owned(builder, arr_local)` + `ctx.drops.register_local(arr_local, array_type, &ctx.type_registry)` after both `gorget_array_new` calls in `lower_array_literal` (non-empty + empty branches); (2) added `move_zero_and_mark` after each per-element `assign_mode(Move, elem_local, ...)` so the now drop-registered source temp doesn't double-free with the array's elem_drop on scope exit (issue surfaced by `tests/fixtures/vector_of_vectors.gg` which builds nested Vectors). The LIR backend elides the actual `MoveZero` emit when liveness proves the source is unobservable. Fixture `tests/fixtures/test_option_resource_field.gg` extended with `option_vector_literal_into_some` regression test. Set literals share the array literal lowering path (parser maps `{a, b, c}` → `Expr::ArrayLiteral`), so this fix covers them too. Full suite: 1070/1070.

- [2026-05-09] **Snag #25 — `Option[String]/Option[Resource]` is_some()/is_none() always returning wrong result in `gg test` mode — fixed by adding `flush_ownership_to_locals` to test/bench/suite function builders.** Root cause: `lower_test_items` and `lower_bench_items` in `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs` called `builder.build()` without first calling `ctx.flush_ownership_to_locals(&mut builder)`. Every regular function lowering path in `functions.rs` calls `flush_ownership_to_locals` to derive `slot_kind` from `(type, ownership)` — `Ptr/MutPtr + is_ref()` → `BorrowedPtr`, `Ptr/MutPtr + !is_ref` → `OwnedPtr`, non-Ptr → `Value`. Without this call, all locals in test functions started with `slot_kind: Value` (the default). When `FieldLoad` of an `Option[String]` field produced a local with type `Ptr(Option__GorgetString)` and ownership `Borrowed { origin: Field { ... } }` (set by `set_field_borrow`), the `slot_kind` stayed `Value` instead of upgrading to `BorrowedPtr`. In `lower_place_addr`, the `is_ref_local` check reads `slot_kind == BorrowedPtr` (§6.8 Stage 4 signal); with `Value`, it fell to the else branch and emitted `SlotAddr` (address of the stack slot) instead of `SlotLoad` (the field pointer value). The subsequent `Borrow` instruction stored this stack address into another slot; `__option_is_some` dereferenced it and read pointer bytes as the tag — always garbage. In run mode (`gg build`/`gg run`), the SSA optimizer happened to eliminate the dead intermediate slot store, collapsing the borrow chain to a direct load, which masked the underlying bug. Fix: added `ctx.flush_ownership_to_locals(&mut builder)` before `builder.build()` at all four build sites in `lower_test_items` (suite setup, suite teardown, test functions) and `lower_bench_items`. Files: `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs`. Added regression fixture: `tests/fixtures/test_option_resource_field.gg`.

- [2026-05-09] **Snag #24 — `Option/Result[Resource]` double-free on unwrap — root cause found and fixed; Option/Result skip removed from `populate_recursive_drop_structs`.** The double-free in `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` was caused by `__option_unwrap`/`__result_unwrap` LIR lowering performing a shallow `FieldPtr + Load` of the payload WITHOUT resetting the Option/Result tag afterward. When the source struct (e.g., a cloned `Stmt` with `SReturn(Option[SpannedExpr])`) was later dropped via the now-unblocked `Option__SpannedExpr__drop`, it tried to free already-freed memory. Fix: added `FieldPtr(field=0) + Store(i32 2)` after payload extraction in all three `__option_unwrap` code paths in `lir/lower/insts.rs`. Tag value 2 is out-of-range for both Option (2 variants: 0=Some, 1=None) and Result (2 variants: 0=Ok, 1=Err), so the drop switch falls through and skips the payload — effectively a consumed-sentinel. With the double-free fixed, the Option/Result skip in `populate_recursive_drop_structs` (`lir/lower/mod.rs`) was safely removed from both the struct-field path and the enum-variant path. Verified with valgrind (zero errors) and full suite (1068/1068 tests pass).

  Final architecture: decision made once in `methods.rs` (`ctx.type_registry.is_resource_type(inner_type)`), encoded as `Operand::Move` on the borrow arg (vs `Operand::Copy` for non-resource payloads), read in `insts.rs` as `matches!(args[0], Operand::Move(_))`. No drop-registry lookup in the LIR. Applies to unwrap / unwrap_or / expect / unwrap_error on both Option and Result.

  Files: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs`, `src/lir/lower/insts.rs`, `src/lir/lower/mod.rs` (skip removal + indentation fix), `TODO.md` (Snag #24 entry removed).

Dict is insertion-order-preserving after the fix. Inner-vector update uses the rebuild-from-scratch pattern (same as `compute_predecessors`) to avoid the `get().push()` mutation-loss issue with nested collections.

ASan-built driver gave a clean trail: `gorget_map_free` first call from `GirModule__drop` (driver.c:8978), second call from `TypeTable__drop` (driver.c:8914) on the same heap block. The shared map: `meta_aliases`, originally allocated by `TypeTable.new_type_table()`, then transferred via `Dict[String, String] meta_aliases = types.meta_aliases` (Site #1 pattern!) and finally `!meta_aliases` into `GirModule(...)`. With the probe, the typed binding is a Ptr-typed Field-borrow; `Expr::Move` zeros the 8-byte Ptr local; the StructInit Move-sigil branch then does `load_ref` on the Ptr — taking a shallow copy of the Dict bytes and storing them in the field. Net: `types.meta_aliases` and `gmod.meta_aliases` both end up pointing at the same heap allocation. Both drop. Bang.

  **Diagnosis: the consumer bug was at `lower_struct_init`'s Move-sigil branch (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:1636`).** None of the three originally-suspected sites (`flush_ownership_to_locals`, C-LIR f-string deref, `is_pure_borrow_for`) were the culprit — the bug was in the StructInit boundary, where an `Expr::Move`-sourced Ptr-typed local was unconditionally `load_ref`'d on the assumption that `Expr::Move`'s pre-init `move_zero_and_mark` had invalidated the source. That assumption holds only for `is_owning_param` (a `!`-sigil param whose param slot pointed at caller-owned bytes); for any other Ptr-typed local, the MoveZero only blanks the 8-byte Ptr local while the source struct field / collection element / parameter cell still owns the bytes — `load_ref` aliases them.

  **Fix: tighten the Move-sigil-at-StructInit branch to require `is_owning_param`** on the source local. Other Ptr-typed locals fall through to `ensure_owned_at_boundary`, which clones the pointee into a fresh owned value (the right action when the source doesn't own). The pre-existing `!self`-on-equip-method tests (`consuming_self.gg`, `async_drop.gg`, `consuming_self_loop_error.gg`) hit the `is_owning_param=true` branch and pass unchanged.

  **Propagation.** With the consumer fix in place, the probe replaces the eager-clone branch with `set_field_borrow` propagation when (a) source is a Field-borrow Ptr local, (b) the inner pointee is a resource type (the optimisation only matters for heap-owning types), (c) the loop-safe predicate accepts (`is_cow_unsafe_at` rejects reassignment-on-forward-path). - [2026-05-06] **JS-interpreter porting feedback round 6: snag #12 + latent extern-signature bug.** Reporter's snag was "match-as-expression breaks codegen when the value type is a struct with resource fields and one arm diverges via `exit(...)`". Two-layer root cause + fix:

  **Layer 1 — extern function signatures weren't registered with the typechecker.** `register_signatures_recursive` in `typecheck.rs` only walked `Item::Function` and `Item::Equip`; `Item::ExternBlock` items had FunctionInfo built in `resolve.rs` but their `def.type_id` was never set to a `ResolvedType::Function`. `Expr::Identifier("exit")` returned `def.type_id` → `None` → `error_id`; the Call-resolution branch then fell into `ResolvedType::Error`, returning `error_id` as the call's result type. `error_id` unifies with anything (`unify`'s "Error type unifies with anything" early return), so void-vs-Big arm-type mismatches in match-as-expression silently slipped through to the IR layer, where the lowerer trusted the type and emitted a struct-init from an int slot. One-line fix: add an `Item::ExternBlock` arm to `register_signatures_recursive` that calls `register_function_signature` per inner function. Net surface: 5 lines. **Latent fixture exposed:** `regex_basic.gg` declared `Option[Match] conv_m = regex_find(...)` but the extern was `extern Result[Match, String] regex_find(...)`. The runtime `gorget_regex_find_pat` actually returns a plain `Match` with `.start = -1` as the no-match sentinel — Option semantics. The Result extern was a misdeclaration; pre-fix the type mismatch was silently swallowed because `regex_find`'s declared signature itself never reached the typechecker (extern signatures unregistered). Restructured `lib/xtd/regex.gg`: extern is now `extern Match _regex_find_pat_raw(...)`, and a Gorget wrapper `Option[Match] regex_find(String pattern, String subject)` mirrors `Regex.find()`'s sentinel→Option conversion.

  **Layer 2 — `noreturn` qualifier on extern functions.** With layer 1 in place the typechecker now correctly rejects `case Error(_): exit(2)` with "expected Big, found void" — clear error vs. broken codegen, but the reporter's preferred match-expression form still didn't compile. Added an `is_noreturn: bool` field on `FunctionQualifiers` (mirroring `is_async`/`is_blocking`) and a `Keyword::Noreturn` to the lexer. Parser's qualifier loop accepts `noreturn` like the others. Propagates to `FunctionInfo.is_noreturn` in `resolve.rs` (3 init sites). Typecheck's Call-resolution branch returns `never_id` instead of the declared return type when the callee's `FunctionInfo.is_noreturn` is true; `unify(Big, Never)` already returns `Big` via the existing Never-unifies-with-anything rule. IR lowering tracks `noreturn_fns: FxHashSet<String>` on `LoweringContext`, populated from both top-level and `ExternBlock` items (insert both the Gorget name and the C symbol so the c_symbol-resolved `call_name` lookup hits). After the call's post-cleanup, emits `builder.unreachable()` so the basic block terminates correctly — the match-expr lowerer's `is_terminated()` guard then skips the bogus arm-value assign. **Stdlib:** `lib/std/os.gg`'s `extern void exit(int code) = "gorget_exit"` becomes `extern noreturn void exit(int code)`. (Panic stays out of scope — it's a hardcoded builtin in the IR, not a Gorget extern declaration; filed as follow-up TODO.)

  **C output before / after** (Error-arm body of `Big b = match make(): case Ok(p): p case Error(_): exit(2)`):
  ```c
  // before — type-mismatched arm assign that the C compiler warns / errors on
  gorget_exit(__v54);
  __v55 = (int32_t)0LL;
  __s4 = (__gg_Big){ .x = __v55 };  // Big.x is Option[String], not int32_t
  goto __bb1;
  // after
  gorget_exit(__v54);
  __builtin_unreachable();
  ```

  Fixture `match_expr_diverging_arm.gg` exercises three shapes: (a) struct-with-resource-field arm + diverging `exit` arm, (b) multi-statement arm body alongside a diverging else, (c) int-typed match value with diverging else. Files touched: `src/lexer/token.rs`, `src/parser/{ast,mod}.rs`, `src/semantic/{resolve,typecheck}.rs`, `src/ir/lowering/{context,mod,exprs/calls}.rs`, `lib/std/os.gg`, `lib/xtd/regex.gg`.

- [2026-05-06] **JS-interpreter porting feedback round 5: snags #10 + #11.** (Snag #9 — `String.len()` codepoint-vs-byte semantics — confirmed by-design per Python/Swift precedent; not a fix.)

  **#10 — `std.process.exec_output` doesn't capture stderr.** `gorget_exec_output` was built on `popen(cmd, "r")` which only opens a pipe for stdout — the function hardcoded `result.errors = ""` and child stderr fell through to the parent's stderr because no pipe redirected it. The API contract (`ExecResult.errors` populated cleanly, no parent-stderr leak) was broken at the runtime level. Replaced with manual fork + two pipes (stdout + stderr) + `execl("/bin/sh", "-c", cmd, NULL)`. The parent uses `poll()` on both pipe fds in non-blocking mode so a busy stream on one side doesn't deadlock the parent waiting on the other; both buffers grow on demand; EINTR retried in both poll and read loops. Includes `<poll.h>` + `<fcntl.h>` scoped to `PROCESS_RUNTIME` so the preamble doesn't bloat for programs that don't use `std.process`. Fixture `exec_output_captures_stderr.gg`. Commit `a8e0dc63`.

  **#11 — `match` as expression with multi-statement arm bodies.** Pre-fix, `T x = match scrutinee: case Pattern:\n    stmts...\n    return` was rejected by the parser ("expected expression, found NEWLINE"). The parser supported single-line arm bodies in expression-form match (`T x = match n: case 0: 0 case 1: 1 else: 2`) but not the multi-line shape natural in `let-style` Rust/ML idioms. Asymmetric — return-position match-expressions worked because their arms were single-line by construction.

  Three layered fixes: (a) **Parser** — `parse_match_expr` routes arm bodies through `parse_arm_body`, the same helper match-statement arms already use; accepts inline expressions or indented blocks (wrapped as `Expr::Block`). (b) **Typechecker** — `Expr::Block` returns `Never` when the block's last statement is divergent (return/throw/break/continue), so `unify` composes a divergent arm with the match's overall value type; closure return-type inference skips a `body_type == Never` classification and falls back to `closure_ret_var` (the Stmt::Return handler already unified it correctly), without which the parser's destructure-desugar `Block { ..., Return(expr) }` would mis-specialize tuple-destructured closures as `Closure[Never(...)]` — caught by the `closure_tuple_destructure` regression during integration. (c) **IR lowering** — `lower_match_expr` seeds `result_local` with `func_state.expected_type` when the surrounding context provides one (VarDecl `T x = match …`, struct field init, return-position match); without this the slot was sized as I64 and corrupted struct/String/Vector arms. Type refines further when the first non-divergent arm produces a concrete type. Arm-value flows into the result slot use `AssignMode::Move` so Phase C's resource-move validator doesn't flag a shallow copy of an owned arm value. Fixture `match_expr_block_arms.gg`. Commit `772ac585`.

  **#6 — `gg sim test` runtime gap on `gorget_string_clone_to_owned`.** The native runtime distinguishes view (cap=0) vs owned (cap>0) String shapes; the CoW machinery emits `gorget_string_clone_to_owned` (and `gorget_string_copy_cow` / `_borrow` / `_materialize_inplace` / `_clone_inplace`) at boundary materialization sites.   **#7 — false `unused import T` warning when T was used only as a type annotation.** Pre-fix, `from X import T` produced a false unused-import warning when `T` appeared only in type-position (function param types, var declarations, return types, struct/enum fields, generic args) — never as an `Expr::Identifier` constructor call. Root cause: `resolution_map` (the resolver's name → DefId map) is populated only by expression-position uses; type annotations are never walked. The unused-import check at `safety/mod.rs` reads `resolution_map.values()` to compute used DefIds, so any import used only in type position appeared unused. The bug was *partially* hidden because struct/enum types are usually constructed somewhere in the project (the constructor call IS an `Expr::Identifier`), but surfaces when no constructor exists in-project — e.g. when values flow from extern sources or hidden constructors. Fix: new `collect_used_type_def_ids` walker in `safety/validation.rs` walks every `Type` annotation reachable from module items (function params/return/throws, struct/enum fields, var decls, type aliases, const/static types, equip target+trait, closure params, rethrow binding) and resolves each `Type::Named` to its DefId. Resolved DefIds union into `used_def_ids` before the unused-import check runs. Uses the shared `ExprVisitor` framework for stmt/expr recursion (compile-time exhaustiveness for new variants); the type-shape recursion is hand-rolled (8 Type variants). Confirmed: the previously-broken case stops warning; genuinely-unused imports still warn. Commit `90c2610b`. 1060/1060 integration green.

- [2026-05-05] **Dict[K, Callable] `.get().unwrap()` double-free fixed (security-flagged from 2026-04-28).** `Dict.get()` returns `Option[V]` by value, unlike `Vector.get()` which returns `Option[Ref[V]]`. With `needs_drop=true` for Callable types after the deep-clone work landed, the unwrap result of `Dict[K, Callable].get()` shared its `env` pointer with the Dict slot — both sites tried to free the same allocation → double-free. **Fix at the LIR lift layer.** `resource_clone_fn_for_payload` in `src/lir/lower/lifts.rs` already deep-cloned every other resource type (`GorgetArray`, `GorgetMap`, `GorgetSet`, `GorgetString`); `GorgetClosure` was missing from the dispatch table. Added one match arm (`"GorgetClosure" => Some("gorget_closure_clone_to_owned".into())`). The Option now owns a fresh independent env; both sites' free calls hit distinct allocations. Mirrors the index-syntax (`d[k]`) path which already deep-cloned via `clone_fn_for_collection_element`. Per the layering discipline: the asymmetry that created the bug LIVED at the lift layer where every other resource was being deep-cloned but closures weren't — closing the gap at the upstream layer is the right move, not adding IR-level CowBorrow workarounds (option c) or changing `Dict.get`'s return shape (option a). Three notable findings during the fix: (1) **`.clone()` on Callable was a red herring** — the underlying bug fired identically without `.clone()`. The companion fixture `dict_callable_get_no_clone.gg` confirms the lift-layer was the issue, not user-level cloning. (2) **Set[Callable] is theoretical only** — Set has no `Option[V]`-returning API surface (`.contains()` returns `bool`); the same lift-shape can't fire there today. The TODO's claim was architectural, not actively reachable. (3) **`Channel.recv()` is unaffected** — its GIR-level return is `ret_elem`, not `Option__T`, so the lift doesn't fire. C: 1061/1061. LLVM: 1058/1058 (sequential, ~21 min). Reproducer BEFORE: `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`. AFTER: `2\n11\ndone`. Two new fixtures (`dict_callable_get_clone.gg`, `dict_callable_get_no_clone.gg`) lock in regression coverage. Related: this added the **seventh** explicit "Callable types still don't have TypeDef registration today" fallback site — Phase A residual #1 in TODO.md updated to flag the growing pattern. Commits: `a4fec466` (agent worktree) → `8ae2d351` (cherry-picked).

- [2026-05-05] **Phase D4: `LocalOwnership::SharedHeap { source }` variant landed (narrow additive shape) — diagnostic + foundation for `string_borrow_sources` retirement.** Two prior attempts (commits `63f7277e` and the post-revert retry on `gorget-2`) failed self_host_bootstrap with the same symptom: stage1.c emitted `ParseError__Empty()` as undefined function call instead of inline struct literal. Both attempts widened `views_of_source` to include SharedHeap targets — that's the load-bearing change. This attempt isolated the regression with a probe-by-probe additive shape: variant + `set_shared_heap` writer in Branch A + sidecar kept + reader unchanged + `views_of_source` left UN-widened. Result: 1056/1056 integration green, self_host_bootstrap + fixed_point pass (303s, 651s sweeps respectively). Root cause finally pinpointed: `cow_before_mutation` Case 4 (`context.rs:2292`) calls `views_of_source(local)` and runs `cow_materialize_view` on every result. SharedHeap targets are NOT cap=0 byte-views — they're 32-byte struct copies whose heap was already deep-cloned at `gorget_string_copy_cow` (the C runtime allocs when source is owned). Forcing `cow_materialize_view` on them emits a second clone-to-owned + a fresh slot rebind, which shifted slot indices in `lir_codegen___emit_call_extern_with` so that subsequent `evp_contains(&m, ev_name)` runtime lookups missed and the variant constructor path emitted "function call" fallbacks. Files: `src/ir/{mod.rs (+SharedHeap variant, +is_ref skip), lowering/{context.rs (+set_shared_heap, +rationale comment on views_of_source non-widening), stmts/mod.rs (Branch A writes both shapes, Owned-propagate skip for SharedHeap)}}`. Net: +60 lines (mostly comments documenting the diagnostic). Sidecar retained at this point — completed by the next 3 commits.

- [2026-05-05] **Snag #8 (heap corruption on move-into-field across alternative branches) and its sibling (chained-if move-into-field) both closed via the CoW 3-way rule.** Two layered fixes:

  **(1) Branch-local `maybe_moved` tracking** for if/elif/else and match. The pre-fix `drops.is_moved` was a function-wide flag — when `lower_if` lowered the then-branch first and called `mark_moved(items)`, the elif-branch's lowering then saw `is_moved(items) == true` and skipped emitting `move_zero` in `emit_field_store_with_cleanup`. At runtime, only the elif path ran → `_items`'s slot was never zeroed AND `f.b` aliased the same heap buffer → double-free at scope exit (`gorget_string_free invariant: cap=... but alloc=NULL`). Added `snapshot_moved` / `restore_moved` / `union_moved` to `DropElaborator`, wired snapshot-restore-union around each branch in `lower_if` and `lower_match_stmt`. Each branch now sees the same pre-branch view; the post-join state is the conservative union (any-branch-moved → moved). Mirrors the borrow-checker's branch-merging semantics. Fixture `move_across_branches.gg` covers if/elif, if/else, three-way if/elif/else, match, and matched-first-branch sanity.

  **(2) Field-assign routed through the CoW 3-way rule.** Field-assign was the only consuming-position site that didn't apply the auto-move/auto-clone/explicit-! rule documented in `docs/internals/copy-on-write.md` §"Ownership Transfer". Every other site (push/put/set/insert/send/v[i]=x, struct init, enum variant init) already routed through `ensure_owned_at_consuming_arg` or `clone_multi_use_resource_args`. `clone_ptr_rhs_if_needed` (the field-store wrapper) only handled Ptr/borrow shapes — missed the live-source-named-local case. Switched to `ensure_owned_at_consuming_arg` (same helper as push/put/set), which adds the `!is_last_use_at(name, span)` check. Result: `f.a = items` auto-clones if `items` is live past the field-store, auto-moves at last use; `f.a = !items` forces a move; `f.a = items.clone()` is redundant but accepted. The user-reported "Compiler internal panic" (`f.a = items; print(items)` → `local _N read after MoveZero` GIR validation panic) and the chained-if heap corruption both fall out — both are now silent auto-clones. Per design ("Rust-grade safety without lifetime-style explicit-move noise"). Fixture `field_store_auto_clones_live_source.gg` covers all six 3-way rule shapes.

  **(2.5) Liveness pass walks f-string interpolation expressions.** Surfaced while validating fix (2): `Expr::StringLiteral(_, interp_exprs)` carries the parsed interpolation sub-expressions in its second field, but `liveness.rs:246` ignored that field — `Expr::StringLiteral(_, _) => {}`. Any local referenced ONLY inside an f-string interpolation was invisible to `is_last_use_at`, so the new auto-clone rule mistakenly auto-moved sources that were still live in a following f-string. Test case: `f.a = items; print(f"items={items.get(0).unwrap()}")` — pre-fix was a `read after MoveZero` panic; post-fix auto-clones correctly.

  **README updated** to surface the 3-way rule under "Ownership without lifetime annotations" — was previously only in `docs/internals/copy-on-write.md` and `AGENTS.md`, easy to miss at the entry point. The compiler contract is now discoverable in 30 seconds; `--show-clones` is mentioned as the audit hook.

  Closes the original snag #8 from the JS-interpreter porting feedback AND the user's "Compiler internal panic (likely related to #8)" report — same root cause, different manifestation. 1058/1058 integration green.

- [2026-05-05] **Audit of redesign-around-gap fixtures: 2 of 3 documented "bugs" turned out to be silently fixed; 1 is live.** Following the §6.6 process work and the new `feedback_no_designing_around_gaps.md` memory, did a sweep for fixtures whose comments admit working around a compiler gap. Three concrete patterns surfaced; three parallel worktree-isolated agents wrote regression fixtures for each. Findings:

  **(1) `Dict[K, Option[V]].len()` codegen bug — silently fixed.** `tests/fixtures/test_collections_nested_advanced.gg:59` had `# use keys().len() as workaround for Dict.len() codegen bug with Option value type` since commit `7b5e6d17` (2026-03-11). Direct `scores.len()` call is correct on every variant tried — `Option[int]`, `Option[String]`, `Option[Vector[int]]`, with int keys, with overwrites/removes/empties, on both C and LLVM backends. ~8 weeks of LIR / CoW / drop-insertion / ownership work between the workaround and today; no single "fix Dict.len" commit, just general drift toward correctness. New fixture `tests/fixtures/dict_len_option_value.gg` exercises the four Option-value-type variants as a regular passing `#[test]` (not `#[ignore]`'d — agent correctly diverged from the brief, since `#[ignore]`-ing a passing test would let the bug regress silently). Workaround comment in `test_collections_nested_advanced.gg` updated to point at the new ground-truth fixture. Commit: `3305eeda`.

  **(2) `gorget_array_clone` shallow-copy leak in for-loops — silently fixed.** `tests/fixtures/leak_for_loop.gg` header claimed "for-loop over Vector[String] and nested Vector[Vector[int]] have known leaks — gorget_array_clone does shallow copy, so element drops on the clone would corrupt the original. Tracked in TODO.md." (it wasn't.) The fixture body deliberately only iterated `Vector[int]` (the non-leaky case), avoiding the shapes the header named. Investigation: `gorget_array_clone` is now deep-clone via per-element `elem_clone` hooks; copies `elem_drop`/`elem_clone`/`elem_materialize` and iterates calling `elem_clone` on each slot — no double-free, no leak. Coverage of the `Vector[String]` and nested cases already lives in `leak_known_patterns.gg` P3/P4, which assert `leaked=false` cleanly. So the gap doesn't exist anymore *and* its coverage already lives elsewhere — header cleaned up to drop the misleading "Tracked in TODO.md" claim, no new fixture added (would be duplicate of P3/P4).   **Meta-finding (the part most worth remembering).** Two of three documented "redesign-around-gap" patterns turned out to be **stale workaround comments outliving the actual fix** — the bug was real when the workaround was written, got fixed by general drift later, but the comment + the redesigned fixture stayed in place. The redesigned fixture became the canonical idiom (`scores.keys().len()` instead of `scores.len()`), surviving long after its justification disappeared. Concrete reinforcement of the `feedback_no_designing_around_gaps.md` principle: even when the redesign was "innocent" at the time, the artifact (the workaround code, the ignored fixture) acquires inertia. The fix is to write a proper failing fixture *at the time of the redesign*, so the next pass over the code has a clear regression-test gate to flip rather than archaeology to do. [Audit: 2026-05-05.]

- [2026-05-05] **Universal `!`-param drop-at-exit leak fixed.** Every `!` resource parameter that the function didn't transfer onward (via a consuming call, push/put, return-`!x`, etc.) was leaking — the GIR drop accountant's `register_param` excluded Move-semantics resources with the rationale "already tracked via VarDecl/body mechanisms," but `!` params have no VarDecl, so the exclusion was unconditional. Fix is layered with the §8.1 dataflow-init work: typed `is_owning_param: bool` field on `Local` (the cross-layer signal — no name-matching, no sidecar map); `register_owning_param` emits a `DropIfAlive` guard at function exit gated by the existing LIR drop-flag dataflow (the flag flips false at every Move-source from the param's slot, true at the entry block, and the elaborator emits the drop only on paths where it's still true). Subtle fallout fixed at the `Expr::Move(!x)` lowering site: `!x` was memcpy'ing into a temp without zeroing the source param's slot, which combined with the new exit drop produced double-frees in transfer-to-recipient cases (`v.push(!s)`, `Some(!r)`, `outer(!r) → inner(!r)`). The `Expr::Move` path now emits `MoveZero` on the source slot in lockstep with the temp creation. Three previously-passing tests had their expected output updated — `drop_flag_param_seed.gg` (the canonical `!` test that the §8.1 agent had redesigned around this very gap), `drop_loop_reinit.gg`, `drop_match_partial_init.gg` — all locked in `consume X` with no following `drop X`, all now emit the drop. The new regression fixture `owning_param_drop_at_exit.gg` covers 6 shapes (simple no-transfer / conditional consume both branches / chained transfer / early-return both branches) and was unignored. **No name-matching introduced** — every transfer site is identified via existing typed signals (`Ownership::Move`, `is_owning_param`, `is_param_borrow_unique`, `has_consuming_self`); the bit of typed metadata at the GIR/LIR boundary is the only new shape. **Cross-layer surface:** 16 files touched — `src/ir/mod.rs` (the new field), `lowering/{drops,functions,closures,traits,context,exprs/mod,exprs/calls,stmts/mod}.rs` (registration + transfer-site `MoveZero` emission), `src/lir/lower/drops.rs` (slot-addr-based guard so the drop-flag elaborator can swap to a bool flag), plus `is_owning_param: false` propagation through every other `Local` constructor. C: 1057/1057 in 690s. LLVM: 1057/1057 in 449s. Lib: 1009/1009. Commit: `837817cd`. (Bug surfaced 2026-05-04 by §8.1 agent during the drop-flag dataflow init work; scope corrected 2026-05-05 from "conditional-consume" to "universal" with a targeted fixture; fixed same day. **Why it slipped through historically:** most uses of `!` in the suite are runtime-collection ops where the runtime helper handles the drop; the canonical user-defined-`!`-recipient test had been redesigned around the gap, locking in the buggy output as "expected"; `leak_*`/`stress_*` heap-accounting tests use `&` borrows and locals exclusively.)

- [2026-05-04] **Snag #4b silent `Some(literal)` field-store fixed.** `fm.desc = Some("hello")` where `desc: Option[String]` was a silent no-op — the field-store wrote only the Some_0 payload bytes into the destination Option slot, leaving the discriminant tag at None=0. `fm.desc.is_some()` returned false right after the assign. Root cause was in `try_enum_payload_extract` (`src/lir/lower/operands.rs:642`), the LIR auto-unwrap shortcut for `T x = some_option_returning_call()`. The function read `gir_func.locals[dst.local].type_id` to decide if dst was non-Option, but `dst.local` is the BASE local of a projection — for `_1.0 = copy _3` where `_1` is FM and `_1.0` is the Option-typed `desc` field, the base type is FM (not Option), so the function fired the payload-extract path and emitted FieldPtr(Some_0) + Load — a 16-byte Str copy into a 40-byte Option slot, leaving the tag at 0. Fix: `let dst_type_id = self.effective_place_type(dst);` instead of `gir_func.locals[dst_idx].type_id` — `effective_place_type` already walks projections for exactly this purpose. No name-matching introduced (the layering was the bug, not a missing list). Fixture `tests/fixtures/option_result_field_store.gg` exercises Some/None/Ok/Error field-stores, projection chains (`outer.inn.v = ...`), and local Option reassignment. 1055/1055 integration green with `GG_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECS=600` (initial 1052/1054 was load-induced flakiness on the self-host driver build, not a regression from the fix). Commits: `0387e803` (fix), `2829b101` (fixture+harness wiring). [Snag #4b from JS-interpreter porting feedback, surfaced 2026-05-01.]

- [2026-05-04] **LIR optimizer converges to true fixpoint instead of a hard 3-iteration cap.** `optimize_function` previously capped at `MAX_ITERS=3` with a fixpoint check that only looked at `(blocks.len(), inst_count)`. Passes that rewrite values without changing either count — `fold_constants`, `simplify_algebraic`, `propagate_copies` — unblock downstream DCE/CSE on the next iteration; the narrow snapshot missed that progress and stopped early on any function still making progress at iteration 3. - [2026-05-04] **Mutex double-lock detected at compile time.** `Guard[int] g1 = m.lock(); Guard[int] g2 = m.lock()` was previously accepted by the borrow checker and would deadlock at runtime on non-reentrant Mutex semantics. New `live_guards: FxHashMap<MutexDefId, (GuardDefId, name, span)>` on `BorrowChecker` tracks live Guards bound from `m.lock()` at VarDecl sites; second lock errors with `MutexDoubleLock`. Threaded through `BranchState` so both arms of an if-else see independent locking states (lock in then-arm doesn't leak to else-arm, but lock in either arm flags a join-point lock as conservative). Block-exit cleanup removes Guards declared inside the block — sequential `if cond: lock` followed by outer `lock` works after scope ends. Per-fn reset clears state. Scope: Mutex.lock only for first cut; RwLock.read/write deliberately omitted (different semantics — would generate noise on legitimate read+read patterns). Existing fixture `attack_56_mutex_double_lock.gg` (untriggered until now) wired into `security_rejected("already locked")`. 1053/1053 integration green.

- [2026-05-04] **Inline `None()` in `Vector[Option[T]]` literals resolves to the right Option variant.** `lower_array_literal` (collections.rs) now propagates the outer Vector's element type as `expected_type` for per-element lowering, so bare `None()` in `[None(), Some(1)]` resolves to `Option[T]::None` instead of falling through to `Constant::Null`. Without this, `Vector[Option[int]] v = [None(), Some(1), None()]` silently assigned `int64_t 0` into `void*` enum slots — runtime values were wrong. Only applies in the non-empty branch (the empty `[]` branch needs the OUTER type for `elem_size`). Initial fix regressed `enum_variant_clone_loop`; fixed-of-fix landed in same commit. Closes "Inline `None()` without typed variable" TODO. Commit: 73e87968. 1053/1053 integration green.

Added `find_root_def_id_with_path` and `find_collection_source_with_path` helpers in `src/semantic/safety/helpers.rs`. New `IndexBorrowSource { root, field_path }` struct in `mod.rs`. Pattern is broader than arena: any code that borrows from one struct field then mutates a sibling benefits. Commit: 4dedf1d1. 1053/1053 integration green.
