- [2026-05-01] **Self-host `Dict[String, _]` state-loss closed — empty-literal ctor routing fix.** Root cause of the runaway re-loading symptom (`std.collections` loaded 286× under stage-1) traced to `lir_codegen.gg`'s magic-name expansion at line 3515: every `Dict[String, _] x = {}` empty-literal-with-hint lowered to `__gorget_map_new_sized_K__GGSEP__V`, which the codegen ALWAYS expanded to `gorget_map_new(sizeof(K), sizeof(V))` — never to `gorget_map_new_str(sizeof(V))`. With `hash_fn = NULL`, the runtime fell back to byte-FNV on the entire 32-byte `Str` struct (data ptr + cap + len + alloc); two `String` instances of the same content with different `data` pointers hashed to different buckets, so `contains` lied after a matching `put`. Only the `{}` empty-literal path was affected — explicit `Dict[K, V]()` ctor calls already routed through `map_monomorphized_to_runtime`'s `gorget_dict_new_str` branch correctly. The 34 broken sites were string-keyed maps for module dedup, named-locals tracking, fn-template registration, etc. Fix: in `lir_codegen.gg` `__gorget_map_new_sized_` branch, check if resolved K c-type name is `Str` / `GorgetString` and emit `gorget_map_new_str(sizeof(V))` in that case. Keeps non-string-keyed maps on the existing `gorget_map_new(sizeof(K), sizeof(V))` path. Proof-of-fix: reverted `Vector[String] loaded` back to `Dict[String, bool] loaded` in `self_host_lowerer/loader.gg`, removed dead `loaded_contains` helper. Stage-1 reaches end of `driver.gg` lowering without re-loading; bootstrap fixed-point (stage-2 == stage-3 byte-equal) holds. Verified stage1.c sweep: 0 raw `gorget_map_new(sizeof(Str), ...)` calls (was 34), 35 `gorget_map_new_str(sizeof(...))` calls. Closes Item 1 from the user's earlier audit. Five other `Vector[String]` / parallel-Vector workarounds in `self_host_lowerer` (LowerCtx.named_locals, GirModule.const_decls/none_decls/enum_names, seen_instances, fn_templates) are also likely now redundant since they faced the same bug; deferred to a follow-up to keep this commit minimal. Full integration sweep 1052/1052 PASS, `self_host_bootstrap` and `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` both pass. Stage-1 mono-gen hang at mi=64/73 also resolved (was the same bug — the failed Dict lookup looped on already-seen instances).

- [2026-05-01] **Self-host span collision fix — per-module `parse_source_with_offset` plumbing closes cross-file `resolution_map` last-write-wins bug.** Investigation of "Self-host Dict[String, _] state-loss" Item-1 in TODO surfaced that the actual root cause behind cli_basic.gg / encoding_basic.gg's comment-length-dependent type-binding loss was NOT a Dict[String, _] runtime state-loss as TODO line 11 hypothesized, but a span collision between imported modules. Tracing identifier resolution for `enc_r2` in `match enc_r2:` showed both files hit `span_start=698`: `enc_r2` in `tests/fixtures/encoding_basic.gg` AND `enc_ch` in `lib/std/encoding.gg`. The resolver's `Dict[int, int] resolution_map` is keyed on `expr.span.start` (a file-local byte offset, not a (file_id, offset) pair), and the second `put(698, 196)` for `enc_ch` clobbered the first `put(698, 171)` for `enc_r2`. The typechecker's `infer_expr_type` for `enc_r2` then read the wrong def_id, getting `enc_ch`'s int-typed scope-id rather than `enc_r2`'s `Result[String, ParseError]`, so the `case Error(enc_msg):` arm hit RTGeneric(Result) lookup that didn't fire, and `enc_msg` never got its type set. Comment-length sensitivity came from byte offsets shifting with comment length — `# URL decode error` shifted `enc_r2` from offset 676 (no collision) to 698 (collision with `enc_ch`). Toggling 1 byte of the comment flipped the failure deterministically. The Rust pipeline doesn't have this bug because `loader::ModuleLoader` tracks `next_offset: usize` and parses each non-entry module via `Parser::new_with_offset(source, base_offset)`, shifting all spans so they're globally unique across the merged module. Fix mirrors that exactly: (1) `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/lexer.gg` — added `lex_base_offset: int` field to `Lexer`, modified `lex_emit` to add it to every emitted span, added public `lex_tokenize_with_offset(source, base_offset)`. (2) `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/parser.gg` — added `parse_source_with_offset(source, base_offset)` that calls the lexer's offset variant; `parse_source(source)` is now `parse_source_with_offset(source, 0)`. (3) `tests/fixtures/self_host_check/loader.gg` — `load_all` takes `entry_source_len`, tracks `next_offset = entry_source_len + 1`, advances by `src.byte_len() + 1` per imported module, and uses `parse_source_with_offset` for every imported module. Also reverted the `Vector[String] loaded` workaround back to `Dict[String, bool] loaded` as proof-of-fix — the workaround was unneeded once spans don't collide. (4) `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/loader.gg` — same pattern in `load_imports`. The `Vector[String] loaded` workaround stays here because the *lowerer* loader runs under stage-1 (a self-host-compiled binary), where a separate, distinct Dict bug surfaces; that bug is unrelated to span collision and is tracked separately. (5) `self_host_check/driver.gg` and `self_host_lowerer/driver.gg` pass `source.byte_len()` to their loaders. Validation: full integration sweep 1052/1052 PASS (zero regressions); `check_comparison` 902 exact → 904 exact (+2: cli_basic.gg and encoding_basic.gg now pass), 13 → 11 mismatches; `parser_comparison` 990 → 998; `resolver_comparison` 572 → 575; `type_comparison` 949 → 959 exact; `self_host_bootstrap` and `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` stay green. Investigation notes were in `project_dict_string_state_loss.md` (removed 2026-06-30 as a closed fossil — fully superseded by this entry + `docs/devbook/{02,04,07,22,29}`). The 11 remaining `check_comparison` mismatches (closure inference, generic param rendering, etc.) are unrelated to this fix.

- [2026-05-01] **`Box[T]` drops in collections / struct fields / enum variants — three-case fix.** Closes the keystone item from prior Box[T] TODO. Cases (a) `Vector[Box[T]]`, (b) `Box[T]` as struct field, and (c) `Box[T]` inside enum variants now all free correctly with proper accounting through `__gorget_box_free_T` (--clone-stats balanced) and recursive inner-T drop where appropriate. Architecture: per-type `Box__T__drop(void* slot)` wrapper emitted by a new `emit_box_drop_wrappers` pass in `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs` (runs after all per-type `T__drop` definitions). The wrapper reads the box pointer from its slot, no-ops on null (drained), recurses into inner T's drop (selected via `box_inner_drop_fn`: trivial-runtime helpers for built-in resource types, `T__drop` for user types in `recursive_drop_structs`/`recursive_drop_enums`, `Box__T__drop` for nested Box, `None` for primitive inners), frees the heap allocation through `__gorget_box_free_T`, and zeros the slot. Wired in by: (1) `infer_drop_strategy` in `src/lir/lower/mod.rs` returns `Trivial("Box__T__drop")` for non-trait Box (trait Box keeps `"free"` and routes through the existing inline trait-box drop path that targets `data` field of the 16-byte trait-obj layout); (2) `elem_drop_fn_for_type` in `src/lir/lower/types.rs` returns `Some("Box__T__drop")` so `gorget_array_free`'s elem_drop / `gorget_map_free`'s val_drop fire the wrapper per element; (3) `monomorphize_struct` in `src/ir/lowering/generics/mod.rs` synthesizes the `_0: T` field on Box monomorphs (skipping trait inners detected via `{Trait}_TraitObj` in the registry or `_TraitObj` AST suffix) so `c_sizeof_with_structs("Box__T")` returns 8 instead of 0 (without this, `Vector[Box[T]]` emitted `gorget_array_new(0)`); (4) the LIR pre-pass for trait Box at `lower_type_defs` registers a fresh 16-byte `{data, vtable}` struct directly so iteration order doesn't matter; (5) `Box.new(value)` in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs` now mirrors the bare-name `Box(value)` ctor — apply `ensure_owned_at_consuming_arg` then `drops.unregister(source)` so the box's heap region takes ownership without aliasing; (6) forward-declarations of `T__clone_inplace` for recursive-drop structs and enums in `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs` (closes the `-Wimplicit-function-declaration` warning that the in-line clone bodies triggered). Fixtures verified: `option_box_enum.gg` (output 42/0/7, valgrind clean for non-Option Box paths); `examples/calculator/main.gg` (full output 5/20/-7/6/49, valgrind 0 errors); `Vector[Box[int]]` push/drop (valgrind 0 errors). 1052/1052 integration tests pass on C backend; 989/989 unit tests pass; bootstrap stays green. Residual: Option/Result variant fields with Box-typed payload still skip drop emission (kept intentional — see TODO entry; enabling the drop unmasks a pre-existing self-host shallow-copy aliasing in `Vector[Stmt].get(i).unwrap()` that needs a compiler-level fix to auto-clone resource elements).

- [2026-05-01] **Borrow checker: `.clone()` breaks the receiver's borrow chain.** After `Callable f = vec.get(i).unwrap().clone()`, the runtime `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned` returns an independently-allocated env — so `return f` is sound. But the static analyzer's `compute_method_call_origin` propagated the receiver's origin through `.clone()` as a passthrough, leaving `f` with `BorrowOrigin::Local(vec)`. Returning then tripped `DanglingReturn { borrows from local variable vec which will be dropped }`. Fix: in `src/semantic/safety/origins.rs`, treat `method.node.as_str() == "clone"` as a fresh-source: return `BorrowOrigin::Static` (no local dep, escape-safe) regardless of receiver chain. Picking `Static` over `Owned` matters because `Owned`'s `contains_local()` is `true` (intended for f-strings inside void contexts where the return-type gate skips the check anyway), while `Static` is `false`. The same rule applies to all resource clones — String / Array / Map / Set / Closure — since each routes through a `*_clone` (or `*_clone_to_owned`) helper that breaks borrow provenance. New fixture `tests/fixtures/clone_breaks_borrow_chain.gg`. 37/37 closure + 31/31 borrow + 90/90 security + 22/22 return + 82/82 string tests pass on C; focused test passes on LLVM; 984/984 unit tests pass.

- [2026-05-01] **`emit_recursive_struct_drops` emits `void(void*)` instead of `void(T*)`.** Closes the latent C11 6.3.2.3p8 UB that `gorget_string_free(GorgetString*)` and `gorget_array_free(GorgetArray*)` were already fixed for. Auto-generated `T__drop` for user structs with Recursive drop strategy was the last remaining typed-pointer signature. When that function pointer is stored in a `void(*)(void*)` slot — `elem_drop` in `GorgetArray`, `val_drop` / `key_drop` in `GorgetMap` — calling through it round-trips per the standard, which UBSan flags as `call to function T__drop through pointer to incorrect function type`. Fix: `static inline void T__drop(void* __p) { T_C_name* self = (T_C_name*)__p; ... }` with field-drop calls passing `(void*)&self->field`. Direct call sites pass `T*` (typed) which implicitly converts to `void*` at the parameter, so the signature change is callwise-compatible. Existing 25 drop_* + 40 vector_* + 30 dict_* + 90 security tests already exercise the path — all green on both C and LLVM backends post-fix; 984/984 unit tests pass.

- [2026-05-01] **Closure param types register on first use; tuple-IIFE no longer folds to `unit`.** Before: `(((int, int) p): p._0 + p._1)((3, 4))` returned `0` instead of `7`. The closure's `p` param ended up GIR-typed `unit` and the body folded to `add unit const unit, const unit`. Root cause: in `lower_closure` (`src/ir/lowering/closures.rs:153`), `closure_param_types` resolved each typed param via `map_ast_type` (immutable). That returns `UNIT_TYPE` for any compound type that hasn't been registered yet — and in the IIFE case, no earlier site introduced `Tuple__int64_t__int64_t`. The same closure passed through `apply(f, (3, 4))` worked because `apply`'s signature registered the tuple type first. Fix: switch the typed-param branch to `map_ast_type_mut` so the tuple/array/slice lazily registers on first use. The diagnostic-only difference between immutable and mutable mapping was leaking through as a wrong-result correctness bug specifically for typed closure params on first encounter. New fixture `tests/fixtures/closure_iife_tuple_param.gg`. 37/37 closure + 7/7 tuple tests pass on both C and LLVM backends; 984/984 unit tests pass.

- [2026-05-01] **Closure block body with bare-expression tail now returns the expression's value.** Before: `int(int, int) f = (int a, int b):\n    a + b` (closure body parsed as `Expr::Block` with `[Stmt::Expr(a + b)]`) panicked at codegen. `lower_block` lowered every stmt and discarded its result; the closure emitter blindly emitted `ret LocalId(0)` against an uninitialized return slot. Different downstream symptoms surfaced over time (SSA dominance violation, `c_lir/mod.rs:1588` index out of bounds); same root cause. Fix: in `emit_closure_call_function`'s `Expr::Block` branch, if the last stmt is `Stmt::Expr(e)`, lower it as the implicit return — mirror the `ensure_owned_at_boundary` + return-type-override + Move-vs-Copy + scope-exit-drops + `ret` shape the bare-expression body already had. Factored shared logic into `emit_implicit_return` so both paths use one source of truth. Pure block bodies whose last stmt isn't an expression (or whose stmts already terminate via `return`/`break`/`continue`) fall through to the original default-`ret` emission. New fixture `tests/fixtures/closure_block_tail_expr.gg` exercises both `(a, b): a + b` (single tail expr) and a multi-stmt block with `let` + tail expr. 36/36 closure tests pass on both C and LLVM backends; 984/984 unit tests pass.

- [2026-05-01] **Roadmap A3: typed `Inst::CollectionCtor` canonical-op + consumer migration** — closes audit item #4 ("drop `original_name` entirely") at the consumer layer; only the post-LIR-lower `promote_collection_ctors` pass still reads `CallExtern.original_name`, all three downstream consumers migrate to typed `Inst::CollectionCtor` / `Inst::SetCollectionBridge` reads. Two commits:

  - **A3 part 1 — variant + emission** (`80a3be25`): new `Inst::CollectionCtor { dst, kind: CollectionCtorKind, elem_or_key: ElemMeta, val: Option<ElemMeta>, args, arg_abis, with_capacity, str_keyed, original_name }` plus supporting `CollectionCtorKind` (Vector / Deque / Dict / HashMap / Set / HashSet) and `ElemMeta::{Primitive(LirType), Resource(ResourceKind), UserType(StructId)}` enums. `lir::runtime::promote_collection_ctors` walks every `Inst::CallExtern` matching a runtime-ctor name (`gorget_dict_new`, `gorget_set_new`, …) plus a monomorphized `original_name` (`Dict__K__V__new`, `Set__T__new`, …) and rewrites it into the typed form. BIR `expand_func` rewrites `CollectionCtor` back to `CallExtern` (using `kind`/`with_capacity`/`str_keyed` to pick the runtime symbol). Backend arms `unreachable!()` since BIR always strips it. BIR validator adds the `CollectionCtor` arm. WASM-forced (roadmap §A3): `ElemMeta` is precisely the shape the WASM backend needs to compute linear-memory allocation sizes at lowering time without a runtime symbol-name parser.

  - **A3 part 2 — migrate consumers** (`14d7c0fd`): `lir::types::wire_collection_bridges` scans `Inst::CollectionCtor` and reads `kind` + `elem_or_key: ElemMeta::UserType(StructId)` directly — the legacy `parse_key()` helper deletes (~20 lines). `lir::optimize::find_hashable_key_types` iterates `Inst::SetCollectionBridge { key_struct }` (typed StructId, no string parsing) and resolves names via `module.structs` — strict superset of the legacy path because `wire_collection_bridges` already filtered to user-keyed ctors; ~80 lines of legacy parsing delete. `c_lir::emit_hashable_key_bridges` (C backend) gets the same treatment; the legacy CallExtern-name scan stays gated under `cfg(any())` for one merge cycle as a defensive fallback (deletes in B1). Pipeline order flips: `promote_collection_ctors` runs FIRST, then `wire_collection_bridges` consumes the typed shape; updated at all five call sites in main.rs / integration.rs / ir/lowering/mod.rs. Net: -210 lines, +194 lines (-16).

  Sweep results: **C 1048/1049** parallel (1 `c_emit_comparison` flake — `Os { code: 13, kind: PermissionDenied }` parallel-rebuild-race; passes solo); **LLVM 1049/1049** sequential, no flakes. Unit 989/989. Bootstrap green.

  `CallExtern.original_name` is preserved for now — it's the only remaining input to `promote_collection_ctors`, which is the source-of-truth for `Inst::CollectionCtor`'s typed metadata. Retiring the field requires migrating the LIR construction sites in `insts.rs` to emit `CollectionCtor` directly (planned alongside B1, where the runtime declaration table makes the size-arg derivation natural).

- [2026-04-30] **C codegen: cast `&self->Some_0` through `void*` in auto-generated enum drop fns.** Closes the `-Wincompatible-pointer-types` warning on `Option[Shared[T]]::drop` (and any other Option/Result variant whose payload is a typedef'd-as-pointer resource — `Mutex[T]`, `Channel[T]`, `Weak[T]`). The Option variant payload field is C-typed `void*` in the monomorphized struct, but the auto-generated `Type__drop(Type*)` wrapper for typedef'd-as-pointer types expects e.g. `GorgetShared**`. Passing `void**` to `GorgetShared**` is a type-mismatch warning; same bit pattern, runtime behavior unchanged. Fix: emit `(void*)&self->{access}` in `emit_enum_drop_fns` and the enum branch of `emit_type_drop_fns` in `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs`. The cast goes void** → void* (implicit by C standard for any object pointer) → T* (also implicit for any non-void T at the parameter). For runtime helpers like `gorget_string_free(void*)` the cast is redundant but harmless. Struct-field drops are untouched: there `&self->field` already has the correct pointed-to type. attack_22 now compiles warning-free under `cc -Wall -Wextra`.

- [2026-04-30] **`vector_task_get` flake fixed by switching the fixture's shared counter to atomic.** Original fixture spawned 3 async increments against `shared int counter = 0` via `&counter` and asserted the post-await count was 3 — but the increments raced without synchronization, so the count was 1/2/3 nondeterministic across runs (1/3/3/1/3 in manual reruns). The fixture's purpose is exercising `Vector[Task[void]]` move semantics via `remove().unwrap()`, not racy increment semantics, so the right fix is `shared(atomic) int counter = 0` + `AtomicInt` param + `counter.add(1)`. Same shape as `shared_atomic.gg` and `stress_atomic_hammer.gg`. 10/10 deterministic at 3 post-fix; passes on both backends.

- [2026-04-30] **Roadmap A2 + A1: typed runtime call dispatch (`RuntimeFn` enum + `Inst::CallRuntime`)** — closes the keystone item from `docs/internals/lir-correctness-roadmap.md`. Two commits:

  - **A2 — `RuntimeFn` enum + signature registry** (`42d4f308`): new `src/lir/runtime.rs` defines one variant per `gorget_*`/`__gorget_*` runtime function (307 total, full parity with `runtime_extern_sig()`'s match arms — verified by name-set diff against `/tmp/runtime_fn_names.txt`). Each variant carries: stable C symbol name (`c_name`), const-buildable `RuntimeSig` (params + ret + per-param `AbiKind` + `SideEffects`), and a `resolve_lir_sig(&StructRegistry) -> ResolvedSig` that lowers the abstract `CRuntimeType` to concrete `LirType` at LIR-build time. The `runtime_table!` macro emits the enum and the parallel `REGISTRY` slice in lockstep — `as usize` ordinal and registry index are structurally synchronized; adding a runtime function is one appended line. `from_c_name(s)` is O(1) via a `OnceLock<FxHashMap<&str, RuntimeFn>>` populated on first call. Five focused unit tests cover round-trip, name uniqueness, unknown-name rejection, signature spot-check, and StructRegistry-empty fallback to `LirType::Ptr`.

  - **A1 — split `CallExtern` → `CallRuntime` + `CallExtern`** (`6ebe3217` + `263208b5`): new `Inst::CallRuntime { dst, callee: RuntimeFn, args, arg_abis, original_name }` for typed-callee dispatch. `CallExtern` keeps its existing shape and is now reserved for **user-declared C externs** only (the open-ended SDL/crypto/audio bindings case). A new post-LIR-lower pass `lir::runtime::promote_runtime_calls` walks every `CallExtern` and promotes it to `CallRuntime` when `RuntimeFn::from_c_name(name)` resolves — runs after `wire_collection_bridges` (which still scans the CallExtern shape) and before BIR lowering. `bir::lower::expand_func` rewrites `CallRuntime` back to `CallExtern` using `callee.c_name()` so backends see the same shape they did before; A3/B1 turn this around (backends pattern-match the enum, the BIR rewrite deletes). Validator gains `check_runtime_call`: arg-count + arg_abi-count cross-check against `callee.signature()` — catches mismatched call-site shape at LIR validation time. Optimizer's `find_hashable_key_types` and DCE name-to-fid root-marking accept both `CallExtern` and `CallRuntime` shapes (the optimizer runs in two contexts: post-BIR via main pipeline, pre-BIR via `src/lir/integration.rs` test path). All five exhaustive `match Inst {}` sites updated (SSA, optimize value-rewriter, display, both backends). LLVM backend's main dispatcher uses a top-of-fn shadowing trick to normalize CallRuntime → CallExtern locally, keeping the huge match arm unchanged; c_lir backend has an explicit arm that delegates to `emit_call_extern` with `callee.c_name()`. Both fallbacks only fire on the `Backend::emit_function` per-function debug path (production `generate(BirModule)` never sees CallRuntime — BIR rewrites it).

  Net foundation for: A3 (CollectionCtor — retires `original_name`), B1 (runtime declaration table — auto-generates the C runtime header from the enum), and the WASM backend (every `RuntimeFn` variant is one `(import …)` declaration; the import set scan is now O(N) over typed insts instead of regex over names). Sweep results on the rebased branch: **C 1048/1048** (parallel), **LLVM 1047/1047** sequential (snapshot taken before the UTF-8 fix added the 1048th fixture; new fixture verified post-sweep on both backends solo). Unit 989/989. Bootstrap green.

- [2026-04-30] **fix_printf_format double-encoded multi-byte UTF-8 in f-string format strings.** Surfaced in self-host stage-1 output where comment headers like `// ── Function Definitions ──` came out garbled. Root cause: `fix_printf_format` (`src/lir/lower/calls.rs`) walked the format string byte-by-byte and pushed `bytes[i] as char` for non-`%` bytes — casting a single UTF-8 byte (e.g. `0xE2`) to a Rust `char` (U+00E2), which then re-encoded as a 2-byte UTF-8 sequence (`0xC3 0xA2`). Each `─` (`0xE2 0x94 0x80`) became `0xC3 0xA2 0xC2 0x94 0xC2 0x80`. Fix: in the non-`%` branch, read a full UTF-8 char from the source slice (`fmt[i..].chars().next().unwrap()`) and advance by `ch.len_utf8()`. Same byte-as-char cast pattern fixed at `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs:731` (`rewrite_inline_c_locals`) — same root cause, narrower impact (only triggers if inline C blocks contain non-ASCII). Regular string literals and concat were never affected: they go through `escape_c_string` which already iterates by chars. The `as char` cast in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs:1532` is safe (always reads a known-ASCII format-specifier byte). New focused fixture `tests/fixtures/fstring_unicode_passthrough.gg`. C 1048/1048, LLVM 1048/1048 (in flight), unit 984/984, security 90/90, both bootstrap tests pass.

- [2026-04-30] **fix(llvm): emit `byval(...)` on x86_64 SysV for >16-byte aggregate-by-value extern args** — closes the residual 304 LLVM-backend failures on Ubuntu CI (passing 743/1047 → expected 1047/1047). After commit `a107f088` switched llc to PIC and cut failures from 630 → 304, the remaining bugs were SIGSEGV / output-mismatch / runtime-panic patterns concentrated in tests that pass `Str` (32 bytes) by value to runtime helpers like `gorget_assert_fail_values`, `gorget_str_eq`, `gorget_str_cmp`, `gorget_str_to_cstr`, `gorget_str_contains`, `gorget_string_push_char`, etc. Root cause: the LLVM emitter declared and called these as `(ptr, ptr, ...)` — which on **AArch64 AAPCS64** matches the C ABI for >16-byte aggregates (caller copies struct to its frame, passes a pointer in `x1`/`x2`) and on **macOS Apple Silicon** (also aarch64) is fine. But on **x86_64 SysV**, large aggregates by value are MEMORY class — the C side reads them off the outgoing stack frame at `[rsp..rsp+sizeof]`, while the Gorget caller was stuffing pointers into `rsi`/`rdx` registers. Result: callees saw garbage where the structs should have been (e.g. `assert_return_fail` printed `assertion failed: left 10 right` with the op replaced by an integer pointer and left/right swapped — a fingerprint of stack-vs-register mismatch). Fix: arch-conditional helper `large_agg_byval_attr` returns `byval(%T) align 8 ` only when `cfg!(target_arch = "x86_64")`. Patched the extern declaration emitter, the main `Inst::CallExtern` arg-builder, the Option-wrapping arg-builder, and four ad-hoc paths (`gorget_str_eq` / `gorget_str_cmp` / `gorget_str_to_cstr` / `gorget_string_push_char`) plus their declarations. AArch64 emission is byte-identical to before — verified by handcrafted IR + cross-llc to both triples (x86_64 produces 4× `movq` onto the outgoing stack, aarch64 keeps the register-pointer convention). aarch64: 1047/1047, no regressions. x86_64 verification deferred to CI since the local box is aarch64. `GG_LLVM_FORCE_X86_64_ABI=1` env var added as a dev affordance for inspecting the x86_64 IR shape from an aarch64 host.

- [2026-04-30] **IR lowering: `Callable[T()]` always resolves to FnPtr at locals — `named_types` cache no longer shadows it after collection-element registration.** Two `Callable[Sig]` locals declared from the same `Vector[Callable[Sig]]` panicked at IR validation with `call to undefined function @f2`. Why: when the first `fns.get(0).unwrap()` ran, `resolve_inner_type` on `Option__Ref__Callable__GorgetClosure` registered `Callable__GorgetClosure` in `TypeMapper.named_types` as `GirType::Named(...)` (collection-element shape). The next `Callable[int()]` VarDecl went through `map_ast_type` → `try_map_ast_type`, found the cached Named entry first, and returned that instead of routing through the mut path's Callable→FnPtr branch (`types.rs:221`). With `local_type` ≠ FnPtr, the call-site dispatch in `exprs/calls.rs:882` skipped the `__gorget_closure_call_N` route and fell through to a regular by-name function call — `call @f2` — which the validator rejects. How to apply: in `try_map_ast_type` AND `map_ast_type_mut`, treat `Callable`/`MutCallable`/`ConsumeCallable` as cache-bypass (always re-resolve fresh: immutable returns `None` to force the mut fallback; mutable skips the named_types lookup and falls through to the existing `base in {Callable, …}` FnPtr branch). The Named form is still used inside collections via `resolve_inner_type` — that path is untouched. Self-host loaders/registries unaffected. C: 1047/1047. Fixture: `tests/fixtures/vector_callable_two_locals.gg` (test `vector_callable_two_locals`).

- [2026-04-30] **SECURITY: match-expression Some-arm value drop (attack_81)** — `int more = match o: case Some(n): f(n); case None(): 0` silently produced 0 instead of `f(n)`. Bug in `lower_match_expr` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs:2052-2085`): the loop unconditionally `switch_to(next_test_bb)` after each arm, including the final arm where `next_test_bb == merge_bb` for non-`else_arm` matches; then the no-`else_arm` branch wrote `Constant::Unit` into the merge block — overwriting whichever arm value the arms had just stored into the result_local. Resulting GIR had `_7 = const unit` at the top of the merge block, clobbering each arm's `_7 = arm_val`. The sibling `lower_match_stmt_as_expr` (~line 2459) had the right shape already: gate `switch_to` on `next_test_bb != merge_bb`, gate the assign on `!builder.is_terminated()`, and only emit a fallback when an `else_arm` actually exists. Mirrored that shape in `lower_match_expr`. attack_81 sum(1→2→3) now returns `6` instead of `1`; fixture moved from `security_known_unsafe(SilentlyProduces "1")` to `security_safe`. C backend: 1047/1047 integration tests pass, 90/90 security tests pass, both bootstrap tests pass.

- [2026-04-30] **Tier-2 architectural: string-typed-fields cluster (3 commits)** — closing the audit's #1/#2/#3 lifts toward the "LIR carries more, backends are dumber" architecture:

  - **`SetCollectionBridge.key_type: String → key_struct: StructId`** (`7f7ed1f5`): the bridge-wiring inst held the user key as a name string; backends string-concatenated it into the bridge symbol. Resolved StructId at insertion time in `wire_collection_bridges`; backends look up the name via `module.structs[id.0].name`. `validate_module` now bound-checks `key_struct.0 < structs.len()`.

  - **`Inst::NamedFieldPtr` retired** (`33ac6135`): the variant carried `struct_name: String` + `field_name: String` for "future symbolic field access on opaque runtime structs," but had **zero emission sites** — the BIR lowering case + 28-line `lookup_named_field_index()` helper + 6 passive match arms in display/ssa/optimize/mod.rs/bir-validate were all dead. -57 net lines, no behavior change. If/when symbolic field access is actually needed, re-introduce with `(StructId, u32)` typing from the start.

  - **`TraitCall trait_name + method → typed (trait_obj_struct: StructId, method_idx: u32)`** (`a5d58450`): the inst carried both as raw strings; `try_emit_trait_call` constructed them and BIR synth `get_or_emit_trait_helper` re-parsed them every cache miss to look up the matching `_TraitObj` / `_VTable` structs. Now resolved at LIR construction time; helper-fn name still recovered from `module.structs[id].name` (stripping `_TraitObj`) and `vtable.fields[method_idx].0` for diagnostic quality, but cache identity and dispatch are typed. `validate_module` bound-checks both the trait-obj struct AND the method index against the matching `_VTable.fields.len()`.

  Tier-2 item #4 (drop `CallExtern.original_name` entirely) deferred — three consumers still string-parse it for collection-ctor key/val/elem extraction; needs a typed `Inst::CollectionCtor` to retire (TODO captured separately).

- [2026-04-30] **Self-host loader: auto-load std.hash on @derive(Hashable)** — mirrors Rust's `module_uses_hashable_derive` (src/loader.rs:569-581) which auto-loads std.hash whenever any struct or enum carries `@derive(Hashable)`. The derived `equip T with Hashable: void hash(self, FxHasher &h)` references std.hash's FxHasher and write_int / write_string / finish, so without the implicit load any fixture deriving Hashable but not importing std.hash explicitly hits unresolved-name errors at the synthesized hash method. Affected fixture: `dict_user_key_auto.gg` — uses `@derive(Equatable, Hashable)` on a Dict-keyed struct without `from std.hash import ...`. Other Hashable-deriving fixtures (`derive_hashable`, `derive_generic`, `dict_user_key_hashable`, `set_user_key_hashable`) all import std.hash explicitly so the auto-load is redundant for them. Add `module_uses_hashable_derive(Module)` scanning `IStruct`/`IEnum` items for "Hashable" in their `derives: Vector[String]`, queue "std.hash" alongside the existing std.iter auto-load in `load_all`. check_comparison: 986 → 987/999 (+1). Bootstrap unaffected (lowerer's loader is a separate file, not touched). Lowerer's loader doesn't need the same fix because the lowerer doesn't run check_comparison.

- [2026-04-30] **Self-host typecheck: param types set in every matching body scope (handles duplicate extern decls across files)** — surfaced 4 fixtures (`bytes_ops`, `utf8_validation`, `uuid_basic`, `uuid_props`) all missing `"data" = Vector[uint8]` from Gorget output. Root cause: `__bytes_to_str_raw` is declared as an extern in BOTH `std/bytes.gg` (param `b64_buf`) and `std/io.gg` (param `data`). Rust's loader wraps each imported file in its own `Item::Module` FileModule scope, so both declarations coexist in separate scopes and BOTH sets of params are typed. Self-host's flat-merge loader appends both to the entry module — the second declaration's name registration silently fails (returns NO_DEF in `define_replace_or_fail`), but `resolve_function` still pushes a body scope for it and registers its params as `DkVariable`. `find_body_scope` returns only the first match by name, so the second declaration's params (`data` here) never got their type_id set. Fix: in `register_function_signature`, after computing `binding_type_id`, iterate ALL `ctx.fn_scope_names`/`fn_scope_ids` entries matching `func.name` and parent_scope (or grandparent for trait/equip nesting), looking each param up via `lookup_in_scope` and setting its type_id where found. Non-matching params skip silently (lookup returns -1). Each duplicate IFunction call types its own params in its own body scope. check_comparison: **982 → 986/999** (+4). Bootstrap green.

- [2026-04-30] **Self-host typecheck: recurse Callable wrappers in `demote_generic_param_to_var`** — closes a binding-vs-signature rendering asymmetry through Callable trait wrappers. Rust renders `f: Callable[T(int)]` at a fn body's BINDING site as `Callable[<error>(int)]` (the binding-side demotion), but keeps the signature's `Callable[T(int)]` as-is. Self-host's demote shim only descended through container types (RTGeneric/RTTuple/RTArray/RTSlice/RTRef), not through the four Callable wrappers (`RTCallableTrait`, `RTMutCallableTrait`, `RTConsumeCallableTrait`, `RTBoxedCallable`) — so the `T` inside `Callable[...]` stayed at bindings, mismatching Rust. Fix: add four wrapper cases that call a new `demote_through_function_type` helper, which walks the wrapped RTFunction's params and return through `demote_generic_param_to_var`. Bare `RTFunction` still falls through to the catch-all (signature-shaped types keep `T` per Rust's behavior). Net: check_comparison **980 → 982/999** (+2: `generic_callable.gg`, `generic_callable_ref.gg`); type_comparison **989 → 991** (same fixes apply at the type-check stage). Bootstrap green.

- [2026-04-30] **Self-host typecheck: pre-pass registers all function signatures before walking bodies** — closes a forward-reference hole. Single-pass typecheck walked items in order: when `main`'s body called an imported function `h` whose item came LATER in the merged-module sequence, `infer_expr_type` for `auto x = h()` looked up `h`'s `def.type_id` while it was still `-1` — and the auto-typed binding silently failed to resolve (rendered as nothing in TYPE output). Manifests on every `auto x = imported_call()` pattern across the loader-driven check path. Mirrors Rust's `register_signatures_recursive` (typecheck.rs:5273) which runs before the body walk for exactly this reason. Fix: split `type_check_function` into `register_function_signature` (sets def.type_id from declared params/return) and the body walk; `type_check_module` runs the signature pre-pass over all `IFunction` items first, then proceeds with the existing item walk. Equip methods still get their signatures via the inline `register_function_signature` call inside `type_check_function`. Net: check_comparison **966 → 979/996** (+13 fixtures, 98.0%); type_comparison superset→exact transitions: 49→37 (was already at 949 exact; this run shows 952). parser_comparison/resolver_comparison unchanged. Bootstrap stays green.

- [2026-04-30] **Tier-1 correctness: drop-elaboration audit + 4 fixes** — closing the highest-priority correctness gaps surfaced by the LIR/BIR/backend audit:

  - **Drop-flag tracks SlotStore re-init (the real bug)**. `src/lir/drop_elab.rs:325` Phase 3 instrumented only `MoveSlot`/`Memset` (flag := false). It missed `SlotStore` (flag := true), so a `MaybeInitialized` slot moved on iteration N (`flag := false`) and re-initialized on iteration N+1 via `R r = R(...)` had its flag stuck at false at the end-of-body drop guard — silent leak with the only signal being `--clone-stats` showing `total_frees=0`. Fix: instrument `SlotStore` too (set flag := true), guarding against feedback by skipping stores whose target is itself a flag slot (the pass emits those). Side-effect: bb0 init flipped from `true` → `false`. Function params get their flag set via the existing param SlotStore at bb0 (`lir/lower::lower():1215`); locals get it via their declaration SlotStore. Three regression fixtures lock in the contract: `drop_loop_reinit.gg` (the actual regression), `drop_early_return.gg` (return-edge drop), `drop_match_partial_init.gg` (multi-arm join). All pass on both backends.

  - **Orphan DropGuardOpen panics instead of silently skipping**. `find_matching_close` returned `insts.len()` when nesting was broken; the caller silently no-op'd elaboration, leaving the runtime guard in place (best case: leak; worst case: a stale `DropGuardClose` paints the wrong drop range in a later pass). Now panics with the open index, block size, and final nesting depth — any future LIR transform that corrupts pairs surfaces immediately rather than producing wrong code.

  - **Runtime invariant assertions on owned/view discriminator**. `gorget_string_free` and `gorget_array_free` documented but didn't enforce the cap=0=view contract: `cap > 0` requires a live `alloc` pointer, but a CoW-demoted string with stale `alloc` would crash inside `s->alloc->dealloc(...)` with no diagnostic. Added always-on null-pointer checks that panic with the offending field state on violation (`gorget: panic: gorget_string_free invariant: cap=N but alloc=NULL`). Cheap (one indirect-call-path null check) and converts silent-corruption-on-deref into a panic with context.

  - **`is_move=true` SlotStore source tracking**: subsumed by the drop-flag fix. The dest side is covered (any SlotStore sets flag := true); the source side was already covered by the existing `MoveSlot` annotation that GIR lowering emits via `emit_move_zero_for_local` for every move source.

  Net: 1047/1047 on the C backend (3 new tests added). Tier-1 correctness items A/B/C/D/E from the audit are closed.

- [2026-04-30] **Rust typechecker: ConstDecl/StaticDecl now set DefInfo.type_id** — closes a long-standing asymmetry where top-level const/static decls (`const float PI = 3.14...`, `public static File stdin = _stdin_handle()`) were typecheck-inferred but never had their type recorded on the def. `format_types_canonical` filters by `def.type_id.is_some()`, so these decls were invisible in TYPE output even though Rust's resolver registered them. Self-host's typecheck DID set the type_id, surfacing stdin/stdout/stderr/PI/NAN/INFINITY/etc. in every fixture that transitively imports std.io or std.math — making those entries appear as "Gorget extras" in check_comparison's diff. Fix: in typecheck.rs:5368-5373, after `infer_expr` on the const/static value, look up the def by name+span and set `def.type_id` to the declared AST type (falling back to the inferred value type if the AST type doesn't resolve). Net: 83 fixtures upgraded from "superset" to "exact" match across check_comparison (797→880 exact); type_comparison saw a similar 12-fixture upgrade (937→949 exact). check_comparison total: 965 → 966 (+1). Bootstrap stays green. Closes the (iv) item in the original check_comparison gap analysis ("std.io stdin/stdout/stderr globals as extras") — turned out to be a typechecker oversight on the Rust side, not a loader/Item::Module wrapping issue.

- [2026-04-30] **Self-host parser: support contextual `T*` extern-pointer syntax + `.drain()` triggers std.iter auto-load** — two related fixes that lift check_comparison from 960 → 965 (+5 fixtures, mostly p2p_*). (1) `parse_type`'s NamedType branch was not consuming a postfix `TOK_STAR` after `Type` or `Type[Args]`, so `extern bool crypto_rsa_verify(RSAKey* key, Vector[uint8] data, Vector[uint8] sig)` parsed as `crypto_rsa_verify(RSAKey, ...)` and the leftover `*` and `key` derailed the rest of the param list. Once any extern in xtd.crypto.gg used `T*` the entire crypto.gg's signatures came out garbled, and downstream every fixture that imported it inherited `<error>`-typed Vector[uint8] in their own functions (because the module-merged scope had a corrupted `Vector` namespace). Symptom: `Vector[uint8]` becomes `<error>` for ANY function in a module that transitively imports xtd.crypto. Fix: consume `TOK_STAR` after both branches of TNamed (with and without generic args). Self-host AST has no TPointer variant — we elide the pointer-ness, same shape as Rust's parser when not in `extern_c` mode (Rust models it but discards downstream); the typechecker doesn't need it for signature inference. (2) `self_host_check/loader.gg`'s `expr_mentions_iter` only triggered std.iter auto-load on `.iter()`; Rust's loader fires on `.iter()` OR `.drain()` (src/loader.rs:315). One-line fix to mirror. Net: check_comparison **960 → 965/996** (96.9%). Bootstrap stays green.

- [2026-04-30] **Self-host parser: skip `blocking` modifier on extern equip methods** — surfaced ~34 check_comparison mismatches across httpserver_*, http_*, async_socket_echo, csv_*, encoding_*, exec_*, and other I/O fixtures, all sharing patterns like `"accept" = Result[Socket, String]()` / `"read_exact" = Vector[uint8](int)` / `"read_line" = Result[String, String]()` missing from Gorget output. Root cause: std.net.socket / std.net.tls / std.io etc. mark blocking-mode externs with `extern blocking Result[...] accept() = "..."` — the `blocking` modifier sits between the optional ABI string and the return type. `parse_equip_item`'s extern path consumed `extern` and the optional ABI string but NOT `blocking`, so `parse_function_def` parsed the `blocking` ident as the return type and the rest of the signature came out garbled. The dual path `parse_extern_block` (top-level `extern "Gorget":` blocks) had this skip already (parser.gg:3654); just needed the same treatment in the equip case. Fix: one-line `if self.check_tok(TOK_IDENT) and token_ident(...) == "blocking": self.advance()` after the ABI-string consume. Net: check_comparison **925 → 959/996** (+34 fixtures, 96.3%). type_comparison/parser_comparison/resolver_comparison unchanged. Bootstrap stays green.

- [2026-04-30] **Self-host parser: fall back to keyword spelling for keyword-named params** — surfaced 17 dataframe `check_comparison` mismatches all sharing the pattern `"on" = String` missing from Gorget output. Root cause: `df_inner_join(DataFrame left, DataFrame right, String on)` (and friends) name a parameter `on`, which the lexer tokenizes as `KwOn`. `parse_param` extracted the param name via `token_ident(name_tok.lex_token)` which returns `""` for keyword tokens, so the param def got registered with empty name, and the typechecker's `lookup_in_scope(body_scope, "")` couldn't find it, leaving the def's `type_id` unset. Symptom: function signature shows `DataFrame(DataFrame, DataFrame, String)` correctly, but no `"on" = String` TYPE entry. Fix: when `token_ident` returns `""`, fall back through `match name_tok.lex_token: case TkKeyword(kw): type_keyword_name(kw) or non_type_keyword_name(kw)`. Net: check_comparison **910 → 925/996** (+15 fixtures, all dataframe). type_comparison/parser_comparison/resolver_comparison unchanged. Bootstrap stays green.

- [2026-04-30] **IR lowering: `Box(value)` now applies the consuming-arg ownership shim** — closes a long-standing aliasing bug. The runtime's `__gorget_box_alloc_T(val)` does `*p = val`, a shallow byte-copy. For resource-typed values whose source is borrowed (bare param, non-last-use local, Ref/CoW), this aliased the box's interior with the caller's data, leading to use-after-free when the source got dropped while the box still held a pointer to its Vector data. Symptoms: 25 self_host `httpserver_*.gg` fixtures + the `generic_callable_ref.gg` parser fixture all segfaulted during typecheck/parse with infinite `Type__clone` recursion — the freed memory happened to contain garbage that, when re-interpreted as a SpannedType chain, formed an unbounded clone graph. Minimal repro: `parse_function_type(named_ty, ...)` calls `Box(ret_ty)` where ret_ty is a borrowed param; the box ends up sharing args.data with the caller's named_ty; named_ty drops; box dangles. Fix: route `Box(value)` through `ctx.ensure_owned_at_consuming_arg` (the same shim used for `push`/`put`/`set`/`insert`/`send`) so a clone is inserted automatically when the source can't be moved. Net: parser_comparison **986 → 990/996** (+4, all crashes resolved); resolver_comparison **571 → 572/996** (+1); check_comparison: 25 crashes → 0 crashes (httpserver fixtures now typecheck end-to-end, just shift to mismatches due to remaining smaller diffs); bootstrap stays green.

- [2026-04-30] **Rust typechecker: FieldAccess now returns the actual field type instead of `error_id`** — closes the typechecker hole that let `parse_meta_for_var_name` silently pass a `Keyword` payload to an `int` parameter (the bug that the `dac0609e` Keyword-signature refactor worked around in self-host code). Three coordinated changes: (1) `Expr::FieldAccess` in `infer_expr` (typecheck.rs:1736) now looks up the field's TypeId in `DefInfo.field_types` and returns it (was always returning `error_id`, which silently pattern-matched any downstream parameter type). (2) `populate_def_field_types` in mod.rs runs BEFORE typecheck (was after — too late for FieldAccess inference to read), and now uses `ast_type_to_resolved` for full Named-type resolution (was `types.resolve_type` which only handled primitives, dropping every Named-type field including the critical `Token lex_token` case). (3) `populate_def_field_types`'s field-collect now uses `.map().unwrap_or_else(|_| error_id)` instead of `.filter_map()` so vector indices stay aligned with field order even when some types fail to resolve. Net: `type_comparison` 985 → 986/996. Closes a class of latent bugs where field-typed values passed silently to mismatched parameters (the `Keyword`/`int` antipattern is one example; non-Copy field assignments without `!` is another, caught simultaneously). One downstream fix in self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg: `final_blk.term = lir_term` → `final_blk.term = !lir_term` — was previously a silent copy of a non-Copy enum, now correctly typed and requires the explicit move sigil. Bootstrap stays green; both `self_host_bootstrap` and `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` pass.

- [2026-04-30] **LIR-level key_drop / key_clone wiring closes the LLVM/C divergence** — `infer_collection_elem_fns` now emits `(120, "T__drop")` and `(128, "T__clone_inplace")` for user-resource Dict/HashMap keys and Set/HashSet elements, in addition to the existing val_drop=104 / val_clone=112 / val_materialize=136 / elem_drop=40 / elem_clone=48 / elem_materialize=56 stores. Both backends compile the resulting `NamedFuncAddr+ElemPtr+Store` insts uniformly, so the LLVM backend now wires user-resource key drops through bucket-eviction — closing the latent leak surfaced during the SetCollectionBridge audit. Gating: `recursive_drop_structs.contains_key(key) || recursive_drop_enums.contains_key(key)` (exactly "this user type has a generated `T__drop`"); primitive keys are naturally excluded; `_str` runtime variants are excluded explicitly via an `is_str_variant` flag (the runtime pre-wires String key handling inside the constructor itself). Offsets verified against `c_runtime.rs` GorgetMap layout: hash_fn=88, eq_fn=96, val_drop=104, val_clone=112, **key_drop=120**, **key_clone=128**, val_materialize=136, key_materialize=144 (GorgetSet is `typedef GorgetMap` so the same offsets apply). With the LIR-level wiring complete, the C-backend's narrowed post-call key_drop/key_clone wiring (~75 lines across `emit_call_extern.rs:1164-1238`) is now redundant and deleted; `original_name` is no longer consumed by the C-backend's CallExtern arm and the parameter is dropped from `emit_call_extern()`'s public signature; the LLVM backend's analogous binding gets pattern-elided. Net: +57 lines in `lir/lower/insts.rs`, -75 lines in `c_lir/emit_call_extern.rs`, -1 line in `llvm/mod.rs`. The C and LLVM backends are now strict peer translators of LIR for ALL collection-ctor side effects. Verified clean across dict_user_key_{auto,hashable} / set_user_key_hashable / test_struct_derive / derive_hashable / derive_generic / dict_higher_order / dict_remove / dict_string_keys / dict_iter / dict_items / test_set on both backends.

- [2026-04-30] **C-backend post-call dedup — kill ~100 lines of redundant elem_drop/val_drop/hash_fn wiring**: with the SetCollectionBridge lift in place and `infer_collection_elem_fns` already emitting `NamedFuncAddr+ElemPtr+Store` insts at the LIR layer for Vector elem_drop/elem_clone/elem_materialize (offsets 40/48/56) and Dict val_drop/val_clone/val_materialize (offsets 104/112/136), the C-backend's parallel post-call wiring at `emit_call_extern.rs:1164-1289` was strictly duplicating LIR-emitted bytes. Two commits collapsed it: `7febec98` (Vector arm) and `324b2449` (Dict/Set hash_fn/val_drop/val_clone arm). What remains C-only is `key_drop`/`key_clone` for user-resource keys (Set + Dict) — those slots have no LIR-level wiring AND no LLVM-side counterpart, so the C-backend's narrow remaining wiring effectively documents the LLVM divergence (TODO 2026-04-30 logs the symmetric LIR fix). `elem_clone_fn_for_c_type` (helpers.rs) became dead code and was deleted; `super::types::elem_clone_fn_for_type` at the LIR layer is now the single source of truth. Net: emit_call_extern.rs 1292→1248 lines (-44); helpers.rs 1865→1837 lines (-28); LLVM backend untouched (already was free of post-call wiring). Verified clean across dict_higher_order/dict_remove/dict_string_keys/dict_user_key_hashable/dict_iter on both backends; full C-backend sweep 1042/1044 (the 2 failures, self_host_bootstrap and self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point, are pre-existing and unrelated — same failure on commit `3d92ed67` from before this session began).

- [2026-04-30] **LIR refactor batch — peer-backend cleanup**: 8 distinct refactors landed on `gorget-2` to make the C and LLVM backends symmetric peers operating on a richer LIR. (1) `LirFunction.pointee_types` shared pass — both backends read pointee info instead of rescanning SlotAddr inline. (2) `lir::queries` module (`is_trait_box`, `struct_contains_resource`, `is_user_hashable_key`, `hashable_key_fn_names`, `is_user_keyable_collection_ctor`, `is_spawn_wrapper`) — single source of truth for LIR-level questions, formerly duplicated in c_lir/helpers and llvm/mod. (5) `is_spawn_wrapper(func)` LIR query consumes both backends' inline `name.starts_with("__spawn_wrap_")` checks. (6) Typed `GlobalInit::Extern { name, args: Vec<GlobalInitArg> }` retired the string-textual `RuntimeCall(String)` representation: `LirGlobalInitArg` enum with `Int / Float / Bool / Sizeof(c_type) / StrLit / AddrOfInline` variants; LLVM backend's `parse_compound_literal`, `parse_compound_literal_field`, `parse_runtime_init_arg`, `split_top_level_args`, `RuntimeInitArg` enum (~200 lines) deleted. (7) `Inst::SetCollectionBridge { collection, is_set, key_type }` LIR instruction + `wire_collection_bridges` post-lower pass — user-keyed Dict/Set bridge wiring is now an explicit LIR inst that both backends compile inline (LLVM: GEP+store; C: field-store statement); LLVM's `emit_user_key_bridge_wiring` (62 lines) deleted. (8) Sequential LLVM full sweep verifies parity. End result: C backend at 2994 lines (down from baseline), LLVM backend at 6346 lines (down from baseline), LIR with two new shared modules (`queries.rs`, expanded `types.rs`) doing the heavy lifting. - [2026-04-29] **Self-host bootstrap: missing `traits.gg` symlink in `self_host_lowerer/`** — root cause of bootstrap link-time `undefined reference to 'build_trait_registry'`, `resolve_method_full`, `resolve_method_for_generic_receiver`, `resolve_method_by_name`, `intrinsic_resolve`, `resolve_method_shape`, `infer_method_targs`, `substitute_return_type`. When `typecheck.gg` (symlinked into the lowerer dir) imported `from traits import build_trait_registry`, the loader resolved "traits" to `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/traits.gg`, which didn't exist — the file was created in `self_host_typechecker/` during the Phase 2c work but never symlinked into the lowerer dir. The loader silently skipped it: stage-0 emitted CALLS to traits.gg functions (bare names — no `traits___` prefix because nothing populated `call_redirects` for them) but no DEFINITIONS, leaving every traits.gg symbol undefined at link. Stage-0 emission verified to include 214 `traits___*` lines (was 0). `self_host_bootstrap` and `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` integration tests both PASS.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host parser: tighten `type_keyword_name` / `non_type_keyword_name` / `is_type_keyword` to take `Keyword` instead of `int`** — eliminates the primitive-obsession antipattern that was masking through the demotion-bug for years. Symptoms surfaced when `df3a3a94` (trait-bounded equip skip) tightened typechecker correctness and exposed the latent Keyword→int implicit conversion at `parse_meta_for_var_name`'s call into `type_keyword_name`. Rather than launder Keyword through `keyword_tag` (the workaround in `3d92ed67` was option 1), the real fix is to make the function signatures honest: lookup-style functions that need exhaustive matching over Keyword variants take `Keyword`, with bodies converted from int-keyed if/elif chains to `match kw: case KwInt: ... else: return ""` for exhaustiveness. Identity-check helpers (`check_kw`, `match_kw`, `expect_kw`, `peek_kw`) stay on int — they don't benefit from Keyword typing because they're trivial equality. Updated 9 call sites across parser.gg to destructure `case TkKeyword(kw):` and pass the bound Keyword directly (no more `int kw = keyword_tag(tok); type_keyword_name(kw)` ritual). Net: bootstrap C compilation now succeeds (was failing with `incompatible type for argument 1 of parser___type_keyword_name`); remaining bootstrap linker errors (undefined refs to traits.gg functions) are pre-existing — verified at d7e08e05 baseline — separate problem logged in TODO. Comparison metrics unchanged: parser 986/996, resolver 571/996, type 985/996, check 908/996. The accompanying TODO entry flags the deeper question — Rust gorget should reject implicit Keyword→int conversions at typecheck time, not silently emit broken C.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host: meta-for-in-match expansion (variant_payloads)** — implements the AST + parser + meta.gg pipeline for `meta for vname, T in variant_payloads(EnumName): case vname(c): ...` inside match bodies. Before this fix, the parser threw away loop vars + range via `skip_meta_header()` and `parse_block` silently dropped inner case arms (no case handler). Equip method bodies using the macro typechecked as empty matches; the FIRST method appeared correct but SUBSEQUENT methods showed self as `<error>` (lost self_type_id state). Fix: new `SMetaForMatch(Vector[String], SpannedExpr, Vector[MatchArm])` Stmt variant; parser captures loop vars + range expr + inner case arm templates; `expand_meta_for_match(Module &m)` in meta.gg walks IFunction + IEquip method bodies, evaluates `variant_payloads(EnumName)` by looking up the enum's variants, clones each template arm with the first loop variable substituted in the pattern's PConstructor head. Recurses through nested control flow (if/while/for/match arms). Format/resolve/typecheck got no-op SMetaForMatch cases for exhaustiveness. Wired into both `self_host_typechecker/driver.gg` and `self_host_check/driver.gg`. Verified: dataframe `equip Column:`'s `is_null_at` / `value_as_str` / `dtype_name` / `null_count` now resolve self type as Column (was `<error>`). type_comparison/check_comparison metrics stay at 985/908; per-variant `c` bindings show as distinct defs (extra surface lines), but the underlying semantic typing is now correct.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host parser: extern equip methods now parsed instead of skipped** — `self_host_typechecker/parser.gg`'s `parse_equip_item` was explicitly skipping `extern int bytes_used() = "..."` declarations inside equip blocks, marked with a comment about "garbled AST." But `parse_function_def` already handles the `Type name(params) = expr` form (storing the expression as a return-statement body), so the fix is to consume the leading `extern` keyword (plus optional `"C"` ABI string) and let parse_function_def parse the rest. Without this, extern equip methods on Arena/File/Socket/etc. types from std were dropped during parsing, never showed in TYPE output, and masked impl dispatches against std runtime APIs. Net: check_comparison **802 → 908/996** (80.5% → 91.2%, +106 fixtures). type_comparison/parser_comparison/resolver_comparison unchanged.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host loader: clean typecheck-side multi-file loader + auto-load std.iter + check_comparison test** — ships the second-tier comparison test for the full check path (loader + analyze) sister to type_comparison's analyze-in-isolation. Architecture: new `tests/fixtures/self_host_check/` dir, symlinks for shared files (parser, ast, scope, types, typecheck, infer, traits, etc.), fresh `loader.gg` (~430 lines) written from scratch for the typecheck path — explicitly NOT a copy of `self_host_lowerer/loader.gg` (which intermixes loading with C-codegen concerns: name mangling, extern-stub filtering, call-redirect tables; those belong to lowering, not loading). Pure pipeline stage: `void load_all(Module &entry, String entry_path, String lib_dir)` discovers transitive imports + auto-loads std.iter when the heuristic fires + appends imported items to entry (resolver's two-pass top-level collection makes order independent). Auto-load heuristic mirrors Rust's `module_should_auto_load_std_iter`: triggers on Iterator/Iterable/Drainable references or `.iter()` calls, suppressed when module already imports std.iter or shadows VectorIter. New `check_comparison` integration test in `tests/integration.rs` runs `analyze_with_loader` (Rust: ModuleLoader + merge_modules + analyze) vs `self_host_check/driver` (self-host: loader.gg + typecheck) for every fixture. Baseline: **802/996 (80.5%) match**, 169 mismatched, 25 crashed. The mismatches and crashes expose PRE-EXISTING self-host typechecker bugs that surface when more code is loaded (extern equip-method handling, multi-import body-typechecking interactions) — not loader bugs. type_comparison unchanged (985/996, 98.9%). Loader infrastructure now in place; closing remaining gaps is incremental fixture-by-fixture work.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host Phase 2c residual (2): impl-override return-type substitution + two-pass body-scope** — closes the deferred TODO item that paired with stdlib-design.md §10 Phase 2c. (1) `EquipInfo` gains `Vector[Type] method_return_types_ast` parallel field — AST return type for EVERY impl method (not just method-generic ones). Populated in `collect_equip` (traits.gg). (2) `resolve_method_for_generic_receiver` Phase 1+2 (where the method is found directly on the impl) now substitutes the AST return type through `resolve_with_bindings` using the impl-arg → receiver-arg binding map. So `equip [T] Vector[T] with Iterable[T]: VectorIter[T] iter(&self)` called on `Vector[int]` returns `VectorIter[int]` instead of `VectorIter[T_placeholder]`. Mirrors what (a2) default-method Self/T substitution did, but for impl-OVERRIDE sigs. (3) **Two-pass body-scope walk** in `find_body_scope` — direct-parent match always wins over grandparent match, regardless of order. Without this, when std.iter is loaded (defining `chain` as a method on VectorIter) and a user fixture has a top-level `chain` function, std.iter's grandparent-match (module → equip → method-fn-scope) was beating the user's direct-parent match because std.iter's entry came first in `fn_scope_names`. (4) `try_prepend_std_iter` in `driver.gg` remains available but is intentionally NOT called for the comparison test path — Rust's `gorget::semantic::analyze(&mut module, &[])` doesn't multi-load either, and prepending would dump ~150 lines of iter trait/adapter entries with no Rust counterpart, dropping every fixture from "exact" to "superset" matching. The substitution kernel still earns its keep for any context that does load std.iter (explicit `from std.iter import ...`). Net: type_comparison **985/996 unchanged** (substitution doesn't fire on the comparison test path); foundation for future iterator-chain work; no regressions.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host: equip-T un-demote rule generalized to explicit `[T]` prefix; ECall preserves type args for constructors** — investigated `borrow_field_lazy_dict_iter.gg`'s `DictIterKV[K, V]` mismatch; turned out to be two distinct bugs. (1) `equip [K, V] DictIterKV[K, V]:` (inherent equip with EXPLICIT `[K, V]` prefix) was being demoted, but Rust keeps impl-T un-demoted whenever `[T]` is explicitly declared, regardless of whether the equip is trait-bounded. Generalized the trait-bounded skip in `IEquip` to also fire when `eqblk.type_params.len() > 0`. The Box2-style implicit form (`equip Box2[T]:`) still demotes. (2) `infer_expr_type` for ECall on a struct/enum constructor returned bare `RTDefined(def_id)` even when the call had `targs`. Fixed both the RTDefined-callee branch and the EIdentifier-fallback to resolve `targs` and build `RTGeneric(def_id, [resolved targs])`. So `auto walker = DictIterKV[int, int](d, 0)` now infers `walker = DictIterKV[int, int]` instead of bare `DictIterKV`. Net: type_comparison **984 → 985/996** (+1 fixture, borrow_field_lazy_dict_iter).

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host: derive Hashable preserves [Hasher H] in generated method** — `derive.gg`'s `gen_struct_hashable` and `gen_enum_hashable` were emitting `void hash(self, FxHasher &h):` (concretized) instead of Rust's `void hash[Hasher H](self, H &h):` (kept generic). One-line fix in each generator. Bodies work unchanged because `h.write_int(...)` and `self.field.hash(&h)` both route through Hasher trait dispatch on the H type parameter. With H now method-level generic, the binding-side demote shim correctly demotes the `h` param (renders as `<error>`), matching Rust. Net: type_comparison **978 → 984/996** (98.2% → 98.8%, +6 fixtures: derive_hashable, derive_generic, dict_user_key_auto, dict_user_key_hashable, set_user_key_hashable, test_struct_derive).

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host: trait-bounded equip skips demote on impl-T** — fixes the asymmetry observed during Gap 1.5: Rust keeps the impl's `[T]` un-demoted inside trait-bounded equip blocks (`equip [T] VectorIter[T] with Iterator[T]:`), so `self = VectorIter[T]` and `next = Option[T](VectorIter[T])` instead of `<error>`-flavored output. Inherent equip blocks (`equip Box2[T]:`) and regular generic functions still demote. Method-level generics inside trait-bounded equips (e.g. `void hash[Hasher H](self, H &h):`) ALSO still demote — verified via trait_bound_transitive.gg where `h` correctly renders as `<error>` while equip's impl-T is left alone. Mechanism: `trait_equip_scope_id: int` on TypeTable, set to the equip's scope_id when inside a trait-bounded equip; demote helper checks `def.scope_id == trait_equip_scope_id` to distinguish impl-T from method-T. Net: type_comparison **977 → 978/996** (98.1% → 98.2%, +1 fixture, vector_iter_userdef.gg fixed without regressing trait_bound_transitive.gg).

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host: recursive demote through container types** — extends the binding-side demotion to walk through `RTGeneric`, `RTTuple`, `RTArray`, `RTSlice`, `RTRef` args. Now `Pair[T, U]` binding renders `Pair[<error>, <error>]`, `Vector[T]` renders `Vector[<error>]`, etc. Does NOT descend into `RTFunction`/`RTCallableTrait`/`RTBoxedCallable` — those are signature-shaped types where Rust keeps `T` (e.g. `Callable[T(int)]` stays `Callable[T(int)]`). Net: type_comparison **973 → 977/996** (97.7% → 98.1%, +4 fixtures: generic_method_chain, generic_typearg_well_typed, generic_typearg_result_mismatch_error, meta_variant_payloads, test_generic_functions). One regression (vector_iter_userdef.gg): trait-bounded equip method `self` binding now `VectorIter[<error>]` while Rust keeps `VectorIter[T]` — Rust's behavior for trait-bounded equip blocks differs from generic functions; documented in MEMORY for future investigation.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host: generic-param binding demotion → `<error>`** — closes Gap 1 of the remaining type_comparison gaps. Mirrors Rust's two-tier signature/binding representation: SIGNATURE slots keep `RTDefined(generic_param_def_id)` (renders as `T`), BINDING slots get a fresh tagged `RTVar` (renders as `<error>`). Implementation: new `generic_var_ids: Dict[int, bool]` side-channel on TypeTable + `fresh_generic_var()` constructor + `demote_generic_param_to_var()` helper applied at 6 binding sites (function params, closure params, VarDecl, const decl, static decl, type alias). Formatter checks the side-channel before printing `?N` vs `<error>`, so closure-inference vars keep `?N`. Net: type_comparison **953 → 973/996** (+20: 95.7% → 97.7%); parser/resolver scores unchanged. Lowerer auto-inherits via symlinks. Files: `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/{types.gg,typecheck.gg,format_types.gg}`.

- [2026-04-29] **Self-host: pattern fallback to direct variant lookup** — resolve_variant_field_types now falls back to looking up the variant name directly in variant_field_types when the scrutinee-driven path yields nothing (e.g. when a binding shadows the original enum-typed scope, like `r is Shape.Rect(w, h)` where `r` got bound to a float earlier in the same fn). Now iterates the parser's pre-parsed `exprs` sidecar. (2) derive.gg's expand_struct_derives / expand_enum_derives didn't recognise 'Debuggable'; added gen_struct_debuggable + gen_enum_debuggable mirroring the Displayable shape. - [2026-04-28] **Self-host typechecker: spawn → Task[T] / await → T inference** — added type-inference cases for ESpawn (looks up Task in scope, wraps the operand's inferred type as RTGeneric(Task, [inner])) and EAwait (extracts type arg from RTGeneric(Task | Future, [T]) when present). Mirroring Rust's per-call-site fresh-scope approach in `register_function_signature`: switch the parser's current scope to the function's body_scope (where type params are defined as DkGenericParam) for the duration of sig resolution, then restore. New `substitute_default_return_generic` extends the (a2) substitution kernel: pre-resolves the impl's `trait_generic_args` AST through the impl-arg bindings BEFORE adding `Self → recv_type_id` and `trait_generic_params[i] → resolved trait arg[i]` to the bind map. (2) **`infer.gg`** captures the receiver's RTGeneric type args and routes through the new resolver before falling back to name-based / intrinsic. **Smoke test (chain-past-one-step)**: `equip [I, T] TakeIter[I, T] with Iterator[T]: pass` + `t1: TakeIter[MyIter, int]` + `auto t2 = t1.take(3)` → correctly types as `TakeIter[TakeIter[MyIter, int], int]`. Defined but **NOT called by default** — calling it causes 4 fixture regressions because impl-override method sigs (e.g. `equip [T] Vector[T] with Iterable[T]: VectorIter[T] iter(&self)`) still return the abstract-T placeholder TypeId, masking user-fixture locals when body-scope walks find shadowed `chain` symbols. Closing the gap requires extending the substitution kernel to also rewrite impl-override sigs (store AST return type for ALL methods, not just default-bodied ones; substitute through impl_generic_params at call time). Tracked under (2) in TODO. **`type_comparison` score** unchanged at 903/996 — same caveat as (a2): no fixture stresses generic-impl chain dispatch in the canonical-output bindings the harness scores against. (4) `traits.gg`: `collect_trait` populates the default-shape vectors for any method whose body is non-empty (`is_expr_body` or `body.len() > 0`); `collect_equip` lifts the AST args from `eq.trait_generic_args` into `EquipInfo`; new `substitute_default_return` runs the binding map through `resolve_with_bindings`; new `resolve_method_full` is the substitution-aware variant of `resolve_method` (phases 1+2 unchanged; phase 3 substitutes before returning). Baseline (without substitution) leaves both `a` and `b` untyped because the registry returned `error_id` from the placeholder slots. **`type_comparison` score**: 903/996 unchanged (existing fixtures stress trait override paths, not default inheritance — most equip blocks override every method); **`parser_comparison`** also 939/996 unchanged (parser change preserved). Substrate ready for (a3) adapter-constructor defaults; user-defined-trait + default-body fixtures will see immediate type-resolution improvements once added.
