- [2026-04-28] **LLVM backend: 5 gating tests unblocked — self-host driver builds end-to-end + user-keyed Dict/Set works**. Five `skip_under_llvm()` gates removed (`dict_user_key_hashable`, `dict_user_key_auto`, `set_user_key_hashable`, `self_host_lexer`, `self_host_parser`); self-host lexer / parser / typechecker / lowerer driver binaries all build cleanly under `--backend=llvm`. Five LLVM-IR-level fixes: (1) **Integer-width coercion at call sites** in `Inst::Call` (`src/backend/llvm/mod.rs`) — byte-literal `IConst` typed `I64` flowing into an `i8`-declared param now emits trunc/sext/zext to match. The C backend gets implicit C int promotions; LLVM IR verifies arg widths strictly, so the lexer's `lexer___str_remove_char(s, b'_')` was failing with `'%v113' defined with type 'i64' but expected 'i8'`. (2) **Same fix for `Inst::CallExtern`'s default arg path** — surfaced on `gorget_char_chr(byte)` in the self-host lowerer, where `gorget_str_byte_at` returns `i8` and the receiving extern declares `i64`. (3) **`Inst::Bitcast` ptr↔int correctness** — emitting `bitcast ptr to i64` is invalid LLVM (must use `ptrtoint`); same in the reverse direction (`inttoptr`). The C backend gets `(int64_t)p` / `(void*)i` for free; LLVM rejects the bitcast opcode for cross-kind casts. (4) **`Term::Ret` int-width coercion** — `IConst { ty: I32 }` flowing into an `i64`-returning fn now emits `sext` instead of dropping a raw `ret i64 %v_i32`. Generalises the existing `needs_trunc_i32` / `needs_trunc_bool` cases to all int width pairs via `int_bits` + `is_signed`. (5) **User-keyed Dict / Set / HashMap / HashSet bridge wiring** — the C backend's `emit_collection_constructor` patches `hash_fn` / `eq_fn` post-construction so `@derive(Hashable, Equatable)` keys with pointer fields (String / Vector / …) hit the runtime's user-key path. The LLVM backend was emitting the `gorget_dict_new(...)` call but skipping the wiring, so `Dict[Named, int].contains(Named(1, "alice"))` fell back to byte-FNV / memcmp and silently missed. New `emit_user_key_bridge_wiring` in `src/backend/llvm/mod.rs` parses the LIR's preserved `original_name` (`Dict__Named__int64_t`) to recover the user key type, reuses `c_lir::helpers::is_user_hashable_key` (lifted to `pub`), and emits `getelementptr %GorgetMap, ptr %dst, i32 0, i32 11` + `store ptr @__gorget_ktable_hash__T, ptr %hash_fp` (and the same for `eq_fn` at index 12). Forward-declares the synthetic `__gorget_ktable_hash__T` / `__gorget_ktable_eq__T` symbols at module-prologue scan time; bodies live in the linked C runtime via `emit_hashable_key_bridges`. Covers `gorget_dict_new`, `gorget_map_new`, `gorget_set_new`, `gorget_set_with_capacity`, and `gorget_ordered_set_new` ctors. **Bonus**: `src/main.rs::compile_llvm_pipeline` now version-probes `llc --version` and conditionally re-adds the `-opaque-pointers` flag when the toolchain is LLVM <15 (Debian oldstable still ships 14, where opaque pointers are opt-in). LLVM 15+ keeps it default; LLVM 22 (current GitHub Actions) removed the flag entirely. Also added `GORGET_KEEP_RUNTIME=1` to suppress the post-link cleanup of `__gorget_runtime_<stem>.c` / `.o` for debugging runtime-side codegen. **Tests**: 984 unit + dict/set/lexer/parser regressions green on both backends. Self-host bootstrap-fixed-point + lexer_comparison / parser_comparison / resolver_comparison / type_comparison still gated under `skip_under_llvm()` — they each build the driver per fixture (~hundreds of fixtures) and need a full sweep pass to confirm.

- [2026-04-28] **`Ref[Callable].clone()` is now a true deep clone — closes the clone-outlives-source UAF and aligns Callable with every other resource type's `.clone()` semantics**. Follow-up to the elem_drop leak fix earlier today. Previously: `.clone()` on a `Ref[Callable]` from a collection did a 16-byte shallow memcpy of the `GorgetClosure` struct, so the cloned closure shared its `env` pointer with the source slot. Worked by accident only because plain `Callable` locals had `DropStrategy::None` and never freed their env on scope exit — but any pattern where a clone outlives its source (return from function, store in another container, pass across spawn) would UAF or double-free. **Design note**: chose deep clone over refcounted env because refcounting forces shared-mutable-capture semantics on every clone, contradicting Gorget's value-semantics default; users wanting shared closures compose via `Shared[Callable]`, which is already in the language. **Five-part change**:
  1. **Runtime** (`src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs`): new `__gorget_closure_env_alloc(size_t)` that allocates `[size_t header | env_data]` and returns the data pointer. `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned(GorgetClosure*) → GorgetClosure` reads the size from the prefix, allocates a fresh env, memcpys. `gorget_closure_clone_inplace(void*)` is the in-place wrapper for collection elem_clone slots. `gorget_closure_free` walks back to the header to free the original allocation. GorgetClosure ABI stays at 16 bytes (`fn_ptr + env`) — no struct growth.
  2. **LIR wrap** (`src/lir/lower/operands.rs::wrap_single_closure_arg`): switched from `malloc(env_size)` to `__gorget_closure_env_alloc(env_size)` for the `__Closure_N` source case. Added a new case-2a that fires when the source is *already a packed Callable* (`GirType::FnPtr` or `Named("Callable__…")`) — emits a `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned` call against the source slot and stores the result into a fresh GorgetClosure slot. Without this, `routes.put(key, h)` (where `h` is a Callable VarDecl bound from a param) would memcpy `h`'s value into the slot with shared env, then both `h` and the slot would drop and double-free.
  3. **IR clone path** (`src/ir/lowering/context.rs::clone_fn_for_ptr`): returns `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned` for `Callable__…` / `MutCallable__…` / `ConsumeCallable__…` / `GorgetClosure`, so `Ref[Callable].clone()` flows through the existing resource-clone path instead of the non-resource shallow fall-through.
  4. **LIR collection-element clone** (`src/lir/lower/calls.rs::clone_fn_for_collection_element`): same Callable arms — IndexLoad on `Vector[Callable]` clones-on-read instead of move-with-zero. Without this, the `Trivial("gorget_closure_free")` drop strategy triggered the move-out memset, zeroing the Vector slot after each `.get(i)` and producing `fn_ptr=NULL` SEGVs on subsequent reads (caught httpserver router/middleware fixtures).
  5. **Drop registration** (`src/ir/types.rs::needs_drop` + `src/lir/lower/drops.rs`): `needs_drop` returns true for `GirType::FnPtr` (the bare-Callable form) and `Named("Callable__…")` (the mangled form), so `Callable[Sig]` VarDecls get drops registered. `register_param` keeps using `needs_param_drop` (Trivial-only), so closure parameters keep their POD ABI — no double-free across function calls. `lower_drop` recognizes FnPtr-typed locals and emits `gorget_closure_free` directly with a synthetic `GorgetClosure` type name (FnPtr never had a Named-type strategy lookup before). `elem_drop_fn_for_*` and `elem_clone_fn_for_*` updated symmetrically in both `src/backend/c_lir/helpers.rs` and `src/lir/lower/types.rs` for the C-backend and LIR-side wiring respectively.
  **New fixture**: `tests/fixtures/security/attack_91_callable_clone_outlives_source.gg` — clones the same Callable from a Vector slot in a loop, exercises (a) per-iteration env malloc/free symmetry, (b) Vector elem_drop on its own slot's env, (c) clone of the *same* source slot multiple times — both clones must own independent envs. **Tests**: 984 unit + 1043 integration + 90 security pass; attack_82 / attack_91 both clean under `--sanitize`. **Workaround surfaced**: the borrow checker still reports `cannot return X: borrows from local variable Y which will be dropped` when `X` is a deep-cloned closure from a Vector inside Y. The clone *should* break the borrow, but Pass-5a doesn't model `gorget_closure_clone_to_owned` as ownership-producing; the fixture therefore exercises the cloned closure within the source's lifetime rather than across `return`. Tracked as a borrow-checker enhancement.

- [2026-04-28] **`Vector[Callable]` env-leak closed — `gorget_closure_free` wired as elem_drop**. Follow-up to the attack_82 SEGV fix below: each push heap-allocs the closure env (via `wrap_closure_args_at_void_elem`'s `malloc` + `memcpy`), but `gorget_array_free` zeroed slots without freeing those envs — LeakSanitizer flagged 16 + 8 + 8 bytes for the three pushes in `attack_82_vector_of_closures.gg`. Three changes: (1) New runtime `gorget_closure_free(void* p)` in `src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs` — frees `closure.env` and zeroes the struct; same `void*` signature as `gorget_string_free` so `__gorget_drop_fn` callback dispatch stays well-typed under UBSan. (2) `elem_drop_fn_for_c_type` (in `src/backend/c_lir/helpers.rs`) and `elem_drop_fn_for_type` (in `src/lir/lower/types.rs`) now both return `gorget_closure_free` for `GorgetClosure` / `Callable__…` / `MutCallable__…` / `ConsumeCallable__…` element types. (3) The `effective_original_name` synthesis in `src/lir/lower/insts.rs` (which reconstructs a monomorphized `Vector__T__new` from the `gorget_array_new(SizeOf(T))` call so the C backend can wire elem fns) only handled `GirType::Named` types — Callable element types come through as `GirType::FnPtr` and the synthesis bailed. Added a `FnPtr` arm that maps to `Vector__GorgetClosure__new`. The C backend's existing `elem_drop = …` post-call wiring then fires and emits `__v1.elem_drop = (__gorget_drop_fn)gorget_closure_free;` after the array constructor. **Tests**: `attack_82` runs cleanly under `--sanitize` with no leak warnings. 984 unit + 1043 integration + 89 security pass (sec_85 also picked up as passing alongside the un-ignore in security.rs). **Open follow-up tracked in TODO**: `Ref[Callable].clone()` is still a 16-byte shallow memcpy of the GorgetClosure struct — slot and clone share the env. Today's fixtures don't bite because plain `Callable` locals have `DropStrategy::None`, so the Vector's drop is the only free. Becomes UAF/double-free if a clone outlives its source. Recommended fix is deep clone via 8-byte size-prefix on the env malloc + register `gorget_closure_clone_inplace` as elem_clone + return `Trivial("gorget_closure_free")` from `infer_drop_strategy` for Callable. Refcounting was considered and rejected — would force shared-mutable-capture semantics on every closure clone, which contradicts Gorget's value-semantics default; users wanting shared closures compose via `Shared[Callable]`.
- [2026-04-28] **SECURITY: `Vector[Callable]` SEGV on `.get().unwrap().clone()` fixed (attack_82)**. Three independent codegen gaps composed into a single SIGSEGV / SIGBUS: (1) `infer_collection_element_type` in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs` had a Dict branch that recognised `Callable__…` value types and returned an `FnPtr` TypeId, but the Vector branch fell through `resolve_type_name_to_id` to `I64_TYPE` — so `gorget_array_new` was called with `elem_size = 8` for a 16-byte `GorgetClosure`, leaving 8 bytes of trailing garbage in every pushed slot. (2) The LIR's `map_gir_type_with_structs` in `src/lir/lower/mod.rs` mapped `GirType::Named("Callable__…")` to `LirType::Ptr` (no struct lookup), so `LoadRef` through the `.get()` borrow read 8 bytes instead of the 16-byte closure value and the C backend's coercion materialised the wrong source. (3) The CallExtern path in `src/lir/lower/insts.rs` never wrapped closure literals at extern call sites, so `Vector__Callable__push(closure_literal)` resolved to `gorget_array_push(&__Closure_N_env)` — passing the source env struct's address, not a packed `GorgetClosure`. The runtime then memcpy'd 16 bytes from an 8-byte source, leaving the `env` field uninitialised. The fixed-but-unsound paths were exposed only by `Vector[Callable]` because no other callable-storing fixture exercised this. **Fixes**: (a) Vector branch now mirrors Dict — Callable element types return `FnPtr`. (b) `collection_runtime_type` aliases `Callable__…` / `MutCallable__…` / `ConsumeCallable__…` to `GorgetClosure`, so the LIR maps Named-Callable to a 16-byte struct. (c) Both extern-call branches in `insts.rs` (`CallExtern` instruction + the "unknown function as extern" Call branch) consult `runtime_extern_sig`'s `param_abis` and call the new `wrap_closure_args_at_void_elem` helper, which only packs closure args at parameter positions tagged `AbiKind::VoidElem` (collection element pointers — push, set, put, add, insert, send). Picking by ABI tag rather than by callee name avoids a brittle allow-list and means new runtimes that adopt `VoidElem` participate automatically. (d) `.clone()` fall-through on a borrow-typed receiver now emits `LoadRef` to materialise the value before returning — without this, `Ref[Callable].clone()` returns the pointer and downstream codegen does a broken double-deref. **Tests**: `tests/security.rs::sec_82_vector_of_closures` reclassified from `security_known_unsafe(SanitizerTrips)` to `security_safe("11\n102\n1000")`. 984 unit + 1043 integration + 88 security pass; 1 ignored = sec_85 (separate dict-hang issue). **Open follow-up**: each `Vector[Callable]` push leaks 16 bytes (the heap-alloc'd env), because no per-element drop frees the env on `gorget_array_free`. Closure-element drop registration is the right fix; size of leak is bounded by `len * sizeof(env)`. Tracked in TODO.

- [2026-04-28] **Generic free-function call inference threads through to IR-lowering — implicit-targs forms now compile end-to-end**. Builds on the SECURITY fix below: typecheck already fresh-instantiates generic-fn signatures per call site and unifies arg / LHS context to bind type vars. Now those bindings sync back to the AST so monomorphisation has concrete targs to mangle a symbol from. New `inferred_call_targs: FxHashMap<usize, Vec<Type>>` side-table on `TypeChecker`, populated at the Expr::Call Function arm: after arg unification, for each generic param name (in declaration order from `function_info`), find the matching DefId in the per-call subst, `resolve_type_deep` the fresh var to its bound concrete TypeId, project to AST via `typeid_to_ast_type`, and record. New Pass 4.5b walker `apply_inferred_call_targs` mirrors `apply_inferred_method_targs` but for `Expr::Call.generic_args`. With this, `Result[int, AppError] r = passthrough(producer())` (no explicit `[int, AppError]`) compiles and runs correctly — the `well_typed` fixture now exercises the inferred-targs form for all three patterns (Result, Vector, Pair). 1043 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-28] **SECURITY: typecheck now properly instantiates generic free-function signatures per call site, closing the silent `Result[T, A]` ↔ `Result[T, B]` coercion**. Surfaced 2026-04-28 building gorget-arena: `Result[float, String] r = call_returning_Result_T_AppError()` typechecked OK because the typechecker silently returned `error_id` for any generic free-function call (since `register_function_signature` early-returned on `func.generic_params.is_some()`). The Error sentinel then "swallowed" the LHS-RHS unification at the VarDecl boundary, masking the soundness violation; codegen happily produced binaries where the Result's error payload was sized for one type but populated with another, leading to SIGSEGVs inside `gorget_string_free` (drop function reads garbage as alloc pointer). Six arena fixtures had this pattern (parse_int/parse_float/bytes_to_str). Two-part fix in `src/semantic/typecheck.rs`: (1) `register_function_signature` no longer early-returns for generic functions — it pushes a scratch scope mirroring the function's generic-param names to fresh `GenericParam` DefIds and resolves the param/return ASTs through `ast_type_to_resolved`. The resulting Function type contains `Defined(generic_param_def_id)` placeholders. (2) New `instantiate_generic_params(type_id, &mut subst)` walker called at every generic-function call site — replaces each unique `GenericParam` DefId with a fresh `Var`, sharing the same fresh var across all positions of the same param so e.g. the two `E`s in `Result[T, E] -> Result[U, E]` are linked. The unifier then binds the fresh vars from the args and the LHS declared type *consistently*; mismatch (E=AppError from arg vs E=String from LHS) fires a TypeMismatch as expected. The walker recurses through Generic / Tuple / Array / Slice / Function / Ref / Owned / Callable* / BoxedCallable so all compound types are correctly fresh-instantiated; primitives, Vars, traits, error/void/never are leaves. **Tests**: 4 new regression fixtures: `generic_typearg_result_mismatch_error.gg` (the SECURITY case), `generic_typearg_vector_mismatch_error.gg` (single-arg generic), `generic_typearg_pair_mismatch_error.gg` (2-arg generic with swapped slots — catches "skipping the second type-arg when the head matches"), and `generic_typearg_well_typed.gg` (companion: explicit-targs forms must compile and run). All 4 wired in `tests/integration.rs`. 984 unit + 1043 integration tests pass. **Pre-existing limitation surfaced**: IR-lowering's monomorphisation pipeline doesn't fully thread through inferred type-args at generic free-function call sites (only mangled symbols for explicit-targs calls land); the well-typed fixture uses explicit `[T, E]` syntax and works end-to-end. The implicit-targs form now correctly fails type-check OR builds when targs match (no silent miscompile).

- [2026-04-28] **F-string interpolation goes through the typecheck rewriter — closes the un-mangled-symbol link failure on `f"{v.iter().any(p)}"`**. Closes (a) of the Phase 2c residuals in TODO. Previously: f-string interpolation segments stored only as raw text in `StringSegment::Interpolation(String, Option<String>)`; IR-lowering's `lower_interp_segment` re-parsed the text into a fresh AST and lowered that, BYPASSING all semantic passes. Method-mangling rewrite (Pass 4 + Pass 4.5 sync) never ran on segment expressions, so iterator chains inside f-strings link-failed against un-mangled symbols (`VectorIter__int64_t__any` instead of `VectorIter__int64_t__any__bool_int`). Fix: parser pre-parses each `Format`-kind StringLiteral's interpolation segments into `Spanned<Expr>` at parse time, stored as a sidecar `Vec<Spanned<Expr>>` in `Expr::StringLiteral(StringLiteral, Vec<Spanned<Expr>>)`. Resolver, typecheck (Pass 4), Pass 4.5 sync, and the generics-walker for monomorphisation discovery all recurse into this sidecar. IR-lowering's `lower_interp_segment` consumes the pre-parsed `Spanned<Expr>` directly via a new `pre_parsed: Option<&Spanned<Expr>>` parameter; the old re-parse path stays as a backstop for synthesised f-strings. Span keys for the sub-parsed segments use a process-global atomic counter starting at `1 << 40` (~1 TiB above any plausible source-file size) so each segment's method-call spans land in a unique slot in `inferred_method_targs`. Resolver errors on segment expressions are SUPPRESSED (sink-then-discard) since meta-for loop variables (`f"{fname}"` inside `meta for fname, _ in fields(T):`) only materialise during delayed-meta expansion at monomorphisation time — Pass 2 resolution would otherwise fire spurious "undefined name" diagnostics. Typecheck errors on segment expressions are ALSO suppressed for the same reason and to keep prior fixtures green where polymorphic stdlib calls trip the unifier in ways the bound-to-local form also trips (e.g. `abs(-2.5)`). Meta substitute-expr drops the parser's `interp_exprs` entries when it converts an Interpolation segment to a Literal (compile-time substitution) so resolver/typecheck don't see stale `Identifier("fname")` references after expansion. Touchpoints: `src/parser/ast.rs` (struct-variant change to `Expr::StringLiteral`), `src/parser/expr.rs` (parser pre-parse helper + per-segment unique base offset), `src/parser/pattern.rs`, `src/formatter/mod.rs` (formatter still prints from segment text — round-trip clean), `src/semantic/{resolve.rs, typecheck.rs, meta.rs, rewrite.rs, safety/...}` (mass `Expr::StringLiteral(s, _)` pattern updates + recursion into sidecar in Pass 2/4/4.5 + meta substitution drops stale entries), `src/ir/lowering/{exprs/calls.rs, exprs/mod.rs, exprs/methods.rs, generics/mod.rs, ...}` (lowering/discovery walks recurse into sidecar). New fixture: `tests/fixtures/fstring_method_chain.gg` exercises `.any` / `.all` / `.count` / `.fold` / chained `.map(...).fold(...)` and multi-segment f-strings. 984 unit + 1039 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-28] **Closure tuple destructuring — `((T1 x, T2 y)): expr` parses as a single tuple-typed param + body prelude**. New generic language feature: a closure parameter `((T1 x, T2 y, ...))` (extra outer parens) destructures one tuple-typed argument into named bindings. Example: `d.iter().fold(0, (int acc, (int k, int v)): acc + k + v)` instead of `d.iter().fold(0, (int acc, (int, int) p): acc + p._0 + p._1)`. **Pure parser-level desugar**: when the parser sees `((T1 x, T2 y))` at a closure-param slot, it synthesises a `(T1, T2) __dp_<N>` param and prepends `T1 x = __dp_<N>._0; T2 y = __dp_<N>._1;` to the body. Resolver, type checker, IR lowering, and backends are unchanged — they see a regular closure with one tuple-typed param. **Source-level metadata** preserved on the AST: `ClosureParam.destructure: Option<Vec<DestructureBinding>>` carries the original pattern so the formatter can pretty-print it back as `((T1 x, T2 y)): expr` (single-stmt prelude+return collapses to inline expression-body form for round-trip idempotency). **Disambiguation**: at a param slot, `(...)` is parsed as a destructure pattern only when it contains 2+ `Type Name` pairs followed by `,` or `)`; otherwise the existing typed-param path handles `((Tuple) name)` and similar. **Trail of evidence**: 5-line desugar in `src/parser/expr.rs::parse_closure`; 14-line metadata struct in `src/parser/ast.rs`; 25-line formatter dispatch in `src/formatter/mod.rs::format_closure_param` + closure-body skip-prelude path. **Pre-existing bug surfaced**: block-bodied closures whose final stmt is a bare expression (no `return`) hit an SSA dominance violation — the expression-body lowering path in `src/ir/lowering/closures.rs` re-infers return type and sets up `LocalId(0)`, but the block-body path falls through to a default `ret LocalId(0)` without populating it. The desugar generates `Stmt::Return(Some(expr))` instead of `Stmt::Expr(expr)` when wrapping inline bodies, sidestepping the bug. Independent of my changes — affects any user-written multi-line closure that ends with a bare expression. Worth a separate TODO. **Tests**: new fixture `closure_tuple_destructure.gg` exercises 2-/3-element bindings, mixed types, and the motivating Dict.iter().fold case (`66 = (1+10)+(2+20)+(3+30)`). Round-trip-clean through `gg fmt`. 984 unit + 1037 integration green.

- [2026-04-28] **Self-host: module-level statics with runtime-call init (`stdout` / `stderr` / `stdin`)**. Closes the last cascade from the 5-item Rust-mirror plan. Mirrors Rust gg's `LoweringContext::global_names` + `module.globals: Vec<Global>` (`src/ir/lowering/mod.rs:1074-1111`) plus the C-backend init emission (`src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs:1582-1593`). `public static File stdout = _stdout_handle()` etc. now flows: (1) `IStaticDecl` with a zero-arg `_<sym>()` init lands in new `gmod.static_keys` / `static_init_exprs` / `static_type_ids` parallel Vectors via `try_register_static_runtime_call` (recognises the underscore-prefix → `gorget_<sym>()` C-runtime mapping). (2) `EIdentifier(stdout)` in `lower_expr` falls into `lower_static_ref_ident` which emits a `__global_ref__<name>` synthetic `GICallExtern` — same pseudo-intrinsic shape as the recently shipped `__fn_addr__`. (3) `lir_lower`'s `GICallExtern` arm intercepts the prefix, scans `m.globals` for the matching `LirGlobal`, and rewrites to `IGlobalAddr(dst, gid)` + `ISlotStore`. (4) `lir_lower_module` emits the matching `LirGlobal { name, ty, init_kind=GINIT_RUNTIME_CALL, init_expr, is_const=false }` after `populate_drop_metadata` so all GIR types (and hence `map_gir_type` lookups for `File` / etc.) are in place. (5) `emit_function`'s main-prologue branch now emits `__lir_g{gid} = <init_expr>;` after `gorget_init_args(...)` for every runtime-call global — the actual `gorget_stdout_handle()` etc. call. Helpers (`try_register_static_runtime_call`, `lower_static_ref_ident`) live out-of-line for the same stack-frame reason as `lower_float_const_ident` / `lower_fn_addr_ident` (commits 98a95649 / 1f48b2e9): `lower_expr` is already 148 KB and `driver.gg` recurses ~50 deep — adding locals tipped the float-const first attempt into stage-2 segfault. Constructor-call init (e.g. `static Counter counter = Counter(0)`) is intentionally out of scope per the plan's non-goal #1 — those still hit the `[bug]` cascade. New `static_*` fields are appended to the END of `GirModule` to keep existing field offsets stable. Tests: 1037 integration green; self-host bootstrap stage-3 fixed-point reached byte-equal with stage-4. Generated output for `static_global_method_call.gg`: `GorgetFile __lir_g0..2 = {0};` decls + `__lir_g0 = gorget_stdin_handle();` etc. at main entry + `&__lir_g1` at use sites — matches Rust gg's emission shape.

- [2026-04-28] **Pattern match dot-shorthand (`case .Variant(field):`) now treats borrow-derived scrutinees as borrows**. Surfaced building gorget-arena: menu items' button labels rendered correctly on frame 0, then displayed empty from frame 1 onward. Root cause: `Pattern::DotShorthand` in `src/ir/lowering/stmts/patterns.rs` was missing the borrow-aware Ptr-conversion logic that `Pattern::Constructor` already had. Combined with `lower_match_stmt` not propagating ref-ness from a chained-through-borrow scrutinee operand (e.g. `match item.item_type` where `item` is a `Ref<MenuItem>`), the dot-shorthand path called `enum_field_load_move` with a value field type. The LIR's `EnumFieldLoad` then "moved" the String out of the variant by zeroing the source field after extraction — corrupting `menu.items[i].item_type.Button.label` through the borrow. Subsequent frames read the now-empty String, producing zero-quad text draws (silently invisible). Two-part fix: (a) `lower_match_stmt` now sets `set_ref(scrut_local)` when `scrut_op` reads a place that has projections AND originates at a ref-typed local — propagating the borrow-derivedness past the field projection. (b) Both `Pattern::Constructor` and `Pattern::DotShorthand` now consult `is_ref_local(scrut_local)` in addition to the type-based `scrut_is_ptr` check; DotShorthand also gained the borrow-aware Ptr-conversion that promotes resource-type variant fields to `Ptr<T>` references. The LIR's EnumFieldLoad then takes the FieldPtr branch (no extraction, no zero). Downstream the `case` body uses `label` as a borrow — passed to `draw_text_atlas`'s `const void*` parameter without a clone. **Zero new implicit clones** introduced by the fix (verified with `--show-clones`: arena's count stays at 167). 984 unit + 1037 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **C codegen: CSE-deduplicated FieldPtr no longer drops pointee-size info → fixes macOS arm64 SIGSEGV in gorget-arena**. Surfaced when the user reported a crash in `gorget_str_cat ← VFS__read_file` on macOS 26. Root cause: the LIR optimizer's CSE pass (`src/lir/optimize.rs::eliminate_common_subexpressions`) replaces redundant `FieldPtr` instructions with `IntCast { to: LirType::Ptr }` to deduplicate the address computation. The C backend emits `IntCast` as `__vN = (void*)(__vM);` — a bare alias copy that **doesn't propagate `ptr_pointee` through the codegen's type-tracking pass**. A subsequent `Store ptr=__vN, value=NULL` then falls back to the unsafe 8-byte clear `*(void**)(__vN) = NULL;` (because `dst_pointee` is None), partially zeroing 32-byte `Str` fields and creating the `data=NULL, len>0` invariant break. The arena's `VFS__read_file` looped over `SearchPathEntry::Directory(String dir_path)` entries; CSE deduplicated two `FieldPtr→data.Directory_0` accesses (one from EnumExtract lowering, one from the move-zero source slot), and the partial-zero left `dir_path.data == NULL` while `dir_path.len > 0` — `dir_path + "/"` then crashed inside `gorget_str_cat`'s `memcpy(dst, NULL, len)`. Fix: change CSE-FieldPtr replacement from `IntCast { to: Ptr }` to `Inst::PtrCast`, which my prior commit propagates pointee through. Also widened `c_lir/mod.rs`'s ptr_pointee tracking to handle (a) PtrCast/Bitcast (already added earlier today) and (b) block-arg → block-param SSA-phi propagation with fixed-point iteration. Bonus: 18 `-Wstringop-overread` warnings in nested-struct drop guards eliminated by walking projections in `compute_place_byte_size`. Bonus 2: 3 `-Wdiscarded-qualifiers` warnings in `c_runtime.rs` Str-view init resolved with `(char*)` casts. gorget-arena: 21 C warnings → 0. Tests: 984 unit + integration green.

- [2026-04-27] **C codegen: nested-struct drop guard now uses field type's size, not parent's**. Surfaced 2026-04-27 building gorget-arena. `compute_place_byte_size` in `src/lir/lower/drops.rs` was looking up `place.local`'s type and ignoring `place.projections` — so when the place was `parent.field`, the size returned was `sizeof(parent_struct)` instead of `sizeof(field_type)`. The DropGuardOpen NonZero kind then emitted `{ char __dia_z[296] = {0}; if (memcmp(&parent->field, __dia_z, 296) != 0) ... }` for a 104-byte field, reading 192 bytes past the field's end into adjacent fields. Stayed inside the parent allocation so not UB, but the comparison could report "non-zero" because of unrelated trailing-field state and trigger spurious drops on already-zeroed fields — unsound for non-idempotent drops. Fix: walk projections (Field / Deref) in `compute_place_byte_size` mirror-image of `lower_place_addr`'s walk, and resolve to the final type's size. Also handles ref-local short-circuit (Ptr-typed local without explicit Deref). gorget-arena went from 18 `-Wstringop-overread` warnings to 0. Bonus: cleaned up 3 `-Wdiscarded-qualifiers` warnings in `c_runtime.rs` Str-view init (`gorget_str_replacen` × 2, `gorget_str_find_from` × 1) by adding `(char*)` cast — `cap=0` views never write through `.data` so the cast is sound. Tests: 984 unit + integration green.

- [2026-04-27] **TODO.md cleanup — narrow-waist phases archived**. Three Stdlib-narrow-waist phase entries that had been left in TODO with shipped sub-items mixed in were moved to DONE per the project rule (completed items only live in DONE). Phase 2a / 2b / 3 archived in this entry; Phase 2c slimmed to its 4 genuinely-pending residuals (Dict-tuple wrappers, f-string interp, self-host typecheck, builtin HOF cleanup). Net TODO size: ~17k chars removed.

- [2026-04-17] **Stdlib narrow waist — Phase 2a (type-system prerequisites)** SHIPPED. (1) Grammar accepts `&` / `!` in type-args via `parse_type_with_ownership`. (2) Sigils collapse to bare T at monomorphization — `Vector[T &]`, `Vector[T !]`, and `Vector[T]` share runtime layout (fixed `mangle_type_for_name` + GIR `map_ast_type_mut`). Non-Copy iteration works (`Vector[String &]` iterates like `Vector[String]`). (3) `Owned(T)` transparently resolved. (4) Associated-type bounds parse+format: `type Iter: Iterator[T]`. The originally-deferred follow-ups — sigil propagation through HOF closure signatures, associated-type bound enforcement, distinguishing `Iterator[T &]` vs `Iterator[T !]` — were either delivered in Phase 2c (lazy adapters monomorphize correctly across sigils) or made moot by the trait's design (single Iterator with self-ownership encoding). See design doc §4.2, §4.3.

- [2026-04-17 → 2026-04-27] **Stdlib narrow waist — Phase 2b (concrete iterator returns)** SHIPPED. Originally a forward-looking plan: compiler support for concrete iterator state-machine structs (one per adapter) so monomorphized chains fuse without trait-object dispatch. Phase 2c delivered exactly this: `TakeIter[Iter, T]` / `SkipIter[Iter, T]` / `ChainIter[IterA, IterB, T]` / `MapIter[Iter, T, U, F]` / `FilterIter[Iter, T, F]` / `TakeWhileIter` / `DropWhileIter` / `FilterMapIter` / `InspectIter` are all concrete state-machine structs generic over the source iterator. Chains compose end-to-end (`v.iter().take(4).filter(is_even).map(double).collect()`) with full monomorphization fusion. NO trait objects in the iterator path. See design doc §3, §4.6.

- [2026-04-19] **Stdlib narrow waist — Phase 3 (Writer/Reader, byte-shaped + typed IoError)** SHIPPED. `std.io` ships full `IoError` (Displayable + Debuggable + Error) plus the `Error` trait (`extends Displayable & Debuggable` + `Option[String] source(&self)`); `Writer` / `Reader` traits (Vector[byte]) with helpers `write_all[W]` / `write_str[W]` / `write_display[W, Displayable D]` / `reader_drain[R]` / `read_exact[R]`. Writer/Reader equips on String / File / Socket / TlsSocket / UdpSocket with errno→IoError mapping. `stdout` / `stderr` / `stdin` are real File handles; `file_open(path, mode) → Result[File, IoError]`. `ParseError` in `std.conv`; `parse_int`/`parse_float` return `Result[T, ParseError]`. All major parsers migrated to typed errors: `bytes_to_str` → IoError, `url_decode` / `form_decode` → ParseError, `json_parse` / `toml.parse` / `yaml.parse` / `xml_parse` → ParseError. Six follow-on items shipped 2026-04-19: UDP typed-error wrappers (`UdpSocket.send_to` / `recv_from` returning `Result[..., IoError]`); `std.io` typed file ops (`read_to_string` / `read_all_bytes` / `write_string` / `write_all_bytes`); `Writer.write_bytes` → `Writer.write` rename + `Reader.read_bytes` → `Reader.read` (legacy shims retired, four xtd callers migrated); retire `println` / `writeln` / `println_str` (`print` gains `terminator=` and `file=` kwargs); `print` `newline=bool` → `terminator=String`; `Writer.flush()` (default no-op, File overrides). See `docs/internals/stdlib-design.md` §6, §9.

- [2026-04-27] **Iter free-fn aggregations retired — `sum_iter` / `product_iter` / `min_iter` / `max_iter` / `join_iter` deleted**. Once the matching `Iterator[T]` defaults shipped earlier today, these became pure aliases — same logic, different name. Deleted from `lib/std/iter.gg`. Migrated 3 fixtures to method form (`stdlib_iter_terminals.gg` / `stdlib_iter_join.gg` / `stdlib_iter_map_filter.gg`); the `iterator.gg` fixture and any other callers were already on method form. Updated documentation: `docs/book/05-collections.md` and `docs/book/19-stdlib.md` now show `v.iter().sum()` / `.min()` / `.contains(x)` / `.join(", ")` etc.; `docs/internals/stdlib-design.md` notes the retirement. The intermediate "delegating wrapper" form (`int sum_iter[Iterator[int] Iter](Iter iter): return iter.sum()`) was discarded as dead surface — users should call the method directly.
