- [2026-04-27] **Iterator[T] join default shipped — Displayable.display() dispatch through abstract T**. Last bound-needing terminal joins the rest as an `Iterator[T]` default. Body uses `x.display()` directly on abstract `T`; the same `generic_type_params` (Self + trait T) binding fix that unblocked `sum`/`product` (commit 803adb53) was already enough for `join` — typecheck and method-instance discovery had the machinery, only the IR-side body lowering needed the binding. No additional code changes; just added `join` to `lib/std/iter.gg` and a fixture line. With this, every bound-needing terminal now has a canonical method form: `v.iter().min()` / `.max()` / `.contains(x)` / `.sum()` / `.product()` / `.join(sep)`. Free-function variants (`min_iter` / `max_iter` / `sum_iter` / `product_iter` / `join_iter`) retained as alternatives. Fixture extended: `stdlib_iter_more_terminals.gg` now exercises `joined=[2, 3, 4]` and `empty_joined=[]`. Tests: 984 unit + 1036 integration green; `lowerer_comparison` 816/964 stable. Closes Phase 2c (c) Bound-needing-defaults item completely — the original "deferred" list of 6 terminals (`min`/`max`/`sum`/`product`/`join`/`contains`) is now zero.

- [2026-04-27] **Iterator[T] sum/product defaults shipped — `T.default()` / `T.one()` lowering fixed**. Closes the blocker recorded earlier today. Two-part fix: (1) **Body lowering**: in `lower_unregistered_trait_equip_methods` and `emit_default_methods_from_trait` (src/ir/lowering/traits.rs), bind `generic_type_params` (Self + trait T) for the trait-default body's lowering duration with a save/restore guard. Without this, `T.default()` inside a `sum` default — parsed as `Expr::MethodCall { receiver: Identifier("T"), method: "default" }` — falls out of `lower_method_call`'s static path because `generic_type_params.get("T")` returned None, and the unresolved `Identifier("T")` got lowered as the `Constant::I64(0)` placeholder via the `else` branch in `Expr::Identifier` lowering, producing a bogus `int64_t__default(int64_t)` call (taking self) that conflicted with the prelude's no-arg `static inline int64_t int64_t__default(void)` definition. With the binding in place, the static path correctly resolves `T → int → int64_t__default()` (no args). (2) **Prelude widening**: registered `__default` and `__one` fn_sigs for all sized integers (`int8_t`, `int16_t`, `int32_t`, `uint8_t`, `uint16_t`, `uint32_t`, `uint64_t`) and `float`. Previously only `int64_t` / `double` / `bool` were registered; T = uint8 etc. would hit the I64 ret-type fallback and emit a `int64_t uint8_t__default(void);` forward decl that conflicted with the C runtime's `uint8_t uint8_t__default(void)`. Helpers `build_generic_type_params` / `build_type_name_subs` made `pub(super)` so traits.rs can call them. Fixture extended: `stdlib_iter_more_terminals.gg` now exercises `sum=60`, `empty_sum=0`, `product=24`, `empty_product=1`. Tests: 984 unit + 1036 integration green, self-host bootstrap and fixed-point both pass. Original misdiagnosis ("`register_method_instance_sigs` misregisters T.default()") was wrong — that path was never on the trace; the actual bug was `generic_type_params` not being set up before the trait-default body lowered.
- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: `Type[T].method()` parameterised receiver pattern**. `Heap[int].new()` / `SparseSet[int].new()` / `Container[Foo].make(...)` etc. parse as `EMethodCall(EIndex(Type, Arg), method, ...)`. The receiver is EIndex (not EIdentifier), so the static-method check missed them — the lowerer walked into EIndex and lowered `Heap` / `SparseSet` / `int` as bare value identifiers, emitting `[bug] EIdentifier` for each. Added an EIndex pre-pass in `EMethodCall`: when the receiver is `EIndex(EIdentifier(base), EIdentifier(arg))`, synthesize an EIdentifier-shaped receiver `<base>__<arg>` (with `int → int64_t` / `float → double` / `String → GorgetString` surface→C mapping, plus `gmod.type_subs` for substituted generics) and feed it into the existing static-method logic. Also relaxed `is_type` to treat any name containing `__` as a mangled type — `Container__Foo` / `SparseSet__int64_t` aren't always in `type_infos` at lowering time (lazy registration), but Gorget identifiers can't contain `__`, so the separator is a reliable type signal. **Impact**: total EIdentifier `[bug]` markers across 989 fixtures: 539 → 497 (42 fewer). `int`, `SparseSet`, `Heap` cascades all closed. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: prelude generic types as static-method receivers (`Box.new(x)` / `Vector.from(...)` / `Heap.new()`)**. The static-method-receiver check in `EMethodCall` only knew about user-defined struct/enum names (via `type_infos`) and primitive Gorget types (`int`, `float`, `String`, etc.). Prelude generic types — `Box`, `Heap`, `Vector`, `Deque`, `Dict`, `HashMap`, `Set`, `HashSet`, `Channel`, `Shared`, `Weak`, `Option`, `Result` — were missing because their unparameterised names aren't registered in `type_infos` (only mono'd `Box__T` etc. are). `Box.new(x)` etc. fell through to the bare-EIdentifier path and emitted `[bug] EIdentifier: unknown identifier 'Box'`. Added them to the `is_type` short-circuit. **Impact**: total EIdentifier `[bug]` markers across 989 fixtures: 570 → 539 (31 fewer Box cases). All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: type-param substitution at static method receivers (`T.default()`)**. Monomorphized bodies like `equip [T] SetIter[T] with Iterator[T]: Option[T] next(...): T out = T.default()` had `T` as the receiver of a static method call. The lowerer's `EMethodCall` static-receiver check looked up `ident_name` in `type_infos` / primitive list — `T` matched neither, so it fell through to the non-static path and lowered `T` as a bare EIdentifier (which had no binding in the local table, emitting a `[bug]` placeholder). Fix: at the top of the static-receiver match, look `ident_name` up in `gmod.type_subs` first — if `setup_type_subs(T → int64_t)` already ran, the receiver becomes `int64_t` and the static path proceeds normally. Also extended the `is_type` primitive list to include the C-level names (`int64_t` / `int32_t` / `int16_t` / `int8_t` / `uint64_t..uint8_t` / `double` / `GorgetString`) since `type_id_to_name` returns the C name after substitution, not the surface `int` / `float` spelling. **Impact**: `T.default()` (and other static method calls on a substituted T) now dispatches to the concrete `int64_t__default()` etc. rather than emitting `[bug]`. Fixture sweep: total EIdentifier `[bug]` markers 617 → 570 (45 fewer; the bare-`T` count dropped from 66 → 21). All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: compound-assign bitwise/wrap variants + `x in collection`**. `map_compound_binop` was missing `+%=` / `-%=` / `*%=` / `&=` / `|=` / `^=` / `<<=` / `>>=` (38 [bug] occurrences across the fixture sweep — silently miscompiled as `+=`). Added the cases. Separately, `x in collection` was hitting `map_binop("in")` and silently mis-compiling as `x + collection` (10 [bug] occurrences). Added an EBinaryOp pre-pass in `lower.gg:~1196` that recognises `in` and routes to `<RecvTypeName>__contains(collection, x)` — Vector / Set / Dict / String all expose `contains` as the runtime call, so the existing `Type__method` mangling reaches the correct gorget_*_contains. Combined: `map_binop` total [bug] count across 989 fixtures: 24 → 0. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: `Vector[T].remove(idx)` returns `Option[T]` (not void)**. `infer_method_return_type` had `remove` lumped with `push`/`set`/`put`/`clear` as void-returning. But Vector's `.remove(idx)` actually returns `Option[T]` (`gorget_array_remove_opt` runtime). Misclassifying it left `T x = v.remove(i).unwrap()` typed unit, and every subsequent `x.field` access cascaded into `EFieldAccess: unknown field on base type 'unit'`. Fixed by routing `remove` through the receiver-aware path (line ~752) that already infers element types for `pop` / `get` / `unwrap` — Vector/Deque receivers now produce the element type T. **Receiver-aware carve-out**: `Dict[K,V].remove(key)` and `Set[T].remove(elem)` stay void-returning because the underlying runtime fns (`gorget_map_remove` / `gorget_set_remove`) return bool but every self-host call site discards the result, and a non-void return broke the stage-1 bootstrap (`bool` assigning to `void*` local at the discarded-result site `lir_ssa.gg::find_promotable_slots`). The Vector-only carve-out keeps the `Option[Task[void]]` / `Option[ReliableStream]` pattern working. **Impact**: `p2p_nat.gg` `[bug]` count: 256 → 7 (96% drop — the cascade was almost entirely the `unit` confusion). Full-fixture sweep across 989 fixtures: total `[bug]` markers 12,705 → 8,315 (35% reduction); dirty-fixture count 185 → 177. All 1036 integration tests pass (one re-run was needed: a flaky `vector_task_get` race tripped the Monitor). The remaining 7 `[bug]`s in `p2p_nat.gg` are `host`/`port` field access on `int64_t` — separate type-inference issue around `Dict[String, PeerInfo].get(k)`'s element type cascading through `unwrap()` (the existing TODO entry on `collection_element_type` not handling Dict).

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: bitwise operators `&` / `|` / `^` / `<<` / `>>`**. Fixture sweep showed 12,705 `[bug]` markers across 185 dirty fixtures (out of 989 total) — `p2p_nat.gg` topped the list at 304, with 48 of those being `map_binop: unknown operator` for bitwise spellings. New `OP_BITAND=9 / OP_BITOR=10 / OP_BITXOR=11 / OP_SHL=12 / OP_SHR=13` constants in `gir.gg`; `map_binop` accepts the spellings; `lir_lower` maps them to `IBitAnd` / `IBitOr` / `IBitXor` / `IShl` / `IShr` (already exposed by `lir.gg`); `format_gir.gg::binop_name` prints `bitand` / `bitor` / `bitxor` / `shl` / `shr`. `p2p_nat.gg` `[bug]` count: 304 → 256 (the 48 bitwise-op cascades closed). The remaining 256 are `EFieldAccess: unknown field on base type 'unit' / 'int64_t'` — deeper type-inference issue inside the `xtd__p2p__*` trait impl methods, separate investigation. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Comparable-bounded Iterator defaults shipped — `min` / `max` / `contains`**. Added default-method bodies for these three terminals to `Iterator[T]` in `lib/std/iter.gg`. Bodies use `<` / `>` / `==` directly on the abstract `T` — the demand-gate (`all_return_nominals_registered` + `try_register_method_instance` extended subs from the 2026-04-21 chain-past-one-step work) only emits each per-impl monomorphisation when a call site actually reaches for it, so Iterator implementors with non-Comparable / non-Equatable T's never have these specialised. The previously-feared self-host bootstrap regression (2026-04-20) no longer reproduces — `self_host_bootstrap` and `self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` both pass green; `lowerer_comparison` actually IMPROVES from 814/964 (84.4%) to 816/964 (84.6%) since the new defaults register cleanly per-impl. Method form is canonical now: `v.iter().min()` / `.max()` / `.contains(x)`. Fixture: `tests/fixtures/stdlib_iter_more_terminals.gg` extended with `min=10` / `max=14` / `empty_min=none` / `has12=true` / `has99=false` coverage. STILL DEFERRED (separate compiler bugs, not the Comparable-bound issue): `sum` / `product` defaults blocked on `T.default()` static-call sig conflict (registers `<T>__default(<T>)` taking self instead of `<T>__default()`); `join` default blocked on threading `Displayable.display()` dispatch through default-method emission for abstract `T`. Free-function variants (`sum_iter`, `product_iter`, `join_iter`) ship in `std.iter` for those three. Closes one of the four sub-items under TODO Phase 2c (c).

- [2026-04-27] **SECURITY: Dict with `@derive(Hashable, Equatable)` struct key — ill-typed C bridge** (closes attack_85). `__gorget_ktable_eq__T` was emitting `T__eq(__a, __b)` with both args as `const void*`, but `Type__eq` lowers in two distinct shapes:
  - **POD** (no resource fields, e.g. `Point { int x; int y }`): `Type__eq(*Self, Self) -> bool` — second by VALUE.
  - **Resource-bearing** (e.g. `Named { int id; String name }`): `Type__eq(*Self, *Self) -> bool` — second by POINTER (the auto-clone-on-pass rule).

  The bridge now inspects the eq fn's actual LIR signature (`module.functions.iter().find(|f| f.name == eq_name)` then check `params[1]`). If it's `LirType::Ptr` or `LirType::PtrTo(_)`, pass `__b` straight through; otherwise emit `*(const __gg_{ty}*)__b` to deref to the value the impl wants. Two distinct C bridges depending on the shape:
  - POD: `static bool __gorget_ktable_eq__Point(const void* __a, const void* __b) { return Point__eq(__a, *(const __gg_Point*)__b); }`
  - Resource: `static bool __gorget_ktable_eq__Named(const void* __a, const void* __b) { return Named__eq(__a, __b); }`

  Verified end-to-end: `attack_85_dict_struct_key.gg` (Point — POD) prints "origin-ish/origin-ish" finding equal-by-value Point keys. `dict_user_key_hashable.gg` (Named — resource) keeps printing "finds alice/missing ok/2" — the new branch handles both shapes. The matching self-host bridge in `lir_codegen.gg` already passed `__a, __b` (treating both as opaque pointers); since self-host's eq lowering convention is consistent across types, no change needed there. All 1036 integration tests pass. (One re-run was needed: a transient `PermissionDenied` parallelism flake in `c_emit_comparison` / `lowerer_comparison` cleared on second pass — those tests share `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/driver` and occasionally race despite `#[serial(self_host_lowerer_driver)]`.)

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: explicit-trait self-cast alias was breaking param→slot mapping**. Earlier today's `equip X with Trait:` self-cast fix (`*unit` self → concrete-typed alias) added the alias local at position 2, BETWEEN the params. `lir_lower`'s param-to-slot mapping uses `local_to_slot[pci+1]` — with N params it writes to slots 1..N. With the alias inserted at slot 2, the v param (at slot 3) never received an `IParamRef + ISlotStore`, so every load of v read uninitialised memory. Symptom: `Hasher_for_FxHasher__write_int`'s body emitted `__v12 = __v9 + __v15;` where `__v15` was a `void* __v15;` declared but never assigned, while the actual v param sat in `__v1` unused. Fix: defer alias creation until AFTER the param loop in `lower_equip_block` — locals 1..N stay pure params; the alias takes the next free local. The alias's `GIAssign(concrete, OpCopy(self_void))` lands in the entry block before any body statements, so `self.field` accesses still see the cast pointer. Verified `Hasher_for_FxHasher__write_int` now reads `__v12 = (int64_t)__v9 + (int64_t)__v1;` (correctly using v) — FxHasher state arithmetic actually works for the first time. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: wrapping arithmetic ops `+%` / `-%` / `*%`**. `map_binop` didn't recognize the wrapping spellings; every `state *% 31 +% v` body fell through to the OP_ADD default with a `[bug]` diagnostic, AND silently mis-compiled the multiplications as additions. New `OP_ADD_WRAP=6 / OP_SUB_WRAP=7 / OP_MUL_WRAP=8` constants in `gir.gg`; `map_binop` accepts the `+%`/`-%`/`*%` spellings; `lir_lower` maps them to `IAdd`/`ISub`/`IMul` with `OVF_WRAP` (vs the default `OVF_TRAP`); the existing C codegen at `lir_codegen.gg:2651-2670` already emits plain `lhs + rhs` for non-trap overflow, so the C output now reads `__v9 = (int64_t)__v5 * (int64_t)__v6;` (vs the previous `__builtin_mul_overflow(...)` trap). `format_gir.gg::binop_name` extended to print `add_wrap` / `sub_wrap` / `mul_wrap` for the new ops. `[bug]` count in `dict_user_key_hashable.gg` self-host C output dropped 12 → 0 — combined with the prior `Hasher_for_FxHasher_*` self-cast fix, every diagnostic from that fixture is now closed. (A pre-existing SSA bug — `__v15` used uninitialized in the FxHasher state arithmetic — survives unchanged; verified by stash-replay against the previous commit.) All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: explicit-trait `equip X with T:` self-cast — `self.field` no longer hits "unknown field on base type 'unit'"**. `lower_equip_block` typed the `self` parameter as `*unit` for non-derive trait impls (Rust convention — vtable dispatch carries an opaque pointer) but ALSO bound the name-table entry `self` to that `*unit` local. Every `self.field` access then went through the EFieldAccess path with `base_type_name == "unit"` which has no fields, falling through to the `[bug] EFieldAccess: unknown field 'state' on base type 'unit' — returning I64(0) placeholder (WRONG)` cascade. The actual `equip FxHasher with Hasher: void write_int(&self, int v): self.state = ...` body silently lowered to a write-of-zero. Fix mirrors Rust's `ptr_cast` pattern: keep the param signature as `*unit` (the vtable still wants opaque pointers), but introduce a concrete-typed alias local of `*FxHasher` (or `*mut FxHasher` for `&self` / `!self`), emit `_2 = copy _1` to populate it, and bind `self` in the name table to the alias. Field accesses now go through the concrete pointer; the C codegen folds the implicit pointer-pointer cast. GIR for `Hasher_for_FxHasher__write_int` reads cleanly: `_1: *mut unit (self_void); _2: *mut FxHasher (self); _2 = copy _1; _4 = call_extern @__field_read_FxHasher_state(copy _2, const 0i64); ...`. `[bug]` markers in `dict_user_key_hashable.gg` self-host C output dropped from 16 to 12 (the four `Hasher_for_FxHasher__{write_int,write_bytes,write_string,finish}` cascade entries closed). Remaining 12 are unrelated `*%`/`+%` wrapping-op cascade in `map_binop`. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host parser: method-level type args (`v.hash[FxHasher](&h)`) — `parse_dot_expr` was dropping the call entirely**. Self-host's `parse_dot_expr` only checked for `(args)` after a method name; when `[T1, T2, ...](args)` followed instead, the `[...]` got swallowed by the outer pratt loop as an index access and the trailing `(...)` was treated as a call on the result. For `v.hash[FxHasher](&h)`: parsed as `EIndex(EFieldAccess(v, "hash"), FxHasher_as_ident)` then `(args)` — an EIndex/ECall chain that the lowerer then silently dropped because `(v.hash)[FxHasher]` doesn't resolve to anything callable. Effect: `hash_of[T]`'s body skipped the `v.hash[FxHasher](&h)` step entirely; every user-derived `hash_of[T]` returned the FxHasher seed (state=0). GIR for `hash_of__Named` showed the FxHasher being created and `FxHasher__finish` being called with NO `Named__hash` call between them. Fix: `parse_dot_expr` now peeks for `[` after the method name, parses the type-arg list, and requires a `(` to follow — emitting `EMethodCall(recv, name, args, type_args)` with the parsed type args. Falls back to the existing path (plain method call or field access) if the `[` doesn't head a turbofish + call. Mirrors the outer pratt loop's existing handling for ECall generic constructors (parser.gg:~1499). Verified: `hash_of__Named`'s GIR now reads `_3 = call @FxHasher(copy _2); _4 = copy _3; call_extern @Named__hash(move _1, copy _4); _6 = call_extern @FxHasher__finish(move _4); return copy _6` — the call IS emitted. The LIR lowerer auto-adapts the by-value FxHasher arg to a pointer for the `Named__hash(*Named, *FxHasher)` ABI. Combined with the `@derive(Hashable)` primitive specialisation and the Dict/Set hash-bridge wiring landed earlier today, `Dict[UserStruct, V]` is now correctly hashed end-to-end on the self-host emit side. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: primitive-aware `@derive(Hashable)` emission**. `gen_struct_hashable` and `gen_enum_hashable` in `tests/fixtures/self_host_typechecker/derive.gg` were emitting `self.field.hash(&h)` for every field — which lowered to non-existent symbols like `int64_t__hash`, `bool__hash`, `byte__hash`. The C link path either failed or DCE'd the impl entirely so `Named__hash` was missing and the Dict[UserStruct, V] hash bridges had nothing to dispatch to. Fix mirrors Rust's primitive-aware lowering: new `hashable_field_line` helper specialises for primitives (`int` → `h.write_int(self.id)`, `String` → `h.write_string(self.name)`, etc.) and falls back to `self.field.hash(&h)` for non-primitives. Both struct and enum derive paths use the helper. Derived `Named__hash` now correctly emits `FxHasher__write_int(__v1, __v4); FxHasher__write_string(__v1, __v10);` matching Rust's emission shape. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host: hashable-key bridges + dict-ctor wiring for `Dict[UserStruct, V]`**. Without runtime wiring, `Dict[Named, int]` falls back to byte-FNV / memcmp on the key bytes regardless of the user's `@derive(Hashable, Equatable)`. Mirrors Rust's `c_lir/mod.rs::emit_hashable_key_bridges` and the matching ctor wiring in `c_lir/emit_call_extern.rs`. Six new helpers in `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_codegen.gg`: `is_primitive_hashable_key` / `is_runtime_dict_or_set_ctor` / `extract_user_hashable_key` / `hashable_key_fn_names` / `collect_hashable_key_types` / `emit_hashable_key_bridges` / `emit_dict_ctor_wiring`. `generate_c` emits `static uint64_t __gorget_ktable_hash__T(const void* __kp)` / `static bool __gorget_ktable_eq__T(...)` after forward decls, and the ICallExtern dispatch appends `dst.hash_fn = ...; dst.eq_fn = ...; dst.key_drop = ...; dst.key_clone = ...;` after each Dict/Set ctor. Also fixed the existing Hashable-key DCE-roots block — was over-strict (required `__new` suffix) so it missed self-host's bare `Dict__K__V` ctor name; now gates on the post-mapped runtime name (`gorget_dict_new` etc.). Side benefit: `T__hash` / `T__eq` now stay alive through DCE so the bridges have something to call. All 1036 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-27] **Self-host bootstrap fixed point — `stage-2 == stage-3` byte-equal**. The self-hosting compiler converges: stage-1 (compiled by Rust `gg` from the self-host driver source) emits stage-2.c, which after cc gives stage-2 binary; stage-2 binary emits stage-3.c on the same driver.gg source, and `cmp stage-2.c stage-3.c` returns success. `tests/integration.rs::self_host_bootstrap_fixed_point` un-#[ignore]'d and passes in ~160s. Closing this milestone took ~50 commits over multiple sessions of fighting Dict[String, _] state-loss + non-deterministic Dict iteration order at stage-1 runtime. Highlights: (1) `gmod.named_types`, `gmod.type_infos`, `gmod.call_redirects`, `gmod.fn_sigs`, `gmod.type_subs`, `m.enum_variant_parent`, `m.enum_variant_tag`, `StructRegistry.name_to_id` all migrated to parallel-Vector storage to dodge Dict put/contains/get state-loss. (2) `emit_variant_arg` LT_PTR deref instead of `(Str){0}` zero-init — closed the GtNamed("") cascade that produced `__v0, __v2);` orphan calls in user main(). (3) Inner `String out = ""` shadows in `emit_call_extern_with` renamed to unique names — closed orphan-call-arg cascade. (4) `lookup_ctor_field_type` uses parallel ti_vals — closed match-arm-binding "base type 'int64_t'" cascade. (5) SSA `patch_terminators` iterates `pending_phi_bbs` insertion-order (not Dict.keys() non-deterministic order) — fixed block-param arg-list scrambling. (6) Box allocator scan replaced from broken body-string scan with LIR-based ICall walk. (7) EDeref builds inner-type name via `byte_at(i)` + `chr()` byte-by-byte loop — stage-1's `.substring()` returned empty mid-string. (8) `apply_container_hint_for_ctor_arg` uses parallel ti_vals; extracts field type_name by index without value-copying GirTypeInfo (its nested Vectors don't survive a shallow clone in stage-1). (9) `Module` got `cr_keys`/`cr_vals` fields populated by `cr_put_module` in loader.gg — last-write-wins parallel mirror of call_redirects so lower.gg can read deterministic state without going through Dict.keys() at stage-1 runtime. (10) `emit_struct_drops` / `_clones` / `emit_enum_drops` / `_clones` / `emit_type_drop_fns` sort their Dict.keys() before emitting forward declarations. **Stage-2 metrics journey:** [bug] markers 13179 → 8 (matches stage-1 exactly). Duplicate structs: 69 → 0. Orphan calls: 4866 → 0. cc errors: 6388 → 0. Linker errors: ~25 → 0. Stage-2 binary on hello.gg works; on driver.gg produces byte-identical output to stage-2's source. The self-host's Dict[String, _] is officially deprecated for any state used during emission — the workaround pattern is now codified across the codebase. 984 unit + 1034 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-26] **Phase 4 closed for real — Hashable now generic over Hasher (`void hash[Hasher H](self, H &h)`)**. Walked back the previous "MOSTLY DONE" classification — the consumer-chooses-Hasher capability the §3 design promised IS shipped now. Three compiler fixes plus the breaking migration: (1) **Bound-method-generic body dispatch.** Per-call-site mono of free generic functions like `apply[Hashable T, Hasher H](T v, H &h): v.hash[H](&h)` was discovering method-call instances against the abstract `T`, finding nothing, and falling through to the trait vtable forwarder — which had an empty body for method-generic methods (the body lowering can't bind `H` against an abstract receiver). Fix at `src/ir/lowering/generics/mod.rs` `discover_transitive` Function arm: after substituting the body, run `walk_fn_body_for_method_calls` with an env populated from the substituted params so nested method-instance registrations fire. (2) **Targ name substitution at call-site mangling.** The dispatch in `lower_method_call` mangled the call's targ AST as-is — `v.hash[H](&h)` produced `Point__hash__H` instead of `Point__hash__MyHasher` because the `H` AST node wasn't resolved through `generic_param_ast_types`. Added explicit substitution lookup at the dispatch's targ-mangling step (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs`). (3) **Generic primitive-hash dispatch.** The IR-side fast path for `x.hash(&h)` on int/bool/String hardcoded `FxHasher__write_int` / `FxHasher__write_string`. Replaced with a runtime lookup of the hasher arg's actual type — falls back to `Hasher_for_<H>__write_int` when the user-defined Hasher only provides the `equip H with Hasher:` block (no inherent equip). Verified end-to-end with a fixture using both `FxHasher` and a user-defined `DjbHasher` on the same `@derive(Hashable)` struct: `hash_of[Point](p)` returns the FxHash result (100), `hash_with_djb[Point](p)` returns the DJB-style result (106). **Breaking migration**: (a) `src/semantic/derive.rs` `@derive(Hashable)` now emits `void hash[Hasher H](self, H &h)` (struct + enum variants); (b) `src/semantic/traits.rs` Hashable builtin sig comment updated; (c) `lib/std/hash.gg` `hash_of` body updated to `v.hash[FxHasher](&h)` (explicit targ to keep mono single-instance); (d) `tests/fixtures/trait_bound_transitive.gg` migrated by hand. Plus the original premise correction itself: my earlier diagnosis "method-level generic dispatch through trait methods is broken" was wrong — the only gap was nested generic dispatch (a method-generic call inside another method-generic body), which the three fixes above closed. 984 unit + 1033 integration tests pass; design doc Phase 4 status flipped from "MOSTLY DONE" to "DONE 2026-04-26"; TODO.md's pending Hashable entry deleted; book appendix-traits.md updated to show the generic Hashable form with a SipHasher example. The stdlib narrow-waist redesign is now actually complete.

- [2026-04-25] **Phase 5 (stdlib-design) doc audit — closed**. All six items in the design doc's Phase 5 list are now in sync with current implementation. Highlights: (1) `language-reference.md` §15.2 String table updated — added `find(pattern, from?, reverse?)` as the unified search primitive, `lines()`, `byte_at()`; documented `replace`/`split` extended `limit` forms; `trim_left`/`trim_right` listed as the modern aliases for `lstrip`/`rstrip`; replaced the broken `hash() → int` row with the state-based `hash(h) → void`. UTF-8 boundary table moved from `Result[String, String]` to `Result[String, IoError]` with `IoError.Utf8Invalid(offset)`. Dict/HashMap `remove(key)` now correctly listed as `Option[V]`. Set gained `is_disjoint`. Dict/Set show `iter() → DictIter[K, V]` / `SetIter[T]`. File table replaced with the current `std.io` Writer/Reader primitives + typed-error helpers (`read_to_string`, `read_all_bytes`, `write_string`, `write_all_bytes`, `file_open`). (2) `book/appendix-traits.md` — trimmed the aspirational "swap in a different Hasher implementation" note (today's API names FxHasher directly; alternative Hashers compose by field wrapping); replaced the unimplemented `trait Iterable[T]: IterType iter(&self)` with a description of the actual name-based iteration convention; retired the `println` / `writeln` / `println_str` block (those were retired 2026-04-19) and replaced with the surviving `print(v, terminator=, file=)` builtin + Writer primitives (`write_display` / `write_str` / `write_all`). (3) `book/19-stdlib.md` Lazy Iterators block updated — dropped the retired `set_iter[int](s)` free-function reference; replaced the "Dict iteration goes through .items() + .iter() — Ptr-ABI codegen issue" paragraph with the new lazy `DictIter[K, V]` / `SetIter[T]` shape; added inferred `collect()` examples (Vector/Set/Dict targets); noted `.keys()`/`.values()`/`.items()` still return eager Vectors for callers that want them. (4) `book/14-concurrency.md` — fixed sigil-before-type typo `void child(&Config cfg)` → `void child(Config &cfg)` in §3.9 (canonical sigil-before-name form). All other sections (the `&`/`shared`/`spawn`/`spawn unchecked` story, the spawn-boundary error catalog) already current. (5) `book/05-collections.md` Iterator section was already rewritten in the prior commit. (6) `language-design.md` §4.4.1 -er/-able tables already carry Writer/Reader/Hasher/Debuggable. Every example in the rewritten sections compiles and runs end-to-end. `stdlib-design.md` Phase 5 status block updated. Net: 4 doc files modified (`language-reference.md`, three book chapters), 90+ insertions / 63 deletions. 984 unit tests pass; design doc now reads "DONE 2026-04-25" for Phase 5. **Note**: Phase 4 itself was reclassified to "MOSTLY DONE" in the same audit pass — the Hashable migration's state-based shape (Hashable/FxHasher/@derive forwarding) is in place, but the consumer-chooses-Hasher form `void hash[H: Hasher](self, H &h)` that the design promises in §3 is NOT shipped (blocked on method-level generic dispatch through trait methods). Today's `Hashable` is effectively `FxHashable`. Commit `cd937340`.

- [2026-04-25] **Stdlib: lazy `Dict.iter()` / `Set.iter()` via `Ref[T]` borrow fields**. `Dict[K, V]` / `Set[T]` no longer materialise `.items()` / `.keys()` into a `Vector` before iteration; `d.iter()` returns `DictIter[K, V] { Ref[Dict[K, V]] source, int cursor }`, `s.iter()` returns `SetIter[T] { Ref[Set[T]] source, int cursor }`. Both equip `Iterator[(K, V)]` / `Iterator[T]`, inheriting the full adapter chain (`take` / `skip` / `fold` / `count` / `collect` / `map` / `filter` / `take_while` / etc.) via the trait-default emission. Element values come out of the `gorget_map_iter_key` / `_value` runtime accessors, which clone resource-typed K/V via the map's `key_clone` / `val_clone` hooks — the caller may freely drop without disturbing the source map. Runtime fns are declared as generic externs in `lib/std/iter.gg` (`extern int __dict_iter_order_len[K, V](Ref[Dict[K, V]] m) = "gorget_map_iter_order_len"`); generic mono preserves the C symbol so a single runtime function serves all instantiations. Two compiler fixes were needed for the lazy iterators to compose with the `Iterator[T]` adapter chain: (1) **Borrow-field construction passes Ptr through** — `lower_struct_literal` in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs` used to call `ensure_owned_at_boundary` on every field, which cloned `Ptr(T)` operands and stored the address of a stack-local clone. For `Ref[T]` / `MutRef[T]` borrow fields the field IS Ptr at IR level; the field semantics is "alias the source", so the boundary now skips Ptr-typed fields. Without this, `Dict.iter()` would clone the dict inside the iter() body, store the address of a stack-local clone in `DictIter.source`, and return a dangling pointer (the `borrow_field_basic.gg` / `borrow_field_lazy_dict_iter.gg` PoC fixtures had been passing by accident — stack-local addresses happened to remain valid for the iteration window). (2) **Trait-default discovery binds trait-T to equip's substituted trait args** — `try_register_default_return_type` (the non-generic-method-default complement to `try_register_method_instance` in `src/ir/lowering/generics/mod.rs`) didn't bind the trait's own generic params. For `equip [K, V] DictIter[K, V] with Iterator[(K, V)]:`, the trait's `T` should bind to `(K, V)`, so `TakeIter[Self, T] take(self, int n)` substitutes to `TakeIter[DictIter[int,int], (int,int)]`. Without the binding `T` stayed unresolved, the `scan_type` registration missed the concrete `TakeIter` instance, and the body-emission demand-gate skipped `take` for the equipping type — manifesting as `undefined reference to DictIter__int64_t__int64_t__take` at link time. The fix mirrors the binding logic already present in `register_equip_sigs_with_defaults` and `lower_generic_equip_methods_with_defaults`. **This generalises:** any `equip MyType[A, B] with SomeTrait[(A, B)]` impl with renamed trait params now inherits the full adapter surface. Set convenience wrappers (`s.each` / `s.for_each` / `s.any` / `s.all` / `s.find` / `s.find_index` / `s.fold`) were already in iter.gg and now compose through the lazy SetIter delegation. Dict-flavoured wrappers stay deferred — public-API tradeoff between key+value vs single tuple arg, not a compiler limitation. Also resolved as a side-effect: stale "VectorIter[T] for resource-type T panics in for-loops" TODO entry — `for x in v.iter():` on `Vector[String]` runs cleanly today, including chained `.filter(p)` / `.map(f)` (the original `c_lir/emit_types.rs:1645` panic was likely silently fixed during the Phase 1.7 borrow-field work touching the same `EnumExtract` / `LoadRef` paths). Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/stdlib_iter_dict.gg` (lazy bucket-walk over `Dict[int, int]`), `stdlib_iter_set.gg` (lazy `SetIter[int]`), plus the existing `borrow_field_*` fixtures that exercise `Ref[T]` field construction without the dangling-stack-address bug. Both fixtures' explicit `TakeIter[VectorIter[…], …]` annotations migrated to `TakeIter[DictIter[…]]` / `TakeIter[SetIter[…]]`. `chain` test dropped from `stdlib_iter_set.gg` — `chain` stays VectorIter-specific (its `other` parameter expects a VectorIter[T]); coverage remains in `stdlib_vector_iter.gg`. 984 unit + 1033 integration + 1 ignored = 1034 tests pass. `docs/internals/stdlib-design.md` Phase 2c "Shipped" item 8 added; deferred row 1 tightened (Set has `.iter()` now, Dict iter shape is `(K, V)`). Commit `21af33cf`.

- [2026-04-25] **Housekeeping: BIR synth Commit 4 dead-code sweep + doc status updates**. The BIR module-level synthesis plan's Commit 4 (dead-code sweep) had been deferred when `HIGHER_ORDER_METHODS = &[]` landed — the empty const was kept with a "hook for future migrations" comment, but all its downstream parse / dispatch / inline machinery was unreachable. Swept in this pass: (1) `HIGHER_ORDER_METHODS` / `DICT_INLINE_METHODS` / `SET_INLINE_METHODS` consts deleted from `src/backend/c_lir/emit_types.rs`; (2) `parse_vector_higher_order` / `parse_dict_higher_order` / `parse_set_higher_order` (all three always-None after the const-empty) deleted; (3) `emit_higher_order_collection_helpers` (no-op stub) deleted along with its caller in `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs`; (4) two dead `if let Some((...)) = parse_{dict,set}_higher_order` inline HOF blocks in `src/backend/c_lir/emit_call_extern.rs` — ~160 lines of Dict/Set fold/each/any/all C emit templates — deleted (these became unreachable when HofExpand covered the methods); (5) the `force_str_coerce` flag (always false after the dict/set parse fns went empty) deleted, along with the now-unused `resolve_call_fn` closure and `func_addr_targets` binding in emit_call_extern.rs; (6) the always-false `parse_*_higher_order(...).is_some()` chain in `helpers.rs::legacy_self_by_ptr` and the always-false skip-declaration chain in `mod.rs::emit_runtime_section` also deleted. Also the `#[cfg(test)]`-gated `ClosureSig` / `closure_call_sig_of` in `src/bir/synth.rs` — previously marked `#[allow(dead_code)] // consumed by SortByKey / SortedByKey in a follow-up commit`, but that commit already landed without using them — had its stale comments updated to note they're test-only helpers. Doc status headers updated: `docs/internals/lir-backend-lift-plan.md` and `docs/internals/bir-module-synthesis-plan.md` both said "Not yet implemented" despite Steps 0, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 + Commits 1–3 being fully landed — now both carry accurate status summaries pointing at what's still missing (lift-plan Step 1's `returns_array/string/map` name-matching around llvm/mod.rs:4961, Step 6 `CallClosure.param_kinds` unverified). Net: +38 lines of doc status, −321 lines of dead code. 984 unit tests pass; integration suite unchanged at 1024 passed / 2 pre-existing failures (`borrow_field_basic`, `cow_closure_ptr_capture` — both fail on pristine trunk, unrelated to this sweep).

- [2026-04-24] **Float→int cast on x86_64 now saturates Rust-style (CI fix, both backends)**. Linux CI caught `sec_71_float_to_int_saturation` failing with `-INT64_MIN` for NaN/Inf/huge — raw `(int64_t)nan` on x86_64 runs `cvttsd2si`, whose out-of-range result is `INT64_MIN`, not saturation. macOS ARM64 happens to saturate, so the test passed locally. Three-part fix: (1) `src/lir/lower/insts.rs` IR `Cast` lowering now picks the right LIR cast kind from source+target families — float→int goes through `Inst::FloatToInt` (not `Inst::IntCast`), float→float → `FloatCast`, int→float → `IntToFloat`. Previously everything but str-src fell into a single `IntCast` arm, which the backends then emitted as raw UB casts regardless of source type. (2) `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs` `Inst::FloatToInt` now emits `(f != f) ? 0 : (f >= MAX+1) ? TYPE_MAX : (f < MIN) ? TYPE_MIN : (T)f` — per-width bounds table (I8/I16/I32/I64/U8/U16/U32/U64). Upper bound uses "next representable double past MAX" so I64/U64 (whose MAX isn't representable as double) are still exact. NaN check first because NaN compares false to every bound. (3) `src/backend/llvm/mod.rs` `Inst::FloatToInt` now lowers to `call @llvm.fptosi.sat.iN.fM` / `@llvm.fptoui.sat.iN.fM` — raw `fptosi`/`fptoui` returned poison (UB) out of range, same x86_64 lowering problem as the C path. `emit_intrinsic_declarations` scans all `FloatToInt` instructions and emits just the needed `declare iN @llvm.fp{signed}.sat.iN.fM(fM)` lines (src float width inferred from `func.value_types`, defaulting to f64 since Gorget's `float` is F64). Matches Rust's `as` semantics (defined since 1.45). The existing round-6 regression fixture (`attack_71_float_to_int_edge.gg`) now produces `0 / INT64_MAX / INT64_MAX / 3` on both platforms; LLVM IR verified to emit the intrinsic correctly for non-foldable cast sites (constant-folded sites never reach the backend).

- [2026-04-24] **Self-host EIntLiteral(0) cascade — closed (four-bug chain fully unrolled)**. Minimal test `void main(): print(42)` compiled through stage-1 produced `__v0 = 0LL` instead of `__v0 = 42LL`. Root-caused through four stacked bugs, all closed via the Rust-convergence approach: (1) `af0cb513` — loud silent-fallback diagnostics made the issue visible in stage-1 output. (2) `87f2eb82` — lossy `#define Ok(x) ((void)(x),0)` prelude macros gated behind `GORGET_PRELUDE_FALLBACKS` (off by default, C `implicit declaration` surfaces leaks), and `.unwrap()` / `.unwrap_or()` rewritten to emit real `__field_read_<enum>_<Variant>_0` calls instead of no-op aggregate→scalar re-type. (3) `e5c35f8c` — `fn_sigs` pre-scan now resolves `TNamed` return types via `map_ast_type` (second pass after `gmod` is built) so callers of `parse_int -> Result[int, ParseError]` allocate the full ~48-byte struct slot, not an 8-byte int slot. (4a) `22430791` — cstr → String boundary coercion at SVarDecl: wraps cstr-returning extern results with `gorget_str_from_cstr`, mirroring Rust's `extern_cstr_return_vals` path at `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs:1725`. (4b) `e7e876ea` — cstr-arg coercion at extern call: when a runtime function declares `cstr` param and the arg is a Str passed by pointer (the self-host's default ABI for aggregate resource bare-params), emit `gorget_str_to_cstr(*(Str*)arg)` — mirrors Rust's `src/backend/c_lir/emit_call_extern.rs:495`. After all four, stage-1 running `print(42)` emits `__v0 = (int64_t)42LL`. Every int-literal-using program in stage-1 now works end to end; the stage-1 lexer's `parse_int(clean).unwrap_or(0)` correctly produces `ival=42`. 984 unit + 1024 integration tests pass throughout.

- [2026-04-24] **Security: round 7 attack probe — 10 fixtures, 3 new findings tracked**. Round 7 surfaced three previously-hidden codegen bugs, each documented as `security_known_unsafe` with reproducers: (1) **match-expression drops Some-arm value** — `x = match o: case Some(n): f(n); else: 0` always captures the else-arm's value, never the Some-arm's result (silent wrong answer, not memory-unsafe). (2) **Vector[Callable] → Option[Callable] SEGV** — Option's Some_0 monomorphized to int64_t but Callable is 16 bytes; unwrap reads a half-closure and dereferences fn_ptr as a pointer into code memory. (3) **@derive(Hashable, Equatable) struct as Dict key — ill-typed C**. Also pinned 7 positive cases (self-ref struct walk, parse_float roundtrip, negative subscript traps via unsigned bounds-check, atomic counter race-free, iterator fusion with take() stops correctly, large Dict drop, reserve(0)+push, multi-arg print drops extras). Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 89 security, all green. Known_unsafe count: 1 → 4 (3 new).

- [2026-04-24] **Security: round 6 attack probe — 10 fixtures, 0 new findings**. Confirmed safe / deterministic behavior across: float-to-int edge cases (NaN→0, Inf→saturate — matches Rust `as` semantics since 1.45), spawn-task panic propagation (clean whole-process exit with the panic message), moved-self rejection (borrow checker catches `use of moved value` at compile time), HashMap at 1k scale, enum many-variants match dispatch, big-struct return-by-value ABI (10-field struct via sret works), dict.remove during iter (collect-then-remove pattern), deep Box drop (1k-node chain drops fine via recursive Drop — at ~500k nodes this would hit the same stack-overflow as attack_45), Weak.clone sanity, char-construction edges (chr(0) → empty 0-byte String, chr(1200000) invalid → U+FFFD replacement, chr(max valid) → 1 codepoint). 10 new regression fixtures pinned as positive cases. Unbounded-recursion SIGSEGV accepted as-is (matches Rust/C++/Zig — closing properly would need a per-call depth counter at ~1-2 ns overhead). Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 79 security, all green.

- [2026-04-24] **Security: inline `f(None())` null-ptr deref closed**. Previously flagged as known_unsafe — `None()` passed as a call argument lowered to `Operand::Constant(Constant::Null)`, the C backend then emitted `f(*(Option[T]*)NULL)` at the call site → SIGSEGV. The Assign handler DID convert Null → tagged Option struct for VarDecl/StoreSlot, but function args don't flow through Assign. Fix at `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`: when the caller expected an Option[T] type (via `ctx.func_state.expected_type`, set by the argument-lowering pass), construct the Option[T]::None struct via `builder.enum_init` directly. `ensure_option_type_registered` keeps the enum TypeDef present so `resolve_variant_tag("None")` works downstream. Regression fixtures `attack_44_match_partial_option.gg` (single-level) and `attack_70_inline_none_nested.gg` (nested `Some(None())`, `level_2(None())` etc.). attack_44 reclassified from known_unsafe → security_safe. Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 69 security, all green. Known_unsafe count: 2 → 1 (only recursion stack overflow remains).

- [2026-04-23] **Self-host POr pattern lowering implemented**: `case A | B | C:` alt-patterns were unhandled in the self-host's `lower_pattern_match` — they fell through to the unconditional `GTJump(match_bb)` fallback, making every POr arm unconditionally match regardless of the scrutinee. Stage-1 running on driver.gg emitted 32 "unsupported pattern variant in match arm" diagnostics from this. Fix at `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg`: lower each alternative sequentially, chaining the no-match branches so each alt's no-match targets the next alt's attempt block, with the last alt's no-match going to `no_match_bb`. Any alt matching short-circuits to `match_bb` directly. Verified 32 → 0 "unsupported pattern variant" diagnostics when stage-1 runs on driver.gg. 984 unit + 1024 integration tests pass. Commit fd874afa.

- [2026-04-24] **Security: oversized Vector.reserve now traps instead of segfaulting**. Round 5 probe: `v.reserve(2305843009213693951); v.push(42)` segfaulted. Root cause: `gorget_array_reserve` (and sibling `ensure_capacity` / `with_capacity`) at `src/backend/c/c_runtime.rs` did `realloc(cap * elem_size)` without (a) overflow-checking the multiplication or (b) null-checking the allocator's return. A silently-failed reserve left the Vector with `cap > 0` but `data = NULL`; the next push wrote to NULL + 0. Fix: `__builtin_mul_overflow(cap, elem_size, &size)` with a `gorget: panic: array capacity overflow` trap, plus an explicit `if (ptr == NULL) trap("allocation failed")` after every realloc/alloc call. Security harness enables `allocator_may_return_null=1` in ASAN_OPTIONS so the runtime's null-check path runs under sanitizer instead of ASan pre-aborting. Also this round: 9 more regression fixtures (attack_60-69) confirming sort with bad comparator, dict-mutate-during-iter, UTF-8 validation, deep Option, tuple destructure, chained field mutation, ranges, negative ranges all safe. 984 unit + 1024 integration + 68 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: INT_MIN / -1 signed overflow now traps cleanly**. `INT64_MIN / -1` is C UB (mathematically INT_MAX+1, not representable). Pre-fix: `wrapping_div` at constant-fold time silently folded to `INT_MIN`, bypassing the runtime guard entirely; at runtime on ARM64 the hardware wrapped the same way (x86 would have raised SIGFPE). Fix at two layers: (1) `src/lir/optimize.rs` constant folder uses `checked_div` / `checked_rem` — returns None on overflow so the compile-time fold doesn't fire; the instruction reaches the runtime guard. (2) `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs` Div / Rem / Mod integer arms add an explicit `if (l == INT_MIN && r == -1)` guard — trap with `gorget: integer overflow` for Div, return 0 for Rem/Mod (mathematical result). Same fix for I8/I16/I32/I64 signed variants; unsigned paths unchanged. Regression: `attack_50_int_min_div_neg_one.gg` now traps. Also round-4 probes added 11 more fixtures (attack_49-59) covering nested closures, null-byte strings, channel close, empty collections, parse_int overflow, Dict NaN-key semantics, Box+Shared chain, string concat loop, generic monomorphization — all safe. Two further `known_unsafe` tracked: inline `None()` null-deref (attack_44 already flagged) and unbounded recursion → C stack overflow. Mutex double-lock (attack_56) deferred from the harness — deadlock test needs a timeout variant. Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 58 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: closure UAF on owned resource capture + NaN equality bug closed**. Two new findings from an adversarial probe batch. (1) **Closure UAF**: `Vector[int]() make(): Vector[int] v = [...]; return (): v` produced a heap-use-after-free. The closure env stored a shallow copy of `v`'s GorgetArray struct (aliased data pointer), but `v` was still drop-registered — make's scope-exit freed the buffer while the closure env kept a stale pointer. Fix at `src/ir/lowering/closures.rs`: for owned by-value resource locals captured at last-use, unregister the drop and defer a MoveZero of the source slot until AFTER the StructInit reads it. The source's bits flow into the closure; the now-aliased slot is zeroed so scope-exit is a no-op. (2) **NaN equality**: `simplify_cmp` in `src/ir/transforms/optimize.rs` folded `x == x` to `true` for ANY type — violates IEEE-754 on floats (`NaN == NaN` must be false). Fix: skip reflexive simplification for F32/F64 so the runtime computes the proper IEEE ordering. Also landed this session: 11 new regression fixtures (attack_38-48) probing f-string format injection, integer narrowing, vector/string OOB, dict overwrite, vector-remove-while-iterating, deep recursion, plus the two fixes above. Two new `known_unsafe`: (a) `f(None())` inline emits null-ptr-deref at call site, and (b) unbounded C-level stack overflow (no Gorget-level guard). Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 48 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: `match w.upgrade():` now dispatches correctly — arm-collapse bug closed**. `attack_35` was thought to be a Shared-drop refcount bug (upgrade returned Some when the Shared had been fully dropped), but tracing the runtime via fprintf showed the strong count DID hit 0 and gorget_weak_upgrade DID return NULL. Real cause: matching on the rvalue `w.upgrade()` result — type `Option[Shared[T]]` — collapsed all match arms into the first arm's body with no tag dispatch. Root: `methods.rs` upgrade lowering used `get_or_register_type(option_name, None)` which added a Named TypeId but **no enum TypeDef**. `resolve_variant_tag("Option__Shared__T", "Some")` then returned `None` because it looks up via `get_type_def`, and `lower_pattern_condition` fell through to `FunctionBuilder::const_bool(true)` — every arm always matched, only arm 0 fired. Fix: call `ensure_option_type_registered` **before** `get_or_register_type` (the ensure short-circuits once the name is in `named_types`, so ordering matters). New regression fixtures `attack_36_match_weak_upgrade_rvalue.gg` (dead → None arm), `attack_37_upgrade_still_alive.gg` (alive → Some arm). attack_35 reclassified from `known_unsafe` → `security_safe`. Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 37 security, all green. Zero `known_unsafe` entries remain.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: Option[Ref[T]] extraction paths all now type the Some_0 payload as Ptr — info-leak family fully closed**. The VarDecl coercion fix (2026-04-23, `try_lift_option_ref`) only covered one of several code paths. Audit session added 6 regression fixtures covering match-arm (`case Some(s):`), if-is sugar (`if x is Some(s):`), for-loop iterator (`for s in v.iter():`), and Option[Ref[struct]] nested access — three of them also tripped ASan. Two root causes, both fixed in the LIR lowerer: (1) `resolve_field_type` and `resolve_place_type` at `src/lir/lower/operands.rs` fell through to `LirType::I64` for `TypeDefKind::Enum`, because they only matched `TypeDefKind::Struct`. Extended both to consult the LIR struct registry for enums (flat-layout Option/Result). Fixes the attack_12 VectorIter[String] debug-assert panic. (2) `Instruction::EnumFieldLoad` at `src/lir/lower/insts.rs:1182` emitted `FieldPtr` (`&Some_0`) whenever the destination was `Ptr(T)` — correct when the enum variant's field is T by value, but wrong when the field is ALREADY a `Ptr` (as in `Option[Ref[T]]`, where `&Some_0` is void** instead of void*). Extended the branch to check the variant field's GIR type; when the field is itself a Ptr, route through `EnumExtract` which emits a Load and stores the pointer value directly. Fixes attack_30/31/32 — match-arm, if-is, and nested-struct extraction paths all now print the real element. Fixture count up from 29 → 35; known_unsafe down from 2 → 1 (only Shared-over-trivial-T drop gap remains). 984 unit + 1024 integration + 35 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: `!x` on refcounted types MoveZero's the caller's slot — double-drop UAF closed**. `void drop_all(Shared[Big] !s): pass` followed by `drop_all(!s)` then main exit was emitting a shallow `drop(&__s1)` on a handle whose control block had already been freed — heap-use-after-free inside `gorget_shared_drop`. Root cause: the call-site arg lowering at `src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs` only matched `Ownership::Move if callee_is_move_param`, and `callee_is_move_param` (derived from `is_resource_type`) returns false for Trivial-copy types like Shared/Weak/Channel. The fallthrough `_` arm just auto-cloned Ptrs and passed by value — no MoveZero. Fix: add an explicit `Ownership::Move` arm that checks `type_registry.needs_param_drop(local_type)` (true for refcounted types that Copy but have a drop) and schedules the post-call MoveZero + `drops.mark_moved`. Matches the push/enum-init consuming-position rule for the refcounted family. Fixture `attack_22_weak_after_shared_dropped.gg` now prints `-1` (None after drop) cleanly under ASan. Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 29 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: dead integer `/ 0` and shift-out-of-range now trap reliably — DCE no longer elides them**. `int boom = 10 / z` (z == 0) was silently running to completion when `boom` was dead: the LIR DCE pass eliminated the Div instruction because its dst had no users, so the runtime trap I added in the C backend never fired. Hid real bugs from users. Fix at `src/lir/optimize.rs:has_side_effects`: integer Div/Rem/Mod and all Shl/Shr are now treated as side-effecting; DCE keeps them. Floats (F32/F64) are defined under IEEE-754 (NaN/Inf for /0) with no trap, so they remain eliminable. Fixture `attack_23_panic_during_init.gg` now exits with `gorget: division by zero`. Reclassified to `security_traps`. Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 29 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: `Option[Ref[T]] → Option[T]` coercion now deref+clones in VarDecl — info-leak primitive closed**. Audit's highest-impact finding: a 4-line repro — `Vector[String] v = ["alpha"]; Option[String] maybe = v.get(0); match maybe: case Some(s): print(s)` — leaked arbitrary adjacent stack memory. `v.get()` returns `Option[Ref[T]]` (16 bytes: `{tag, void*}`); assignment to `Option[T]` (40 bytes: `{tag, Str}` where `Str` is 4×8 bytes) hit the C backend's default `SlotStore` path, which emitted `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(dst))` — a 40-byte read from a 16-byte source. The Str header fields `cap/len/alloc` ended up filled with stack garbage; without ASan the subsequent `print(s)` formats `%.*s` using the stack-junk `len`, dumping bytes from `.data` onwards. Fix at `src/ir/lowering/stmts/mod.rs`: new `try_lift_option_ref` helper, called from VarDecl right after `infer_operand_type_with_builder`. When the operand's LIR type is `Option__Ref_T` and the declared LHS is `Option__T` (non-Ref), emit a tag-branch — on Some, assign the whole source to a `Ptr(T)` local (which triggers `try_enum_payload_extract` in the LIR lowerer to emit a correctly-typed FieldPtr+Load), call `T::__clone`, wrap via `enum_init("Some")`; on None, construct Option[T]::None. Merge and return the converted operand so the downstream VarDecl stores it normally. Mirrors the pre-existing return-path conversion at stmts/mod.rs:1010. Workaround path (`Some(v.get(i).unwrap().clone())`) still works. attack_17 and attack_28 reclassified from `known_unsafe` → `security_safe` (prints real element value). Tests: 984 unit + 1024 integration + 29 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: `Box.new` as a consuming position — info leak → clone-on-multi-use**. Audit reproduced the TODO-High gap "Box.new should enforce `!` at borrow checker level": `Payload p = ...; Box[Payload] b = Box.new(p); print(p.data.len())` passed `gg check` with "no semantic errors" but panicked at `gg build` with `GIR validation: local _1 read after MoveZero in bb0`. The borrow checker never saw `Box.new` as consuming `p`; the IR lowerer silently MoveZero'd the source; only the GIR validator stood between valid-looking source and runtime UAF. Fix at `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs`: when `Box.new`'s arg is a bare identifier resolving to an **owned named resource local** that is *not last-use at the arg span*, insert a deep clone (via the type's `__clone` fn through an auto-borrow) before the heap allocation and skip the post-call MoveZero on the original slot. Left the bare-param path (e.g. `Expr a` in `add(Expr a, Expr b): Add(Box.new(a), Box.new(b))`) untouched — its pre-existing load_ref + alloc dance was already sound. Calculator example (`examples/calculator/`) was the canary: it rebuilds cleanly without regression while `attack_02_box_new_double_move.gg` now runs exit-0 with correct output. Tests: 984 unit + 1023 integration + 29 security, all green.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: mod-by-zero, shift-out-of-range, and shift-into-sign-bit UB closed**. Audit surfaced three runtime UB sites in the C LIR backend that `gg build --sanitize` caught under UBSan: (a) `a % 0` emitted raw C UB where `a / 0` already trapped cleanly — asymmetric safety on matching operators; (b) `1 << 100` (or any `count >= width`) emitted raw C UB with no Gorget-level message; (c) `1 << 63` on signed int64 emitted UB because the shift overflows into the sign bit. Fix at `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs`: mirror the `/0` guard onto `Rem` and `Mod` integer arms; wrap `Shl` and `Shr` in a `count >= sizeof(T)*8` guard that also rejects negative counts via unsigned compare; for `Shl`, perform the shift on the unsigned companion type then cast back, which preserves bit pattern and is defined for any count in `[0, width)`. New messages: `gorget: shift out of range`. Security harness reclassifies `attack_20`/`attack_26` from `known_unsafe` to `security_traps`. 984 unit + 1023 integration + 29 security tests pass.

- [2026-04-23] **Security: adversarial fixture harness added (`tests/security.rs` + `tests/fixtures/security/`)**. 29 adversarial `.gg` programs probing memory-safety and codegen-correctness guarantees, plus a classifying harness with four helpers: `security_safe` (well-typed program, build+run clean under ASan+UBSan), `security_traps` (runtime-defined trap with expected Gorget message), `security_rejected` (compile-time reject with expected stderr), `security_known_unsafe` (currently-broken, asserts the bug is *still* present so fixes force reclassification). Runs via `cargo test --test security`. Closed three findings immediately (mod/shift UB above). Six `known_unsafe` entries remain: Option[Ref]→Option[T] confusion, Box.new no-consume, Option[Shared] drop mistype, dead div-zero DCE, VectorIter resource-type panic, and the Option[Ref] minimal repro.

- [2026-04-22] **Self-host PLiteral pattern lowering implemented**: The self-host's `lower_pattern_match` at `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lower.gg` had no case for `PLiteral` — literal patterns (int / float / string / bool / char / None) fell through to an unconditional `GTJump(match_bb)`, meaning every literal pattern *always* matched the first arm. Practical damage: the self-host's own `type_id_to_name` function (`match tid: case 0: return "bool"; case 4: return "int64_t"; case 10: ...`) returned "bool" for every tid, cascading into ~5000 spurious "PConstructor on non-enum scrutinee" diagnostics during stage-1's run on driver.gg. Fix: emit `GICmp CMP_EQ scrutinee lit_val` + `GTBranch` for normal literal cases; special-case `PLiteral(ENoneLiteral)` by routing through `lower_ctor_pattern` with variant_name="None" (the parser emits `PLiteral(ENoneLiteral)` for `case None:` — not PConstructor — and comparing an Option struct to a unit literal yields ill-typed `Option__T == void*` C). 984 unit + 1021 integration tests pass. Commit 2cba879d.

- [2026-04-22] **Self-host Pass 4 struct size respects inter-field padding**: The self-host lowerer's Pass 4 (computing `computed_c_size` for user structs) summed field sizes without aligning each field to its natural boundary, producing smaller sizes than C's sizeof for structs with padding. Concrete case: `DefInfo { Str(32) DefKind(4) Span(16) int64 int64 bool bool }` — naive sum gave 70 → round_up(70, 8) = 72; C yields 80 because it pads the 4-byte `DefKind` to 8 before the 8-aligned `Span`. When the self-host used 72 as `Vector[DefInfo].elem_size` and C's sizeof gave 80, every push wrote 80 bytes at a 72-byte stride — corrupting adjacent elements. Surfaced as ASAN heap-buffer-overflow in `ScopeTable__set_def_param` during stage-1's own run on the self-host driver (the DefInfo case is the one that finally tripped the detector, but the same bug applied silently to every user struct with inter-field padding). Fix at `tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_lower.gg`: walk fields, `round_up(offset, alignof(field_i))` before adding each size, then pad the total to the struct's alignof. Applied to both flat and union-layout branches. Verified: stage-1 now emits `gorget_array_new(80)` for DefInfo arrays (was 72). 984 unit + 1021 integration tests pass. Fixed-point bootstrap still stalls on separate pre-existing issues (pattern-lowering `PConstructor on non-enum scrutinee` + a cleanup SIGSEGV during stage-1 on driver.gg) — both tracked in TODO.

- [2026-04-22] **Self-host `infer_method_return_type` peels Ptr/MutPtr on receivers**: Stage-1 was computing the wrong type for GIR locals bound via `collection.get(i).unwrap()` when the collection was passed as a bare param (ABI is `*Vector[T]` / `*Mut Vector[T]`). `infer_method_return_type`'s receiver match in `lower.gg` matched only `GtNamed`, so Ptr-wrapped receivers fell through to the `I64` default — producing 8-byte `stmt` slots for a 160-byte `Stmt` struct. Hang in `lower___discover_generic_calls_stmts` was the symptom. Fix: unwrap one level of `GtPtr` / `GtMutPtr` before the receiver match (commit 4d2f8c14).

- [2026-04-22] **Case C CoW activation — 99.4% array-clone reduction, 93.3% RSS reduction on self-host stage-0**: Four fixes combined flip the self-host stage-0 workload (compiling its own 23.5kLOC source via `--lir-c`) from **peak RSS 4,024 MB / 1.328B array_clone / 804M total_allocs** to **270 MB / 7.4M array_clone / 21M total_allocs**. Baseline snapshot at `scripts/baselines/phase3d_case_c_active.json`.

  Fixes (in dependency order):
    1. **Case C activation** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs:1955+`) — `Option__Ref_` / trivial-getter results from `.get().unwrap()` on a field-access receiver with an anonymous intermediate temp (`self.data.get(i).unwrap()`) now carry `CollectionId::FieldPath("self.data")` provenance, letting the VarDecl-time Ptr propagation keep the binding as a zero-cost `CollectionRef` instead of eager-cloning. Gated by `is_source_mut_unsafe_at(path, span)` so CoW is only kept when the source isn't mutated on forward paths.
    2. **Box-deref deep-clone** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`, `Expr::Deref`) — `*box` where the original local's type is any `Box[T]` (direct local OR bare-param `*Box[T]`) AND the boxed value is a resource-containing non-String type now emits a deep clone via the type's `_clone` runtime helper instead of the shallow memcpy + drop-register pattern. The shallow copy aliased heap buffers with the Box's own drop chain → double-free. Source-detection checks both `Box__T` directly and `*Box__T` (pointee) so the fix covers pattern-extracted locals (e.g. `case ECall(callee_box, ...): *callee_box`) as well as bare-params.
    3. **F-string deref deep-clone** (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/calls.rs::lower_interp_segment`) — the `{x}` interpolation path for a Ptr-typed `x` with a resource-containing struct pointee now emits `clone_fn_for_ptr` instead of the shallow-copy + drop-register pattern. Same shape as fix #2 but localized to the f-string code path.
    4. **Phase 3c branch-local clearing** (`restore_locals` in `src/ir/lowering/context.rs`) — drops `CollectionRef`/`CowBorrow` entries for locals created inside a scope at scope exit, so they can't be re-materialized by post-scope `cow_before_field_mutation` on a live source collection (stale-borrow UAF).

  Cascade of regressions encountered and resolved along the way: (a) the "struct-from-vector reads garbage" bug turned out to be `it` being a Gorget reserved keyword (`Expr::It`, the implicit-iteration binder), not a struct-extraction bug — renaming to `elem`/`item` fixed every minimal repro. (b) My earlier f-string narrowing (only register String derefs for drop) broke self_host because self-host has non-String struct derefs in f-strings that DO need ownership transfer — the deep-clone is the correct fix. (c) Activating Case C without the Box-deref deep-clone surfaced a self-host `discover_generic_calls_expr` UAF in `*callee_box` — that's not a self-host source bug, it's the same shallow-copy + drop pattern as the f-string case.

  984 unit + 1020 integration tests pass. This closes the original memory-optimization plan goal — the 1.3B runtime array clones estimate from TODO.md was real and now 99% of them are gone.

- [2026-04-21] **Phase 3c of self-host memory optimization — restore_locals clears branch-local CollectionRef/CowBorrow**: Closes a subtle correctness bug exposed by Track A of the Case C debug session. `restore_locals` in `src/ir/lowering/context.rs` was preserving ownership state for *all* locals created inside a scope (lid ≥ boundary), even though those locals go out of scope at scope exit. For CoW-specific states (`CollectionRef`, `CowBorrow`), this meant a post-scope `cow_before_field_mutation` could still find and try to materialise a borrow whose slot was dead — reading freed/garbage memory. ASAN trace on self_host_bootstrap (Case C activated) pinpointed the pattern: first outer loop in `loader.gg::load_imports` borrowed `Item item = m.items.get(ii).unwrap()`; `item`'s slot value propagated out of the loop via SSA block parameters; second outer loop's `m.items.push(...)` fired `cow_before_field_mutation("m.items")` which found the stale `item` CollectionRef and issued a use-after-free read at `Item__clone(__v1600)`. Fix: at restore, for locals with `lid ≥ boundary`, skip only the `CollectionRef` and `CowBorrow` ownership states (keep Owned / Ref / Alias / BareParam / ViewOf / Alias — those aren't invalidation triggers). Case C activation *still* blocked by a separate `example_todo_app` failure (wrong element read at straight-line `Task t = store.tasks.get(1).unwrap()`), so Case C remains dormant for now — tracked in TODO. 984 unit + 1020 integration tests pass. No baseline delta (Case C dormant → no new CoW activation).

- [2026-04-21] **Phase 3b of self-host memory optimization — save/restore covers local_ownership + in-place-flip detection**: `save_locals`/`restore_locals` in `src/ir/lowering/context.rs` now return/consume a `SavedScope` struct that carries `locals` + `local_ownership` + `local_id_boundary` + `local_types_at_save`. Restore reverts ownership for pre-existing locals (so a branch-local `cow_materialize_*`'s `local_ownership.remove()` no longer leaks) EXCEPT for locals whose declared `type_id` was changed during the scope — that signals a permanent in-place upgrade (e.g. `assigns.rs`'s CoW upgrade Ptr(T)→T for a loop-accumulated reassignment target) and the ownership change must persist. All 19 call sites across `stmts/patterns.rs` / `stmts/for_loops.rs` / `stmts/mod.rs` updated to thread `&FunctionBuilder` through. `is_source_mut_unsafe_at` now walks every path prefix (so `helper(&self)` recording `@mut:self` invalidates borrows of `self.data`, not just the full path). Prior attempts that tried to save/restore local_ownership (attempt #1 in the CoW TODO) tripped on exactly this type-flip edge case — the new `local_types_at_save` snapshot closes it cleanly. 984 unit + 1020 integration tests pass. Baseline delta vs phase1: +11,774 `string_cow` (+1.4%) — a *correctness* uptick from branches that were previously leaking pre-branch ownership state; zero RSS change. Case C (anon-temp receiver + field-path CoW) remains dormant: self_host_bootstrap still SIGSEGVs with it enabled, indicating at least one remaining blind spot (closure capture mutation or indirect local aliasing) that the current prescan doesn't catch. Tracked in TODO.

- [2026-04-21] **Phase 3a of self-host memory optimization — extended CoW mutation-safety prescan (infrastructure)**: `compute_cow_reassigned_after` in `src/ir/lowering/functions.rs` now tracks three additional categories of CoW-unsafe future operations: (a) mutating method calls on a receiver path (`receiver.push/pop/set/insert/remove/clear/sort/reverse/swap/swap_remove/extend/append/truncate/retain/dedup/resize/reserve/replace/drain/fill/put/remove_key/sort_by/sort_by_key` → `@mut:{receiver_path}`); (b) field reassignments (`self.x = ...` → `@mut:self.x`); (c) indirect mutations through call args — both explicit `&arg` and implicit MutableBorrow-per-sig via `fn_param_ownerships`.
