(2) `b7b9170f` Phase 1 canonical ops — IBoxAlloc/IAddressOf/IStructInit/IEnumInit + FieldInit, with IBoxAlloc type inference preferring registered `Box__<inner_struct_name>` struct id (falling back to `LT_PTR_TO_BASE + inner_sid`) so downstream `Some(Box(x))` can resolve to `Option__Box__T`. No producers yet. (3) `1a4d5ada` Phase 2 Box/variant migration — GICall+GICallExtern arms intercept `Some/None/Ok/Error` (SlotAddr + IEnumInit fills slot in place) and `Box(x)` (IBoxAlloc with `box_inner_ty_from_operand` unwrapping `LT_PTR_TO_BASE+sid` to the pointee struct so move-param Box args find their `Box__` wrapper). File-IO ptr args hoisted to `needs_ptr_arg`. All three phases keep `lowerer_comparison` + `self_host_bootstrap` green.

- [2026-04-18] **Set iterator sugar — SetIter + set_iter + take/skip/chain**: `SetIter[T]` wraps a pre-materialized `Vector[T]` (via the new `Set.items()` builtin method backed by `gorget_set_to_array`) so the VectorIter state machine and the take/skip/chain adapter chain work uniformly on Set keys. Free function `set_iter[T](s) -> SetIter[T]` as entry point — adding an equip method on `Set[T]` shadows the builtin protocol's `items()` / `map()` / `filter()` surface at method resolution, so the free-function path is a cleaner entry until method-resolution merging lands. Dict key/value iteration deferred — DictKeyIter trips the pre-existing Ptr-ABI codegen panic in TODO.md. Fixture `stdlib_iter_set.gg` exercises the full chain; book §19 Lazy Iterators updated. 974 unit tests + 1002 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-18] **Fix: formatter drops `public` on static globals**: `public static T x = …` was round-tripping to `static T x = …` through `gg fmt` because `format_visibility` drops the default-public keyword, but static globals are private-by-default so the drop actually flips visibility on re-parse. Added an explicit `public ` emit in `format_static_decl` that kicks in when the decl is Public — the other-item convention doesn't apply here. Two new idempotency tests in `src/formatter/mod.rs` lock the behavior down. 974 unit tests pass.

- [2026-04-18] **Fix: prevent phantom generic struct registration from partially-substituted equip methods**: Equip methods that carry their own generic params (`map[U, F]` inside `equip [T] VectorIter[T]:`) were leaking as phantom struct instantiations. `register_equip_sigs_with_defaults` ran `substitute_and_map_mut` on the return type `MapIter[T, U, F]` with only T→int substituted; the partially-mangled `MapIter__int64_t__U__F` got registered as a concrete struct (with `F f` becoming `void f`) and its broken vtable silently no-op'd the map pipeline. Three fixes: (a) skip sig registration for methods with their own generics in `register_equip_sigs_with_defaults`; (b) `substitute_function_body` now retains uncovered generic params so the transitive-discovery `scan_function` still treats them as unresolved rather than silently registering; (c) `lower_generic_equip_methods_with_defaults` skips method-level-generic methods too, leaving them for per-call-site specialization. .map/.filter method sugar on VectorIter still not fully enabled — per-call-site monomorphization of methods with method-level generics isn't wired through yet, tracked in TODO Phase 4 remainder. The take/skip/chain sugar path is unaffected and still works end to end. 972 unit tests pass.

- [2026-04-18] **Phase 4: Hashable state-based + Dict runtime hash_fn/eq_fn wiring for user keys**: Trait signature went from `int hash(self)` → `void hash(self, FxHasher &h)`. `@derive(Hashable)` now emits field-forwarding bodies (`self.x.hash(&h); self.y.hash(&h)`) instead of the old multiplicative xor combine — struct impls compose without each one reinventing a mix function. New `lib/std/hash.gg` ships the `Hasher` trait (write_int / write_bytes / write_string / finish) and one concrete implementor `FxHasher` (simple `state *% 31 +% v` mix, fast, not DoS-resistant). `hash_of[Hashable T](T v)` one-shot helper for callers that just want an int. Primitives (int / bool / uint* / String) are dispatched at IR-lowering time in `src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs` — the primitive path unwraps `Ptr(T)` receivers so generic bodies specializing to `T=String` / `T=int` hit `FxHasher__write_string` / `FxHasher__write_int` instead of the legacy `gorget_str_hash` / `__gorget_hash_int`. `FxHasher` is registered as a prelude type (resolve.rs) so `@derive(Hashable)`-generated method signatures resolve without a mandatory import. Runtime wiring: `c_lir/mod.rs::emit_hashable_key_bridges` scans Dict/Set constructors, emits `__gorget_ktable_hash__T` / `__gorget_ktable_eq__T` bridges per user-key type, and `emit_call_extern.rs` wires them into `GorgetMap.hash_fn` / `eq_fn` + key_drop / key_clone so Dict membership uses value equality rather than byte-FNV/memcmp. Works when the derived methods are reachable (fixture `dict_user_key_hashable.gg` keeps them alive via an explicit `hash_of` + `==`); types used only as Dict/Set keys still need the IR lowerer to treat derived methods as reachability roots (logged in TODO). Fixtures migrated: `derive_hashable.gg`, `derive_generic.gg`, `test_struct_derive.gg` use `hash_of[T](v)`; `trait_bound_transitive.gg` uses the new trait method. Self-host `derive.gg` mirror updated. Docs: `docs/internals/stdlib-design.md` §3, `docs/book/appendix-traits.md`, `docs/book/07-traits.md`, `docs/language-reference.md` §15, `docs/language-design.md`. 972 unit + 1000 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-18] **Iterator method sugar wired — `.take()` / `.skip()` / `.chain()` on VectorIter**: Follow-up to the two-pass monomorphization fix. Added `equip [T] VectorIter[T]:` with three concrete-adapter methods in `lib/std/iter.gg`: `take(self, int n) -> TakeIter[T]`, `skip(self, int n) -> SkipIter[T]`, `chain(self, VectorIter[T] other) -> ChainIter[T]`. Each constructs the corresponding state-machine struct and returns by value — no boxing, no trait-object dispatch. Chains like `v.iter().take(3)`, `v.iter().skip(2)`, `v.iter().chain(w.iter())` now work directly in user code. `.map(f)` / `.filter(p)` deferred — they trip a monomorphization side-effect where the partially-substituted return type (`MapIter[int, U, F]` with T→int done but U/F still abstract from method-level generics) accidentally registers as a concrete type during the Phase 3 sig walk. Users construct these directly via the struct literal until that's resolved. Fixture `iter_method_sugar.gg` updated to exercise all three working adapter chains. 999 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-18] **Iterator method sugar unlocked — two-pass monomorphization**: `v.iter().take(3)` now works end to end. Root cause was a forward reference in monomorphization order: `TakeIter[int]` got registered first (from type annotation), but its `inner: VectorIter[T]` field depended on `VectorIter[int]` which was only discovered later in `discover_transitive`'s walk of equip method bodies. Pass 3 then resolved `inner` through `map_ast_type_mut` while `VectorIter[int]` wasn't yet in `named_types`, falling through the user-generic branch to `UNIT_TYPE` (= void). Downstream FieldPtr/Load on `self.inner` emitted illegal `*(void *)`. The upstream BIR `Load.ty Void` → `ptr_pointee` fallback (commit `ecdc48c8`) didn't help because `ptr_pointee` derives from the struct definition's field types, which were already void. Fix in `src/ir/lowering/generics/mod.rs`: run monomorphization in two passes. Pass 1 registers names (possibly with void fields). Pass 2 rebuilds user struct/enum TypeDefs in place via `get_type_def_mut`, resolving forward references correctly. Two helpers `remonomorphize_struct_fields` / `remonomorphize_enum_fields` handle the rebuild, preserving Pass 1's metadata. Runtime collection types (Vector, Dict, Channel, Mutex, Guard, etc.) explicitly skip Pass 2 — their templates are `pass` placeholders and re-running perturbs downstream FieldPtr resolution on unrelated types (self-host lowerer tripped on "FieldPtr on Str field 4 OOB" without that guard). New fixture `iter_method_sugar.gg`. 999 integration tests pass, all self-host comparisons clean.

- [2026-04-18] **Vector.swap / swap_remove / fill + audit pass**: Three new Vector methods from the design doc. `swap(i, j)` in-place swap. `swap_remove(i)` — O(1) order-destroying removal by moving the last element into the hole (saves the N-i shift that `remove(i)` does). `fill(n, v)` replaces contents with `n` copies. All three land as builtins in `src/ir/lowering/builtins.rs`, backed by new runtime helpers `gorget_array_swap` / `gorget_array_swap_remove` / `gorget_array_fill` in `c_runtime.rs`. The `fill` void*-arg wiring registered in `collection_void_param_indices` so the codegen wraps the elem arg as `&(T){val}` at the call site. `retain(pred)` deferred — needs closure-over-C-runtime ABI plumbing that's not yet wired. Concurrency audit pass: the 997 passing integration tests exercise spawn patterns across stdlib + xtd + fixtures; safety check is already in effect and all patterns are clean. New fixture `vector_swap_fill.gg`. Book 05-collections + language-reference §15.2 updated. 998 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-18] **Phase 2c start: MapIter / FilterIter + sum/any/all/fold terminals**: Extended `std.iter` with two new adapters — `MapIter[T, U, F]` (transforms elements via closure) and `FilterIter[T, F]` (predicate filter) — both as concrete state-machine structs storing the source iterator + closure inline (no trait-object dispatch, no boxing). Added terminals `sum_iter[Iter]`, `any_iter[T, Iter, F]`, `all_iter[T, Iter, F]`, `fold_iter[A, T, Iter, F]`. Workaround discovered: `self.f(x)` / `self.pred(x)` inside an equip method on a struct with a closure field link-fails — the call is resolved as a method on the field type rather than a closure invocation. Fix is to hoist the closure into a local (`F cb = self.f; cb(x)`). Documented in iter.gg. New fixture `stdlib_iter_map_filter.gg` exercises map → collect, filter → collect, sum, any, all. 997 integration tests pass. Still pending: textual join (needs Displayable-bound HOF closure propagation), method sugar on VectorIter (monomorphization ordering gap from earlier), Phase 2b/c full iterator trait rollout (Iterable/IntoIterable, v.map(f) shortcuts).

- [2026-04-18] **Phase 4 partial: `spawn unchecked` escape hatch + docs**: New keyword `unchecked` (added to lexer) and parser-level support for `spawn unchecked <expr>` / `spawn blocking unchecked <expr>` / `spawn unchecked blocking <expr>`. The `Expr::Spawn` and `Expr::SpawnBlocking` AST variants gain an `unchecked: bool` field; the safety checker's `Expr::Spawn` / `Expr::SpawnBlocking` arms early-return when set, skipping `check_spawn_args` + `check_spawn_closure_captures`. Formatter round-trips the keyword. IR lowering treats them identically to regular spawns. New fixtures `spawn_unchecked.gg` (syntax round-trip with a Copy capture) and `spawn_unchecked_bypasses_check.gg` (verifies the opt-out — a String capture that would normally be rejected compiles and runs clean). Book chapter 14-concurrency.md extended with §3.9 / §3.10 / "Escape Hatch" sections. 996 integration tests pass. Phase 4 still has the Hashable migration (trait rework + Dict/Set internals rewrite) — deferred as a separate multi-session effort.

- [2026-04-18] **Phase 5 wrap: concurrency rules + language-reference §15**: book/14-concurrency.md documents the borrow-checker's spawn-crossing rejections (§3.9 borrowed arg, §3.10 borrowed closure capture). language-reference.md §15.1 adds Debuggable, Writer, Reader, Error to the built-in traits table. §15.2 documents Vector.capacity / sort_by_key / sorted_by_key / windows / chunks. §15.3 std.conv updates parse_int/parse_float to return Result[T, ParseError] and documents ParseError. §15.3 std.io has the full surface area — File struct, stdin/stdout/stderr, file_open, read_to_string, read_all_bytes, write_string, write_all_bytes, write_all/write_str/write_display/writeln/println/reader_drain/read_exact/from_string_error, Writer/Reader/Error traits, IoError enum.

- [2026-04-17] **Phase 3 complete: typed-error file I/O helpers**: New free functions in std.io: `read_to_string(path) -> Result[String, IoError]`, `read_all_bytes(path) -> Result[Vector[byte], IoError]`, `write_string(path, content) -> Result[int, IoError]`, `write_all_bytes(path, buf) -> Result[int, IoError]`. These compose `file_open` + the Reader/Writer machinery so callers get typed errors for whole-file operations (as opposed to the infallible `std.fs.read_file` / `write_file` which panic on failure and stay as convenience shortcuts). UTF-8 validation in `read_to_string` surfaces as `IoError.Utf8Invalid(0)`. New fixture `stdlib_io_fs_typed.gg` exercises round-trips and the IoError.NotFound path. Phase 3 is now effectively complete: Writer/Reader equips on String, File, Socket, TlsSocket; stdout/stderr/stdin are real handles; file_open + typed read/write convenience; ParseError for parsers; IoError for I/O. UDP left for a future DatagramWriter design (datagram-oriented, doesn't fit stream Writer/Reader). 993 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-17] **Phase 3 (a) extension: Socket + TlsSocket Writer/Reader**: `equip Socket with Writer: / Reader:` and `equip TlsSocket with Writer: / Reader:` shipped. New runtime functions: `gorget_socket_write_bytes_buf` / `gorget_socket_read_bytes_buf` (send/recv → count or -errno), `gorget_tls_write_bytes_buf` / `gorget_tls_read_bytes_buf` (SSL_write/SSL_read → count or -errno; SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN maps to Ok(0) for readers and ECONNRESET for writers). Socket/TLS each declare the byte-oriented extern as a method on its struct so the compiler wires `&self` correctly without the caller needing to manage pointers. The existing string-typed externs (`write`, `read`, `write_str`, `read_line`) stay untouched — they collide with the free-function Writer helper names (`write_str`, `read_exact`), so callers wanting typed errors go through the Writer trait methods (`write_bytes`, `read_bytes`) or the unambiguous `write_all` / `reader_drain`. New fixtures: `stdlib_io_socket_writer.gg` (local TCP echo round-trip via Writer.write_bytes + Reader.read_bytes + write_all), `stdlib_io_tls_writer.gg` (compile-only smoke — no cert/key, just verifies monomorphization). 991 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-17] **Fix: method call with `&self` on static globals** (`stdout.write_bytes(...)` now works): The IR lowerer's receiver-preparation branch in `lower_method_call` (`src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs`) had cases for local places (→ `emit_borrow` to get a pointer), field access (→ borrow the field), and string constants (→ materialize into a local then borrow), but fell through the else-branch for `Operand::Constant(Constant::GlobalRef(name))`. The GlobalRef was passed as-is, and the backend's default emission for GlobalRef loaded the value from the global address, so a struct-typed `&self` method got the value by copy. Added a dedicated branch that looks up the global's type name via `ctx.global_type_names`, and — unless it's a primitive or by-value handle type (AtomicInt, Barrier, Semaphore, …) — converts the `GlobalRef(name)` into `GlobalRefPtr(name)`. That constant emits as `&global_name` at the C level, giving the method the pointer it expects. Primitives and by-value handles still pass the GlobalRef (value) form. Fix is ~25 LOC; added regression fixture `static_global_method_call.gg` exercising both a user `Counter` struct and stdlib `stdout`/`File`. 989 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-17] **Phase 3 (b): migrate stdlib parsers from Result[T, String] to typed errors**: `std.bytes.bytes_to_str` → `Result[String, IoError]` (maps invalid UTF-8 to `IoError.Utf8Invalid(offset)`). `std.encoding.url_decode` / `form_decode` → `Result[String, ParseError]`. `xtd.json.json_parse` → `Result[Json, ParseError]` (via `ParseError.InvalidSyntax(offset, msg)`). `xtd.toml.parse` → `Result[TomlValue, ParseError]`. `xtd.yaml.parse` / `parse_all` → `Result[T, ParseError]`. `xtd.xml.xml_parse` → `Result[XmlNode, ParseError]`. Also migrated `xtd.httpserver.HttpRequest.json()` to return `Result[Json, ParseError]` (was `Result[Json, String]`). Touched ~10 stdlib/xtd files + ~10 test fixtures (all the ones with explicit `Result[T, String]` annotation — the majority of callers use `.unwrap_or(...)` / `.unwrap()` and needed no changes). Shared `ParseError.InvalidSyntax(byte_offset, message)` variant is the workhorse for the four parsers, carrying both the position and a parser-specific message. Each parser can evolve its own richer variants additively without changing its error type name. 988 integration tests pass, self-host comparisons intact.

- [2026-04-17] **Phase 3 (a) complete: File + stdout/stderr Writer/Reader**: `File` moved from `std.collections` to `std.io` (it's I/O, not a collection) with a `handle` int field matching the C `GorgetFile` layout. New runtime functions: `gorget_file_write_bytes_buf` (writes bytes, returns count or -errno), `gorget_file_read_bytes_buf` (reads into caller-owned Vector[byte]), `gorget_stdout_handle` / `gorget_stderr_handle` / `gorget_stdin_handle` (return File wrapping C stdio streams), `gorget_file_open_try` (returns 0/-errno, fills out-param). Static globals `stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` extended to recognize extern getter init in `eval_static_init` — `public static File stdout = _stdout_handle()` now emits the C call at main() start. New `_errno_to_io_error(int)` helper maps ENOENT / EACCES / EEXIST / EPIPE / ECONNREFUSED / ECONNRESET / ECONNABORTED / ENOTCONN / EADDRINUSE / ETIMEDOUT / EAGAIN / EINTR / EINVAL to named IoError variants; unknown codes fall through to `IoError.Other(f"errno {code}")`. `equip File with Writer: / Reader:` and new `file_open(path, mode) -> Result[File, IoError]` free function. **Known limitation**: direct method call on static globals (`stdout.write_bytes(...)`) fails due to a pre-existing codegen bug that dereferences the global and passes by value — the free functions `write_str[File](&stdout, s)` / `write_display[File, D](&stdout, v)` / `write_all[File](&stdout, buf)` work correctly and are the intended API anyway (narrow-waist: generic over concrete Writer, no trait-object dispatch). Workaround for method-style calls is `File f = stdout; f.write_bytes(...)`. New fixture `stdlib_io_file_writer.gg` exercises stdout/stderr Writer + round-trip write/read via `file_open`. 988 integration tests pass (+1).

- [2026-04-17] **ParseError + typed parse_int / parse_float**: `std.conv` now exports `ParseError` (enum Empty / InvalidNumber(String) / OutOfRange(String) / InvalidSyntax(int, String) / Other(String)) with Displayable + Debuggable + Error equips. `parse_int` and `parse_float` return `Result[T, ParseError]` instead of `Result[T, String]`. The C-layer `_parse_last_error()` still reports a combined string; the Gorget wrapper re-surfaces "out of range" as `OutOfRange` and everything else as `InvalidNumber`. Migration touched 5 callsites with explicit `Result[T, String]`: `lib/xtd/db.gg`, `lib/xtd/dataframe.gg` (3 sites), `tests/fixtures/conv_stdlib.gg`, `tests/fixtures/string_conversions.gg`, `tests/fixtures/modules_import_shadow/main.gg`. All other 20+ callers use `.unwrap_or(0)` / `.unwrap()` and needed no changes. `error_trait_namespace_split.gg` extended to exercise `ParseError` through the same `Error` trait generic as `IoError`. 987 integration tests + 4 self-host comparisons pass. Also: false alarm on "cross-module enum lowering bug" — the earlier failure was a stale binary, `include_str!("lib/std/io.gg")` means std changes only take effect after `cargo build`. TODO entry removed.

- [2026-04-17] **Error trait + type/value namespace separation (Option B+)**: `trait Error extends Displayable & Debuggable:` now coexists with the `Result.Error(x)` variant constructor. Scope split into disjoint `types` and `values` maps, each DefKind classified by `def_namespace()` — Trait/TypeAlias/GenericParam→Type; Variable/Function/Variant/Const/Static→Value; Struct/Enum/Newtype/Import→Both (dual-role names + ambiguous imports). `scopes.lookup_type` / `scopes.lookup_value` for context-aware resolution; bare `lookup` tries values first then types (back-compat). Demoted `None`/`Some`/`Ok`/`Error` from keywords to prelude-registered identifiers (parser now emits `NoneLiteral` when it sees identifier `None` in expression/pattern position). Imports shadow prelude variants (recognised via `Span::dummy()`) so `from std.io import Error` isn't a duplicate-definition. `process_impl` uses `scopes.lookup_type` for trait-name resolution so `equip IoError with Error:` finds the trait (not the variant). `build_registry` recurses into `Item::Module` wrappers so imported-module traits + impls land in the registry; relaxed duplicate-inherent-impl check to method-level (multiple `equip X:` blocks are fine as long as methods don't collide — matches Rust behaviour). Name-based sig-mismatch check has display-equality fallback for cross-module TypeId differences. Added auto-derivable method exemption (`clone`/`debug`/`display`/`hash`) from NoMethodFound — these are intrinsic even when not in any registered equip block. Fixed httpserver_router + httpserver_middleware fixtures that had `!resp` middleware params (masked by the previously-incomplete registry; now correctly rejected by Callable sig check — middleware now returns via `with_header(...)`). New `lib/std/io.gg`: `trait Error extends Displayable & Debuggable: Option[String] source(&self)`, `equip IoError with Error: source() → None`. New fixture `error_trait_namespace_split.gg` exercising both namespaces side-by-side. 987 integration tests pass (+1).

- [2026-04-17] **Split-equip supertrait satisfaction + formatter extends-separator fix**: `trait Child extends ParentA & ParentB:` no longer rejects a type whose ParentA / ParentB methods live in sibling equip blocks. Relaxed `traits.rs`'s missing-method check to also consult other impls on the same self-type for *inherited* (not own) methods. Negative path still fires when a supertrait method is genuinely missing everywhere. Revealed a latent formatter bug: `format_trait_def` emitted ` + ` between supertrait names but the parser only accepts ` & ` (via `parse_trait_bound_list`'s Ampersand match) — round-trip failed for any multi-`extends` trait. No existing stdlib / fixture used multi-extends so it was never exercised. Formatter now emits ` & `. New fixtures: `equip_supertrait_split.gg` (positive — Displayable + Debuggable + MyError as three equip blocks), `equip_supertrait_missing_error.gg` (negative — missing Debuggable errors). 986 integration tests pass (+2).

- [2026-04-17] **Codegen gap: `equip <PrimitiveType>:` now lowers correctly**: Fixed the five equip-lowering sites in `src/ir/lowering/mod.rs` + `traits.rs::extract_type_name` that filtered on `Type::Named` and silently dropped primitive-typed equip blocks (`equip String:`, `equip int:`, …). Added `types::equip_target_name` helper that maps Named to its name and Primitive to its mangled C name (StringType → "GorgetString", Int → "int64_t", Bool → "bool", etc.). Call-site dispatch at `infer_type_name_from_operand_full` now returns names for all scalar primitive TypeIds (previously only GorgetString / uint8_t had explicit cases). `lower_equip_method` takes primitive self by value (not Ptr) to match the call-site's `recv_type_id.0 < PRIMITIVE_TYPE_COUNT` dispatch. Net: ~40 LOC across 3 files. No existing fixture used `equip <Primitive>:` with bodies, so nothing regressed. New: `equip_on_primitive.gg` fixture (String.my_len returning Result, int.doubled/is_positive, bool.to_int). Unblocked `equip String with Writer:` in `lib/std/io.gg` — String now implements the Writer trait end-to-end (wraps `gorget_bytes_to_str` to reinterpret Vector[byte] as String and appends via `.push()`). Updated `stdlib_io_writer.gg` to exercise both the ByteSink path and String-as-Writer. 984 integration tests pass (+1 equip_on_primitive). See `docs/internals/codegen-gap-spike.md`.

- [2026-04-17] **Stdlib Phase 3 foundation — Writer/Reader byte-shaped traits + typed IoError**: New `std.io` module:  (1) `IoError` enum with all 16 variants from design doc §9.1 (NotFound, PermissionDenied, AlreadyExists, BrokenPipe, ConnectionRefused, ConnectionReset, ConnectionAborted, NotConnected, AddrInUse, TimedOut, WouldBlock, Interrupted, UnexpectedEof, InvalidInput, InvalidData, Utf8Invalid(offset), Other(String)) + Displayable impl.  (2) `Writer` trait: `Result[int, IoError] write_bytes(&self, String bytes)` (named `write_bytes` to avoid a name collision with the legacy `File.write` extern; method-level resolver binds bare `read_all` / `write` to existing File methods).  (3) `Reader` trait: `Result[int, IoError] read_bytes(&self, Vector[uint8] &buf)`.  (4) Generic free-function helpers: `write_all[W](&w, bytes)` with short-write loop, `write_display[W, Displayable D](&w, v)` via Displayable.display(), `reader_drain[R](&reader)` for read-until-EOF, `read_exact[R](&reader, n)`.  (5) `from_string_error[T]` bridge: `Result[T, String] -> Result[T, IoError]` for gradual migration.  All helpers generic over the concrete Writer/Reader type — no trait-object dispatch required.  Bug fix: C backend's RUNTIME_ARRAY-inclusion trigger missed the case where a user type's Option/Result clone function references `gorget_array_clone` via nested generics (e.g. Result__Vector__uint8_t__IoError). Now fires on `Vector__` anywhere in a struct name.  984 integration tests pass (+2: stdlib_io_writer, stdlib_io_reader). Wiring Writer onto String/File/stdout/stderr and the `Error` supertrait are deferred — both blocked on separate codegen/checker gaps, tracked in TODO.

- [2026-04-17] **Verified: borrow checker already rejects multi-use `!` on strings**: `!arg` on a String inside a loop (`consume(!name)` in a for-body) correctly errors with "cannot move `name` inside loop". Same for `!key` where `key` comes from `dict.keys()`. Use-after-move (`consume(!name); print(name)`) also errors. TODO item was stale — this works today without changes.

- [2026-04-17] **std.iter — TakeIter, SkipIter, ChainIter adapters + collect_vec / count_iter terminals**: Three concrete iterator state-machine structs composing over `VectorIter[T]`. Adapters are constructed directly via struct literals (`TakeIter[int](v.iter(), n)`) because the `.take()` / `.skip()` method-sugar on VectorIter trips a monomorphization ordering bug — Vector__T__iter lowers before VectorIter[T]'s equip methods have pulled in TakeIter__int64_t / SkipIter__int64_t. Terminals: `collect_vec[T, Iter](iter) -> Vector[T]` materializes via for-loop, `count_iter[Iter](iter) -> int` counts elements. Both fully generic over the concrete iterator type — no trait-object dispatch. 982 integration tests pass (+3: stdlib_iter_adapters, stdlib_iter_collect, stdlib_vector_iter).

- [2026-04-17] **std.iter module + Vector.iter() → VectorIter[T]**: User-defined equip methods now take precedence over hardcoded collection signatures in `register_collection_method_sigs` — previously Vector__T__iter was blindly re-registered as returning GorgetArray, shadowing user-defined equip return types. Added `lib/std/iter.gg` with `VectorIter[T]` struct and `equip [T] Vector[T]: iter(self) -> VectorIter[T]`. `from std.iter import VectorIter` works end-to-end through a for-loop.

- [2026-04-17] **for-loop over user types that implement Iterator directly**: The for-loop lowerer previously required an `iter()` method (Iterable trait). Types that just `equip` Iterator now work in for-loops — the lowerer treats the collection as its own iterator when `next()` is present without `iter()`. Mirrors Rust's "Iterator is trivially IntoIterator<IntoIter=Self>" blanket. Unblocks the simple `equip MyCounter with Iterator[int]: Option[int] next(&self): ...` pattern being `for x in my_counter: …`. 977 integration tests pass (+1 iterator_direct).

- [2026-04-17] **Primitives intrinsically satisfy Cloneable/Displayable/Debuggable**: Trait registry's intrinsic-satisfaction path only covered Numeric and Hashable/Equatable. Generic bounds `T: Cloneable`, `T: Displayable`, `T: Debuggable` now accept primitives (int, float, bool, String, …) without requiring `@derive`. Also routed `.clone()` on POD receivers through the primitive-method intercept as a no-op (copy types copy by assignment), so monomorphizing `dup[T: Cloneable](T x) -> x.clone()` with `T = int` works. Closes the "Cloneable trait for generic bounds" sub-item. 976 integration tests pass (+1 cloneable_primitive_bound).

- [2026-04-17] **Stdlib Phase 2a — sigils in type-arg positions collapse to bare T at monomorphization**: Fixed the runtime-unsound case where `Vector[String &]` previously monomorphized to `Vector__Ref_GorgetString` (a distinct type with Ptr elements) while the type checker accepted `Vector[String]` passed to a `Vector[String &]` parameter via auto-deref. Made `Type::Ref` transparent inside generic type arguments: `mangle_type_for_name` and `map_ast_type_mut` now treat `Ref(T)` identically to `T` when inside `[...]`. Parameter-level `&` / `!` still use `Param.ownership` (unaffected — they go through a separate path). Phase 2a grammar + resolver + basic monomorphization shipped. `Vector[String &]` / `Vector[String !]` / `Vector[String]` all share one runtime layout; iteration over borrow-sigiled containers now yields the correct values (no more pointer-print garbage). Also shipped: associated-type bound parsing `type Iter: Iterator[T]` (parser was dropping the `: TraitBound` suffix; formatter updated to round-trip). 967 unit + 975 integration tests pass (+1 sigil_type_args).

- [2026-04-17] **Stdlib Phase 2a.1 — sigils in type-arg positions + assoc type bounds** (superseded by the 2a completion entry above): Grammar confirmed, Owned transparent, assoc-bound parsing added.

- [2026-04-17] **Stdlib Phase 1.5 — Debuggable trait + @derive(Debuggable) + primitive .debug()/.display() methods**: (1) Registered `Debuggable` trait in resolve.rs + traits.rs (mirrors Displayable: `String debug(self)`). (2) Added `Debuggable` to DERIVABLE_STRUCT_TRAITS and DERIVABLE_ENUM_TRAITS in derive.rs. (3) Wrote `generate_struct_debuggable` (outputs `TypeName { field: <field.debug()>, ... }` via f-string with literal braces via `{{`/`}}`) and `generate_enum_debuggable` (outputs `Variant` for unit variants and `Variant(<a0.debug()>, ...)` for tuple variants). (4) Added `Debuggable` to `primitive_satisfies` alongside Displayable so int/float/bool/String auto-satisfy the bound. (5) Primitive `.debug()` and `.display()` intercepted in `lower_method_call` (src/ir/lowering/exprs/methods.rs) and routed to runtime: int/bool/float → reuse `gorget_{int,float,bool}_to_str`; String.debug() → new `gorget_string_debug` (quotes + escapes `"` `\\` `\n` `\r` `\t` `\0` and bytes < 0x20 / 0x7F as `\xNN`); String.display() → identity. Narrow-int/float variants auto-widen via cast. (6) Receiver Ptr(String) → deref before dispatch, so f-string-generated `self.field.debug()` calls work on field projections. (7) Added `gorget_string_debug` to `runtime_extern_sig` LIR sig table (src/lir/lower/calls.rs) and to the RUNTIME_TOSTR conditional include in c_lir/emit_types.rs. (8) Type checker returns owned_string_id for `debug`/`display` on primitives and on String. (9) Also did Dict/Set Hashable+Equatable bound checking — turned out to be already wired end-to-end (machinery at `struct_generic_bounds` + `check_struct_type_bounds`); added `set_no_hashable_error` fixture + integration test next to existing `dict_no_hashable_error`. 967 unit + 974 integration tests pass (+2: derive_debuggable + set_no_hashable_error).

- [2026-04-17] **Stdlib Phase 1.5 — 3 quick wins shipped**: (1) `Vector.capacity()` method — exposed `gorget_array_capacity` runtime fn through type checker + LIR sig; the runtime was missing the function, added as `return arr->cap`. (2) `Vector.sort_by_key(f)` / `sorted_by_key(f)` — closure returns K: Comparable; TLS closure pointer + static comparator extracts keys via call_fn twice then compares with type-specific key comparator (int64/float/Str). Both C backend and sim implemented. (3) `Vector.windows(n)` / `chunks(n)` — eager Vector[Vector[T]] materialization; inline C codegen generates nested GorgetArray with gorget_array_free as outer elem_drop. 972 integration tests pass (+2: vector_sort_by_key, vector_windows_chunks). Deferred: Debuggable trait + @derive(Debug) and Dict/Set Hashable+Equatable bounds (both larger than Phase 1.5 quick-win scope — need primitive trait methods / monomorphization-time bound enforcement).

- [2026-04-17] **Stdlib narrow waist design doc revised** (post independent review). Major changes to the plan, no code changes yet: (1) Iterator returns a **concrete monomorphized type**, not a trait object — trait objects defeat inlining and make lazy fusion impossible. (2) **Two-tier iterator ownership** via sigils in type-argument positions: `Iterator[T &]` (mut-borrow, `iter()`) and `Iterator[T !]` (consuming, `into_iter()`). Third tier (immutable const-borrow) deferred. Requires grammar + type-system extension. (3) **Writer/Reader are byte-shaped** (`Result[int, IoError]`), not text-shaped — supports TLS, compression, binary protocols. Short-write semantics preserved. (4) **Typed IoError** enum in prelude (NotFound, PermissionDenied, UnexpectedEof, Utf8Invalid(offset), Other, …) — no `Result[T, String]`. (5) **Debuggable trait** + `@derive(Debug)` — Display is hand-written (user-facing), Debug is derivable (dev-facing). (6) **Hashable uses Hasher state** (`void hash(self, Hasher &h)`) — composes via field-forwarding. (7) **Spawn-boundary concurrency model**: `&` stays non-exclusive (local mut borrow, Python-ergonomics preserved), but `&` captures are forbidden across `spawn` boundaries — must be `shared T` or `spawn unchecked`. Rust-style exclusive `&` was considered and rejected (ergonomic cost too high for Gorget's target audience). (8) **No eager Iterator interim** — ship lazy from day one or not at all; eager trains users onto the old API permanently. (9) Phase 1.5 folds in: `sort_by_key`, Debuggable, drop `String.join` in favor of `iter().join(sep)`, explicit `Dict[K: Hashable + Equatable]` bounds, `Vector.capacity()`, `windows/chunks`. Design doc at `docs/internals/stdlib-design.md` (sections 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10 substantially rewritten). TODO.md re-phased.

Also fixed Inst::Memcpy coercion bug in emit_void_ptr_option_wrap (was using CallExtern with wrong abi tags → bad `memcpy(*(Str*)__v, ...)` codegen).

- [2026-04-16] **LLVM backend: CStr null-termination fix (JSON array zero-read)**: View strings (cap==0, from slices/substrings) passed to C functions via CStr ABI were not null-terminated. The LLVM backend loaded raw `.data` pointers, but views point into the original string's data which has trailing characters. Fix: use `gorget_str_to_cstr()` for all CStr-annotated parameters. Root cause: `json_parse("[7]")` → `parse_number("7")` where "7" is a view into "[7]" → `strtoll("7]")` fails → returns 0. Also added `gorget_parse_int`/`gorget_parse_float` to `runtime_extern_sig` with CStr ABI. Fixes json_parse, json_pretty, json_edge_cases, xml_parse.

- [2026-04-16] **Lift elem_drop/elem_clone from C backend to LIR lowerer**: Added `Inst::NamedFuncAddr` to LIR. Collection constructors now emit explicit byte-offset stores for elem_drop/elem_clone/elem_materialize function pointers via the LIR lowerer (not backend-specific code). Removed ~70 lines from C backend's `emit_call_extern.rs`. Both backends emit these as regular stores. Only built-in resource types (GorgetArray/Map/Set/String) get elem_drop — user types are handled by the ownership system.

- [2026-04-16] **LLVM backend: Option/Result combinator inline handlers**: Added inline expansion for all 9 Option/Result combinator methods (map, filter, and_then, or_else, or, flatten, unwrap_or_else, flat_map, map_err) in the LLVM backend. Previously these fell through to non-existent extern function calls, producing 0 or garbage values. Implementation: branch-based tag dispatch with closure calls, supporting sret/small-aggregate/scalar return conventions. Also skips extern declarations for combinator names and adds val_types inference for combinator result types. Fixed 6+ FAIL tests (test_option_all, test_option_chaining, option_result_combinators, test_result_all, test_result_advanced, coroutine_result_combinators). Also declared `llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64` and `llvm.memset.p0.i64` intrinsics in preamble.

- [2026-04-15] **Self-host LIR C codegen — 0→205 fixtures compiling**: Fixed 7 codegen issues: (1) void-return suppression in TRet terminators, (2) I64 fallback for unknown CallExtern return types (was void→void*), (3) struct constructor type inference moved before extern lookup (Some/Ok/Error now get correct struct types), (4) expanded runtime_fn_return_type with ~50 more runtime functions, (5) is_void_runtime_fn for gorget_array_push/set_add/etc., (6) defensive gorget_str_eq/cmp emission for ICmp on aggregate operands, (7) monomorphized method→runtime name mapping (int64_t__push→gorget_array_push, etc.). Infrastructure: emit_mono_typedefs for Vector__T/TaskGroup/etc. typedefs, is_runtime_defined_named for TaskHandle/GorgetRange. Remaining 442 failures are overwhelmingly self-host LIR lowering bugs (wrong function names, wrong arg counts), not codegen issues.

- [2026-04-15] **LIR lift #3 — move semantic logic from C backend to LIR lowerer**: Lifted all 7 Tier 1-3 pattern categories from `emit_call_extern.rs` (~490 lines stripped). **Tier 1** (block-splitting, 6 patterns): (1a) nullable void*→Option (gorget_array_get, gorget_map_get, etc.), (1b) nullable cstr→Option[String] (regex match group, getenv), (1c) last_error→Result (socket, tls, crypto, regex, parse), (1d) sentinel scalar→Option (str_index_of, etc.), sentinel struct→Option (regex_find), nullable ptr→Option (Weak upgrade). **Tier 2b**: tag checks (is_some/none/ok/err) → Load(I32)+Cmp. **Tier 3**: type casts → IntToFloat/FloatToInt/IntCast; str_cat dispatch → gorget_int_to_str etc.; str_push dispatch → gorget_string_push_int etc. Infrastructure: `lower_instruction` returns `BlockId`; new `lifts.rs` module. **SSA fix**: changed `construct_ssa` to process blocks in reverse postorder (RPO) instead of sequential order — fixes value-threading bug where definitions in high-numbered merge blocks were invisible to low-numbered GIR blocks. 967 unit + 968 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-15] **Promote disguised CallExtern to dedicated LIR instructions (Rust MIR model)**: Added `Inst::CallClosure` (with `ClosureDispatchKind::CallableParam` / `EscapedClosure`, per-arg `arg_abis`, explicit `ret_ty`) and `Inst::DropGuardOpen` / `Inst::DropGuardClose` (with `DropGuardKind::Bool` / `NonZero { size }`) as first-class LIR instruction variants. The LIR lowerer now emits these instead of `CallExtern` with magic name strings. Stripped ~230 lines of string-pattern dispatch from both backends' `emit_call_extern` / `emit_inst` handlers. Updated `drop_elab.rs` to match on enum variants instead of parsing `"__gorget_drop_if_alive_open__"` strings. All match arms updated across mod.rs, display.rs, ssa.rs, optimize.rs, types.rs, helpers.rs. 967 unit + 966 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-14] **Complete AbiKind migration — all CallExtern instructions carry arg_abis**: Every `Inst::CallExtern` emission in the LIR lowerer now populates `arg_abis` from the canonical `runtime_extern_sig` / `ensure_extern` pipeline. Added `lookup_arg_abis` helper to `FuncLowering` (replaces 4 manual `pending_externs` lookups). Added 5 missing entries to `runtime_extern_sig` (malloc, memset, __gorget_alloc/dealloc). Fixed 22 unannotated call sites across `insts.rs` and `operands.rs` — 17 added lookup after existing `ensure_extern`, 3 moved `ensure_extern` before push, 5 added new `ensure_extern` calls. Legacy C backend whitelists (`collection_void_param_indices`, `legacy_self_by_ptr`) deprecated as safety nets. 967 unit + 966 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-14] **Lift Call-site closure wrapping from backends to LIR**: When passing a `__Closure_N` struct or bare function reference (`FuncRef`) as an argument to a function expecting a callable, the LIR lowerer now emits `ClosurePack + SlotAddr` to wrap the argument. Previously both C and LLVM backends detected `__Closure_N` args and `FuncAddr` values in Call handlers and constructed inline `{fn_ptr, env}` pairs (~40 lines each). Stripped this detection from both backends. Also fixed: (1) `ClosurePack` FuncId references now tracked in dead-function-elimination (`collect_inst_func_refs` + `rewrite_func_refs`), preventing stale FuncId panics after optimization; (2) `ClosurePack { needs_adapter: true }` now triggers adapter function generation in both backends (alongside `FuncAddr`). 967 unit + 966 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-14] **FuncAddr→GorgetClosure via ClosurePack + Null→Memset lift**: Two more backend→LIR lifts: (1) Bare function refs assigned to GorgetClosure slots now emit `ClosurePack { needs_adapter: true }` with NullPtr env — stripped FuncAddr→GorgetClosure adapter detection from C backend's SlotStore handler (~8 lines). Added `needs_adapter` flag to ClosurePack so backends know to wrap with `__adapt_` prefix. (2) `Constant::Null` assigned to aggregate destinations now emits `Memset(ptr, 0, sizeof)` directly instead of `NullPtr + Store` — eliminates O(n²) block scans in both backends' Store/SlotStore handlers. Also skips redundant NullPtr stores to already-zero-initialized aggregate fields in StructInit.

- [2026-04-14] **LIR value type metadata — shared `compute_module_value_types()`**: Added `value_types: Vec<Option<LirType>>` field to `LirFunction`. New shared `compute_module_value_types()` in `src/lir/types.rs` derives per-value types from instructions in a single pass — handles all instruction kinds including CallExtern with runtime function return types, polymorphic Option/Result combinators (excluded to avoid merged-type conflicts), and struct-field payload extraction for unwrap/expect. Runs after SSA + optimization in all pipeline paths (5 call sites in main.rs, integration.rs, lowering test). LLVM backend migrated: reads from `func.value_types` with Struct→PtrTo mapping, dropping ~30 lines of Phase 1 type inference. C backend retains its own computation (its multi-phase fixups depend on ptr_pointee context), with shared types available for future migration. Self-host `LirFunction` struct updated. 967 unit + 966 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-14] **`Inst::ClosurePack` — explicit closure→GorgetClosure coercion in LIR**: Lifted `__Closure_N → GorgetClosure` detection from C and LLVM backends into the LIR lowerer. New `Inst::ClosurePack { slot, env_ptr, call_func }` instruction emitted during Assign lowering when source is `__Closure_N` and dest is `GorgetClosure`. LIR lowerer emits `malloc + memcpy` for env heap-allocation, then `ClosurePack`. Both backends now have trivial 2-line match arms. Stripped ~40 lines of type-reconstruction logic from each backend's SlotStore handler. Self-host LIR files updated (lir.gg, lir_ssa.gg, lir_codegen.gg). 967 unit + 965 integration tests pass.

- [2026-04-13] **Operand::Move ownership propagation + consuming-arg clone fix**: GIR lowering marks consuming call args as `Operand::Move`; LIR emits generic post-call MoveSlot. Fixed `ensure_owned_at_consuming_arg` to clone non-last-use resource args through Ptr. Hardcoded function-name fallback removed.

- [2026-04-14] **Drop elaboration V7 — eliminate EnumInit Memsets + mark_moved for error paths**: Removed the remaining 848 redundant Memsets from EnumInit source zeroing (872 → 24, 97% reduction). Three changes: (1) EnumInit handler in LIR lowering now emits MoveSlot only (no Memset) for resource-type source slots — C zero-initialization provides null-safety for uninitialized paths. (2) Rethrow/throw/try-except error paths now call `move_zero_and_mark` on consumed error values before early-exit drops, preventing double-free. (3) The 24 remaining Memsets are genuinely necessary: IndexLoad element zeroing (zeroing inside heap-allocated collection data) and projected field-level MoveZero (Deref/Field).

- [2026-04-14] **Drop elaboration V6 — eliminate all non-projected MoveZero Memsets**: Two root-cause fixes enabled removing the last Memset safety net: (1) **Liveness bug**: while/for loop Pass 1 incorrectly recorded last-use spans that don't account for the back-edge (match scrutinee in loop body falsely marked as last-use). Fix: Pass 1 discards last-use decisions into a throwaway set; only Pass 2 records them. (2) **Match ownership for non-dead scrutinee**: when a match scrutinee is alive (not last-use), extracted user-struct fields with resource sub-fields were incorrectly registered for drop (taking ownership of shared data). Fix: only take ownership when `scrutinee_clone_elision` is active (last-use); otherwise extracted fields are zero-cost views into the scrutinee copy, which is dropped at scope exit. `Instruction::MoveZero` now emits only `MoveSlot` for non-projected places — zero runtime cost. 958/958 integration + 967 unit tests + gorget-arena clean.

- [2026-04-14] **Self-host LIR drop metadata population**: Added `GirTypeInfo`/`GirFieldInfo`/`GirEnumVariantInfo` structs to gir.gg for carrying struct/enum field type info through the pipeline. lower.gg now populates `type_infos` on GirModule with resolved field type names from AST. lir_lower.gg's `populate_drop_metadata` scans type_infos + resource_types to build `recursive_drop_structs`, `recursive_drop_enums`, and `type_drop_fns` on LirModule. Resource detection uses hardcoded names (GorgetString→gorget_string_free, etc.) + collection prefixes (Vector__→gorget_array_free) + transitive resource_types from GIR. End-to-end working: self-host generates correct per-type drop/clone functions.
- [2026-04-14] **Self-host LIR Phase 4b — drop/clone codegen** (394 lines): Added 5 drop/clone emission functions to lir_codegen.gg: `emit_struct_drops` (recursive struct field drops via `recursive_drop_structs`), `emit_struct_clones` (deep-copy with drop→clone mapping: gorget_string_free→gorget_string_clone_to_owned, etc.), `emit_enum_drops` (switch-on-tag variant drops via `recursive_drop_enums`), `emit_enum_clones` (tag-dispatched deep clone), `emit_type_drop_fns` (unified drop/clone from `type_drop_fns` with user_drop_fn support). All read LirModule metadata populated by the Rust LIR lowerer. The self-host LIR lowerer doesn't populate this metadata yet — that's the next step.
- [2026-04-14] **Self-host LIR driver integration + cross-module enum fix**: Root cause of driver build failure: gir.gg's `Instruction`/`Terminator` enums shared variant names (`ICallExtern`, `ICmp`, `TJump`, `TBranch`) with lir.gg's `LirInst`/`LirTerm`. The compiler resolved constructors to the wrong enum type, producing field count mismatches and type errors. Fix: (1) renamed gir.gg variants with `GI`/`GT` prefix across 4 files, (2) renamed `lower_function` in lir_lower.gg to avoid collision with lower.gg, (3) added `find_substr` helper in lir_codegen.gg to avoid `str.find()` Option return type issue. Driver now supports `--lir-c` flag for end-to-end LIR→C codegen.
- [2026-04-13] **Drop elaboration pass V5 — mark_moved for pending move-zeros + guarded reassignment drops**: Three GIR MoveZero sites (`pending_move_zeros` in calls.rs and methods.rs, `maybe_move_zero` in assigns.rs) now call `mark_moved` so their scope-exit drops become `DropIfAlive`. Reassignment drops (`builder.drop()` before `var = new_value`) now check `is_moved()` and emit `DropIfAlive` when the old value may have been consumed. `emit_move_zero_for_local` (LIR-level consuming-arg moves) now emits MoveSlot only — no Memset. `Instruction::MoveZero` (GIR-level explicit moves) retains Memset alongside MoveSlot as a safety net for inline reassignment drops in complex scope interactions. 958/958 integration + 967 unit tests passing.

- [2026-04-13] **Drop elaboration pass V4 — MoveSlot annotations**: New `MoveSlot { slot: SlotId }` LIR instruction replaces the 4-instruction `SlotAddr + IConst 0 + IConst SIZE + Memset` pattern as the "moved" signal in the forward dataflow. `MoveSlot` is a pure dataflow annotation with no runtime cost — consumed by the elaboration pass, then swept from all blocks. Both `Instruction::MoveZero` (explicit `!` moves) and `emit_post_call_zeros` (implicit consuming-position moves) now emit `MoveSlot`. Memsets retained alongside for null-safety of unguarded Trivial drops (not all GIR MoveZero paths call `mark_moved`). Trivial drops (`gorget_string_free`, `gorget_array_free`, etc.) now emit guards when `conditional=true`, enabling the elaboration pass to handle them uniformly. `ElabStats` gains `move_slots_removed`. 958/958 integration + 967 unit tests passing.

- [2026-04-13] **Drop elaboration pass V3 — bool drop flags for MaybeInitialized**: For slots that are conditionally moved (live on some paths, zeroed on others), V3 replaces the runtime `memcmp` guard with a stack-local `bool` drop flag. Flag initialized to `true` in bb0, set to `false` after each move-site Memset, checked at the drop site: `if (flag) { Type__drop(&slot); }`. C backend emits `__gorget_drop_flag_open(v)` → `if (v) {` and `__gorget_drop_flag_close()` → `}`. New `drop_flag.gg` fixture exercises the path with a struct conditionally moved via function parameter. `ElabStats` gains `flags_inserted` field. 958/958 integration tests + 967 unit tests passing.

- [2026-04-13] **Drop elaboration pass V2 — companion Memset removal**: After V1 guard elimination, `removed_slots` (Uninitialized case) tracks slots whose entire guard+drop sequence was deleted. A second pass (`remove_companion_memsets`) scans all blocks and removes `Memset`-to-zero instructions whose `ptr` argument traces back to a `SlotAddr` for a deleted slot. Only companion Memsets (from `emit_post_call_zeros`) are removed — Memsets for plain-Drop types (strings, arrays) are untouched since those drop functions need the zero-sentinel for null-safety. `ElabStats` struct reports both `guards_eliminated` and `memsets_removed`. 957/957 integration tests passing.

- [2026-04-13] **Drop elaboration pass V1**: Forward dataflow analysis on LIR that eliminates provably-dead `__gorget_drop_if_alive_open__SIZE` / `__gorget_drop_if_alive_close` guard sequences. Lattice: `Initialized | Uninitialized | MaybeInitialized` per slot. Transfer: `SlotStore → Initialized`, `Memset(SlotAddr(s)) → Uninitialized`. Worklist dataflow over CFG; per-block scan+mark+sweep with nesting-depth tracking for nested guards. Eliminates Uninitialized guards entirely; strips open/close wrappers from Initialized guards (leaving unconditional drop). - [2026-04-13] **Self-host parser comment-stripping fix**: Root cause — the self-host lexer emits regular comment tokens (`TOK_COMMENT`) without indentation processing (blank-line-style `continue`), so comments between `:` and the newline/indent of block structures land BEFORE the NEWLINE/INDENT tokens. The Rust parser strips comments at init (line 60-71 of `src/parser/mod.rs`); the self-host parser didn't, so `expect_tok(TOK_NEWLINE)` / `expect_tok(TOK_INDENT)` would fail, leaving the INDENT unconsumed and causing cascading corruption (method bodies parsed as method signatures). - [2026-03-25] **Unified `needs_drop_for_temp` with `needs_drop` — Recursive types now tracked for call result drop**: Removed the separate `needs_drop_for_temp()` that excluded Recursive-drop types. `call_tracked()`/`call_extern_tracked()` now register ALL droppable types (including Recursive structs/enums like Column, DataFrame, TypedColumn) for scope-exit drop. Three fixes needed: (1) Missing `move_zero_resource_args` on Call-based EnumInit paths in `calls.rs` (meta-expanded variant constructors like `StrCol(call_result)` went through Call, not DotShorthand). (2) `DataFrame.drop(col_name)` user method collides with generated `DataFrame__drop` destructor — added `drop_collision_types` set to LirModule, populated during `populate_recursive_drop_structs`, used by `lower_field_drops` to inline sub-field drops instead of calling the colliding function. (3) Moved `populate_recursive_drop_structs()` before function lowering so collision info is available during LIR generation. 981 unit + 904 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-25] **Ptr pattern extraction for borrowed enum scrutinees**: Pattern match extraction from Ptr(enum) scrutinees now produces Ptr(T) for collection payloads and StringView for string payloads, matching struct field load behavior. Prevents shallow-copy ownership issues when extracting from borrowed enums. Applied in `patterns.rs` (GIR-level type conversion) and `lower.rs` (LIR EnumFieldLoad: Ptr destinations get field address, StringView destinations get cap-zero). Enables the `needs_drop` unification above.
- [2026-03-24] **ALL 904 TESTS GREEN — struct string ownership complete**: FieldLoad of GorgetString into Str destination zeros cap+alloc to create non-owning view. MoveZero on all 7 EnumInit paths (mod.rs×4, calls.rs×2, methods.rs×1) prevents shallow-copy double-free. Return MoveZero generalized for all droppable types. VarDecl Move for unregistered droppable temps. Provenance classifies local field access returns as Owned (auto-clone). StructInit auto-clones Ptr(collection) operands. P2P library 5 use-after-move fixes. Httpserver library `!resp` move semantics. LIR type inference block-param override.
- [2026-03-24] **Struct fields own GorgetString instead of Str views**: Removed String→Str mapping in struct TypeDefs. Structs now OWN their string fields via GorgetString, enabling recursive drop to free them. Field loads return Str views at load time (not type level). The previous design leaked strings by storing non-owning Str views that pointed to external temps kept alive by `should_unregister_string_args`. The "method chain temp lifetime" blocker turned out to be a test fixture bug (double unwrap = use-after-move, correctly caught by GIR validator). 981 unit + 904 integration tests pass, no ASan crashes.
- [2026-03-24] **Eliminate unnecessary string clones in C backend**: Two optimizations: (1) struct-by-value GorgetString stores use memcpy instead of clone+free (the clone+free round-trip was equivalent to memcpy since the source is a C temporary); (2) propagate GIR AssignMode::Move to LIR SlotStore via `is_move` flag so pointer-to-string stores use memcpy instead of clone when the source is being moved. Combined: 66% fewer gorget_string_clone calls (290→100 in yaml_parse). No ASan issues.
- [2026-03-24] **Universal drop registration for call results via call_tracked/call_extern_tracked**: Added `call_tracked()` and `call_extern_tracked()` wrappers on LoweringContext that auto-register call results for drop. Uses narrow `needs_drop_for_temp()` check (Trivial/Custom drop + collections) to avoid registering user structs with Recursive drop that would be double-freed. Replaces 5 explicit `register_local`/`register_owned_string_for_drop` sites in calls.rs, methods.rs, operators.rs, and assigns.rs. 981 unit + 904 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-23] **Collection field loads return Ptr(T) references**: Struct field access on collection-type fields (Vector, Dict, Set) now returns `Ptr(T)` (a reference into the struct) instead of a raw `T` (shallow copy). Prevents double-free from shared heap buffers. LIR FieldLoad stores field address as pointer for Ptr destinations; IndexLoad correctly handles Ptr-typed bases without double-deref (ref_locals already get SlotLoad). `.len()` optimization resolves through Ptr for field-load refs. Strings excluded (GorgetString header copy is safe as a Str view). Also fixed hot-reload `current_exe()` returning `(deleted)` path via `canonicalize()`. 981 unit + 904 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-23] **Fix GorgetString temp leak in C backend SlotStore clone**: C backend cloned GorgetString on every by-value SlotStore but never freed the original transient value. Each gorget_str_cat/format/int_to_display produced a heap temp that leaked after being cloned. Now frees originals immediately after cloning (+224 string frees in gorget-arena, 211→435). 981 unit + 903 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-23] **Fix collection temp leaks — register call results for drop + field assignment drop-before-reassign**: Three fixes: (1) `lower_drop` now resolves GIR type through projection chain (`resolve_gir_place_type`) so field drops like `bot.nav.path = Vector[int]()` free the old array before overwrite (+8 new frees in gorget-arena); (2) collection-returning function/method calls now register their temps for drop at scope exit (+61 new frees in gorget-arena); (3) `try_resolve_field_place` fast path now move-zeroes registered temps after field assignment (prevents double-free). Previously blocked by 8 p2p test failures — resolved by also move-zeroing anonymous collection temps after they're passed as function arguments. 981 unit + 904 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-22] **Fix closure f-string capture** — Variables used inside f-string interpolation in closure bodies weren't detected as free variables, so they weren't captured in the closure environment. Root cause: `collect_free_vars` in closures.rs didn't visit `Expr::StringLiteral` segments — interpolated identifiers like `{prefix}` in `f"{prefix} {name}"` fell into the `_ => {}` catch-all. Fix: added `Expr::StringLiteral` handler that extracts leading identifiers from `StringSegment::Interpolation` text and registers them as free variable references. 981 unit + 903 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-22] **Fix match guard bindings invisible in arm body** — `case Some(v) if v > 10:` would match correctly but `v` was 0 in the body. Root cause: `emit_pattern_bindings` ran in the guard basic block, creating SSA values there. The body ran in a different basic block where those values weren't defined. Fix: re-emit pattern bindings at the start of the body block. 981 unit + 901 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-22] **Fix Set.insert() missing in LIR backend** — `Set.insert()` mapped to `gorget_set_insert` which doesn't exist in the C runtime (the runtime function is `gorget_set_add`). Added `"insert" => "gorget_set_add"` mapping in `map_monomorphized_to_runtime`. Updated `collection_empty_edge.gg` to include Set operations, added `set_insert_contains.gg` fixture. 981 unit + 901 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-22] **Fix trait methods with `throws` segfault** — Trait method signatures with `throws` now correctly wrap the return type in `Result[T, E]`. Previously, vtable registration, equip method lowering, and trait method body lowering all used the bare return type (e.g., `int`) instead of `Result[int, String]`, causing the caller to interpret the return value as a Result struct while the callee returned a raw int — segfault via type confusion. Fixed in three places: vtable VTableMethod registration (traits.rs), lower_equip_method (functions.rs), and lower_trait_method_body (traits.rs). Also set `current_throws_result_type` so return/throw statements properly wrap values. 981 unit + 900 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-22] **Fix IndexLoad clone-on-read for collection-type elements** — `Vector[Vector[int]]` indexing (`matrix[0]`) now clones the inner vector instead of moving+zeroing it. Previously, reading a resource-type element from a collection via IndexLoad would zero the source slot (move semantics), destroying the original. Now collection-type elements (Vector, Dict, Set, Str) are deep-cloned via `gorget_*_clone()` runtime functions, preserving the original. Non-collection resource types (Task, user structs) retain move+zero semantics for intentional consumption patterns (e.g., `tasks[j].await()`). 981 unit + 897 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-22] **Fix nested pattern matching codegen** — `lower_pattern_condition` now recursively checks inner enum discriminants for nested constructor patterns (e.g., `Some(Shape.Circle(r))`). Previously only the outer tag was checked, so `Inner.B(99)` would incorrectly match `Inner.A(n)` and extract `n=0`. Fix uses short-circuit branching: inner field extraction only runs when outer tag matches (avoids reading garbage from wrong union variant). Also fixed ambiguous `resolve_enum_variant` for bare prelude variants (`Some`/`None`/`Ok`/`Error`) when multiple monomorphizations exist — now prefers `type_name(scrut_type)` to select the correct monomorphization. 981 unit + 897 integration tests pass.

Library files: `lib/xtd/toml.gg` (`start_section !hdr_path`), `lib/xtd/yaml.gg` (`merge_into` refactored from `!` return-pattern to `&` mutable borrow), `lib/xtd/dataframe.gg` (`df_group_by`/`df_group_by_multi`/`df_cast` — copy before struct storage), `lib/xtd/log.gg` (3 constructors `!log_level`), `lib/xtd/db.gg` (`FromRow::from_row !row`), `lib/xtd/math3d.gg` (`Ray.new !origin`). - [2026-03-22] **Borrow checker: reject storing borrowed resource params** — Added compile-time restriction: borrowed parameters (bare and `&`) of resource types cannot be stored in struct constructors, enum variant constructors, or return statements. Reuses existing `check_non_owned_param_move()` in `check_expr.rs` (StructLiteral + constructor Call sites) and `check_stmt.rs` (Return + expression-body). Extended `is_copy_type()` to recognize user-defined enums as Copy (eliminates false positives for ordinal enums like LogLevel). Fixed `lib/xtd/toml.gg` (`start_section` → `!hdr_path`) and `lib/xtd/yaml.gg` (`merge_into` → `!yaml_target`). Added 6 unit tests. Documented the rule in `docs/language-design.md` section 3.2. IR unregister-on-pass workaround retained for uncovered paths (method calls on struct fields). 980 unit + 893 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-22] **Phase 6: Collection scope-exit drops via ownership tracking** — Enabled `needs_drop()` for collection types (Vector, Dict, Set, Deque, HashMap, HashSet) using name-based detection in `src/ir/types.rs` — no TypeDef registration, avoiding transitive struct field upgrade. Added `is_collection_type_name()` helper. VarDecl move-zero (stmts/mod.rs): zero source temp when assigned to collection variable. Return move-zero (stmts/mod.rs): zero source local on collection return. Assignment move-zero (assigns.rs): zero source temp on collection reassignment. `gorget_map_free` null-alloc guard (c_runtime.rs): early return for zeroed/freed structs. `lower_field_drops` fix (lower.rs): use `infer_drop_strategy()` instead of `get_type_def()` to detect collection fields for Custom/Recursive drop structs. Unregister collection args passed by value to functions (calls.rs, methods.rs): prevents shared-data-pointer use-after-free when callee stores shallow copy. Drop-before-reassign excluded for collections: RHS may modify target in-place through pointer (e.g., `dict = merge_into(dict, x)`). 974 unit + 844 integration tests pass, 0 double-frees, 0 use-after-free (verified with ASan).
- [2026-03-21] **Phase 6: Ptr-for-all-types in collection element reads** — Changed collection element reads (`get/first/last → unwrap`) to return Ptr references for ALL element types, not just direct collections. Previously, user structs with resource fields (e.g., Container with Vector field) were deref'd to shallow copies → double-free when both copy and collection were dropped. Now ALL unwrapped Ptr values stay as Ptr, matching Rust's `&T` semantics. Fixed `lower_place_addr` to handle Deref vs non-Deref projections correctly for collection_ref_locals (Deref-first → SlotAddr, otherwise → SlotLoad). Removed `is_collection` check (~10 lines). Updated `drop_struct_collection_fields` expected output (no more duplicate drops from shallow copies). Scope-exit drops for collection locals deferred — shallow copy semantics in function returns/assignments still prevent safe drops. 974 unit + 844 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-21] **Phase 6 investigation: collection scope-exit drops** — Attempted registering collection TypeDefs with `CopySemantics::Resource` + `DropStrategy::Trivial` for Vector/Dict/Set. Found that enabling drops causes 42+ double-free crashes because collection element reads create shallow copies sharing heap buffers. Added infrastructure for future enablement: `deep_clone_resource_fields()` in c_lir (handles struct payloads with resource fields), `is_collection_type()` on TypeRegistry (distinguishes direct collections from user structs), `infer_drop_strategy()` fallback in LIR lower_drop. Dict Ref (Ptr payloads for Dict.get()) also attempted and reverted — breaks write-back pattern. Closed "variable shadowing aliases storage" TODO (already working, verified by `shadowing_nested.gg`). 974 unit + 844 integration tests pass.

- [2026-03-21] **Return ownership contract enforcement — implemented then reverted** — Implemented callee-side validation for `T !` / `T &` return sigils, `Owned()` wrapping for allocating string methods, `BareNonCopyReturn` warning, and return sigil documentation. The sigils added cognitive overhead without enabling new safety checks. The `Type::Ref`/`Type::Owned` AST/type infrastructure remains (pre-existing from 2026-03-20) but is not enforced or documented as recommended practice.

Restored broken symlink (parser/lexer.gg). 974 unit + 844 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-21] **GorgetString temp leak: extend void-callee heuristic to unknown/extern functions** — Changed `should_unregister_string_args` fallback for unknown callees (not in `fn_param_abis`) from conservative `true` (leak) to `false` (keep in drop tracking). Sound because: (1) void return already checked (no view escapes via result), (2) C runtime functions take Str by value (no ByMutPtr in Gorget sense), (3) Gorget-defined functions with ByMutPtr params are always in `fn_param_abis`. Eliminates leaks for all void-returning runtime/extern calls. File: `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`. 974 unit + 844 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-21] **GIR copy propagation re-enabled + string temp leak reduction** — Two optimizations. (1) **Copy propagation fix**: `propagate_copies` in `src/ir/transforms/optimize.rs` was disabled due to 143/844 integration test failures. Root cause: `Drop`, `DropIfAlive`, and `MoveZero` instructions destroy a local's value but weren't invalidating copy entries — stale copies were substituted after the source was zeroed/freed (use-after-free). Fix: added explicit match arm to invalidate copies whose source is destroyed. The existing type-equality guard (`dst_type == src_type`) was already correct; the original "TypeId aliasing" diagnosis was wrong. Added 4 unit tests. (2) **Targeted string temp leak reduction**: `unregister_gorget_string_args` unconditionally leaked GorgetString temps passed as call args. Added `should_unregister_string_args` heuristic: for void-returning calls with no `ByMutPtr` params (checked via `fn_param_abis`), the str view cannot escape the callee's stack frame, so temps stay in drop tracking and are freed at block scope exit. Recovers `print(f"...")`, `assert(f"...")`, and similar patterns. Unknown/extern callees conservatively unregister (leak). Files: `src/ir/transforms/optimize.rs`, `src/ir/lowering/exprs/mod.rs`, `calls.rs`, `methods.rs`. 974 unit + 844 integration tests pass.

Only VIEW_METHODS list now drives extern downgrades. Updated 3 borrow-checker tests to expect conservative-owned behavior for bodyless functions. Kept `"as_str"` (semantically correct view method). (3) **Match arm provenance**: `check_assignments` now iterates match arm bodies (via `Expr::Block` unwrap) for reassignment tracking; `recurse_into_stmt` now calls `infer_block` on match arm bodies for nested VarDecl provenance. Files: `src/semantic/provenance.rs`, `src/semantic/safety/tests.rs`. 970 unit + 843 integration tests pass (1 flaky).

(1) `collect_string_decls` only handled `Pattern::Binding` — added recursive `collect_string_pattern` for Tuple/Constructor patterns, and extended to handle `Type::Inferred`/`Type::Tuple` AST types. (2) Tuple VarDecl lowering didn't call `provenance_adjusted_string_type` for field bindings — added the adjustment call. Fixes unnecessary GorgetString allocations for `auto host, port = parse_url(...)` patterns. 970 unit + 844 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-21] **Union-based enum layout** — Large enums (>4 fields) use C union layout instead of flat sequential fields. Stmt: 39KB → ~1.3KB. Fixes self-host resolver/typechecker stack overflow. Small enums (Option, Result) keep flat layout for C backend compatibility. 970 unit + 844 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-21] **Phase 3b: Ptr payloads for collection borrowing reads** — Collection borrowing methods (`get`/`first`/`last`) on resource-type elements now return `Option__Ref_T` with `Ptr(elem_type)` payload. The collection retains ownership; caller gets a reference (no clone, no drop, no double-free, no leak). GIR unwrap detects `Ref_` prefix and emits `Ptr(pointee)`. For primitives/strings: immediate Deref. For collections: Ptr propagates through var decls, auto-reinference, and function return locals. LIR `lower_place_addr` uses `SlotLoad` for `collection_ref_locals`. C backend `__option_unwrap` handler detects Ptr payload fields. `collection_ref_locals` set on GIR Function, populated at GIR lowering, consumed at LIR lowering. 970 unit + 844 integration tests pass.
- [2026-03-20] **T &/T ! return type sigils — Phases 1-5** — Implemented suffix ownership syntax for return types and generic args. (1) **AST+Parser**: `Type::Ref(Box<Spanned<Type>>)` and `Type::Owned(Box<Spanned<Type>>)` variants; `parse_type_with_ownership()` for suffix `&`/`!`; used in generic args and function return types. (2) **Semantic**: `ResolvedType::Ref(TypeId)`/`Owned(TypeId)`; `Ref` is Copy, `Owned` is not; `Ref` is a reference type for lifetime tracking. (3) **IR**: `Type::Ref` → `GirType::Ptr(inner)`, `Type::Owned` → unwrap to inner. (4) **Type checker**: Auto-deref coercion `Ref(T)↔T` and `Owned(T)↔T` in `unify()`; cast validation unwraps Ref/Owned; collection methods return `Option[T &]` for get/first/last, `Option[T !]` for pop/remove, `Option[V &]` for Dict.get. (5) **C backend**: Ptr payload detection in Option structs — stores pointer directly instead of dereferencing. - [2026-03-20] **LIR: two-pass type registration fixes self-host parser forward references** — The `lower_type_defs` function in `src/lir/lower.rs` processed type definitions in a single pass. When an enum referenced a struct defined later in the file (forward reference), that struct wasn't yet registered, so the field type degraded to `LirType::Ptr`. This corrupted the self-host parser's AST types (e.g., `Item.IFunction_0` became `void*` instead of `FunctionDef`). Fix: (1) Split `lower_type_defs` into two passes — Pass 1 pre-registers all type names with empty placeholder structs, Pass 2 fills in actual fields using `map_gir_type_with_structs` (which can now resolve all names). (2) Regular `Box[T]` types registered with hardcoded `_0: Ptr` field to break recursive type cycles (Expr → Box__SpannedExpr → SpannedExpr → Expr). Trait boxes (with data/vtable) go through normal two-pass registration. (3) Topological sort for C struct definitions in `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs` — Kahn's algorithm ensures inline struct fields are defined before structs that contain them, preventing "incomplete type" C compilation errors. Known limitation: flat enum layout (all variant fields sequential, not union) causes Stmt struct to grow from 1.3KB to 39KB when forward references resolve to large inline types, causing stack overflows in deeply-recursive self-host resolver/typechecker. Files: `src/lir/lower.rs`, `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs`. 970 unit + 843 integration tests pass (bench_basic pre-existing failure).

Clone is a no-op for views (cap=0), deep-copies for owned (cap>0). Also fixed `httpserver_json.gg` test fixture (moved body1 inline to avoid borrow-after-move). - [2026-03-16] **LIR backend: 596/596 A/B parity (100%)** — Fixed last 2 failures (async_select, stress_channel_select) caused by select loop deadlock. Root cause: `__gorget_select_yield()` called `__gorget_try_run_one()` which could steal a blocking spawn task from the executor queue and run it inline on the main thread. When the stolen producer task blocked on `gorget_channel_send` (channel full), the main thread could never return to `poll_recv` to drain the channel → deadlock. Fix: added `__gorget_try_run_one_nonblocking()` that only steals poll-based (coroutine) tasks, skipping run-based (blocking) tasks. Select yield now uses this variant. This caused cwnd=0 in all p2p reliable stream tests (flush_send never sent data because can_send=cwnd-flight_size=0). Fix: enlarged static buffer to 4096 bytes with heap fallback for elements exceeding that. Fixed p2p_reliable_basic, p2p_reliable_bidir, p2p_reliable_large, p2p_stream_robust. - [2026-03-16] **LIR backend: fix TaskGroup spawn segfault (580→586/596)** — When a spawn result was stored into a `void*` destination (the `dst_is_spawn_ptr` path), the codegen extracted only `.__task` from the `Task__void` struct, discarding the `.__drop` function pointer. Later, `gorget_task_group_submit` cast the raw `void*` value as `*(Task__void*)ptr`, reading garbage memory for `__drop` (segfault). Fix: added `spawn_source_fn` tracking vector in the pre-pass to record which spawn function produced each `void*` value, then in `task_group_submit` emit `gorget_task_group_submit_raw(group, task_ptr, __spawn_drop_fn)` directly, bypassing the macro and providing the correct drop function. Fixed stress_shared_comprehensive + 5 other tests. File: `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs`.
- [2026-03-16] **LIR backend: fix Str→GorgetString coercion in SlotStore/Store** — When a function returning `Str` (16 bytes) had its result stored into a `GorgetString` slot (32 bytes), the backend emitted `memcpy(&slot, &val, sizeof(GorgetString))` — reading 32 bytes from 16-byte Str data (stack-buffer-overflow). Root cause: the SlotStore handler had coercion for GorgetString→Str (downcast) but not the reverse Str→GorgetString (upcast). Added `gorget_string_from_str()` coercion for both pointer and by-value cases in SlotStore, plus Str*→GorgetString* coercion in Inst::Store. Fixed httpserver_json segfault (exit 139). File: `src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs`.

Phase 4: Private-in-Public — errors when `public` function exposes a `private` type in signature (`PrivateTypeInPublicSignature`). For `Result[str, str] r = bytes_to_str(...)`, Result is not in `ref_type_structs` (only structs, not enums), so `r`'s origin isn't tracked in `var_origins`, and `compute_expr_origin(r)` returns `Local(r_def_id)` instead of `Static`. Fix: added `imported_module_depth` counter to `BorrowChecker` — DanglingReturn/UnresolvedBorrowOrigin checks are skipped when inside `Item::Module` wrappers (imported code is validated by its own project's checker). - [2026-03-11] **Fix: compound index assign (`obj[i] += val`)** — `lower_compound_assign()` in `src/ir/lowering/stmts/assigns.rs` had no handler for `Expr::Index` targets, silently producing no code. Added full handler: reads current value via `index_load` (built-in collections) or getter method (custom types), computes the binary op (including string concat and operator overloads), writes back via `Vector__T__set` / `Dict__K__V__put` / custom setter. Handles nested field access (`self.vec[i] += val`) by copying the field to a temp local for the read (so the C backend can determine collection type) while using the original field Place for the write. Supports all compound ops: `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, bitwise, wrapping.

- [2026-03-11] **Fix: augmented assignment on struct fields (`self.field += 1`)** — `lower_compound_assign()` in `src/ir/lowering/stmts/assigns.rs` only handled `Expr::Identifier` targets, silently producing no code for `Expr::FieldAccess`. Added FieldAccess handler that resolves the field to a Place via `try_resolve_field_place`, reads the current value, computes the binary op (including string concat and operator overloads), and writes back. Supports `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `<<=`, `>>=`, bitwise ops on struct fields through `&self` and on local struct copies.

- [2026-03-11] **Fix: Dict/Vector index assign on struct fields (`self.dict[key] = val`)** — `lower_index_assign()` in `assigns.rs` called `lower_expr()` on the object, which for `FieldAccess` targets copied the collection struct to a temporary. After `gorget_map_put`, the copy's updated metadata (count, order_len) and reallocated pointers (after hash table resize) were discarded. Fixed by resolving FieldAccess objects via `try_resolve_field_place` to get a Place pointing to the original field, and using the resolved field type for dispatch (since `infer_operand_type_full` doesn't walk projections).

- [2026-03-10] **Benchmarks (`bench` blocks)**: Implemented `bench "name":` blocks with `gg test --bench`. Full pipeline: `Bench` keyword in lexer, `BenchDef` AST node, `Item::Bench` through parser/resolver/typecheck/borrow/meta/rewrite/loader, `BenchFnInfo` in IR, `lower_bench_items()` in lowering, `emit_bench_runner_main()` in C backend, `run_bench_suite()` in simulator. Bench runner: 3-iteration warmup, auto-calibrate from 100 iterations doubling until >= 1 second, auto-scaled output (ns/us/ms/s per iteration).
