- [2026-02-23] Async/Await Phase 7 — RAII for Async State Structs. Non-Copy fields in async state structs are now properly dropped at every completion site, preventing memory leaks for String, Vector, Dict, user structs with Drop, etc. **Architecture**: `AsyncAnalysis` extended with `drop_entries: Vec<DropEntry>` computed at analysis time — params use `drop_action_for_type()` (full AST type available), locals use AST type when explicit or fall back to new `drop_action_for_c_type()` (C-string-based, buffer-level drops). `emit_async_cleanup()` emits drops in reverse order with `__self->` prefix, then `free(__self); __future->state = NULL;`. `async_return_skip_var()` prevents double-free when returning a non-Copy local (ownership transferred to `__future->result`). **4 cleanup sites updated**: (1) `Return(Some(expr))` with skip_var, (2) `Return(None)`, (3) implicit void return at end of block body, (4) expression-body async functions. `drop_entries` threaded through `emit_async_stmts`/`emit_async_stmt` for returns inside control flow. **New helper**: `drop_action_for_c_type()` in c_stmt.rs — determines drop action from mangled C type strings (GorgetString, GorgetArray, GorgetDict/GorgetMap, GorgetSet, pointer types, primitives, user structs). Visibility: `drop_action_for_type()` and `emit_drop_entry()` promoted to `pub(super)` for cross-file access. **Zero-init safety**: State structs are `malloc+memset(0)` — all drop functions handle zero data safely (gorget_string_free checks cap>0, gorget_array_free calls free(NULL), StructDrop uses memcmp zero-check). **Test**: `async_drop.gg` — `Tracked` struct with Drop, `compute` creates and drops local before returning int, `main` prints result and drops its own local. Files: `src/codegen/c_item.rs`, `src/codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `tests/fixtures/async_drop.gg`, `tests/integration.rs`. All 525 unit + 292 integration tests pass, 0 regressions.
- [2026-02-23] Async/Await Phase 6 — Await Inside Control Flow. Implemented Duff's device pattern: `case N:` labels placed inside `while`/`loop`/`if`/`elif`/`else` bodies within the existing `switch(__self->__state)`, enabling `await` inside control flow. **Analysis**: Extracted `analyze_async_block`/`analyze_async_stmt` recursive methods from the flat `analyze_async_function` loop. Only recurses into control flow bodies that contain await — variables in non-await bodies stay as normal C locals (not lifted to state struct). **Emission**: Extracted `emit_async_stmts`/`emit_async_stmt` recursive methods from flat `emit_async_poll_body` loop. Control flow with await in bodies emits normal C control flow (`while(cond){...}`, `if(cond){...}`) with Duff's device `case N:` labels inside for suspension/resume. Control flow without await falls through to `gen_stmt`. Also added `Assign` with await support (bonus fix). **Helpers**: Added `block_contains_await`/`stmt_contains_await` recursive walkers for fast-path detection. **Test**: `async_control_flow.gg` — `sum_loop` (while+await), `pick` (if/else+await), `even_sum` (nested if-inside-while+await). **Scope**: while+await, loop+await, if/elif/else+await, nested combinations, break/continue. Not supported yet: for+await, match+await, await in conditions. Files: `src/codegen/c_item.rs`, `tests/fixtures/async_control_flow.gg`, `tests/integration.rs`. All 525 unit + 291 integration tests pass, 0 regressions.
- [2026-02-23] Async/Await Phase 5 — Thread-Local Error Handling + `std.channel`. **Part A**: Added `_Thread_local` to 5 global declarations in `c_runtime.rs`: `__gorget_cleanup[256]`, `__gorget_cleanup_top`, `__gorget_jmp_stack[64]`, `__gorget_jmp_top`, `__gorget_last_error`. Fixes UB when throwing in spawned tasks (each thread now gets its own error/cleanup state). **Part B**: Bounded MPMC channel for inter-task communication. `Channel[T]` maps to `GorgetChannel*` in C — type-erased ring buffer with mutex + two condvars (`not_full`/`not_empty`) + `closed` flag. Copy semantics (pointer copy = shared access). API: `Channel[int](cap)` constructor, `ch.send(val)` (blocks while full, panics if closed), `ch.recv()` (blocks while empty, panics if closed+empty), `ch.close()` (sets closed, broadcasts all waiters). **Runtime**: `CHANNEL_RUNTIME` constant (~75 lines C) with `gorget_channel_new/send/recv/close/free`. **Module**: `std.channel` registered as synthetic module in `stdlib.rs` with `gen_channel_module()` (generic struct + equip block with `decl_method` entries). **Type system**: `Channel` added to built-in generics in `resolve.rs`, `Channel` → `GorgetChannel*` in both `ast_type_to_c` and `type_id_to_c`, `Channel` marked Copy in `is_copy_type` via `ResolvedType::Generic` arm (added `scopes` parameter to `is_copy_type`). **Codegen**: constructor via `gen_generic_call` Channel arm, method dispatch via `gen_channel_method` (send/recv/close), `Channel` excluded from struct-call rewrite in `rewrite.rs` and generic struct template collection in `c_item.rs`, conditional `CHANNEL_RUNTIME` emission + `#include <pthread.h>` when no spawn, `needs_threads = has_spawn || has_channel`. **Integration test**: `async_channel.gg` — two producers each sending 3 values via bounded channel, consumer summing all 6 values, verifies deterministic sum (21). **Files**: `src/codegen/c_runtime.rs`, `src/stdlib.rs`, `src/semantic/resolve.rs`, `src/semantic/borrow.rs`, `src/semantic/rewrite.rs`, `src/codegen/c_types.rs`, `src/codegen/mod.rs`, `src/codegen/c_item.rs`, `src/codegen/c_expr_generic.rs`, `src/codegen/c_expr_call.rs`, `src/codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `tests/fixtures/async_channel.gg`, `tests/integration.rs`. All 525 unit + 290 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-23] Async/Await Phase 4 — Runtime: Thread-Pool Executor. Implemented pthread-based thread-pool executor so `spawn` creates tasks that run concurrently on worker threads. **Architecture**: `GorgetExecutor` with N worker threads (default = CPU count via `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`), mutex-protected FIFO task queue, lazy-init on first spawn. Per-`Future[T]` type: `__SpawnCtx__T` (embeds `GorgetTask` base + `Future__T`), `__SpawnCtx__T__run` (polls future to completion, signals done via condvar), `Task__T` (user-facing handle with `GorgetTask*` pointer). **Spawn flow**: evaluate args → construct `Future[T]` → heap-alloc `SpawnCtx` via `calloc` → init mutex/condvar → submit to executor → return `Task[T]` handle. **Await on Task[T]**: blocking condvar wait (NOT a suspension point) — `pthread_mutex_lock` → `while (!done) pthread_cond_wait` → extract result from `SpawnCtx.future.result` → destroy mutex/condvar → free. **Await on Future[T]**: unchanged busy-poll (Phase 3 behavior). **Key design decisions**: (1) `Task[T]` is now a distinct C type (`Task__T`) separate from `Future__T` (was aliased in Phase 3). (2) Task-await in async poll body treated as regular blocking assignment, NOT a suspension point — uses `is_task_await_static` check to skip sub-future state machine logic. (3) `analyze_async_function` skips Task-await expressions when counting sub-futures. (4) Type checker accepts both `Future[T]` and `Task[T]` in `await` expressions. (5) Executor shutdown called after async main completes (conditioned on `has_spawn`). **Detection**: `SpawnDetector` visitor walks all function/equip bodies for `Expr::Spawn` to set `has_spawn` flag, which gates executor runtime emission, Task typedef emission, and `-lpthread` linking. **Files**: `src/codegen/c_runtime.rs` (+`EXECUTOR_RUNTIME` ~80 lines C), `src/codegen/mod.rs` (`needs_threads` in CodegenOutput, `has_spawn` in context, SpawnDetector visitor), `src/codegen/c_types.rs` (Task[T] → `Task__T`), `src/codegen/c_item.rs` (`emit_task_typedefs`, `is_task_await`/`is_task_await_static`, poll body Task-aware, main shutdown), `src/codegen/c_expr.rs` (Spawn → executor submit, Await → Task vs Future branch), `src/codegen/c_stmt.rs` (`infer_c_type_from_expr` Spawn/Await cases), `src/semantic/typecheck.rs` (Await accepts Task[T]), `src/main.rs` (`add_thread_flags` at 4 cc_cmd sites), `tests/fixtures/async_spawn.gg`, `tests/integration.rs`. **V1 limitations**: thread-pool deadlock possible; `__gorget_jmp_stack` global (not thread-local); spawned-but-never-awaited tasks leak; `await Task` only in async functions. All 525 unit + 289 integration tests pass, 0 regressions.

- [2026-02-23] Async/Await Phase 3 — C Codegen: State Machine Transformation. Each async function becomes three C artifacts: (1) `__AsyncState_funcname` struct holding state tag + params + locals + sub-future fields, (2) `funcname__poll` function with switch-based dispatch that resumes at correct state on re-entry, (3) constructor function that allocates state and returns `Future[T]`. `Future[T]` monomorphized per-T with `{poll, state, result}` fields. `await` in poll body: store sub-future → set next state → fall through → poll sub-future → extract result. `await` in sync context: busy-poll fallback (GCC statement expression). `spawn`: identity (Task[T] = Future[T] for Phase 3). Async main emitted as `gg__async_main` + C `main` wrapper that busy-polls to completion. Variable prefixing via `async_lifted_vars: Option<HashSet<String>>` — same pattern as existing `mutable_captures` / `pointer_params` prefixing in `gen_expr` for `Expr::Identifier`. `Future`/`Task` type mapping in `ast_type_to_c` and `type_id_to_c` (Task maps to Future). V1 restrictions: await only at statement level (VarDecl RHS, expr-stmt, return), no await inside if/for/while/match, no async closures, no RAII for owned state fields. New integration test: `async_basic.gg` (multi-level async with await). Updated 2 codegen unit tests from stub checks to real async output. Dead peer (state 7) declared when silence exceeds timeout; `p2p_poll` scans for state 7, emits STREAM_CLOSED, transitions to CLOSED. `last_recv_ms` updated on every received stream packet. **(C) Message Framing**: `p2p_stream_send_frame()` prepends 4-byte big-endian length header. `p2p_stream_recv_frame()` reassembles into `frame_buf`, returns one complete frame or empty vector. Fix: before generating field expressions for a single-type-param generic enum variant constructor, peel one layer off `decl_type_hint` (e.g., `Option[Option[int]]` → `Option[int]`), then restore after. Works recursively for arbitrary nesting depth. Multi-param generics (like `Result[T, E]`) are unaffected — the `generic_args.len() == 1` guard skips them. - [2026-02-19] Implement `.enumerate()` for for-loops. Syntactic sugar that exposes a sequential index via tuple destructuring: `for (i, elem) in items.enumerate():`. Zero-cost universal counter approach — detects `.enumerate()` MethodCall in `gen_for_loop()`, unwraps to inner iterable, emits a `size_t` counter before the loop, and binds `int64_t idx = (int64_t)counter++` after element binding. Works for all iterable types (Vector, str, Set, Iterable trait, etc.) because the counter increments only when a valid element is reached (map/set `continue` for deleted entries happens before binding). Type checker extended to assign proper types to enumerate tuple pattern bindings (int for index, element type for value) — also fixes the broader issue that for-loop variables over Vector/Set didn't have type_id assigned, which would cause wrong printf format specifiers in string interpolation. Files: `typecheck.rs` (enumerate in `builtin_method_type()` + pattern type assignment in `Stmt::For`), `c_stmt.rs` (enumerate detection + counter in `gen_for_loop()`), `enumerate.gg` + `integration.rs`. - [2026-02-19] Phase 22: Deep-Clone on Collection Write/Read + Full Element Drops. Removed the `safe_element_drop()` safety filter that stripped collection-field drops from struct elements stored in collections (e.g., `Vector[TomlSection]` where `TomlSection` has Dict/Vector fields). Elements now get full drops including nested collection cleanup. To prevent double-frees from shallow copies, deep-clone infrastructure ensures collection elements independently own their buffers. **Write-side (push/set/put):** `source_is_safe_for_push()` checks whether the source expression will be move-zeroed (Identifier with drops, FieldAccess with zero target) or is a fresh allocation (function return, constructor call). Unsafe sources get deep-cloned via `compute_push_clone_code()` before insertion. **Read-side (.get()):** `.get()` deep-clones non-Copy elements, returning an independently-owned copy. The `deep_cloned_expr` flag signals VarDecl to register user Drop only (not field drops) to avoid double-frees when the deep-cloned result's fields are shallow-copied elsewhere (the TOML parser's get→modify→set pattern). **Clone infrastructure:** `gorget_string_clone()`, `gorget_set_clone()` in c_runtime.rs; `gorget_array_clone()` already existed; `{mangled}__clone()` for each monomorphized Dict/HashMap type in c_item.rs. `CloneAction` enum (`ArrayClone`, `StringClone`, `MapClone(String)`, `SetClone`) drives `compute_clone_fields()` which inspects struct field types to determine per-field clone actions. Known limitations: deep-cloned `.get()` results' collection-field buffers leak if not consumed (tracked in TODO); `set()`/`put()` doesn't pre-drop old values (tracked in TODO). Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_runtime.rs`, `codegen/c_item.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `codegen/c_expr_methods.rs`, `tests/fixtures/drop_struct_collection_fields.gg`, `tests/integration.rs`. All 475 unit + 246 integration tests pass.

- [2026-02-18] Phase 20: Field-Level Move-Zeroing. When a non-Copy struct field is consumed (e.g., `items.push(h.data)` or `Vector[int] v = h.data`), the source field is now zeroed via `memset(&obj.field, 0, sizeof(obj.field))`, making the copy the sole owner. Implementation reuses existing `pending_move_zeros` + `flush_move_zeros()` infrastructure — pushing `"h.data"` generates valid C `memset(&h.data, 0, ...)`. Added `queue_field_move_zero()` helper with safety gates: only fires for simple Identifier objects, non-pointer-params, structs without user Drop (partial zeroing + user Drop = UB), and non-Copy field types. Extended all 4 consuming-site queue functions in `c_expr_call.rs` with `FieldAccess` branches alongside existing `Identifier` checks. New integration test `drop_field_move_zero.gg` validates: push-field-into-collection (was double-free) and assign-field-to-variable (was leak). - [2026-02-18] Phase 19: Move-Guard + Partial Element Drops for Structs with Collection Fields. Two focused changes: (1) Added zero-guard to user Drop calls in `emit_drop_entry()` — wraps `StructDrop` user Drop calls in `memcmp(&var, &zero, sizeof(var)) != 0` check using `__typeof__` block scope. Move-zeroed structs (via `.push()`, etc.) now correctly skip their user Drop at scope exit instead of calling it with NULL/zero fields (previously printed "drop (null)"). (2) Changed `safe_element_drop()` from full filtering to partial stripping — struct elements with collection fields now preserve user Drop + non-collection field drops, stripping only collection field drops (aliasing-unsafe). Previously the entire `StructDrop` was filtered to `None`. Types with user Drop but no non-collection fields (like `Container` with `str label` + `Vector[int] data`) now get `StructDrop { user_drop: true, field_drops: [] }`. Types without user Drop and only collection fields (like `TomlSection`) still filter to `None` — TOML aliasing chain remains safe. New integration test `drop_struct_collection_fields.gg` validates: Vector[Container] element drops fire user Drop ("drop first", "drop second") while move-zeroed local variables skip user Drop (no "drop (null)" output). - [2026-02-18] Phase 18: Collection Drops for Function/Method-Returned Collections. Expanded the drop registration gate beyond constructor-initialized collections to also cover collections returned by function and method calls. Added `DropAction::buffer_only()` method that strips element/key/value drops while preserving buffer-level cleanup — safe because function/method-returned collection elements may be shallow-copied from the source (e.g., `.keys()` copies key structs sharing internal pointers). Added `is_fresh_allocation_source()` predicate: accepts all `Expr::Call` (user function calls return freshly-constructed collections) and a whitelist of `Expr::MethodCall` methods known to allocate fresh buffers (`keys`, `values`, `items`, `filter`, `map`, `sorted`, `slice`, `split`, `union`, `intersection`, `difference`). Methods like `.get()` and `.unwrap()` are excluded — they return shallow copies that share the source's buffer. Updated VarDecl drop registration from two-tier to three-tier logic: (1) non-collection → full drops always, (2) constructor-initialized → full drops with element iteration, (3) fresh allocation source → buffer-only drops, (4) otherwise (variable copy/field access) → no drop. The whitelist approach was necessary because accepting all method calls caused double-frees in `nested_generics.gg` where `.get()` on `Vector[Vector[int]]` returns an aliased inner vector. Known limitation: function-returned collections of non-Copy elements leak element destructors (buffer freed but elements not iterated). Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `drop_fn_return_collection.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 475 unit + 241 integration tests pass.

- [2026-02-18] Add date/time formatting to `std.time`. Added `format_time(int, str) -> str` (strftime wrapper via `gorget_format_time`) and `parse_time(str, str) -> int` (strptime wrapper via `gorget_parse_time`). `format_time` returns a human-readable string from epoch seconds using the given format pattern; `parse_time` returns epoch seconds from a date string or -1 on failure. Also fixed `escape_string` bug: split into `escape_string` (for regular string literals) and `escape_printf_string` (with `%` → `%%` for printf/sprintf contexts). Previously, all string literals had `%` doubled, breaking strftime format strings like `"%Y-%m-%d"` which became `"%%Y-%%m-%%d"`. Updated `c_expr_print.rs` to use `escape_printf_string` for printf/fprintf/gorget_format contexts. New integration test `time_format.gg`. Files: `c_runtime.rs`, `stdlib.rs`, `c_expr_call.rs`, `c_expr.rs`, `c_expr_print.rs`, `time_format.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 475 unit + 241 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Phase 17: Element-Level Collection Drops. When a collection is destroyed, it now iterates non-Copy elements and runs each element's drop action before freeing the buffer. Extended `DropAction::ArrayFree`, `MapFree`, `SetFree` with element/key/value drop info: `ArrayFree { element_drop, element_c_type }`, `MapFree { mangled_name, key_drop, value_drop }`, `SetFree { element_drop, element_c_type }`. `drop_action_for_type()` recursively computes element drops for collections — `Vector[String]` gets `ArrayFree { element_drop: Some(StringFree), element_c_type: Some("GorgetString") }`, `Dict[str, String]` gets `MapFree { value_drop: Some(StringFree) }`, etc. `emit_drop_entry()` gains `depth: usize` parameter for unique loop variable names (`__di0`/`__de0`, `__di1`/`__de1`, ...) enabling nested collections like `Vector[Vector[String]]`. Element iteration: ArrayFree loops `0..len` casting `void*` elements to typed pointers; MapFree loops `0..cap` checking `states[i] == 1` for live entries; SetFree loops `0..cap` with state check and typed key cast. Safety gate: `safe_element_drop()` filters out `StructDrop` elements that `involves_collection()` — struct elements with collection fields are skipped because field-level move-zeroing isn't implemented yet, and shallow copies (e.g., passing Vector by C value) can alias inner collection buffers causing use-after-free (TOML module canonical example). Test-body cleanup (`emit_test_cleanup_for_action`) updated to match new struct variants but stays buffer-only (no element iteration in panic path). Extended `drop_collections.gg` with `Vector[Tracked]` (proving element destructors fire via print), `Vector[String]`, `Dict[str, String]`, and `Vector[Vector[String]]` (nested). Together with Phase 16's move-zeroing, this completes the ownership story for collection elements (except struct elements with collection fields — tracked separately). Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `drop_collections.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 475 unit + 240 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Add HTTP redirect following to `std.http`. Extracted single-request logic into `http_single()`, wrapped `http_request()` with a redirect loop (max 10 hops). 301/302/303 switch method to GET and drop body; 307/308 preserve original method and body. Handles both absolute and relative (path-only) Location headers. Returns error on >10 redirects, returns response as-is if no Location header present. File: `lib/std/http.gg`. All 475 unit + 240 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Fix memory leak in all String-returning string methods and conversion functions. Added `gorget_string_adopt(char* s)` to c_runtime.rs — wraps a freshly-malloc'd `char*` into a `GorgetString` without copying (zero-copy ownership transfer). Replaced `gorget_string_new(gorget_string_X(...))` with `gorget_string_adopt((char*)gorget_string_X(...))` at all 17 sites: 14 string methods in `c_expr_methods.rs` (trim, strip, lstrip, rstrip, to_upper, to_lower, replace, substring, repeat, join, removeprefix, removesuffix, pad_left, pad_right) and 4 conversion functions in `c_expr_call.rs` (int_to_str, float_to_str, char_to_str, codepoint_to_str). Previously each call leaked the intermediate malloc'd `const char*` because `gorget_string_new()` malloc'd again and copied. Files: `c_runtime.rs`, `c_expr_methods.rs`, `c_expr_call.rs`. All 474 unit + 240 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Refactor: Centralize move-zeroing via semantic ownership data. Consolidated 6 scattered move-zero sites across 3 files into 3 centralized helpers in `c_expr_call.rs`: (1) `builtin_consuming_arg_indices()` — static lookup table replacing hardcoded knowledge in 4 collection method arms (Vector.push/set, Dict.put, Set.add); (2) `queue_method_arg_move_zeros()` — two-tier hook called at top of `gen_method_call`, first checking the static table for built-in methods, then falling back to `method_resolutions → FunctionInfo.param_ownerships` for user-defined methods with `Ownership::Move` parameters; (3) `queue_constructor_move_zeros_call_args()`/`queue_constructor_move_zeros_exprs()` — constructor helpers replacing inline loops in enum variant, struct literal, and struct/newtype-via-gen_call codegen. Threaded `method_resolutions: FxHashMap<usize, DefId>` from typechecker through `AnalysisResult` into `CodegenContext` (previously discarded after borrow checker). Changed `gen_method_call` and `gen_generic_method_call` signatures from `method_name: &str` to `method: &Spanned<String>` to preserve span for `method_resolutions` lookup. Fixed latent newtype bug: `MyNewtype(droppable_value)` now queues move-zeroing (struct/newtype constructor path in `gen_call` was missing it). Removed 4 inline move-zero blocks from `c_expr_methods.rs`. Files: `semantic/mod.rs`, `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_expr.rs`, `codegen/c_expr_call.rs`, `codegen/c_expr_generic.rs`, `codegen/c_expr_methods.rs`. All 474 unit + 240 integration tests pass.

Added pure Gorget `base64_encode(Vector[uint8]) -> str` and `base64_decode(str) -> Result[Vector[uint8], str]` implementing RFC 4648. - [2026-02-18] Phase 16: Enable Collection Buffer Drops with Move-Zeroing. Activated `DropAction::ArrayFree`, `MapFree`, `SetFree` in `drop_action_for_type()` for Vector/List/Array, Dict, HashMap, Set/HashSet. Added move-zeroing infrastructure: `queue_move_zero_if_droppable()` queues droppable variables for post-statement `memset(&var, 0, sizeof(var))`, making scope-exit drops no-op (`free(NULL)` safe per C standard). Zeroing at consumption sites: `.push()` arg, `.put()` value, `.set()` value, `.add()` arg (collection methods in `c_expr_methods.rs`); enum variant constructor args (`c_expr_call.rs`); struct literal field args (`c_expr.rs`). Extended return handler with `collect_consumed_identifiers()` recursive tree walker that finds all identifiers consumed by calls/constructors/variants in return expressions (handles `return Arr(items)`, `return Tbl(dict)`, etc.). Key safety gate: `is_owning_collection_init()` restricts collection drops to constructor-initialized variables only (avoids aliased-buffer double-frees from copies, field access, or function returns). Non-collection drops (Box, File, user Drop) unaffected. `DropAction::involves_collection()` method distinguishes collection-related drops from non-collection ones, including recursive struct field inspection. Extended `drop_collections.gg` test with nested vector push and enum variant wrapping. Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `codegen/c_expr.rs`, `codegen/c_expr_call.rs`, `codegen/c_expr_methods.rs`, `drop_collections.gg`. All 474 unit + 240 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Restrict `str` from `&`/`!` parameter modes. Added `InvalidParameterMode` error variant to `SemanticErrorKind` that rejects mutable borrows (`&str`) and moves (`!str`) at declaration time — `str` is Copy, pointer-sized, and immutable, so these modes are semantically meaningless. Validation via `validate_str_param_modes()` in `resolve.rs`, called from three sites: top-level functions, equip methods, and trait method declarations. 3 new unit tests. - [2026-02-18] Phase 15: Box[T] Deep Drops + Collection Drop Infrastructure. Replaced `DropAction::BoxFree` with `BoxDrop { inner_drop: Option<Box<DropAction>> }` — when `Box[T]` goes out of scope, the inner type's destructor runs on `*var` before `free(var)`. E.g., `Box[Tracked]` where `Tracked` has `equip with Drop` now calls `Drop_for_Tracked__drop(&(*b))` then `free(b)`. Added three new `DropAction` variants (`ArrayFree`, `MapFree { mangled_name }`, `SetFree`) with full `emit_drop_entry()` and `emit_test_cleanup_for_action()` handlers — ready for activation when move-zeroing infrastructure exists. Collection drops are NOT yet registered in `drop_action_for_type()` because collections are non-Copy value types with shallow copy semantics: `.push(v)`, `.put(k,v)`, `.get()`, and constructors create shared-buffer copies that would cause double-free on scope-exit drops. The enabling work (move-zeroing after consumption sites, non-owning `.get()` returns, recursive return expression walking) is tracked in TODO.md. New integration test `drop_collections.gg` validates Box deep drops with `Tracked` struct's Drop printing before free. Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `drop_collections.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 471 unit + 239 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Fix `print()` format for trait object method return types. `print(traitObj.method())` now emits the correct printf format (`%s`/`%lld`/`%f`/`%s` for str/int/float/bool) instead of always falling back to `%lld`. Root cause: `resolve_expr_type_id()` in `c_expr.rs` couldn't resolve method return types for trait object receivers because `infer_receiver_type()` returns `"Unknown"` for them — no equip block matched. Fix: after the equip block search fails, use `resolve_trait_object_type(receiver)` to detect trait objects, then look up the method's return type from `TraitInfo.methods` in `self.traits.traits`. Also walks the `extends` chain for inherited methods. Files: `c_expr.rs`, `print_trait_object.gg`, `integration.rs`.
- [2026-02-18] Struct constructor str↔String field coercion. When a struct has a `String` field but a `str` literal is passed (e.g., `Holder("hello")`), the codegen now emits `gorget_string_new("hello")` instead of the bare string literal. Reverse coercion (String→str field) also works via `.data`. The fix lives in two codegen paths: (1) `Expr::StructLiteral` in `c_expr.rs` — the primary path after the `rewrite.rs` pass converts `Expr::Call` to `Expr::StructLiteral` for struct constructors; (2) `gen_call` in `c_expr_call.rs` — the fallback path for newtypes (which aren't rewritten). Both paths look up field types from `field_type_names` and apply `coerce_arg_to_str()` per field. Also added newtype inner types to `field_type_names` in `generate_c()`. New integration test `struct_string_coerce.gg`. Files: `codegen/c_expr.rs`, `codegen/c_expr_call.rs`, `codegen/mod.rs`, `tests/fixtures/struct_string_coerce.gg`, `tests/integration.rs`. - [2026-02-18] Phase 14: Automatic Drop Glue for Structs. Structs with non-Copy fields (String, Box, File, or nested droppable structs) now automatically drop their fields when going out of scope, even without an explicit `equip with Drop`. Added `DropAction::StructDrop { type_name, has_user_drop, field_drops }` variant encoding per-field cleanup. When a struct variable drops: (1) user's `drop()` method runs first (if any), (2) each non-Copy field is recursively dropped in reverse declaration order. `drop_action_for_type()` maps AST `Type` → `DropAction` (or None for Copy types), `compute_field_drops()` walks struct fields via `struct_fields` + `field_type_names` to find non-Copy fields. `maybe_register_droppable()` refactored to use `drop_action_for_type()`, eliminating duplicate Box/File/Named/String matching logic. Test-body cleanup (`__gorget_cleanup_push`) handled by `emit_test_cleanup_for_action()` which recursively emits per-field cleanup entries. Also hardened `gorget_string_free` with `cap > 0` guard — struct literals like `Holder("hello")` store string literal pointers in GorgetString.data with cap=0; calling `free()` on a string literal is UB. The cap guard makes this safe (same pattern as move zeroing where memset→0 makes cap=0). Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `codegen/c_runtime.rs`, `drop_struct_fields.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 472 unit + 237 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Fix cross-module span collisions in resolution_map. Added `base_offset: usize` to Lexer so each module is lexed with a cumulative byte offset, making all spans globally unique across merged modules. Previously, `resolution_map: FxHashMap<usize, DefId>` used bare `span.start` byte offsets as keys — when multiple file-based stdlib modules were merged, their spans all started at byte 0, causing key collisions (wrong C types, unresolved methods). Fix: Lexer gets `new_with_offset()` constructor and `span()` helper that applies the offset to all 28 `Span::new` call sites; Parser gets `new_with_offset()` that threads offset to Lexer; ModuleLoader tracks `next_offset` and assigns unique ranges to each parsed module; `load_imports()` returns concatenated source text matching the span offsets for use by ErrorReporter and CodegenOptions. This also fixes `method_resolutions` and `expr_types` maps. Files: `lexer/mod.rs`, `parser/mod.rs`, `loader.rs`, `main.rs`. All 472 unit + 236 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Add `Measurable` trait + fix `len(x)` free function. Registered `Measurable` as built-in trait in `resolve.rs` and `traits.rs` with signature `int len(self)`. Fixed `len(x)` codegen in `c_expr_call.rs` — replaced broken `sizeof(x)/sizeof(x[0])` (C array idiom, wrong for all Gorget types) with delegation to `gen_method_call`, which routes through the existing dispatch chain: built-in types → `try_gen_builtin_method` (Vector/Dict/Set/str/String inline C), user equip types → trait method call. Added `"len"` to return type resolution in `c_expr.rs`. New integration test `measurable_trait.gg` exercises `len()` on Vector, str, and a user type equipped with Measurable. Updated language-reference.md: trait table row, `len` free function description, `#### Measurable` subsection. Files: `resolve.rs`, `traits.rs`, `c_expr_call.rs`, `c_expr.rs`, `measurable_trait.gg`, `integration.rs`, `language-reference.md`. All 472 unit + 236 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Phase 13: Block-Scoped Drops. Added `DropScopeKind::Block` and wrapped `if`/`elif`/`else` branches, `match` arms, `with` blocks, and `unsafe` blocks with push/pop Block scope. Previously, variables declared inside these blocks registered their drops in the enclosing scope (Function or Loop), but the C variables are block-scoped — causing the cleanup code to reference variables outside their C scope. Block scopes ensure cleanup is emitted inside the C block (before `}`), where variables are still in scope. Applied to both main codegen path (6 sites) and break-flag code path for for-else/while-else (4 sites). All existing scope-traversal helpers (`emit_cleanup_to` for break/continue/return) already iterate through intermediate scopes, so Block scopes between variables and their enclosing Loop/Function scope make cleanup more correct. Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `drop_block_scope.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 472 unit + 235 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Fix Drop trait ownership: changed `self_ownership: None` (immutable borrow) to `Some(Ownership::Move)` (consuming `!self`) in built-in trait registration (`traits.rs:216`). Updated test fixtures (`drop_raii.gg`, `drop_reassign.gg`) from `void drop(self)` to `void drop(!self)` to match the language reference. This ensures correct `void*` (non-const) vtable slots when traits extend Drop, and makes the C function signature non-const so destructors can modify the object.
- [2026-02-18] Phase 12: Drop Safety (Move Zeroing + Drop-on-Reassign). Two codegen fixes for memory safety: (1) **Move zeroing** — when `!var` (move) transfers ownership, `memset(&var, 0, sizeof(var))` is emitted after the statement, making the scope-exit drop a no-op (`free(NULL)` is safe per C standard). Prevents double-free when both source and destination survive to scope exit. Uses `pending_move_zeros: Vec<String>` on `CodegenContext` to collect moved variables during `gen_expr`, flushed via `flush_move_zeros()` after each statement type (Expr, Assign, CompoundAssign, Return, VarDecl). (2) **Drop-before-reassign** — when a non-Copy variable is reassigned, the old value is dropped before the new one is stored. Uses temp-variable pattern (`__drop_tmp_N = new_expr; drop(old); var = __drop_tmp_N`) to avoid use-after-free when RHS references the target. `find_drop_action()` helper searches the drop scope stack. Key insight: zeroing keeps the drop scope entry, so no add/remove tracking is needed — the zeroed value produces a no-op drop, and on reassignment the new value replaces it. Files: `codegen/mod.rs`, `codegen/c_expr.rs`, `codegen/c_stmt.rs`, `drop_reassign.gg`, `drop_move_zero.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 472 unit + 234 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Documentation audit — fixed conflicts and filled gaps. language-reference.md: added missing keywords (directive, via, test/suite/assert), added Iterable/Default/From/TryFrom traits to §15.1 with examples, fixed @derive example and listed derivable traits, added 6 missing std.fs functions and codepoint_to_str, documented 11 missing stdlib modules (json, toml, xml, bytes, crypto, http.client, net.socket, gfx, sdl, ecs, ssh), added CLI features (--hot-reload, --shared, --show-borrows, -i, package commands), added directive hot-reload, fixed std.sync import example. language-design.md: fixed Displayable method to_string→display everywhere, updated test syntax @test void→test "name", fixed operator traits to use generic parameter pattern (not associated types), fixed auto array literal inference, marked 12+ unimplemented features (concurrency, @cfg, @deprecated, @bench, doc tests, Debuggable, Copy, Sendable, Syncable, BTreeMap/LinkedList/etc, std.sync/thread/async/regex/log/encoding). traits.rs: fixed stale 4-trait comment. - [2026-02-18] Lifetime inference Phase 11: Reassignment invalidation. When a non-Copy owning variable is reassigned, all existing references borrowing from the old value are now detected as dangling. New `reassignment_invalidated: FxHashMap<DefId, (String, Span)>` field in `BorrowChecker` tracks dependent variables whose borrow source was reassigned. Unlike `invalidated_origins` (which marks the source and would prevent new borrows), this marks the specific dependent variables — preserving the source's usability for new borrows after reassignment. Three insertion points: (1) `Stmt::Assign` walks `var_origins` for dependents when a non-Copy variable is reassigned and inserts them into `reassignment_invalidated`. (2) `check_use` checks the map before the existing `invalidated_origins` check, reusing `UseAfterSourceMoved` error. (3) When a dependent variable is itself reassigned, its entry is removed (fresh value). `BranchState` extended with `reassignment_invalidated` for correct save/restore/merge across branches (union semantics). 5 new unit tests (reassignment_invalidates_borrow, reassignment_new_borrow_ok, reassignment_reborrow_ok, reassignment_copy_type_ok, reassignment_transitive). 2 new integration tests: `lifetime_reassign.gg` (positive — reassignment then re-borrow), `lifetime_reassign_error.gg` (negative — borrow invalidated by reassignment). Files: `borrow.rs`, `lifetime_reassign.gg`, `lifetime_reassign_error.gg`, `integration.rs`. All 471 unit + 230 integration tests pass (1 pre-existing hot_reload platform issue).
- [2026-02-18] Fix multiple `From[T]`/`TryFrom[T]` impls per type (mangling collision). When a type had both `From[int]` and `From[str]`, both generated the same C symbol `From_for_Type__from`, causing a duplicate symbol error. Fix: encode trait generic type arguments into the mangled name — `From[int]` for UserId now produces `From__int64_t_for_UserId__from`, `From[str]` produces `From__const_char_ptr_for_UserId__from`. Non-generic traits (e.g., `Displayable`) are unchanged. Changes: (1) `mangle_trait_method` gains `trait_type_args: &[String]` param; (2) `function_signature`/`emit_function_prototype`/`emit_function_def` method_info tuple widened to include trait type args; (3) New helpers `impl_trait_type_args`, `impl_trait_type_args_raw`, `lookup_trait_type_args` for extracting and looking up trait type args (with base-name fallback for monomorphized generics); (4) `TraitRegistry::trait_impls` key widened from `(DefId, TypeId)` to `(DefId, TypeId, Vec<TypeId>)` to allow multiple impls of same parameterized trait; (5) All call sites (`From`, `TryFrom`, `Index`, `IndexMut`, `Iterable`, `Iterator`, `Equatable`, `Add`/`Sub`/`Mul`/`Div`/`Rem`/`Neg`, `Comparable`, `Default`, `Drop`, `Displayable`) updated to thread trait type args through. Files: `c_mangle.rs`, `c_item.rs`, `c_expr.rs`, `c_expr_call.rs`, `c_expr_generic.rs`, `c_expr_methods.rs`, `c_expr_print.rs`, `c_stmt.rs`, `traits.rs`, `from_trait_multi.gg`, `integration.rs`. 467 unit + 229 integration tests pass (1 pre-existing hot_reload platform issue).
- [2026-02-18] Borrow analysis diagnostics and origin tracking improvements. Three features: (1) **`--show-borrows` diagnostic flag** — `gg check --show-borrows` and `gg build --show-borrows` print the inferred `return_borrows_from` for every function, showing which parameters' data flows to the return value. Helps programmers understand what the compiler inferred and builds trust in the inference system. (2) **Enriched error messages** — `UseAfterSourceMoved` now shows a secondary label at the move site ("`source_name` moved here"); `DanglingReturn` shows where the local variable was declared ("will be dropped when function returns"). Uses `codespan_reporting` secondary labels for precise multi-span diagnostics. (3) **Reduced `Unknown` origin fallbacks** — `compute_expr_origin()` now explicitly handles 15+ expression types that previously fell to the catch-all `Unknown`: value-type literals (int/float/bool/char → Static), binary/unary ops (→ Static), Range (→ Static), Is (→ Static), comprehensions (→ Static), OptionalChain/MutableBorrow/Await/Spawn (→ propagate inner), Path (→ resolve like Identifier). Fewer `Unknown` origins means more precise tracking and fewer missed bugs. Also filed two future analysis items to TODO.md: demand-driven refinement and `@guarded` self-referential struct support. Files: `main.rs`, `errors.rs`, `semantic/errors.rs`, `semantic/borrow.rs`, `TODO.md`. All 466 unit + 228 integration tests pass.
- [2026-02-18] Lifetime inference Phase 10: Cross-function callable lifetime tracking. Extended lifetime tracking to closures received from function calls (e.g., `auto f = make_closure(v)` where `make_closure` returns `Callable[void()]`). Previously, `compute_function_return_borrows` (Pass 5a) gated on `is_reference_type`, excluding callable return types — so `compute_call_origin` returned `Unknown` and the closure variable got no origin in `var_origins`. Six changes: (1) Extended `compute_function_return_borrows` gate to also accept `is_callable_type`. (2) Added `Expr::Closure` arm to `trace_expr_to_params` with `trace_closure_body_to_params` / `trace_closure_body_stmts` recursive walkers that find outer function params captured in closure bodies (excludes closure's own params and nested closures). (3) Extended elision fallbacks (declaration/extern and body-analysis) to include callable-typed params. (4) Extended VarDecl handler to track callable-typed variables from any expression (not just direct `Expr::Closure`), using `is_callable_type` check with `Expr::Closure` fallback for `auto` vars. (5) Extended `Stmt::Assign` handler to insert fresh origins for callable-typed reassignments. (6) Extended `mark_pattern_origins` and `collect_captured_ref_origins` to include callable types. 4 new unit tests (cross_function_closure_source_moved, cross_function_closure_ok, closure_reassignment_tracks_origin, closure_pattern_binding_origin), 1 new integration test (lifetime_closure_cross_fn_error). Files: `borrow.rs`, `lifetime_closure_cross_fn_error.gg`, `integration.rs`.
- [2026-02-18] Lifetime inference Phase 9: Closure lifetime safety. Two new safety checks: (1) **Use-after-source-moved through closures** — closures capturing ref-type variables now have their origins stored in `var_origins`, so `check_use()` detects when a closure's captured reference source is invalidated. (2) **Dangling closure return** — `Stmt::Return` and expression-body function checks now cover callable types (via new `is_callable_type()` helper), catching closures that capture local references from being returned. Added `is_callable_type()` to `types.rs` (matches Function, CallableTrait, MutCallableTrait, ConsumeCallableTrait, BoxedCallable). VarDecl handler stores `compute_expr_origin()` for closure-valued variables when origin is non-Unknown. - [2026-02-17] ConsumeCallable single-call enforcement: When the borrow checker encounters `Expr::Call` where the callee is a `ConsumeCallable`-typed variable (including `ConsumeCallableTrait` and `BoxedCallable { kind: ConsumeCallable }`), the call is now treated as a **move** of that variable. First call marks the variable as `Moved` (succeeds); second call triggers `DoubleMove` error; use after call triggers `UseAfterMove`; call in a loop triggers `MoveInLoop`; call in one branch conservatively marks as `Moved`. - [2026-02-16] Fix GorgetString coercion memory leaks: Temporary GorgetString expressions (function call results like `gorget_string_from_concat(...)`) coerced to `const char*` via `.data` leaked the malloc'd buffer because the wrapper struct was abandoned. Fixed by adding a `string_temps` side channel on `CodegenContext`: when coercing a temporary GorgetString to `const char*`, codegen materializes it as a named `__strtmp_N` variable before the containing statement and frees it inline after consumption. Heuristic: `expr.contains('(') && !expr.starts_with('(')` identifies function-call temporaries (excludes dereferences `(*s)` and casts). Inline cleanup (not drop scope registration) avoids C block scoping issues — temps are freed at the same scope level they were declared. VarDecl/Assign coercion left as `.data` (no temp) since the `const char*` outlives the statement and would become a dangling pointer if freed. Return handler uses `__ret_tmp` pattern: flush temps, assign to temp, free, return. elif conditions with string temps use wrapper block pattern (`} else { <temps>; if (...) { ... } <frees>; }`). Updated 10 coercion sites across `c_expr.rs`, `c_expr_call.rs`, `c_expr_methods.rs`, `c_expr_print.rs`. Added `flush_string_temps` calls in 10 statement handlers (`Stmt::Expr`, `Assign`, `CompoundAssign`, `If` with elif wrapper, `Throw`, `Assert`, `Match`, `VarDecl`, `Return`). `c_types.rs:format_for_c_type` left as-is (free function, no `self` access) with TODO comment. New files: `tests/fixtures/hot_reload_basic.gg`. - [2026-02-13] `@derive(Displayable, Equatable, Hashable)` for generic enums: three fixes — (1) derive macro now emits `equip [T] Wrapper[T]` syntax (generic params before type name) so parser populates `generic_params` on the EquipBlock AST, (2) typecheck.rs pushes a scope with GenericParam defs for generic equip blocks in both pre-pass and main pass so `T` resolves correctly in `ast_type_to_resolved`, (3) skip Displayable check for GenericParam types in string interpolation; also fixed 3 codegen issues: `type_id_to_c_substituted` helper applies `type_subs` mapping for GenericParam TypeIds — used in `resolve_enum_c_type_for_scrutinee` (enum tags), `format_for_type_id` (string interpolation), `infer_receiver_mangled_type` and `infer_receiver_c_type` (method dispatch); added `format_for_c_type` in c_types.rs for C-type-to-printf mapping
- [2026-02-13] Mutable borrow parameters in free functions: `Type &name` params in non-method free functions now emit `Type*` pointer parameters in C, with `(*name)` dereference for identifier reads, `name->field` for field access, and `&arg` wrapping at call sites; also handles method calls on pointer params (pass pointer directly instead of `&(*name)`), string interpolation dereference, and generic method/equip block pointer params; integration test `mutable_borrow_params.gg` with increment, reset, swap_values free functions
- [2026-02-13] `@derive` for generic structs/enums: type parameter forwarding in generated equip blocks (`equip Pair[T] with Equatable:` instead of `equip Pair with Equatable:`); added `format_generic_params()` helper + `gs` parameter through all 8 derive generators; fixed 5 codegen issues for generic trait equip blocks: (1) `is_generic_equip()` now checks enum templates too, (2) `discover_generic_usages()` skips generic equip blocks to prevent spurious template instantiations, (3) `emit_vtable_instances()` skips generic equip blocks, (4) `emit_generic_method_definitions()` handles both struct and enum equip blocks, (5) trait method call sites use mangled type names via new `infer_receiver_mangled_type()` helper; also fixed `resolve_enum_c_type_for_scrutinee()` for `SelfExpr` and variant constructor resolution in monomorphized method bodies; struct Equatable/Displayable/Cloneable/Hashable all work for generic structs; enum Cloneable works for generic enums (Displayable/Equatable/Hashable blocked by separate semantic issue with pattern binding type resolution)
- [2026-02-13] `@derive(Cloneable)` for enums: generates `clone()` method via match on self with variant reconstruction (unit variants return bare constructor, tuple variants bind and reconstruct fields); mirrors existing enum derive pattern (Equatable, Displayable, Hashable)
- [2026-02-13] ECS battle simulation showcase (`examples/ecs/`): reusable ECS library with `EntityPool` (ID allocation + recycling via free list) and `SparseSet[T]` (generic sparse set container with O(1) insert/remove/lookup using swap-and-pop), turn-based battle game with `World` struct composing EntityPool + 4 SparseSets (health, attacks, teams, names), combat system targeting highest-HP enemy with tie-break on lowest ID, dead entity cleanup; demonstrates generic structs with equip blocks, multi-file modules, `@derive(Displayable)`, `&self` mutation
- [2026-02-13] Generic equip block monomorphization in codegen: `equip SparseSet[T]:` methods now correctly monomorphized for each concrete instantiation (e.g. `SparseSet__Health__insert`); added `generic_equip_templates` storage, forward declarations for generic struct instantiations, split emission into type definitions (before user types) and method definitions (after), type substitution in method bodies, `infer_receiver_type` fallback from mangled to base name for field lookups
- [2026-02-13] `@derive(Hashable)` for structs and enums: built-in `.hash()` method on all primitive types (int/float/bool/char/str) via `__gorget_fnv1a`/`__gorget_hash_str` runtime functions; wired into `builtin_method_type` (semantic), `try_gen_builtin_method`/`gen_string_method`/`builtin_method_return_type` (codegen); struct derive combines field hashes via `h *% 31 +% field.hash()` (wrapping arithmetic); enum derive hashes variant index + fields via match; also fixed `SelfExpr` typing in typecheck — added `current_self_type` field to TypeChecker, set from equip block target type, so `match self:` pattern bindings get correct type_ids for codegen dispatch
- [2026-02-13] `@derive` macro expansion: `@derive(Equatable, Displayable, Cloneable)` on structs and `@derive(Equatable, Displayable)` on enums auto-generates equip blocks with correct method bodies; template expansion approach generates Gorget source, parses it, and splices EquipBlock AST nodes before semantic analysis; struct Equatable (field-by-field ==), Displayable (format("Type(f1={self.f1},...)")), Cloneable (constructor copy); enum Equatable (nested match on tag + fields), Displayable (match on tag with field formatting); UnderivableTrait error for invalid derives; also fixed two codegen bugs: (1) match on `self` in enum methods now dereferences the self pointer, (2) match arm block bodies now generate statements directly instead of wrapping in GCC statement expressions
- [2026-02-12] Closure mutable reference captures: closures that assign to captured variables now capture them by mutable reference (pointer) so mutations propagate to the outer scope; added CaptureMode enum (ByValue/ByMutRef), mutation detection via AST walk, `(*__env->var)` codegen for ByMutRef reads/writes, `TYPE*` in env struct with `&var` population; also fixed `walk_free_vars` to handle Block/Match/TupleFieldAccess/nested Closure/StringInterpolation and added `walk_free_vars_in_stmt` for full statement-level recursion; fixed `stmt_to_inline_string` for CompoundAssign, `infer_c_type_from_expr` for Block/Do void inference, and void-returning lifted closure emission
- [2026-02-12] Closure parameter type inference: untyped closure params like `(a, b): a + b` now infer types from calling context; typecheck writes fresh type vars to DefInfo for untyped params, finalization pass with deep resolution walks composite types (Function, etc.) to replace all type vars with concrete types before substitution map is dropped, codegen looks up inferred types from DefInfo when AST annotation is missing
- [2026-02-12] Refactor codegen to `&mut self`: removed all `RefCell` wrappers from `CodegenContext` fields (13 fields), changed ~80 method signatures from `&self` to `&mut self` across c_item.rs/c_expr.rs/c_stmt.rs, replaced all `.borrow()`/`.borrow_mut()` calls with direct field access; fixes 2 borrow-checker conflicts via `.cloned()` on `field_type_names.get()` before calling `ast_type_to_type_id`; eliminates runtime overhead of RefCell and makes mutation explicit in the type system
- [2026-02-12] Fix Deref type inference and cross-module span collision in semantic analysis: (1) `Expr::Deref` in typecheck.rs now unwraps `Box[T]` → `T` instead of returning `Box[T]` unchanged — was masked in single-file mode because variant constructors resolved to error_id, but exposed in multi-module mode where function signatures are fully registered; (2) added `resolve_name()` helper to typecheck.rs with name-validation guards on all 8 `resolution_map.get()` sites, matching the codegen fix; fixes `examples/calculator/main.gg` regression
- [2026-02-12] Multi-file pipeline showcase (`examples/pipeline/`): Student struct with Displayable, reusable stats functions (sum via fold, max/min/count via for-loops), data processing pipeline with filter/map/fold on Vector[Student], cross-module imports; also fixed cross-module span collision bug in codegen: resolution_map keyed by `span.start` (byte offset) collides when merged modules have overlapping file-relative offsets — added name-validation guards to all 5 `resolution_map.get()` call sites in c_expr.rs so collisions fall through to `lookup_by_name_anywhere` fallback
- [2026-02-12] Pattern-bound variable type inference in match: `assign_pattern_types` in typecheck.rs propagates scrutinee type through patterns to assign type_ids to bindings; handles built-in Option/Result generics, user-defined enums (with generic substitution via `variant_field_types` on `EnumVariantInfo`), tuples, and or-patterns; `print("{e}")` in `case Error(e):` for `Result[int, str]` now correctly prints strings instead of garbage `%lld` output; updated `match_option_result.gg` to test `Result[int, str]`
- [2026-02-12] Multi-file todo_app showcase (`examples/todo_app/`): Task struct with Displayable trait, Priority enum, TaskStore wrapping `Vector[Task]` with filter/count methods; demonstrates Vector of user-defined structs, closures with struct types in filter, `&self` mutation, cross-module trait equip, format() with field access; required fixing `infer_vector_elem_type` to extract element type from AST field annotations when `resolve_expr_type_id` can't resolve generic field types like `Vector[Task]`
- [2026-02-12] Multi-file calculator showcase (`examples/calculator/`): recursive `Expr` enum with `Box[Expr]` payloads (Num, Add, Mul, Neg), recursive `eval()` using match destructuring + Box dereference, helper functions with expression-body syntax, cross-module imports; required fixing two codegen bugs: (1) `box_inner_c_type` now uses `resolve_expr_type_id` for reliable type resolution instead of falling back to `int64_t`, (2) `Expr::Deref` handler always emits C dereference `(*inner)` since Gorget `*` is exclusively Box dereference

- [2026-02-12] Match on generic enum variants (`case Some(x):` for `Option[int]`, `case Ok(v):`/`case Error(e):` for `Result[int,int]`, `is Some`/`is None`): fixed tag constant names in `pattern_to_condition` (c_stmt.rs) and `pattern_to_condition_expr` (c_expr.rs) to use monomorphized enum names (e.g. `Option__int64_t_TAG_Some`) instead of raw names (`Option_TAG_Some`); added `resolve_enum_c_type_for_scrutinee()` helper to resolve scrutinee type to mangled C name via `ResolvedType::Generic`; also fixed `Pattern::Literal(NoneLiteral)` to generate tag checks instead of `== NULL` when matching on Option enums; integration test `match_option_result.gg`

- [2026-02-12] Implement automatic `Box[Trait]` dispatch: semantic resolves `Box[Trait]` to `ResolvedType::TraitObject` (added `DefKind::Trait` to allowed types in `ast_type_to_resolved`), codegen detects `Box[Trait]` patterns in `extract_trait_object_construction` for trait object construction (`{.data=..., .vtable=&vtable}`), vtable dispatch via `recv.vtable->method(recv.data)` in `gen_method_call`, `TraitObjFree` drop action (`free(.data)`), `ast_type_to_c` maps `Box[Trait]` to `Trait_TraitObj`; updated `dynamic_dispatch.gg` fixture to exercise both direct and vtable dispatch

- [2026-02-11] Wrapping operators `+%`/`-%`/`*%` and `+%=`/`-%=`/`*%=`: per-expression opt-out from overflow checking (Zig-style), full pipeline: 6 new lexer tokens, 3 BinaryOp variants, parser at same precedence as regular ops, typecheck, codegen emits plain C arithmetic (skips checked macros), formatter, integration test
